# @ledger/design-system 0.6.0

Ledger, the product design system, as one file for agents and tools that cannot reach the running Storybook. Generated by `npm run build:llms` from the Storybook pages under `src/stories`, the token sheet in `src/generated/docs.json` and the public export inventory; do not edit by hand. The running Storybook and its MCP server remain the contract for verifying a change. The repository's `packages/design-system/AGENTS.md` says how to work on the package.

<!-- page: Introduction (src/stories/docs/Introduction.mdx) -->

# Ledger

Ledger is the design system behind the programme assurance product: one set of decisions about colour, type, space, shape, motion and behaviour, shipped as a package that any React and Tailwind project can install.

It is built on three ideas.

**Every design value is a token.** A colour is `color.text.subtle`, not a hex code and not a Tailwind grey. A space is `space.200`, not `16px`. A control is `dimension.control.medium` tall. Tokens are named for their role, so a screen reads as intent and the visual DNA lives in one place. Change a token and every screen follows; add a colour mode and no component changes.

**States are tokens too.** Hovered, pressed, selected and disabled are their own tokens, never alpha on a base colour. That is what makes dark mode a mechanical flip instead of a redesign, and it is the rule the lint enforces most strictly.

**Layout goes through primitives.** Box, Stack, Inline, Flex and Grid take token-typed props. Product code says `<Stack space="space.200">` and never writes a margin.

## Where things are

- **Tokens** are the sheets: the palette ramps, the semantic colours in both modes, the type ramp, the space scale, shape and the control metrics. Each sheet is read from the generated docs, so it is the build, not a drawing of it.
- **Primitives** are the layout and text elements every screen is made from.
- **Components** are the parts: buttons, badges, controls, tabs and the rest, each with representative examples and a docs page with usage guidance. Matrices help when variants need comparison.
- **Guidance** covers the grammar, the lint rules and how to install the package.

Switch the **Mode** toolbar above to see any page in dark.

<!-- page: Guidance/Getting started (src/stories/docs/GettingStarted.mdx) -->

# Getting started

The package is `@ledger/design-system`. It ships TypeScript source, a generated CSS layer and an ESLint preset. Its only peers are React and Tailwind 4.

## Install

```sh
npm install @ledger/design-system
```

The package ships `dist/` (ESM with declarations, from `npm run build`) and `src/`. A bundler that sets the `development` condition (Vite in dev) resolves to source; everything else resolves to dist. The stylesheets always come from `src`, because `ledger.css` scans the source for the classes your build needs.

## CSS

One stylesheet, in this order. The reset must come before the system: it clears Tailwind's default namespaces (colours, spacing, radii, shadows, fonts) so that only token utilities exist, and it would clear the system's own mappings if it came after them.

```css
@import "tailwindcss";
@import "@ledger/design-system/reset.css";
@import "@ledger/design-system/ledger.css";
@import "@ledger/design-system/base.css";
```

`ledger.css` carries an `@source` directive pointing at the package, so Tailwind generates the classes the components use even though they live in `node_modules`. `base.css` is optional: it sets the colour scheme, the default border colour and the body's type and colour.

## Components

```tsx

export function Empty() {
  return (
    <Stack space="space.200" alignInline="center">
      <Text color="color.text.subtle">No controls match these filters.</Text>
      <Button variant="primary">Clear filters</Button>
    </Stack>
  );
}
```

Standard reusable components follow the local shadcn Base UI reference with flat named parts,
native props and refs, and Ledger token styling. Breadcrumb is the first family migrated;
other existing families keep their documented APIs until explicitly migrated. Assemble
convenience layouts in patterns while keeping the component parts available.

Components never import a router. Breadcrumb uses `render` to compose your router's link;
the link must accept the merged attributes, handlers and ref:

```tsx

export function RecordTrail() {
  return (
    <Breadcrumb aria-label="Breadcrumb">
      <BreadcrumbList>
        <BreadcrumbItem>
          <BreadcrumbLink render={<Link to="/controls" />}>Controls</BreadcrumbLink>
        </BreadcrumbItem>
        <BreadcrumbSeparator />
        <BreadcrumbItem>
          <BreadcrumbPage>New control</BreadcrumbPage>
        </BreadcrumbItem>
      </BreadcrumbList>
    </Breadcrumb>
  );
}
```

The list, links, current page and separators are explicit parts. `BreadcrumbEllipsis` is a
decorative overflow mark; compose it inside a named menu trigger when an overflow menu is needed.
The default list wraps. See [Breadcrumb](?path=/docs/components-breadcrumb--docs) for the full
anatomy and migration examples.

For navigation with button styling, put `buttonVariants` on the router link. It keeps its native
link behavior. Action composition uses Button's `render`; TabsTrigger uses `render` with
`nativeButton={false}` for a navigation tab.

```tsx

<Link to="/controls/new" className={buttonVariants({ variant: "primary" })}>
  New control
</Link>;
```

## Colour mode

Tokens flip on `data-color-mode="dark"` on the root element, or on the system preference when no attribute is set. Nothing in a component knows which mode it is in.

```html
<html data-color-mode="dark"></html>
```

## Lint

The package exports an ESLint flat config. `recommended` makes every token rule an error and layout-through-primitives a warning.

```js

export default [...ledger.configs.recommended];
```

## Utilities in product code

Token utilities (`bg-surface-raised`, `text-subtle`, `p-200`, `rounded-medium`) are legal in product code; primitives are preferred for layout. Tailwind's own design utilities (`bg-blue-500`, `text-sm`, `p-4`, `rounded-md`) do not exist after the reset and the lint reports them.

<!-- page: Guidance/Agents (src/stories/docs/Agents.mdx) -->

# Working with Ledger as an agent

This Storybook is the contract. A coding agent that uses Ledger reads it the same way a person does: the family page says what a part is for, the generated props say what it accepts, and the stories show every state the part supports. Nothing about a part is true because another design system does it that way.

## Where the instructions are

| Question                                   | Read                                                                                                                                                                    |
| ------------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Which part answers this need?              | Guidance/Choosing a part, then the family's page.                                                                                                                       |
| What is a part for, and what does it take? | The family's page here: Components, Patterns, Layout, Primitives. Its `ArgTypes` table is generated from the source.                                                    |
| I know shadcn or Radix; what is different? | Guidance/Coming from shadcn.                                                                                                                                            |
| How do the parts compose into a screen?    | Guidance/Recipes, and the Layout/Pages stories.                                                                                                                         |
| Which value or class do I use?             | Guidance/Which token for the short answer by job; the Tokens sheets and the Grammar page for everything. Tokens are the only styling.                                   |
| How do I install or import it?             | Getting started, and the Importing section of the component library guide in the repo.                                                                                  |
| What does the lint reject?                 | The Lint rules page.                                                                                                                                                    |
| How do I add or change a part?             | The package `AGENTS.md`, which points at the "Adding to the kit" checklist in the component library guide; Guidance/Writing stories for the story and page conventions. |
| Which part does the application use here?  | Not this Storybook. The application's composition contract, `docs/guides/product-patterns.md`, decides that; app compositions stay out of these stories.                |

## Through the MCP server

The Storybook serves an MCP endpoint at `/mcp` while it runs (`npm run storybook`, port 6007). The repository's `.mcp.json` registers it as `storybook-mcp`. Use its tools in this order:

1. `get-storybook-story-instructions` before writing or editing a story. Its output is the source of truth for imports, story shape and test conventions.
2. `docs-list` once, then `docs-show` for a family before using any of its props. A prop that the documentation does not show does not exist; report the gap rather than guessing.
3. `stories-preview` after any change that alters how something looks: a component, a story, a stylesheet or a token. A shared file with no story of its own is previewed through its consumers' stories. Report the returned URLs.
4. `test-run` to run the affected stories, focused while iterating and broad before handoff. Fix failures before reporting completion.

## Without the MCP server

`packages/design-system/llms.txt` is this Storybook's pages, the token sheet and the public export list, generated into one file by `npm run build:llms`. It is committed and the package tests fail when it drifts, so a cold checkout and an agent without MCP access read the same contract. It never replaces the running Storybook for verifying a change.

## What an agent gets wrong most often

- Using a prop from shadcn, Radix or Base UI that Ledger's part does not expose. Look it up first.
- Writing a class the lint will reject: an arbitrary value, a Tailwind colour, a margin, a `dark:` variant. Use a token utility or a primitive prop.
- Copying a kit part into product code instead of importing it. `ledger/no-kit-shadow` names the part to import.
- Editing `src/generated/` by hand. Change `tokens/` and rebuild.
- Putting an application composition into a package story. The package documents neutral contracts; the application is verified in the running app.
- Rendering both colour modes in one story. The toolbar switches the mode; a story renders once.

<!-- page: Guidance/Choosing a part (src/stories/docs/Choosing.mdx) -->

# Choosing a part

The catalog is organised by family. This page is organised by need: find the row that names what the reader has to do, then open the part's own page for its props and states. When two parts look alike, the row says which one and why. A need with no row is a gap to flag, not a reason to build a raw element.

## Show a value

| The reader needs to see                                  | Use                                                                                           | Not                                                  |
| -------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------- |
| A record's status, one word in a pill                    | **Badge** with a tone. One pill per row, in the status column.                                | Indicator, which is never a pill.                    |
| Severity or health beside a label                        | **Indicator** (a Dot and a word), or the bare **Dot** in a tight cell.                        | A second Badge in the row.                           |
| How many: unread, rows behind a filter, findings         | **Count**, after the name of what it counts.                                                  | A Badge holding a number.                            |
| An identifier: AC-2(3), FND-2231, a hash                 | **Id**. Tabular numerals, inherits everything else.                                           | CodeBlock, or a Badge.                               |
| A label and value on one baseline, above the fold        | **Fact**, and **Fact.Group** for the four to six facts under a title.                         | KeyValue, which is a rail row.                       |
| A label and value in a rail, one per line                | **KeyValue**, and **Inspector** for a group of them.                                          | A hand-written definition list.                      |
| A headline number                                        | **Stat**; **Stat.Tile** in a **Stat.Grid** when framed.                                       | A Heading holding a number.                          |
| A value that is missing                                  | **Absent**, the muted dash.                                                                   | An empty string, a hyphen typed by hand, or "N/A".   |
| A section's name in a rail, a record's kind over a title | **Eyebrow**.                                                                                  | A small Heading.                                     |
| A labelled paragraph                                     | **Prose**.                                                                                    | Text with a bold first line.                         |
| A person                                                 | **Person**; **Avatar** and **AvatarGroup** for the mark alone.                                |                                                      |
| A file                                                   | **Attachment**. The application owns upload, retry and removal.                               |                                                      |
| Source, a log, a command to paste                        | **CodeBlock** with `copy` when the reader will take it.                                       | A `<pre>`.                                           |
| A keyboard shortcut                                      | **Kbd**, **KbdGroup** for a chord.                                                            |                                                      |
| Events in order                                          | **Timeline**.                                                                                 | A Table of dates.                                    |
| Steps through an ordered path                            | **Stepper**.                                                                                  | Tabs.                                                |
| The conditions an action waits on                        | **Gates**: a list, never a score.                                                             | Progress.                                            |
| A completion fraction                                    | **Progress**; **ProgressStacked** for parts of a whole.                                       | A Stat with a percentage, unless it is the headline. |
| Numbers drawn                                            | **Chart** and one of its kinds: Bar, Line, Area, Donut, Scatter, Heatmap, Treemap, Sparkline. | A hand-drawn SVG.                                    |

## Lay it out

| The layout is                                  | Use                                                                    |
| ---------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Things stacked top to bottom with one gap      | **Stack** with a `space` token.                                        |
| Things left to right with one gap, wrapping    | **Inline**.                                                            |
| Something Stack and Inline cannot say          | **Flex**.                                                              |
| Columns                                        | **Grid** with token gaps.                                              |
| A padded or coloured block                     | **Box**. Padding and background are token-typed; there are no margins. |
| A child escaping its parent's padding          | **Bleed**, the only negative space.                                    |
| A titled region of a page                      | **Section**, with `count`, `description` and `action` when needed.     |
| The page's name and its actions                | **PageHeader**: Lead, Heading, Title, Description, Actions.            |
| The application frame                          | **Shell** and its areas: Banner, TopNav, SideNav, Main, Aside, Panel.  |
| Two panes the reader resizes                   | **ResizablePanelGroup**.                                               |
| A scrolling region with a visible bar          | **ScrollArea** and **ScrollBar**.                                      |
| A hairline between things                      | **Separator**. The parent owns the spacing around it.                  |
| A raised container for a table, chart or facts | **Card**.                                                              |

Body copy is **Text**; titles are **Heading** with the size from the design and the level from the page.

## Collect input

| The reader enters                   | Use                                                                                         |
| ----------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Any control's label, hint and error | **Field** and its parts. Field owns layout; the form owns values and validation.            |
| One line of text                    | **Input**; **InputGroup** when it carries an icon, a unit or a button.                      |
| Several lines                       | **Textarea**.                                                                               |
| One of a few known values           | **Select**; **RadioGroup** when all the choices should be visible.                          |
| One of many values, by typing       | **Combobox**. It filters; Select does not.                                                  |
| Several values as chips             | **Combobox** with `ComboboxChips`.                                                          |
| Yes or no                           | **Checkbox** in a form; **Switch** when it takes effect at once.                            |
| A pressed state on a button         | **Toggle**; **ToggleGroup** for one-of or many-of.                                          |
| A day                               | **DatePicker**; **Calendar** on its own when the month should stay open.                    |
| A filter on a register              | **FilterChip** in a **Toolbar**.                                                            |
| A short draft with mentions         | **Composer**.                                                                               |
| A whole form                        | The **Forms** pattern: Field, controls, primitives and Buttons. There is no Form component. |

## Pick records

| Choosing                                                     | Use                                                                                   |
| ------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| One value from a short, fixed list                           | **Select**.                                                                           |
| One value from a long list, by typing                        | **Combobox**.                                                                         |
| One record with an id, a name and a status, by typing        | **RecordPicker**: a Command dialog with record rows. The caller supplies the rows.    |
| Many records from hundreds, with filters and a running count | **PickerSheet**: a Sheet whose body is a DataTable with selection.                    |
| Related records the reader must compare before choosing      | **RecordBrowser**: search, compare, preview and select without leaving the record.    |
| A command, not a record                                      | **CommandPalette** (⌘K) over the page; **Command** parts to build a list of your own. |

## Tables and lists

| The collection is                                            | Use                                                                                                     |
| ------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| A register with sort, filters, pages, selection or a toolbar | **DataTable**, columns declared by kind, with **Toolbar** above it and `fill` when it takes the window. |
| A short list with nothing to sort or choose                  | **Table**, the markup alone: a version history, a definition list of sources.                           |
| A hierarchy the reader opens and closes                      | **Tree**; **DataTable** with nested rows when the rows also sort and filter.                            |
| Linked records in a rail or on a page                        | **Related**: a card with a Count, a way to add one, a row or card per record.                           |
| One compact record row with aligned parts                    | **Item**.                                                                                               |
| A checklist or work queue row                                | **TaskRow**.                                                                                            |
| The next record without leaving the list                     | **PreviewNavigation** in a **Shell.Panel**; **PreviewSheet** only when the task must hold focus.        |
| A record's summary on hover                                  | **HoverCard** holding a **Glance**.                                                                     |
| Search, views, filters and actions above a table             | **Toolbar**: search, `views`, `filters`, children, `actions`.                                           |
| Page controls                                                | **Pagination**; DataTable draws its own.                                                                |

## Overlays

Eight surfaces float over the page. The Overlays page holds the full table with what opens and closes each; the short form:

| Need                                       | Use                                                         |
| ------------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------- |
| A short label                              | **Tooltip**. IconButton already draws one from its `label`. |
| A peek at a record, no actions             | **HoverCard**                                               |
| A small task at its button                 | **Popover**                                                 |
| A list of actions                          | **DropdownMenu**                                            |
| A focused task over the page: create, edit | **Dialog**                                                  |
| A modal selection or review                | **Sheet**                                                   |
| A quick task on a narrow screen            | **Drawer**                                                  |
| A decision that needs a word first         | **AlertDialog**                                             |

A value edited where it sits, with no form and no Save, is **Editable**. A larger change is a Dialog.

## Navigate and act

| The reader                            | Use                                                                              |
| ------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Goes somewhere, reading as text       | **TextLink** with a router link through `render`.                                |
| Goes somewhere, looking like a button | A real link styled with `buttonVariants`.                                        |
| Does something                        | **Button**; **IconButton** with a required `label` when the icon is unambiguous. |
| Chooses among joined actions          | **ButtonGroup**.                                                                 |
| Sees where they are                   | **Breadcrumb** in `PageHeader.Lead`.                                             |
| Switches between views of one page    | **Tabs** with `TabsList variant="line"`.                                         |
| Opens a region                        | **Collapsible**; **Accordion** when only one opens at a time.                    |
| Switches colour mode                  | **ModeSwitch**, inside **ModeProvider**.                                         |

## Feedback and states

| The situation                            | Use                                                                                           |
| ---------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| A region with nothing in it              | **Empty** with an illustration, a title, one line and the next step. DataTable draws its own. |
| Something about this record, inline      | **Alert** with a title, a description and an action.                                          |
| Something about the whole site           | **Banner**, one at a time, in the shell's Banner area.                                        |
| Short feedback after an action           | **Toaster**, mounted once.                                                                    |
| Content with a known shape still loading | **Skeleton**; **PageSkeleton** for a page's first paint.                                      |
| An action in flight                      | **Spinner**, or Button's loading state.                                                       |
| A failure                                | An Alert with a retry. Never a blank region.                                                  |
| Density of a table                       | **Table** `density`; DataTable's Columns menu offers Compact rows.                            |

<!-- page: Guidance/Coming from shadcn (src/stories/docs/FromShadcn.mdx) -->

# Coming from shadcn, Radix and Base UI

Ledger's families are built from shadcn's Base UI compositions, so most names are the ones you know. The APIs are not identical, and the differences are exactly where an agent invents a prop. Read this page once, then look every prop up on the family's page before using it.

## The three differences that matter most

**`render`, not `asChild`.** Ledger is on Base UI, not Radix. A part composes another element through `render={<a href="…" />}` (or a function). `asChild` does not exist anywhere in the package.

**Tokens, not the shadcn theme.** There is no `bg-background`, `text-muted-foreground`, `border-input` from shadcn's CSS variables, and no `dark:` variant. Every colour, space, radius and type value is a Ledger token utility (`bg-surface`, `text-subtle`, `border-default`, `p-200`, `font-body-small`) or a primitive prop. The lint rejects the rest; the Which token page lists what to reach for.

**`cn` from the package.** Import it from `@ledger/design-system/cn`. There is no `lib/utils`.

## Name by name

| You know                                                                         | In Ledger                                                 | What differs                                                                                                                               |
| -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Button                                                                           | **Button**, **IconButton**, `buttonVariants`              | A focus-preserving `loading` state. IconButton needs a `label` and draws its own Tooltip. Navigation is a real link with `buttonVariants`. |
| Badge                                                                            | **Badge**                                                 | Six variants plus semantic `tone`s and two sizes. A status is one Badge per row; severity is **Indicator**, a number is **Count**.         |
| Label                                                                            | **FieldLabel**, inside **Field**                          | No standalone Label. Field owns the label, description and error layout.                                                                   |
| Form (react-hook-form)                                                           | The **Forms** pattern                                     | No Form component. TanStack Form owns state and validation; Field, the controls and the primitives are the presentation.                   |
| Input                                                                            | **Input**                                                 | Wraps Base UI's Input. Labels and errors belong to Field.                                                                                  |
| Input Group                                                                      | **InputGroup** and its parts                              | Flat shadcn Base UI composition; addons, text, buttons and a textarea variant.                                                             |
| Textarea                                                                         | **Textarea**                                              | Native.                                                                                                                                    |
| Select, Native Select                                                            | **Select**                                                | Native Select is removed. Select does not filter; a list that needs typing is **Combobox**.                                                |
| Combobox, Command as a picker                                                    | **Combobox**; **RecordPicker** for records                | Combobox is flat Base UI composition with chips. A picker of records with ids and statuses is the RecordPicker pattern.                    |
| Command (cmdk)                                                                   | **Command** parts, **CommandPalette**                     | The palette takes plain command objects and stays presentational.                                                                          |
| Checkbox, Radio Group, Switch                                                    | Same names                                                | Base UI underneath; `render` for composition.                                                                                              |
| Toggle, Toggle Group                                                             | Same names                                                | Icon-only toggles need `aria-label`.                                                                                                       |
| Calendar, Date Picker                                                            | **Calendar**, **DatePicker**                              | react-day-picker underneath. DatePicker holds and reports an ISO day string.                                                               |
| Dialog, Alert Dialog, Sheet, Drawer, Popover, Tooltip, Hover Card, Dropdown Menu | Same names                                                | All Base UI. The Overlays page says which surface fits which task; Drawer is the gesture bottom sheet, Sheet the side panel.               |
| Sonner, Toast                                                                    | **Toaster** and the Toast parts                           | Base UI Toast with a native manager API. Mount once near the root.                                                                         |
| Alert                                                                            | **Alert** with **AlertAction**                            | Explicit title, description and action parts.                                                                                              |
| Tabs                                                                             | **Tabs**, `TabsList variant="line"`                       | The line variant fills its container with one border and scrolls in one row; do not add wrapping or width classes.                         |
| Accordion, Collapsible                                                           | Same names                                                | Base UI.                                                                                                                                   |
| Table                                                                            | **Table** for markup; **DataTable** for state             | DataTable is a TanStack Table 9 instance with columns declared by kind (`defineColumns`), a Toolbar, `fill` and `responsive`.              |
| Data Table (shadcn recipe)                                                       | **DataTable**                                             | It is a pattern with a hook, not a page recipe you copy.                                                                                   |
| Sidebar                                                                          | **Shell** and its areas                                   | The whole application frame: Banner, TopNav, SideNav with an icon rail, Main, Aside, Panel. Not a standalone sidebar.                      |
| Breadcrumb                                                                       | **Breadcrumb**                                            | `BreadcrumbLink` takes a router link through `render`.                                                                                     |
| Card                                                                             | **Card**                                                  | Same parts, token surfaces.                                                                                                                |
| Avatar                                                                           | **Avatar**, **AvatarGroup**, **AvatarBadge**              | Flat shadcn Base UI composition with Ledger sizes and accents.                                                                             |
| Skeleton, Spinner, Progress                                                      | Same names, plus **PageSkeleton** and **ProgressStacked** |                                                                                                                                            |
| Empty, Item, Kbd, Button Group                                                   | Same names                                                | Same part structure. DataTable draws its own Empty.                                                                                        |
| Chart                                                                            | **Chart** and its kinds                                   | Recharts underneath as in shadcn; Ledger adds the Frame, the table twin, drill-down, export and the chart tokens.                          |
| Resizable, Scroll Area, Separator, Pagination                                    | Same names                                                |                                                                                                                                            |
| Typography (`<h1 className=…>`)                                                  | **Heading**, **Text**, **Eyebrow**, **Prose**             | Type is a composite token on a primitive, never a class list.                                                                              |
| Navigation Menu, Menubar, Context Menu, Carousel, Aspect Ratio                   | Not in Ledger                                             | A need for one is flagged in writing before it is built.                                                                                   |

## Parts Ledger has that shadcn does not

These carry the product's vocabulary and have no shadcn analogue, so nothing you know applies: **Id**, **Count**, **Indicator** and **Dot**, **Fact**, **KeyValue** and **Inspector**, **Stat**, **Absent**, **Eyebrow**, **Prose**, **Person**, **Attachment**, **CodeBlock**, **Timeline**, **Stepper**, **Gates**, **Glance**, **Related**, **TaskRow**, **Composer**, **Editable**, **FilterChip**, **Toolbar**, **PickerSheet**, **RecordBrowser**, **PreviewSheet**, **PreviewNavigation**, **PageHeader**, **Section**, **Tree**, **Banner**. Read their pages; the Choosing a part page says when each one is the answer.

<!-- page: Guidance/Recipes (src/stories/docs/Recipes.mdx) -->

# Recipes

How the parts compose into the screens a product is made of. Each recipe names the parts in order and the story that renders it. These are the package's neutral shapes; an application decides which recipe each of its screens uses and records that in its own contract, not here.

## A register

A page that is one collection.

1. **PageHeader** with the name in `PageHeader.Heading` and `PageHeader.Title`. Nothing under the title.
2. **DataTable** with `fill`, so the header sticks, the rows scroll inside and pagination sits at the bottom of the window. Frameless: the toolbar sits flush above and a hairline closes the last row.
3. Its **Toolbar**: search first, saved views in `views`, filters in `filters`, Columns and Settings as children, one small primary in `actions`. The create action lives here, not in the page header.
4. Columns from `defineColumns` by kind. A date column takes the raw value; the name is a **TextLink** to the record; the id column carries the preview eye.
5. `responsive` on every product table, with the name at `priority: 0`. Lower-priority fields move into the row's More fields disclosure; nothing disappears.
6. The empty states are DataTable's own: bare (illustration, title, one line, the same create action) and filtered (Clear filters).

Story: Layout/Pages, Register.

## A record page

1. **PageHeader**: the breadcrumb in `PageHeader.Lead`, the name in `PageHeader.Title`, one primary or an Actions **DropdownMenu** in `PageHeader.Actions`. No back chevron, no sentence, no status badge, no second action row.
2. **Tabs** with `TabsList variant="line"` when the record has more than one view.
3. **Shell.Aside** beside the overview holding an **Inspector** group named Details: **KeyValue** rows for state, owner, identifiers and dates. A tab that is a register fills the work area without the rail.
4. Body content in **Section**s. A single record is never a table; a description is **Prose**; linked records are **Related**.
5. A supported inline change is an **Editable**; a larger change is a Dialog (below).
6. Missing record: an **Empty** with the search illustration, a title, a line and a route back.

Story: Layout/Pages, Record.

## A preview beside a register

1. **Shell.Panel** opened by the row's eye. The collection stays mounted, so filters, sort and selection survive.
2. The panel's outer header holds global navigation only: **PreviewNavigation** with previous, next, the announced position and a real open-in-new-tab link, then Close.
3. The body starts with an inner **PageHeader**: the record's name as its h2 title, its actions in `PageHeader.Actions` (one small primary, the rest behind an overflow **DropdownMenu**).
4. **KeyValue** properties below, then the record's sections at the panel's width; **Tabs** in one scrolling row if the preview has views.
5. **PreviewSheet** replaces the panel only when the task must hold focus, such as a version review.

Story: Layout/Pages, Queue with panel; Patterns/PreviewNavigation.

## A create or edit form

1. **Dialog** titled with the operation and the singular noun. The trigger, the title and the primary say the same words.
2. **Field** groups over the controls, in a **Stack**; the first field takes focus.
3. Validate on submit with the primary enabled. An error says what fixes it and the entered values stay.
4. **DialogFooter** outside the scrolling field region: Cancel as a subtle Button, then the primary. The footer belongs to the form through `form` on the submit button.
5. A dirty dismissal goes through an **AlertDialog**: Keep editing keeps the values, Discard closes. A pending save blocks dismissal and repeat submission.

Story: Patterns/Forms; Components/Dialog.

## Choosing records

- One record: **RecordPicker**.
- Many records from hundreds: **PickerSheet** with a search, filters, a DataTable body with selection and a footer that says how many and what happens to them. It may collect one shared rationale.
- Records the reader must compare first: **RecordBrowser**. Its preview belongs to the selection task and never becomes a second record workflow.

## States

- Loading a page: **PageSkeleton**. Loading a region with a known shape: **Skeleton**. An action in flight: **Spinner** or Button `loading`.
- Nothing here: **Empty** (`size="compact"` in a small region). A missing scalar: **Absent**.
- Failure: an **Alert** with a retry, with the stale content kept usable underneath. A failure is never a blank table.
- Empty data and an empty filter result are different states.

## A toolbar without a DataTable

**Toolbar** over a plain **Table** or a list: the same slots, `filters` collapse into More when space runs out, search takes its own row on a phone. Story: Patterns/Toolbar, Constrained.

## Confirming a decision

**AlertDialog** with a title that names the decision, one line of consequence, Cancel and the verb. It may open over the Dialog or Sheet that owns the decision.

<!-- page: Guidance/Which token (src/stories/docs/WhichToken.mdx) -->

# Which token

The Token grammar page explains the naming; the token sheets list every value. This page is the short answer to "which one": the tokens a screen reaches for most, by job, with the utility class beside each. Primitive props (`<Stack space="space.200">`, `<Box padding="space.150" background="elevation.surface.sunken">`) take the token name; classes take the utility.

## Text

| Job                                         | Token                                                                 | Utility                             |
| ------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------- |
| Body text                                   | `color.text`                                                          | `text-default`                      |
| Secondary: meta lines, labels, descriptions | `color.text.subtle`                                                   | `text-subtle`                       |
| Tertiary: placeholders, timestamps, Absent  | `color.text.subtlest`                                                 | `text-subtlest`                     |
| Disabled                                    | `color.text.disabled`                                                 | `text-disabled`                     |
| On a bold background                        | `color.text.inverse`                                                  | `text-inverse`                      |
| Selected item                               | `color.text.selected`                                                 | `text-selected`                     |
| A link, the brand                           | `color.text.brand`                                                    | `text-brand`                        |
| Danger, warning, success, information       | `color.text.danger` and the rest; `.bolder` for text on a subtle tone | `text-danger`, `text-danger-bolder` |
| A categorical accent (charts, avatars)      | `color.text.accent.blue` … `purple`                                   | `text-accent-blue`                  |

Icons have their own ramp, `color.icon.*`, at the same roles.

## Surfaces

| Job                                       | Token                                                   | Utility                             |
| ----------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------- |
| The page                                  | `elevation.surface`                                     | `bg-surface`                        |
| A recessed region: a sunken table, a well | `elevation.surface.sunken`                              | `bg-surface-sunken`                 |
| A card                                    | `elevation.surface.raised`, `elevation.shadow.raised`   | `bg-surface-raised shadow-raised`   |
| A menu, popover, dialog                   | `elevation.surface.overlay`, `elevation.shadow.overlay` | `bg-surface-overlay shadow-overlay` |
| A scroll edge                             | `elevation.shadow.overflow`                             | `shadow-overflow`                   |

Each surface has `.hovered` and `.pressed` siblings; use those, never opacity on the base.

## Backgrounds by meaning

| Job                                   | Token family                           | Utilities                                                                                   |
| ------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| A neutral control or chip             | `color.background.neutral`             | `bg-neutral`, `-hovered`, `-pressed`, `-subtle`, `-bold`                                    |
| The primary action                    | `color.background.brand.bold`          | `bg-brand-bold`, `-hovered`, `-pressed`                                                     |
| A tinted brand region                 | `color.background.brand.subtlest`      | `bg-brand-subtlest`                                                                         |
| A selected row or item                | `color.background.selected`            | `bg-selected`, `-hovered`, `-bold`                                                          |
| An input                              | `color.background.input`               | `bg-input`, `-hovered`, `-pressed`                                                          |
| Danger, warning, success, information | `color.background.danger` and the rest | `bg-danger` (the tone), `-subtler`, `-subtle`, `-bold`, each with `-hovered` and `-pressed` |
| Something on a dark surface           | `color.background.inverse.subtle`      | `bg-inverse-subtle`                                                                         |
| A blanket under a modal               | `color.blanket`                        |                                                                                             |
| A skeleton                            | `color.skeleton`                       |                                                                                             |

Text on a subtle tone is the `.bolder` text token of the same tone; text on a bold tone is `color.text.inverse`.

## Borders

| Job                              | Token                                                | Utility                                 |
| -------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------- |
| Every divider and default border | `color.border`                                       | `border-default`                        |
| A stronger border                | `color.border.bold`                                  | `border-bold`                           |
| An input                         | `color.border.input`                                 | `border-input`                          |
| Focus ring                       | `color.border.focused`, 2px                          | `border-focused`                        |
| Selected                         | `color.border.selected`, 2px                         | `border-selected`                       |
| Disabled                         | `color.border.disabled`                              | `border-disabled`                       |
| A tone                           | `color.border.danger`, `.subtle` for a tinted region | `border-danger`, `border-danger-subtle` |

Widths: `border.width` 1px for everything, `border.width.selected` and `border.width.focused` 2px.

## Space

| Token        | Value | For                                                    |
| ------------ | ----- | ------------------------------------------------------ |
| `space.025`  | 2px   | A hairline.                                            |
| `space.050`  | 4px   | Tight: icon to text, dot to text.                      |
| `space.075`  | 6px   | Compact: the gap inside a control cluster.             |
| `space.100`  | 8px   | Standard small: control clusters, chip rows.           |
| `space.150`  | 12px  | Standard medium: cell padding, a card header's inset.  |
| `space.200`  | 16px  | Standard large: card padding, form grids, most Stacks. |
| `space.250`  | 20px  | Comfortable.                                           |
| `space.300`  | 24px  | Relaxed: between a header and its actions.             |
| `space.400`  | 32px  | Spacious: page gutters.                                |
| `space.600`  | 48px  | Between sections.                                      |
| `space.800`  | 64px  | Between page sections.                                 |
| `space.1000` | 80px  | A hero.                                                |

Utilities take the same key on any spacing or sizing property: `p-200`, `gap-100`, `w-400`. Margins exist only as `space.negative.*` through **Bleed**; product code never writes a margin.

## Type

| Token                  | Size  | For                                                                               |
| ---------------------- | ----- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `font.body`            | 13/18 | Controls, cells, tabs, inputs, menu items. The UI size.                           |
| `font.body.large`      | 15/22 | Reading text, dialog body.                                                        |
| `font.body.small`      | 12/16 | Table headers, field labels, badges, KeyValue; labels add `font.weight.medium`.   |
| `font.body.xsmall`     | 11/14 | Eyebrow, counts, metadata.                                                        |
| `font.heading.medium`  | 22/28 | Page and record titles. The only semibold.                                        |
| `font.heading.small`   | 20/26 | Section headings.                                                                 |
| `font.heading.xsmall`  | 15/22 | Dialog and card titles.                                                           |
| `font.heading.xxsmall` | 11/14 | Eyebrows, group headings, menu section labels (the component adds the uppercase). |
| `font.heading.large`   | 28/34 | A stat value, a dashboard number. Not a page title.                               |
| `font.code`            | 12/18 | Code blocks only.                                                                 |

Prose never grows past `dimension.layout.measure`, 720px (`max-w-layout-measure`).

## Sizes

| Token                      | Value | For                                                                   |
| -------------------------- | ----- | --------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `dimension.control.xsmall` | 24px  | Button xs.                                                            |
| `dimension.control.small`  | 28px  | Button sm, chips, menu items, sidebar items, everything in a Toolbar. |
| `dimension.control.medium` | 32px  | The default: Button md, inputs, selects, combobox triggers.           |
| `dimension.control.large`  | 36px  | Hero forms only.                                                      |
| `dimension.row`            | 40px  | A table row; `.compact` 36px; `.header` 32px; `.menu` 28px.           |
| `dimension.icon.small`     | 14px  | An icon inside a small or medium control.                             |
| `dimension.icon.medium`    | 16px  | A standalone icon, an icon button's glyph.                            |
| `dimension.layout.rail`    | 272px | The rail beside a record: Inspector, Aside.                           |
| `dimension.layout.panel`   | 320px | The preview panel before the reader resizes it.                       |
| `dimension.layout.sidenav` | 228px | The side nav, expanded.                                               |
| `dimension.layout.topnav`  | 48px  | The top nav, and the banner above it.                                 |

## Radius

| Token            | Value | For                                 |
| ---------------- | ----- | ----------------------------------- |
| `radius.xsmall`  | 2px   | Checkbox, tiny chips.               |
| `radius.small`   | 3px   | Badges, count chips, Kbd, skeleton. |
| `radius.medium`  | 5px   | Buttons, inputs, chips, menu items. |
| `radius.large`   | 7px   | Cards, popovers.                    |
| `radius.xlarge`  | 9px   | Dialogs, sheets.                    |
| `radius.xxlarge` | 12px  | Large surfaces, spotlight cards.    |
| `radius.full`    | pill  | Dots, avatars, pills, meters.       |

## Motion

| Token                                       | Value | For                                                                        |
| ------------------------------------------- | ----- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `motion.duration.micro`                     | 70ms  | A toggle's thumb, a checkbox's tick, a chevron turning.                    |
| `motion.duration.fast`                      | 110ms | Hover and press colour, a tooltip's fade, a menu leaving.                  |
| `motion.duration.medium`                    | 150ms | A menu arriving, a section expanding, a dialog leaving.                    |
| `motion.duration.moderate`                  | 240ms | A dialog or sheet arriving, the panel sliding in, a toast, content rising. |
| `motion.duration.slow`                      | 400ms | Chart marks arriving, a drill-down redrawing.                              |
| `motion.duration.slower`                    | 700ms | The blanket dimming the page.                                              |
| `motion.easing.standard`, `.enter`, `.exit` |       | `ease-standard`, `ease-enter`, `ease-exit`. Honour reduced motion.         |

## What has no token on purpose

Structural utilities carry no design value and are allowed as written: `flex`, `grid`, `relative`, `absolute`, `sticky`, `truncate`, `whitespace-nowrap`, `sr-only`, `overflow-auto`, `pointer-events-none` and their kin. Everything with a colour, a length, a weight or a duration goes through a token. A value you cannot find here or on the sheets is a token to propose, not a number to type.

<!-- page: Guidance/Token grammar (src/stories/docs/Grammar.mdx) -->

# Token grammar

Tokens are named on one grammar: **property . role . emphasis . state**.

| Segment  | Examples                                                                                                             | What it says                                                                                                           |
| -------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| property | `color.background`, `color.text`, `color.icon`, `color.border`, `elevation.surface`, `space`, `font`, `shape.radius` | What is being painted. Text, icon, border and background are separate properties because they need different contrast. |
| role     | `brand`, `neutral`, `selected`, `success`, `warning`, `danger`, `information`, `disabled`, `input`, `inverse`        | Why. A role names the meaning, not the colour.                                                                         |
| emphasis | `subtlest`, `subtler`, `subtle`, (default), `bold`, `bolder`, `boldest`                                              | How loud. Default sits in the middle; bold is a solid fill with inverse text.                                          |
| state    | `hovered`, `pressed`, `selected`, `focused`                                                                          | Interaction. A state is always its own token, never alpha on the default.                                              |

Every token has one CSS variable, `--ds-<name with dashes>`, and most have one Tailwind utility.

| Token                                 | CSS                                        | Utility                                   |
| ------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------- |
| `color.background.brand.bold.hovered` | `--ds-color-background-brand-bold-hovered` | `bg-brand-bold-hovered`                   |
| `color.text.subtle`                   | `--ds-color-text-subtle`                   | `text-subtle`                             |
| `color.icon.danger`                   | `--ds-color-icon-danger`                   | `icon-danger`                             |
| `color.border.focused`                | `--ds-color-border-focused`                | `border-focused`                          |
| `elevation.surface.raised`            | `--ds-elevation-surface-raised`            | `bg-surface-raised`                       |
| `elevation.shadow.overlay`            | `--ds-elevation-shadow-overlay`            | `shadow-overlay`                          |
| `space.200`                           | `--ds-space-200`                           | `p-200`, `gap-200`, `h-200` …             |
| `shape.radius.medium`                 | `--ds-shape-radius-medium`                 | `rounded-medium`                          |
| `font.body.small`                     | `--ds-font-body-small`                     | `font-body-small`                         |
| `dimension.control.medium`            | `--ds-dimension-control-medium`            | `h-control-medium`, `size-control-medium` |
| `motion.duration.fast`                | `--ds-motion-duration-fast`                | `duration-fast`                           |

## Tiers

1. **Palette.** Six ramps (neutral, dark neutral, blue, green, orange, red) with numbered step names, plus alpha steps for translucent fills. Never used directly.
2. **Semantic.** Colour and elevation tokens that reference the ramps. Each has a light value and a dark value. This is the only tier a component reads for colour.
3. **Typography, space, shape, dimension, motion.** Mode independent.
4. **Component.** Where a component needs a value no semantic token gives it, the value is added to the tokens, not written in the component.

## Where a value comes from

- **Surface.** `elevation.surface` is the page; `raised` is a card; `overlay` is a menu or dialog; `sunken` is a well. Box sets `utility.elevation.surface.current` when it paints a surface, so children can read the surface they sit on.
- **Text.** `default` for content, `subtle` for secondary, `subtlest` for hints and captions, `disabled` for off. Status text (`success`, `warning`, `danger`, `information`) sits on the matching status background.
- **Border.** `default` for hairlines, `bold` for emphasis, `input` for fields, `focused` and `selected` for those states.
- **Type.** Composite tokens: `body` (13/18) for interface text, `body.small` (12/16) for captions, `body.xsmall` (11/14) for micro labels, `body.large` (15/22) for reading; three heading sizes; `code`.
- **Space.** 0, 2, 4, 6, 8, 12, 16, 20, 24, 32, 40, 48, 64, 80. Names are the value in quarter-rems: `space.100` is 8px.
- **Shape.** `xsmall` 2, `small` 3, `medium` 5, `large` 7, `xlarge` 9, `xxlarge` 12, `full`.
- **Metrics.** Controls are 24, 28, 32, 36 tall; rows 36 with compact, header and menu variants; icons 14 and 16.

<!-- page: Guidance/Lint rules (src/stories/docs/Lint.mdx) -->

# Lint rules

The package exports an ESLint plugin whose allowlist is generated by the token build, so the rules and the tokens cannot drift. Two presets: `package` (what this package lints itself with) and `recommended` (for a consumer).

| Rule                     | Reports                                                                                                              | Instead                                                                                                            |
| ------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `no-arbitrary-value`     | `text-[13px]`, `w-[240px]`, `bg-[#eee]`                                                                              | A token utility or a primitive prop.                                                                               |
| `no-alpha-token`         | `bg-brand-bold/80`, `text-default/60`                                                                                | The hovered, pressed, subtle or disabled token.                                                                    |
| `no-dark-variant`        | `dark:bg-neutral`                                                                                                    | Nothing. Every colour token flips by itself; a `dark:` class means a token is missing.                             |
| `no-margin`              | `mt-200`, `-mx-100`                                                                                                  | Stack or Inline space, or Bleed. `m-auto` is allowed.                                                              |
| `no-static-design-value` | `rounded`, `opacity-50`, `duration-200`, `border-2`, `ring-2`, `bg-white`, `text-transparent`                        | `rounded-small…full`, `opacity-disabled`, `duration-fast`, `border-w-selected`, `outline-focused`, a colour token. |
| `no-non-token-class`     | Any class that is not a token utility or a documented structural utility (`flex`, `truncate`, `sticky`, `sr-only` …) | A token utility.                                                                                                   |
| `no-deprecated-token`    | A deprecated token's utility                                                                                         | Its replacement, applied by `--fix`.                                                                               |
| `use-primitives`         | A `div` or `span` carrying `flex`, `grid`, padding or gap classes                                                    | Box, Stack, Inline, Flex or Grid. Error in the package, warning in `recommended`.                                  |
| `prefer-text-link`       | A `Link` or `a` carrying `text-brand` or `hover:underline`; a `Button variant="link" asChild`                        | TextLink around the link element.                                                                                  |
| `no-colgroup`            | `<colgroup>`                                                                                                         | `width` on each Table.Header.                                                                                      |
| `no-deprecated-name`     | A part's old name (`Shell.Sidebar`, `Shell.NavItem`)                                                                 | Its replacement; `--fix` does the one-to-one renames.                                                              |
| `cell-plain`             | A Table.Cell carrying a neutral colour, weight or type token                                                         | Nothing; only a status colour may differ.                                                                          |
| `id-not-blue`            | An Id with `text-brand` outside a link or a button                                                                   | Wrap it in a link, or drop the class.                                                                              |
| `no-kit-shadow`          | A local component named like a kit part (`Badge`, `Table`, `Stack`)                                                  | Import the kit part.                                                                                               |
| `button-icon-slot`       | An element with `size-icon-*` inside a Button or an IconButton                                                       | `iconBefore`, `iconAfter` or `icon`, passed bare; the button sizes it.                                             |

Inside the package a portability rule also blocks any import from a consumer (`@/…`), from the prototype, or from a router.

## What counts as structural

Display, position, alignment, overflow, text flow and interaction utilities are allowed as written, because they carry no design value: `flex`, `grid`, `relative`, `absolute`, `sticky`, `truncate`, `whitespace-nowrap`, `select-none`, `pointer-events-none`, `overflow-auto`, `overscroll-none`, `sr-only`, `cursor-pointer`, `transition-colors`, `animate-spin` and their kin. Sizes with a token key are allowed on every sizing property: `w-200`, `min-h-800`, `size-150`.

## Running it

```sh
# inside the package
npm run lint

# in a consumer, after adopting the preset
npx eslint src
```

## Product layout rules

`product-responsive-table` requires explicit `responsive` on DataTable. `product-line-tabs` requires `variant="line"` on TabsList and rejects wrapping, intrinsic-width and local overflow overrides. These are opt-in application conventions, not generic recommended rules: filled tabs and horizontally scrolling comparison tables remain supported by the kit. The application enables both rules in its product-file configuration. Required props must follow unknown spreads so the spread cannot override them.

<!-- page: Guidance/Writing stories (src/stories/docs/Stories.mdx) -->

# Writing stories

The Storybook is the package's test suite and its documentation at once: every story renders in both colour modes with its play function and an axe pass (`npm run test:a11y`), every exported part must appear in one (`npm run ds:check`), and the family's MDX page draws its examples from the same file. The MCP tool `get-storybook-story-instructions` is the generic Storybook 9 guidance; this page is what this package adds to it.

## Shape of a stories file

```tsx

const meta = {
  title: "Components/Badge",
  component: Badge,
  parameters: { layout: "padded" },
  args: { children: "Featured", variant: "default" },
} satisfies Meta<typeof Badge>;
export default meta;
type Story = StoryObj<typeof meta>;

/** The six reference variants beside the icon positions. */
export const Matrix: Story = { render: () => <Matrix rows={…} cols={…} render={…} /> };
```

- Imports come from `@storybook/react-vite` and `storybook/test`, never the `@storybook/test` or `@storybook/react` names.
- Parts are imported by relative path from `../../components`, `../../primitives`, `../../patterns`, `../../layout`. The package never imports its own root.
- `title` is `<Category>/<Family>`: Primitives, Components, Layout, Patterns, Tokens, Guidance. One family, one file, one `title`.
- The JSDoc comment above a story is its description on the docs page. Write it as the sentence the reader needs, not the story's name again.

## What to cover

- Every named part of the family, rendered. `ds:check` fails on an export with no story.
- Representative states, not every permutation: default, hover and pressed through the tokens, disabled, invalid, loading, empty, error, the sizes that change behaviour. The `_lib/matrix` **Matrix** and **Specimens** helpers lay a family's variants out for comparison; **Pair** in `_lib/pair` puts a Do beside a Don't with one line each on why; every family's page carries one.
- One playground covers the controls. Keep distinct regression cases as their own stories rather than folding them into the playground.
- A `play` function on every interactive story: drive it with `userEvent`, assert the visible outcome with role and label queries on `canvas`, and assert `fn` callbacks were called. Wait for a menu to mount before asserting `aria-expanded`.
- Render once. Josef switches the mode in the toolbar; a story never renders light and dark side by side.

## What fails a story

- A console error. `test/storybook.setup.ts` fails any story that emits one.
- An axe violation in either mode. Fix semantic and structural violations directly; a contrast or spacing violation is a design decision, so raise it instead.
- A stale `api/public-api.json`: `npm run ds:api:check` when declarations changed, `ds:api:update` when they changed on purpose.
- Drift in `eslint-plugin/components.json` or `llms.txt`; the package build regenerates both.

## The MDX page

One `<Family>.mdx` beside the stories, attached with `<Meta of={Stories} />`, so its title is the stories file's. It opens with what the part is for in a sentence or two, then `<Canvas of={Stories.X} />` for the examples worth reading, `<ArgTypes of={Part} />` for each named part, and the usage and accessibility guidance that helps. No required heading set and no "Not applicable" filler. A larger migration gets one focused guide the page links to.

`api/axis-policy.json` holds optional notes on package-specific meanings of `variant`, `size`, `tone` and the other shared axes; a new part or prop does not need an entry.

## What does not belong here

An application composition. A screen from the product is verified in the running app, never mounted in a package story; the package documents neutral contracts and the application's pattern contract decides how they are used there.

## After changing a story

Call `stories-changed`, then `stories-preview` for the stories that matter, then `test-run` for the family. Report the URLs. Add a `CHANGELOG.md` entry that names the story showing the change.

<!-- page: Guidance/Testing and review (src/stories/docs/TestingAndReview.mdx) -->

# Testing and review

The system should help a person understand the situation, choose an action, complete it, and recover if it fails. A familiar visual style alone does not establish that contract. Test the whole task with realistic content, keyboard input and the conditions people actually encounter.

## Before adding an API

Start with the user's task and the semantic HTML element. Reuse a native control when its behavior answers the task. A new prop needs a distinct consumer need and a documented default, valid combinations, ownership of state, and behavior when absent. Avoid booleans that encode several mutually exclusive modes. Prefer a union when only one mode can apply. Preserve native names for native behavior.

| Question                       | Required evidence                                                                                          |
| ------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Who owns the state?            | Controlled and uncontrolled behavior, defaults, reset, and async external updates.                         |
| What reaches the DOM?          | The target for `id`, `name`, `form`, `aria-*`, `data-*`, handlers, and the ref.                            |
| What can fail?                 | Pending, rejected save, retry, cancellation, and stale completion examples.                                |
| What can be composed?          | Compound slots and valid nesting; no interactive element inside another interactive element.               |
| What does a dependency expose? | Explicit adapter types for toast, table and chart APIs; all other implementation internals remain private. |

## State and content

Every collection needs loading, empty, filtered empty, error, ready, and refreshed states where applicable. A filtered empty state keeps filters visible and offers Clear filters. A save failure keeps the draft. Announce success only after the command succeeds; if persistence is local to this browser, say so. Permissions are business rules enforced by commands as well as reflected by controls.

Use sentence case, a specific verb for actions, and an error that says what the person can do next. Name the affected record when ambiguity is possible. Essential guidance belongs beside the control. Disabled actions need a visible reason; an enabled control must navigate or perform its stated action. Do not use a notification to conceal an unimplemented operation.

## Keyboard, focus and targets

Check Tab and Shift+Tab, Enter and Space, Escape, arrow keys, Home/End and typeahead where the widget requires them. Trees maintain one tab stop and expose level, expansion and selection. Closing a modal returns focus to its opener or an explicitly supplied replacement. Failed form submission focuses the first invalid control and exposes all errors. A sticky header or action bar must not fully obscure focused content.

The web minimum target requirement is **24 by 24 CSS pixels**, subject to the WCAG 2.2 spacing, equivalent, inline, user-agent and essential exceptions. Document any exception on the actual control. Native platform point guidance is not a CSS pixel requirement. Prefer larger targets for frequent touch actions. Measure both the target and the distance to neighboring targets; a small icon inside a sufficiently large button is fine.

Inspect 320 CSS pixel width, 200% text enlargement and 400% browser zoom. A dense data table may scroll in its own region; surrounding search, headings, dialogs and actions must reflow. Check focus after scrolling, opening menus, validating a long form, collapsing navigation, and removing the selected item. Reduced-motion preference should remove nonessential movement while keeping pending state understandable through text and semantics.

## Automated checks and their limits

`node scripts/ds-check.mjs` resolves public exports through the TypeScript compiler, counts executable story references, checks story coverage and documentation, and rejects a growing exception baseline. `node scripts/ds-public-api.mjs` prints the full public value/type inventory. A reference proves use, not correctness; interaction assertions establish behavior.

The retired Shapes catalog no longer requires ActionBar or WorkPane stories. Their exports remain in the API baseline, which checks declarations rather than rendering or accessibility. Block and Inspector continue to render in existing integration stories. New component families still require stories and documentation.

Keep one family page with useful examples, generated props and relevant usage/accessibility guidance. There is no required heading set. Omit sections that add no information, and review the prose against the current examples and implementation. Keep migration guidance in one place and link to it from the changelog.

`npm run test:a11y -w packages/design-system` runs every story in light and dark Chromium using Storybook’s built-in `test` tag. Each story gets a render check; its `play` function adds interaction assertions. Axe and unexpected-console checks run alongside them. Dark mode also checks reduced motion.

Keep examples and their interaction tests in the same component’s `.stories.tsx` file. Add assertions to an existing example before introducing another render fixture. Use `fn()` from `storybook/test` for callbacks instead of rendering test counters or “check refs” buttons. Add a distinct story only for a distinct useful state or workflow. The Interactions panel shows the test steps; test-only controls do not belong in the component showcase.

Storybook applies `dev` and `test` automatically. No custom tag is needed to opt in. Use `!test` only for a documented case that cannot run automatically; intentional accessibility anti-examples can scope an exception to the demonstrated axe rule, with an explanation beside the story. The other accessibility checks and the render test still run. Do not recreate a separate hidden story catalog.

See [Storybook interaction tests](https://storybook.js.org/docs/writing-tests/interaction-testing) and [tags](https://storybook.js.org/docs/writing-stories/tags). The package unit suite covers nonvisual logic and token generation. The packed consumer suite verifies installation, declarations, SSR and generated CSS.

Axe does not certify keyboard quality, reading order, useful labels, focus visibility, zoom or screen-reader announcements. Review representative workflows with a screen reader and Firefox/WebKit before release. Contrast results cover the declared pairs, including alpha compositing and interactive states; they do not prove every possible composition. Resting input borders now meet 3:1 against their declared adjacent surfaces; text and non-text checks keep their separate thresholds.

## Reference workflows for review

| Workflow                     | Story or product surface           | Review focus                                                             |
| ---------------------------- | ---------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Validate and repair a form   | Patterns/Forms stories             | All errors, first focus, preserved values, custom control wiring.        |
| Pick and submit a date       | Components/DatePicker stories      | Closed picker FormData, external form, reset, disabled omission.         |
| Save inline with failure     | Patterns/Editable stories          | One pending operation, rollback ownership, external updates.             |
| Complete a nested modal task | Components/Dialog stories          | Escape, successful close, return to correct opener.                      |
| Navigate a hierarchy         | Components/Tree stories            | One tab stop, hierarchy, typeahead, selected item removal.               |
| Filter records and recover   | Risks, controls and findings pages | Empty results, clear filters, visible labels, durable supported actions. |
