| Read a chart                 | Patterns/Chart stories             | Table equivalent, deterministic formatting and color mode.               |

## Ownership and lifecycle

The repository maintainers own the package contract and review changes to tokens, accessibility behavior and adapters. A contribution names a responsible reviewer and intended consumer. Mark experimental additions and known limitations; promote after the documented checks and consumer review. Deprecations identify the replacement and migration in the changelog. User testing and assistive-technology review remain release work even when all automated checks pass.

<!-- page: Tokens/Color (src/stories/tokens/Color.mdx) -->

# Colour and elevation

Semantic colour is tier 1. Every token references a palette step and carries a light value and a dark value, so a component never knows which mode it is in. Utilities are generated per property: a text token is only reachable as `text-*`, a background as `bg-*`, an icon as `icon-*`, a border as `border-*`. A `default` segment drops out of the name: `color.text.default` in the source is `color.text` on the sheet and `text-default` in a class.

The ramps are on the Palette sheet (Tokens/Palette). No ramp step has a utility. A component reads a semantic token or nothing.

## One accent

The canvas is white: `elevation.surface` is `color.neutral.0` in light. Blue is the only accent. Brand, selected, information and focus all draw on the blue ramp, so blue is spent on action, selection, focus and links and on nothing else.

| Job                                                          | Token                                            | Utility                              |
| ------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------ |
| The primary button                                           | `color.background.brand.bold`                    | `bg-brand-bold`                      |
| An active row, a checked menu item, an open dropdown trigger | `color.background.selected`                      | `bg-selected`                        |
| A selected tab's text and underline                          | `color.text.selected`, `color.border.selected`   | `text-selected`, `border-selected`   |
| The focus ring                                               | `color.border.focused` at `border.width.focused` | `border-focused`, `border-w-focused` |
| A link                                                       | `color.text.brand`                               | `text-brand`, or TextLink            |

Ids and counts stay neutral, and so does an avatar by default. An Id is blue only inside a link or a button (`ledger/id-not-blue`). Colour that carries no meaning is the accent family: `color.background.accent.*` in six hues, `subtler` under `color.text.accent.*` and `bolder` under `color.text.inverse`, for an avatar's tint, fill or gradient and, later, a tag. Teal and purple reach only the accent family and `color.chart.*`; a status is never drawn in them.

## Text and icons

| Job                                                        | Text                  | Icon                  |
| ---------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------- | --------------------- |
| Content, sentence-case headings, buttons                   | `color.text`          | `color.icon`          |
| Secondary: navigation, field labels, subtle links          | `color.text.subtle`   | `color.icon.subtle`   |
| Tertiary: metadata, breadcrumbs, placeholders, helper text | `color.text.subtlest` | `color.icon.subtlest` |
| Off                                                        | `color.text.disabled` | `color.icon.disabled` |
| On a bold fill                                             | `color.text.inverse`  | `color.icon.inverse`  |

An icon mirrors its text, one step bolder where a thin glyph needs it. Text and Heading take these as `color="color.text.subtle"`; a class says `text-subtle`.

## Status

A tone is one decision. The subtle fill takes the tone's text. The bold fill takes inverse text; warning's bold fill is light, so it takes `color.text.warning.inverse`. A dot takes the tone's icon colour.

| Tone          | Subtle fill                    | Text                     | Bold fill                           | Icon                     |
| ------------- | ------------------------------ | ------------------------ | ----------------------------------- | ------------------------ |
| `neutral`     | `color.background.neutral`     | `color.text.subtle`      | `color.background.neutral.bold`     | `color.icon.subtlest`    |
| `information` | `color.background.information` | `color.text.information` | `color.background.information.bold` | `color.icon.information` |
| `success`     | `color.background.success`     | `color.text.success`     | `color.background.success.bold`     | `color.icon.success`     |
| `warning`     | `color.background.warning`     | `color.text.warning`     | `color.background.warning.bold`     | `color.icon.warning`     |
| `danger`      | `color.background.danger`      | `color.text.danger`      | `color.background.danger.bold`      | `color.icon.danger`      |

Reach these through the `tone` prop on Badge, Dot, Indicator, Alert, Progress and Stat, never by hand. The `subtler` and `subtle` emphases are for lozenges and non-interactive chips. `hovered` and `pressed` are their own tokens, never alpha on the default (`ledger/no-alpha-token`). What each tone means in the product is in `docs/guides/status-vocabulary.md`.

## Minted, not yet drawn

The matrix is complete on purpose: every fill has `hovered` and `pressed`, every tone has `subtler`, `subtle`, the default and `bold`, the inverse subtle fill exists for a control on a bold fill, and the bolder text colours exist for a word on a tone's label. About forty of them have no part that draws them yet. That is accepted (2026-09-05): a token is minted when its place in the grammar is clear and drawn when the part arrives, so a part never invents a colour. The families still open, and the part each waits for:

| Family                                                                                                       | Waits for                                                                                                                                              |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `color.background.{danger,warning,success,information}.{hovered,pressed}` and `.subtler.{hovered,pressed}`   | A status fill that is pressed: a toned chip that filters, a status pill that opens its record.                                                         |
| `color.background.{warning,success,information}.bold.{hovered,pressed}`, `neutral.bold.{hovered,pressed}`    | A bold button in a tone other than brand and danger.                                                                                                   |
| `color.background.brand.boldest` and states, `brand.subtlest.{hovered,pressed}`, `selected.bold` and states  | A pressed primary, a hovered brand tint, a bold selected control.                                                                                      |
| `color.background.danger.subtler`, `warning.subtler`, the three `.subtle`                                    | A lozenge emphasis between the subtle fill and the bold one.                                                                                           |
| `color.background.inverse.subtle`                                                                            | The resting fill of a control on a bold surface; its `hovered` and `pressed` are drawn by the Banner's action.                                         |
| `color.text.{danger,warning,success,information}.bolder`, `color.border.warning`, `color.border.information` | A word on a tone's label; a 3:1 status border in those tones.                                                                                          |
| `color.icon.warning.inverse`, `color.border.inverse`                                                         | An icon and a border on a bold warning fill; the Box paints its text inverse and icons follow it, so the icon token is reached through `currentColor`. |
| `elevation.surface.pressed`, `elevation.surface.overlay.{hovered,pressed}`, `elevation.shadow.overflow`      | A pressed page surface, a hovered overlay, a scroll edge.                                                                                              |

Drawn this pass: `color.background.input.pressed`, every field on focus; `color.background.inverse.subtle.hovered` and `.pressed`, the Banner's action under the pointer. The chart tokens are reached at runtime through `tone`, which a name scan cannot see; Patterns/Chart.

## Borders

Every border is a 1px hairline: `border.width` is 1px and `color.border` is the default colour. Prefer a rule to a box.

| Job                             | Token                   | Utility                             |
| ------------------------------- | ----------------------- | ----------------------------------- |
| Hairlines, dividers, flat cards | `color.border`          | `border-default`                    |
| Emphasis that must pass 3:1     | `color.border.bold`     | `border-bold`                       |
| Text fields, checkboxes, radios | `color.border.input`    | `border-input`                      |
| Focus ring, 2px                 | `color.border.focused`  | `border-focused border-w-focused`   |
| Selected tab or item, 2px       | `color.border.selected` | `border-selected border-w-selected` |
| Off                             | `color.border.disabled` | `border-disabled`                   |

Input boundaries meet at least 3:1 against the supported page, sunken, raised, overlay and input surfaces, including hovered and pressed input fills. This supersedes the earlier 1.5:1 resting-border decision. Decorative rules and disabled controls use separate tokens; a decorative border must not be the only visible boundary of an interactive control.

The automated contrast contract covers default, hovered and pressed text/fill pairs, selected rows, status fills, focus and input borders, and translucent fills on their actual parent surfaces in both modes. Alpha blends are composed in encoded sRGB before calculating WCAG luminance. These token checks complement rendered interaction and manual accessibility checks; they do not establish conformance for arbitrary custom combinations.

A status border comes in `default` (3:1) and `subtle` (decorative): `color.border.danger`, `color.border.danger.subtle`, and the same for warning, success and information.

## Blanket and skeleton

`color.blanket` (`bg-blanket`) is the scrim under a dialog, a drawer and the open side nav on a small screen. `color.skeleton` (`bg-skeleton`) is the loading fill; `color.skeleton.subtle` is its shimmer.

## Chart

A series on a chart is a `color.chart.*` token: a status tone when the series is a status, `brand` for the one the reader is asked to look at, `neutral` for context, or the categorical set, six hues in a fixed order validated for colour vision, then Other. Two scales exist for a heatmap: `sequential`, one hue from near zero to the most, and `diverging`, red against blue around grey. Every step is the same in both modes, and every series tone has a `hovered` step (one darker in light, one lighter in dark) for the mark under the pointer. The parts read these through `tone` on a series; `fill-chart-*`, `stroke-chart-*` and `bg-chart-*` let a bespoke SVG take the same paint. How each is used is on Patterns/Chart.

_Example: story `Stories.Chart`._

## Sheets

_Example: story `Stories.Background`._

_Example: story `Stories.Text`._

_Example: story `Stories.Icon`._

_Example: story `Stories.Border`._

## Elevation

Hairline plus soft lift, never heavy. A surface pairs with a shadow; nothing else casts one.

| Sits                                    | Surface                     | Utility              | Shadow                                          |
| --------------------------------------- | --------------------------- | -------------------- | ----------------------------------------------- |
| The page                                | `elevation.surface`         | `bg-surface`         | none                                            |
| A well: the side nav, a grouped list    | `elevation.surface.sunken`  | `bg-surface-sunken`  | none                                            |
| A card                                  | `elevation.surface.raised`  | `bg-surface-raised`  | `elevation.shadow.raised` (`shadow-raised`)     |
| A menu, popover or dialog               | `elevation.surface.overlay` | `bg-surface-overlay` | `elevation.shadow.overlay` (`shadow-overlay`)   |
| Content scrolling under a sticky header |                             |                      | `elevation.shadow.overflow` (`shadow-overflow`) |

Each surface has `hovered` and `pressed` states. In dark, surfaces climb in lightness instead of casting more shadow. These three shadows are the only ones; `ledger/no-kit-shadow` reports any other.

The pairing is a rule: `surface.raised` always with `shadow.raised`, `surface.overlay` always with `shadow.overlay`, and never the other way round; `surface.sunken` casts nothing and never sits on a raised surface; the page casts nothing. A card inside a card is not a deeper elevation, it is a decision to make with a rule or a well instead. `shadow.overflow` is the one shadow without a surface: the edge of content scrolling under a sticky header, which no part draws yet.

`utility.elevation.surface.current` (`bg-surface-current`) is the surface an element sits on. Box sets it when it paints a surface; a sticky header or a masking fade reads it so it matches its parent.

`opacity.disabled` (0.4) is for a disabled element when no disabled token exists. `opacity.loading` (0.2) is for content that is loading. Motion is on its own page (Tokens/Motion).

_Example: story `Stories.Elevation`._

<!-- page: Tokens/Icons (src/stories/tokens/Icons.mdx) -->

# Icons

The icons are Lucide's, at two sizes on the dimension tokens, drawn at Lucide's stroke, coloured like the text beside them, and named when they stand alone. On names: an icon alone needs one, an icon beside a word is decoration.

## Sizes

| Token | Value | Utility | Where |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `dimension.icon.small` | 14px | `size-icon-small` | Inside a small or medium control; beside body, small or xsmall text; a chevron, a check, a Dot's glyph, a chip's cross, a validation mark. |
| `dimension.icon.medium` | 16px | `size-icon-medium` | Standing alone: an IconButton's glyph, a Banner's mark, an Empty's mark, a toast's mark, an icon beside a heading. |

Two sizes, and no third. A larger mark is an Empty's circle around a medium icon or an Avatar; a smaller one does not exist, because 12px strokes fall apart. Lucide's `size` prop is not used; the class sets width and height from the token.

## Stroke

Lucide's default, 2, everywhere, at both sizes. A thinner stroke at 14px breaks up; a heavier one at 16px reads as bold. A check or a chevron that must carry more weight is a size up, not a stroke up. The prototype's few `strokeWidth` overrides (1, 1.5, 2.5, 3) are a sweep item in `docs/next.md`.

## Colour

An icon mirrors its text, one step bolder where a thin glyph needs it: `color.icon` with `color.text`, `color.icon.subtle` with `color.text.subtle`, the tone's icon with the tone's text. On a bold fill the icon takes `currentColor` from the Box, which sets `color.text.inverse`, so an icon on `color.background.brand.bold` needs no class. The classes are `icon-*`; a Dot, a Badge and an Indicator set them through `tone`.

| Job | Class |
| --- | --- |
| Beside content text | `icon-default` |
| Beside subtle text, a chevron, a sort arrow | `icon-subtle` |
| Beside meta, a placeholder's mark | `icon-subtlest` |
| A status mark | `icon-success`, `icon-warning`, `icon-danger`, `icon-information` |
| Off | `icon-disabled` |

## Names

- **An icon beside a word is decoration.** `aria-hidden` is set by the parts that draw one (Button's `iconBefore`, Item's `leading`, a Banner's mark); a raw icon beside text carries `aria-hidden`.
- **An icon alone is named.** IconButton takes `label`, which is the name and the tooltip; a raw icon standing for a value (a check in a cell) takes `aria-label` or a visually hidden Text. Never a `title` attribute alone.
- **The name is the verb or the value**, not the glyph: "Edit properties", not "Pencil"; "Met", not "Check".
- **The target is the control, not the glyph.** An IconButton is `dimension.control.small` or `.medium` square around a 16px icon, so the target is 28 or 32px; a bare icon is never a target.

## Pairing with type

| Text | Icon |
| --- | --- |
| `font.body.xsmall`, `font.body.small`, `font.body` | 14px, `space.050` from the word |
| `font.heading.xsmall` and up | 16px, `space.100` from the words |
| A Button | 14px inside small and medium, before or after the label |
| An IconButton | 16px, alone |

The icon sits on the text's centre line (`alignBlock="center"`), not its baseline; Lucide's glyphs are drawn centred in their box.

## Don't

- **Don't mix sizes in one row.** A toolbar's icons are all 16; a row's marks are all 14.
- **Don't let colour carry the meaning.** A red mark has the word beside it or a name.
- **Don't invent a glyph.** A concept without a Lucide icon is a word; a word is always allowed.
- **Don't use an icon as a bullet.** A list is a list.

## Related

- [Metrics](?path=/docs/tokens-metrics--docs): the tokens.
- [Colour](?path=/docs/tokens-color--docs): the icon colours beside the text colours.
- [Button](?path=/docs/components-button--docs) and IconButton: where a named icon lives.
- [Badge](?path=/docs/components-badge--docs): Dot and Indicator, the status marks.

<!-- page: Tokens/Metrics (src/stories/tokens/Metrics.mdx) -->

# Metrics

Dimension is this system's own tier. Control heights are a themed axis rather than each component's own, so a control, a row, an icon and a layout region each have a token. The motion tokens share this sheet and have their own page (Tokens/Motion); the icons have theirs (Tokens/Icons).

## Controls

| Token                      | Value | Utility                                   | Use                                                    |
| -------------------------- | ----- | ----------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------ |
| `dimension.control.xsmall` | 24px  | `h-control-xsmall`, `size-control-xsmall` | Button xsmall, the densest chrome.                     |
| `dimension.control.small`  | 28px  | `h-control-small`, `size-control-small`   | Button small, chips, menu items, side nav items.       |
| `dimension.control.medium` | 32px  | `h-control-medium`, `size-control-medium` | The default: Button, Input, Select, Combobox triggers. |
| `dimension.control.large`  | 36px  | `h-control-large`, `size-control-large`   | Reserved for hero forms.                               |

## Rows

| Token                   | Value | Utility         | Use                          |
| ----------------------- | ----- | --------------- | ---------------------------- |
| `dimension.row`         | 40px  | `h-row`         | The default table row.       |
| `dimension.row.compact` | 36px  | `h-row-compact` | A compact table row.         |
| `dimension.row.header`  | 32px  | `h-row-header`  | The table header row.        |
| `dimension.row.menu`    | 28px  | `h-row-menu`    | Menu, command and tree rows. |

## Icons

| Token                   | Value | Utility            | Use                                        |
| ----------------------- | ----- | ------------------ | ------------------------------------------ |
| `dimension.icon.small`  | 14px  | `size-icon-small`  | An icon inside a small or medium control.  |
| `dimension.icon.medium` | 16px  | `size-icon-medium` | A standalone icon, an icon button's glyph. |

The sizes, the stroke, the colour and the naming rules are on the [Icons](?path=/docs/tokens-icons--docs) page.

## Layout

| Token                      | Value | Utility                | Use                                                           |
| -------------------------- | ----- | ---------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `dimension.layout.banner`  | 48px  | `h-layout-banner`      | The banner area above the top nav, when one is shown.         |
| `dimension.layout.topnav`  | 48px  | `h-layout-topnav`      | The top nav.                                                  |
| `dimension.layout.sidenav` | 228px | `w-layout-sidenav`     | The side nav, expanded. The reader may resize it.             |
| `dimension.layout.panel`   | 320px | `w-layout-panel`       | The panel beside the main area, before the reader resizes it. |
| `dimension.layout.list`    | 340px | `w-layout-list`        | The list column of a WorkPane.                                |
| `dimension.layout.rail`    | 272px | `w-layout-rail`        | The rail beside a record: Shell.Aside and property groups.    |
| `dimension.layout.measure` | 720px | `max-w-layout-measure` | The widest a run of prose grows.                              |

## Breakpoints

| Token                        | Value  | Variant  | Use                                                                              |
| ---------------------------- | ------ | -------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `dimension.breakpoint.md`    | 48rem  | `md:`    | Tailwind's md. The product folds the top nav's end items into a menu below it.   |
| `dimension.breakpoint.lg`    | 64rem  | `lg:`    | Tailwind's lg. The side nav is inline from here and an overlay below.            |
| `dimension.breakpoint.aside` | 75rem  | `aside:` | The aside sits beside Main from here while no panel is open.                     |
| `dimension.breakpoint.panel` | 80rem  | `panel:` | The panel is a full-height column beside the page; below, it replaces Main.      |
| `dimension.breakpoint.wide`  | 110rem | `wide:`  | The aside sits beside Main even while a panel is open.                           |

One source for three readers: `layout.css` writes `@media (width >= theme(--breakpoint-panel))`, the shell reads `tokenValue("dimension.breakpoint.panel")` for `matchMedia`, and a class takes the variant. `md` and `lg` restate Tailwind's values so a class and a media query cannot drift apart.

`src/styles/layout.css` adds the few templates a class string cannot say, each reading these tokens: `grid-cols-main-rail`, `grid-cols-list-detail`, `sticky-rail`, `min-h-work`, `fill-window` and `shell-root`, the navigation grid. The shell sets `--shell-top` (banner plus top nav) so a sticky rail knows where to stop, and its main area sets `--shell-inset-bottom` so a filled register knows where to end.

_Example: story `Stories.Dimension`._

<!-- page: Tokens/Motion (src/stories/tokens/Motion.mdx) -->

# Motion

Fast and quiet: six durations by the size of the move, three curves by whether the thing arrives, leaves or stays, and one stagger step for a set arriving together. Nothing in a component names a number; every transition and animation reads a token, and every one collapses under `prefers-reduced-motion`. This is a task-focused product and every move is a productive one: there is no expressive set, no bounce, no stretch.

_Example: story `Stories.Specimens`._

## Durations

| Token | Value | Utility | For |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `motion.duration.micro` | 70ms | `duration-micro` | A toggle's thumb, a checkbox's tick, a chevron turning: the smallest moves. |
| `motion.duration.fast` | 110ms | `duration-fast` | Hover and press colour, a tooltip's fade, a menu or a popover leaving. |
| `motion.duration.medium` | 150ms | `duration-medium` | A menu or a popover arriving, a section expanding or collapsing, a dialog or a sheet leaving. |
| `motion.duration.moderate` | 240ms | `duration-moderate` | A dialog or a sheet arriving, the panel sliding in, a toast, a page's content rising. |
| `motion.duration.slow` | 400ms | `duration-slow` | Marks arriving on a chart, and a drill-down redrawing it. |
| `motion.duration.slower` | 700ms | `duration-slower` | The blanket dimming the page under a dialog or a sheet. |
| `motion.stagger` | 20ms | in `stagger-children` | Between one item's entrance and the next when a set arrives together. Six at most. |

The bigger the move, the longer it takes: a colour change is micro or fast, a thing arriving in place is medium, a thing travelling across the screen is moderate, a whole page dimming is slower.

## Curves

| Token | Value | Utility | For |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `motion.easing.standard` | cubic-bezier(0.2, 0, 0.38, 0.9) | `ease-standard` | What stays on screen throughout: colour, a chevron, a sort, a side panel leaving. |
| `motion.easing.enter` | cubic-bezier(0, 0, 0.38, 0.9) | `ease-enter` | What arrives: in quickly, slowing to a stop. |
| `motion.easing.exit` | cubic-bezier(0.2, 0, 1, 0.9) | `ease-exit` | What leaves for good: speeding up out of view. |

A side panel leaves on the standard curve, not the exit curve, because it stays nearby.

## What moves, and how

| Part | Arrives | Leaves | Utility |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A button, a row, a chip, a tab: colour | fast · standard | | `transition-colors duration-fast ease-standard` |
| A chevron turning, a sort arrow | fast · standard | | `transition-transform duration-fast ease-standard` |
| A Switch thumb | micro · standard | | `transition-transform duration-micro ease-standard` |
| A tooltip | fast · enter | fast · exit | `animate-fade-in`, `animate-fade-out` |
| A menu, a popover, a hover card, a select list | medium · enter | fast · exit | `animate-enter`, `animate-exit` |
| A dialog, an alert dialog, the command palette | moderate · enter | medium · exit | `animate-dialog-in`, `animate-dialog-out` |
| The blanket under them | slower · enter | medium · exit | `animate-dim-in`, `animate-dim-out` |
| A sheet, the panel below the large breakpoint, the side nav's flyout | moderate · enter | medium · standard | `animate-slide-in-end`, `animate-slide-out-end`, and `-start` |
| A Collapsible section, alone or in a Group | medium · enter | medium · exit | `animate-collapse-open`, `animate-collapse-close` |
| A page's content, the panel at the large breakpoint, a Stat tile, a Related card | moderate · enter | | `animate-rise` |
| The panel's column opening or closing the page | moderate · standard | | `shell-root`'s grid transition |
| A set of tiles or cards arriving | one stagger step apart | | `stagger-children` on the parent |
| A chart's marks | slow | | Patterns/Chart |

Base UI components use `data-open`/`data-closed` or starting/ending styles; `src/styles/motion.css` defines the shared token-based animation utilities. Accordion reads Base UI’s `--accordion-panel-height`. Drawer’s `drawer.css` combines measured height, snap offset and swipe progress with Ledger motion tokens, and disables transitions under reduced motion.

## Transitions

- A button, a row, a chip or a tab transitions colour only: no press-down movement, no scale.
- A hover or a press is a token (`bg-brand-bold-hovered`, `bg-neutral-subtle-pressed`), never a brightness filter and never alpha on the resting fill.
- A thing that moves transitions `transform`, never `left` or `width`; the shell's grid is the one exception, and it transitions its template.

## Stagger

A set that arrives together arrives one thing at a time: `stagger-children` on the parent delays each child's entrance one step after the last, capped at six, so the last of a long list lands within a moderate duration and nothing waits for the end. Stat tiles and Related cards do this; a table's rows do not, because a register is read from the top and should be there when the eye arrives.

## Reduced motion

Under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` every animation runs in 0.01ms, every stagger is 0, the shell's grid does not transition, and a skeleton's pulse stops. A spinner keeps turning, because the turning is the message. A chart draws its marks in place (`src/styles/chart.css` and the Chart's motion hook read the same query).

## Don't

- **Don't bounce, stretch or stop suddenly.** The three curves are the only curves.
- **Don't animate what the reader is reading.** A register's rows, a form's fields and a record's facts are there when the page is; only the page itself rises.
- **Don't move a thing for decoration.** Every move says something: this arrived, this left, this opened, this is the same thing over there.
- **Don't name a number.** A duration or a curve in a component is a token; `duration-[200ms]` does not pass the lint.

<!-- page: Tokens/Shape (src/stories/tokens/Shape.mdx) -->

# Shape

Radius is a set of named absolute steps on a 5px base. Bare `rounded` is banned: it is a static 4px no reset can remove. Border width is 1px by default and 2px for focus and selection.

## Radius

| Token            | Value | Utility           | Use                                            |
| ---------------- | ----- | ----------------- | ---------------------------------------------- |
| `radius.xsmall`  | 2px   | `rounded-xsmall`  | Kbd, tiny chips.                               |
| `radius.small`   | 3px   | `rounded-small`   | Count, checkbox, Skeleton, inline hit targets. |
| `radius.medium`  | 5px   | `rounded-medium`  | Button, Input, Chip, Tooltip, menu items.      |
| `radius.large`   | 7px   | `rounded-large`   | Card, Popover, HoverCard.                      |
| `radius.xlarge`  | 9px   | `rounded-xlarge`  | Sheets.                                        |
| `radius.xxlarge` | 12px  | `rounded-xxlarge` | Dialog, CommandPalette, spotlight cards.       |
| `radius.full`    | pill  | `rounded-full`    | Badge, Dot, Avatar, Switch, meters.            |

The rule of thumb: the bigger the surface, the larger the radius. A control is medium, a card is large, a dialog is xxlarge.

## Border width

| Token                   | Value | Utility             | Use                                                       |
| ----------------------- | ----- | ------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------- |
| `border.width`          | 1px   | `border-w-default`  | Every standard border and divider.                        |
| `border.width.focused`  | 2px   | `border-w-focused`  | The focus ring, in `color.border.focused`.                |
| `border.width.selected` | 2px   | `border-w-selected` | An active tab, a chosen item, in `color.border.selected`. |

## Focus and selection

`outline-focused` is an outline of `border.width.focused` (2px) in `color.border.focused`, offset `space.025` (2px) outside the element's edge. Buttons, links and other actions use it on `:focus-visible` without changing the element's size.

Fields use `outline-field-focused` instead: the same 2px line sits inside the edge and covers the existing border, producing one continuous stroke without a gap, glow or layout shift. Input, Textarea, Select, DatePicker, InputGroup, Combobox and Calendar dropdowns share this treatment. Invalid fields use `outline-field-danger` so the whole focused edge keeps the error color. A grouped input leaves the edge to its container. Both outline treatments follow the element's radius.

Selection is not a ring. A selected tab or a chosen item takes `border.width.selected` (2px) in `color.border.selected` on one edge: the underline of a tab, the start edge of an item in a rail. A selected row takes a fill, `color.background.selected`, and no border. The two never appear together on one element: a focused, selected tab shows the ring outside and the underline beneath.

_Example: story `Stories.Radius`._

<!-- page: Tokens/Space (src/stories/tokens/Space.mdx) -->

# Space and layout

Space is tier 3 and mode independent. A name is the value in quarter-rems: `space.100` is 8px, `space.200` is 16px. Product code reaches it through primitive props (`<Stack space="space.200">`); the package reaches it through the regenerated spacing utilities (`gap-100`, `p-150`, `px-200`). Tailwind's numeric scale is reset: `p-4` does not exist and `ledger/no-non-token-class` reports it.

## Scale

| Token        | Value | Use                                               |
| ------------ | ----- | ------------------------------------------------- |
| `space.0`    | 0     | No space.                                         |
| `space.025`  | 2px   | Hairline.                                         |
| `space.050`  | 4px   | Tight: icon to text, dot to text.                 |
| `space.075`  | 6px   | Compact: control gap.                             |
| `space.100`  | 8px   | Standard small: control clusters, chip rows.      |
| `space.150`  | 12px  | Standard medium: cell padding, card header inset. |
| `space.200`  | 16px  | Standard large: card padding, form grids.         |
| `space.250`  | 20px  | Comfortable.                                      |
| `space.300`  | 24px  | Relaxed: between header and actions.              |
| `space.400`  | 32px  | Spacious: page gutters.                           |
| `space.500`  | 40px  |                                                   |
| `space.600`  | 48px  | Section spacing.                                  |
| `space.800`  | 64px  | Page section.                                     |
| `space.1000` | 80px  | Hero.                                             |

The negative steps (`space.negative.025` to `space.negative.400`) are read by Bleed alone, through `m-negative-*`, `mx-negative-*` and `my-negative-*`: the one place a negative value is written.

## Margins do not exist

A component decides its inside; its parent decides the space around it. Box takes padding and a surface and has no margin props. Stack and Inline own the gap between siblings. `ledger/no-margin` reports a margin class in product code.

## Density

Heights come from the dimension tokens (Tokens/Metrics); insets come from space.

| Where               | Value                                                                                                            |
| ------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Controls            | `dimension.control.medium` 32px; `small` 28px for toolbars, rows and rails; `xsmall` 24px for the densest chrome |
| Table rows          | `dimension.row` 40px; `compact` 36px; `header` 32px; menu, command and tree rows 28px                            |
| Cell padding        | `space.150`                                                                                                      |
| Card and form inset | `space.200`                                                                                                      |
| KeyValue            | a 104px label column, `space.150` between label and value, `space.050` block padding                             |

Compact and data-dense, never cramped.

## Page structure

The shell is a grid of named areas: Banner, TopNav, SideNav, Main, Aside, Panel. Their widths are `dimension.layout.*` tokens, and Main takes the rest; there is no fixed content column. Inside Main a page is PageHeader, then Section, Block or Card. IndexPage and ShowPage stack their regions on `space.200`; a ShowPage body runs `space.400` between sections. Prose never grows wider than `dimension.layout.measure` (720px).

## Separation

Prefer a hairline rule to a box. Section is a heading with a rule under it (`border-b border-default`) and no enclosure. Card is the enclosure, for when a region must read as one object.

_Example: story `Stories.Scale`._

<!-- page: Tokens/Typography (src/stories/tokens/Typography.mdx) -->

# Typography

A type token is one font shorthand: family, weight, size, leading and its letter-spacing. Its utility sets `font` and `letter-spacing` together, so `font-body` is the whole style, and restates the weight as a longhand under the shorthand, so `font-medium` or `font-semibold` beside it wins whichever order the two land in the stylesheet. No half pixels exist. Labels are `font.body.small` plus `font.weight.medium`, not a size of their own.

## One face

| Token | Value | Use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `font.family.body` | Geist, Inter, system sans | Everything. Identifiers, dates and numbers use it too. |
| `font.family.heading` | Same as body | A token so a theme may split them. |
| `font.family.code` | Geist Mono, JetBrains Mono, monospace | Code blocks and data previews only. Never UI text. |

## Scale

`font.body` is the UI size. Weight 600 belongs to page and record titles and nothing else.

| Token | Utility | Size | Weight | Use |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `font.heading.large` | `font-heading-large` | 28/34 | semibold | Display: a stat value, a dashboard number. Not a page title. |
| `font.heading.medium` | `font-heading-medium` | 22/28 | semibold | Page and record titles. The only semibold. |
| `font.heading.small` | `font-heading-small` | 20/26 | medium | Section headings. |
| `font.heading.xsmall` | `font-heading-xsmall` | 15/22 | medium | Dialog and card titles. |
| `font.heading.xxsmall` | `font-heading-xxsmall` | 11/14 | medium | Eyebrows, group headings, menu section labels. The component adds the uppercase. |
| `font.body.large` | `font-body-large` | 15/22 | regular | Reading text and dialog body. |
| `font.body` | `font-body` | 13/18 | regular | Controls, cells, tabs, inputs, menu items. |
| `font.body.small` | `font-body-small` | 12/16 | regular | Table headers, field labels, badges, KeyValue. Labels add `font-medium`. |
| `font.body.xsmall` | `font-body-xsmall` | 11/14 | regular | Eyebrow, counts, metadata. |
| `font.code` | `font-code` | 12/18 | regular | Code blocks only. |

Text takes the body ramp as `size` (`large`, `medium`, `small`, `xsmall`). Heading takes the heading ramp the same way (`large`, `medium`, `small`, `xsmall`). Eyebrow is `font.heading.xxsmall`, uppercased.

## Weight

| Token | Utility | Use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `font.weight.regular` | `font-regular` | Body, cells, controls. |
| `font.weight.medium` | `font-medium` | Labels, UI headings, emphasis inside body text. |
| `font.weight.semibold` | `font-semibold` | Page and record titles only. |

## Letter-spacing

Tracking tightens as size grows. Each composite carries its own step; there is no utility.

| Token | Value | Carried by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `font.letterSpacing.100` | -0.004em | `font.body.small`, `font.body.xsmall` |
| `font.letterSpacing.200` | -0.008em | `font.body`, `font.body.large` |
| `font.letterSpacing.300` | -0.015em | `font.heading.small`, `font.heading.xsmall` |
| `font.letterSpacing.400` | -0.02em | `font.heading.medium`, `font.heading.large` |
| `font.letterSpacing.500` | 0.06em | `font.heading.xxsmall`: uppercase micro labels |
| `font.letterSpacing.0` | 0 | `font.code` |

## Identifiers and numerals

Control numbers, finding ids, package ids, hashes and STIG rule ids are wrapped in `Id`. It inherits the font, size and colour around it and adds tabular numerals; it exists for semantics and grep-ability. A table cell is one style, `font.body` regular in `color.text`; only Badge, Dot, Indicator or a status colour may differ (`ledger/cell-plain`). An Id is blue only inside a link or a button (`ledger/id-not-blue`).

`base.css` sets `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums` on every table. Add `tabular-nums` yourself for aligned numbers anywhere else: percentages, counts, dates in a column.

_Example: story `Stories.Specimen`._

<!-- page: Primitives/Bleed (src/stories/primitives/Bleed.mdx) -->

# Bleed

The one place a negative margin is written: a child that escapes its parent's padding, by the token that padding is. A strip that runs to a card's edges, a table that meets a card body's sides, a list of rows that reaches a panel's top and bottom, a rail row's hover fill to the rail's edge. `all`, `inline` or `block`, and a scale that stops short, because a bleed is never larger than the padding it escapes. Here the scale is the tokens with a negative in the source, `space.025` to `space.400`, the page gutter.

_Example: story `Stories.BleedMatrix`._

## Anatomy

| Part    | What it is                                                                                          |
| ------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Wrapper | A `div`, or the layout element `as` names, with a negative margin on the axis named. The child inside keeps its own padding and fill. |
| `inline` | Escapes the inline padding: left and right.                                                       |
| `block` | Escapes the block padding: top and bottom.                                                          |
| `all`   | Both.                                                                                               |

## Variants

| Bleed  | Use                                                                                                       |
| ------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Inline | A strip, a table, a row's hover fill: to the card's or the rail's sides.                                  |
| Block  | Rows to a panel's top and bottom, a tab strip to a card header's top.                                     |
| All    | A cover on a card, a media block under the radius.                                                        |

Not built, and why: a bleed beyond `space.400` (nothing is padded more than a page gutter, so nothing has more to escape); one edge at a time (a child that escapes one side only is a layout of two columns, not a bleed); a bleed on a Box (the Bleed is its own element, so the child keeps its padding and fill and the negative margin is in one place); a bleed that clips (the child hangs past the parent's radius unless it has its own; the card's `overflow` is the card's decision).

## Sizes

The tokens with a negative in the source:

| Token       | px  | Escapes                                            |
| ----------- | --- | -------------------------------------------------- |
| `space.025` | 2   | A hairline inset.                                  |
| `space.050` | 4   | A tight inset.                                     |
| `space.075` | 6   | A small control's inset.                            |
| `space.100` | 8   | A rail's inset, a compact row's.                    |
| `space.150` | 12  | A cell's, a card header's.                          |
| `space.200` | 16  | A card's, a dialog body's.                          |
| `space.250` | 20  |                                                     |
| `space.300` | 24  | A dialog's, a page section's.                       |
| `space.400` | 32  | A page gutter.                                      |

The bleed equals the padding it escapes. A bleed larger than the padding hangs outside the parent; smaller, it stops short of the edge and reads as a mistake in the inset.

## Modifiers

- **`all`**, **`inline`**, **`block`**: the token, on the axis. One or two; `all` alone.
- **`as`**: `li` when the bleeding child is a list item, `section` when it is a region; the layout elements.
- **`className`** for the rare case the child needs a width or a clip the parent does not give it. No `style`: a computed width is a Box's.

## Content

- **The bleed is the padding.** Read the parent's `padding` and write the same token; when the card's inset changes, change both.
- **The child keeps its inset.** A strip that bleeds `space.200` has its own `paddingInline="space.200"`, so its text lines up with the card's.
- **Never to move a thing.** A Bleed pulls a child to its parent's edge; it does not pull a sibling closer. The distance between siblings is a Stack's.

## Style

| Element | Token                                                          |
| ------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Margin  | `space.negative.*`, read by `m-negative-*`, `mx-negative-*`, `my-negative-*`: the negative token, not the positive one negated |

## Accessibility

- **Nothing changes for a screen reader.** The child is where it was in the tree; only its box moved.
- **Order is kept.** A bleed cannot put a child before or after a sibling.
- **A bleeding table is still a table.** Its caption and headers are its own; the Bleed is a div around it.

## Props

_Props: generated from `Bleed`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._

### Playground

_Example: story `Stories.Playground`._

_Rendered in the Storybook: Controls._

## Related

- [Box](?path=/docs/primitives-box--docs): the padding a Bleed escapes.
- [Card](?path=/docs/components-card--docs): the card body a table bleeds inside.
- [Table](?path=/docs/components-table--docs): the thing that most often meets a card's edges.
- [Space](?path=/docs/tokens-space--docs): the scale and its negatives.

## Don't

_Example: story `Stories.Dont`._

<!-- page: Primitives/Box (src/stories/primitives/Box.mdx) -->

# Box

The fundamental block: padding on any edge, a fill or a surface, and the element it is. Nothing else. There are no margin props, because a component decides its inside and its parent decides the space around it: the distance between siblings is Stack's and Inline's, and the one negative margin is Bleed's. Every value is a token, so an invalid padding is a type error and a valid one is a literal class the scanner sees. A Box is never a link or a button; a surface is named, not counted, so nesting does not step the background; and a class held to tokens, not a style prop per property, is the escape hatch.

_Example: story `Stories.BoxMatrix`._

## Anatomy

| Part            | What it is                                                                                                                                                  |
| --------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Element         | A `div`, or the container, landmark or list part `as` names. Never `a` or `button`.                                                                        |
| Padding         | `padding` on every side; `paddingInline` and `paddingBlock` per axis; `paddingInlineStart`, `paddingInlineEnd`, `paddingBlockStart`, `paddingBlockEnd` per edge. Space tokens. |
| Fill            | `backgroundColor`: a semantic background (`color.background.*`) or an elevation surface (`elevation.surface.*`).                                            |
| Text colour     | Set by the fill: a bold, bolder or boldest fill paints `color.text.inverse`; the warning bold, which is light, paints `color.text.warning.inverse`.         |
| Current surface | A surface fill is published as `utility.elevation.surface.current`, so a sticky or masking child paints the surface it is on and matches.                  |

## Variants

| Box              | Use                                                                                                                                    |
| ---------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Plain            | Padding only: the inset of a region, a cell, a rail.                                                                                   |
| Surface          | `elevation.surface`, `.sunken`, `.raised`, `.overlay`: the page, the well, the card, the popover. The shadow or hairline is a class.    |
| Fill             | A semantic background: a chip, a callout, a selected row. A bold fill paints its text inverse by itself.                               |
| Landmark or list | `as="section"` with `aria-labelledby`, `as="article"`, `as="ul"` and `"li"`: the element is the semantics, the Box is the inset.       |

Not built, and why: margin props (the parent owns the distance); width and height props (a Box is as wide as its parent gives it, and the widths a layout needs are a Grid's template and the layout tokens); `as="a"` or `"button"` (TextLink and Button carry the ring, the pressed face and the name); a style prop for the rest (a class is the escape hatch, and the lint holds it to tokens); automatic layer stepping (a surface is named, not counted: a card inside a card is a decision, not a default).

## Sizes

The space scale, on any edge:

| Token       | px  | Where                                                |
| ----------- | --- | ---------------------------------------------------- |
| `space.025` | 2   | Hairline: a chip's block inset.                      |
| `space.050` | 4   | Tight: icon to text.                                 |
| `space.075` | 6   | Compact: a small control's block inset.              |
| `space.100` | 8   | A rail's inset, a row's block inset, a chip's inline. |
| `space.150` | 12  | A cell, a card header.                               |
| `space.200` | 16  | A card, a form grid, a dialog body.                  |
| `space.250` | 20  | Comfortable.                                         |
| `space.300` | 24  | Relaxed: a dialog's inset, a page section.           |
| `space.400` | 32  | A page gutter.                                       |
| `space.500` to `space.1000` | 40 to 80 | Sections, a hero. Rare inside a Box.     |

The scale, with every token, is on the [Space](?path=/docs/tokens-space--docs) sheet.

## Modifiers

- **`padding`**, **`paddingInline`**, **`paddingBlock`**, and the four edges by name. Per-axis over per-side: one Box, not two.
- **`backgroundColor`**: a background or a surface token. A surface publishes itself; a bold fill paints inverse text.
- **`as`**: the element, from the layout elements: `div`, `span`, `section`, `article`, `aside`, `nav`, `header`, `footer`, `main`, `ul`, `ol`, `li`, `dl`, `dt`, `dd`, `fieldset`, `form`, `figure`, `figcaption`.
- **`className`** for the radius, the border and the shadow, from the token classes.
- **`style`**, runtime values only: a width measured or computed at render, a story's fixed frame. Box and Grid are the two layout primitives that take it; a Stack, an Inline or a Text of a fixed width sits in a Box.

## Content

- **A Box holds; it does not say.** Text inside it is a Text or a Heading, so the size and the colour are tokens too.
- **A bold fill needs no colour on its text.** Write `<Text>` inside `color.background.brand.bold` and it is inverse. A colour on the Text overrides it.
- **Name a section.** `as="section"` with `aria-labelledby` pointing at its Heading; a section without a name is a div to a screen reader.
- **One Box, not two.** `paddingInline="space.200" paddingBlock="space.100"` on one Box, not a Box for each axis.

## Style

| Element         | Token                                                                                           |
| --------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Padding         | `space.*`, as `p-*`, `px-*`, `py-*`, `pt-*`, `pb-*`, `ps-*`, `pe-*`                            |
| Fill            | `color.background.*` · `elevation.surface`, `.sunken`, `.raised`, `.overlay`                    |
| Inverse text    | `color.text.inverse` on `*.bold`, `*.bolder`, `*.boldest` · `color.text.warning.inverse` on `warning.bold` |
| Current surface | `utility.elevation.surface.current`, set from the surface the Box paints                        |
| Radius, border, shadow | By class: `rounded-*` from `radius.*`, `border-default` from `color.border`, `shadow-raised` and `shadow-overlay` from `elevation.shadow.*` |

## Accessibility

- **The element is the semantics.** A `div` says nothing; `as="section"`, `"nav"`, `"aside"`, `"ul"` say what the region is, and `aria-labelledby` names it.
- **Never interactive.** No `role="button"`, no `onClick`, no `tabIndex` on a Box: it has no focus ring, no pressed face and no keyboard. A Button or a TextLink has all three, and `as` will not render either.
- **Inverse text is chosen by the token**, so the pairs are the ones the [Color](?path=/docs/tokens-color--docs) sheet measures: `text.inverse` on every bold, `text.warning.inverse` on the warning bold.
- **Logical edges.** `paddingInlineStart` is the left in a left-to-right page and the right in a right-to-left one.
- **A surface is not a landmark.** Painting `elevation.surface.raised` says nothing to a screen reader; a card that is a region says so with `as` and a name.

## Props

_Props: generated from `Box`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._

### Playground

_Example: story `Stories.Playground`._

_Rendered in the Storybook: Controls._

## Related

- [Stack](?path=/docs/primitives-stack--docs) and [Inline](?path=/docs/primitives-inline--docs): the distance between children, which a Box never sets.
- [Bleed](?path=/docs/primitives-bleed--docs): the child that escapes a Box's padding.
- [Card](?path=/docs/components-card--docs): the raised surface with a header, built on a Box.
- [Text](?path=/docs/primitives-text--docs) and [Heading](?path=/docs/primitives-heading--docs): what goes inside.
- [Space](?path=/docs/tokens-space--docs) and [Color](?path=/docs/tokens-color--docs): the scales the props are typed on.

## Don't

_Example: story `Stories.Dont`._

<!-- page: Primitives/Flex (src/stories/primitives/Flex.mdx) -->

# Flex

The general flex container, for the layouts Stack and Inline do not express: a row distributed `space-around`, a column whose children stretch, a wrap with its own column and row gaps. Stack and Inline are Flex with the choices made; reach for them first, and for Flex when the choice they made is the wrong one. There is no reverse direction and no reverse wrap: a reversed row reads in one order and tabs in the other.

_Example: story `Stories.FlexMatrix`._

## Anatomy

| Part      | What it is                                                                                     |
| --------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Container | A flex box: a `div`, or the layout element `as` names.                                         |
| Direction | `row` or `column`. No reverse.                                                                 |
| Gap       | `gap` on both axes; `rowGap` and `columnGap` over it.                                          |
| Main axis | `justifyContent`: `start`, `center`, `end`, `space-between`, `space-around`, `space-evenly`.   |
| Cross axis | `alignItems`: `start`, `center`, `end`, `baseline`, `stretch`.                                |
| Wrap      | `wrap` or `nowrap`.                                                                            |

## Variants

| Flex     | Use                                                                                                          |
| -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Row      | A row that Inline cannot say: `space-around`, `space-evenly`, or children stretched to the tallest.          |
| Column   | A column that Stack cannot say: a `baseline` alignment, children distributed `space-around`.                  |
| Wrapping | Cells of their own width with a column gap and a row gap that differ, and a distribution across each row.    |

Not built, and why: `row-reverse` and `column-reverse` (the eye reads one order and the keyboard another; write the children in the order they should read); `wrap-reverse` (the same); `inline-flex` (Inline's `display`, for a row inside text); a per-child `alignSelf` or `order` (a child that sits differently carries its own class, and order is DOM order); a responsive direction (a layout that changes at a breakpoint is a Grid with one template per breakpoint).

## Sizes

`gap`, `rowGap` and `columnGap` take the space scale, the same steps Stack and Inline take: `space.050` for an icon and its word, `space.100` for chips and controls, `space.200` for cards, `space.300` for a header from its actions. The scale is on the [Space](?path=/docs/tokens-space--docs) sheet.

## Modifiers

- **`direction`**: `row` (the default) or `column`.
- **`gap`**, **`rowGap`**, **`columnGap`**: tokens. The two axes over the one.
- **`justifyContent`**: the six distributions along the main axis.
- **`alignItems`**: the five positions on the cross axis. `stretch` for cards of one height in a row.
- **`wrap`**: `wrap` or `nowrap`.
- **`as`**: the layout elements.
- **No `style`.** A computed dimension is a Box's.

## Content

- **Stack and Inline first.** A Flex with `direction="row" alignItems="center"` and a gap is an Inline; with `direction="column"` and a gap, a Stack. Flex is for what those cannot say, and the reader of the code learns something when they see it.
- **Order is written order.** A child that should come last is written last.
- **A two-column layout is a Grid.** Widths in a Flex are on the children, in three places; a Grid's template says them once.

## Style

| Element   | Token                                                          |
| --------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Gap       | `space.*`, as `gap-*`, `gap-x-*`, `gap-y-*`                    |
| Direction | `flex-row`, `flex-col`                                         |
| Axes      | `justify-*`, `items-*`                                         |
| Wrap      | `flex-wrap`, `flex-nowrap`                                     |

## Accessibility

- **Visual order is DOM order.** The reverse directions are not offered, so a Flex cannot put the eye and the keyboard out of step.
- **The element is the semantics.** A Flex is a `div` unless `as` says a list or a region.
- **`stretch` is not a size.** Cards stretched to the tallest are still their own targets.

## Props

_Props: generated from `Flex`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._

### Playground

_Example: story `Stories.Playground`._

_Rendered in the Storybook: Controls._

## Related

- [Inline](?path=/docs/primitives-inline--docs) and [Stack](?path=/docs/primitives-stack--docs): the row and the column, first.
- [Grid](?path=/docs/primitives-grid--docs): columns of a template, for a layout with widths.
- [Space](?path=/docs/tokens-space--docs): the scale.

## Don't

_Example: story `Stories.Dont`._

<!-- page: Primitives/Grid (src/stories/primitives/Grid.mdx) -->

# Grid

Columns and rows on a template. The template is a string, the CSS value itself, or one string per breakpoint; the gaps are tokens. It is the primitive for a layout with widths: a main column and a rail, a label column and a value column, cards of equal width, a form's fields in two columns that become one on a narrow page. The one thing past a plain grid is the template per breakpoint, which travels as a CSS variable a static class reads, so a page never writes an arbitrary class. A page grid with gutters and margins is the Shell's areas' job, not this.

_Example: story `Stories.GridMatrix`._

## Anatomy

| Part      | What it is                                                                                                                                            |
| --------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Container | A grid: a `div`, or the layout element `as` names. `as="dl"` for label and value pairs.                                                               |
| Template  | `templateColumns`, a `grid-template-columns` value, or `{ base, sm, md, lg, xl }`, each applying from that width up; `templateRows`; `templateAreas`. |
| Gap       | `gap` on both axes; `rowGap` and `columnGap` over it. Tokens.                                                                                         |
| Alignment | `alignItems` on the block axis, `justifyContent` on the inline axis.                                                                                  |
| Flow      | `autoFlow`: `row`, `column`, `dense`, `row-dense`, `column-dense`.                                                                                    |

## Variants

| Grid            | Use                                                                                                                                                      |
| --------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Equal columns   | `repeat(n, minmax(0, 1fr))`: cards, stats, fields of a form.                                                                                             |
| Label and value | `104px 1fr` as a `dl`: the facts of a rail, a settings list. KeyValue draws one row of it.                                                               |
| Main and rail   | `minmax(0, 1fr) 272px`: the record page's body and its rail, at `dimension.layout.rail`. The Shell's `grid-cols-main-rail` is this with the rail's rule. |
| Named areas     | `templateAreas` with `templateRows`: a head over two columns, a form with a full-width row.                                                              |
| Responsive      | One template per breakpoint: one column, two from `md`, main and rail from `lg`.                                                                         |

Not built, and why: a column count per breakpoint as a number (the template says the widths as well as the count, and `repeat(3, minmax(0, 1fr))` is one string); a page grid with gutters and margins (the Shell's areas and the page's gutter tokens do this, and a page here is a form or a register, not a magazine); `justifyItems` and `alignContent` (no layout here has needed them, and a cell that sits differently carries its own class); `templateAreas` as an array of rows (one string is the CSS value, and the reader can paste it).

## Sizes

The gaps are the space scale: `space.050` between facts, `space.100` between cells, `space.200` between cards and form fields, `space.300` between the main column and the rail. The breakpoints, the `dimension.breakpoint.*` tokens (`md` and `lg` on Tailwind's values; the shell's `aside`, `panel` and `wide` are on the Metrics page):

| Key    | From   |
| ------ | ------ |
| `base` | 0      |
| `sm`   | 640px  |
| `md`   | 768px  |
| `lg`   | 1024px |
| `xl`   | 1280px |

The widths a template names come from the layout tokens where one exists: `dimension.layout.rail` 272px, `.panel` 320px, `.list` 340px, `.measure` 720px, on the [Metrics](?path=/docs/tokens-metrics--docs) sheet.

## Modifiers

- **`templateColumns`**: a string, or an object with `base` and any of `sm`, `md`, `lg`, `xl`. Write `minmax(0, 1fr)`, never a bare `1fr`: a fraction's minimum is its content, and a long file name would widen its column past the frame.
- **`templateRows`**, **`templateAreas`**: strings.
- **`gap`**, **`rowGap`**, **`columnGap`**: tokens.
- **`alignItems`**: `start`, `center`, `end`, `baseline`, `stretch`. **`justifyContent`**: the six distributions and `stretch`.
- **`autoFlow`**: `dense` to fill holes in a grid of spanning cells.
- **`as`**: `dl` for pairs, `ul` for a list of cards; the layout elements.

## Content

- **Widths in the template, once.** Not on the children in three places.
- **`minmax(0, 1fr)`**, so a column can shrink below its content and the content truncates or wraps inside it.
- **One template per breakpoint** when the layout changes with width. Three columns at every width is 90px each in a rail.
- **Chips are not a grid.** Things of their own width that wrap are an Inline; a Grid stretches each to its column and leaves a hole in the last row.
- **Pairs are a `dl`.** A label column and a value column with `dt` and `dd` children, so the pairs are pairs to a screen reader.

## Style

| Element   | Token                                                                                                               |
| --------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Gap       | `space.*`, as `gap-*`, `gap-x-*`, `gap-y-*`                                                                         |
| Template  | Inline `grid-template-columns` for a string; `grid-cols-(--ds-grid-<bp>)` per breakpoint, the value in the variable |
| Widths    | `dimension.layout.rail`, `.panel`, `.list`, `.measure` where the template names a layout width                      |
| Alignment | `items-*`, `justify-*`, `grid-flow-*`                                                                               |

## Accessibility

- **Visual order is DOM order.** `autoFlow="dense"` can fill a hole with a later cell, moving it before an earlier one to the eye; use it for cells that have no order, tiles of a dashboard, never for fields of a form.
- **Pairs are a `dl`**, list cards a `ul`; a grid of cells with no relation stays a `div`.
- **A responsive template does not reorder.** The cells keep their order at every width; only the columns change.
- **`templateAreas` may reorder.** A named area can place a later cell first; a form's fields keep their template in order.

## Props

_Props: generated from `Grid`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._

### Playground

_Example: story `Stories.Playground`._

_Rendered in the Storybook: Controls._

## Related

- [Inline](?path=/docs/primitives-inline--docs): things of their own width, wrapping.
- [Flex](?path=/docs/primitives-flex--docs): a row or a column distributed, without widths.
- [KeyValue](?path=/docs/components-keyvalue--docs): one row of the label and value grid.
- [Stat](?path=/docs/components-stat--docs): `Stat.Grid`, a grid of tiles with the grid's own rules.
- [Pages](?path=/docs/layout-pages--docs): the record page's main column and rail, on `grid-cols-main-rail`.
- [Space](?path=/docs/tokens-space--docs) and [Metrics](?path=/docs/tokens-metrics--docs): the gaps and the layout widths.

## Don't

_Example: story `Stories.Dont`._

<!-- page: Primitives/Heading (src/stories/primitives/Heading.mdx) -->

# Heading

A title. The size is the design's and the level is the page's: `size` picks the style from the heading ramp and an element to go with it, and `as` overrides the element when the outline needs another level. Four sizes, four jobs: a displayed number, a page title, a section heading, a card or dialog title. The colour is the text colour, or its inverse on a bold fill, which a Box sets for you; a tone is not a heading colour. A required `size`, a default element per size, `as`, and `color` limited to three. The sizes are fixed, and the level is semantic and separate from the style.

_Example: story `Stories.HeadingMatrix`._

## Anatomy

| Part    | What it is                                                                                                                                              |
| ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Element | By size: `large` a `div`, `medium` an `h1`, `small` an `h2`, `xsmall` an `h3`. `as` overrides it with a `HeadingElement`: a level, a `div` or a `span`. |
| Size    | `large`, `medium`, `small`, `xsmall`: the four `font.heading` tokens.                                                                                   |
| Colour  | `color.text`, inherited; `color.text.inverse` or `color.text.warning.inverse` from a bold Box.                                                          |

## Variants

| Heading  | Use                                                                                               |
| -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `large`  | A displayed number: a Stat's value, a dashboard figure. A `div`, because a number is not a title. |
| `medium` | The page's title, the record's name. One per page, the `h1`.                                      |
| `small`  | A section heading in a page body, a tab's heading. The `h2`.                                      |
| `xsmall` | A card's title, a dialog's title, a rail section's heading. The `h3`, or `h4` under a section.    |

Not built, and why: `xxlarge` and `xlarge` (the product has no hero, and 22px is the biggest text on a page); `xxsmall` as a Heading (it is the Eyebrow, uppercase and subtle, on the Typography page); a subtitle slot (the line under a title is a Text, and the PageHeader draws it); an icon before (a Heading is words; the mark beside a record's title is the PageHeader's); a tone (a red heading says the word is the problem; the count beside it is).

## Sizes

| Size     | Token                 | Size / leading / weight | Element | Where                             |
| -------- | --------------------- | ----------------------- | ------- | --------------------------------- |
| `large`  | `font.heading.large`  | 28 / 34 / semibold      | `div`   | A displayed number.               |
| `medium` | `font.heading.medium` | 22 / 28 / semibold      | `h1`    | The page title.                   |
| `small`  | `font.heading.small`  | 20 / 26 / medium        | `h2`    | A section heading.                |
| `xsmall` | `font.heading.xsmall` | 15 / 22 / medium        | `h3`    | A card, a dialog, a rail section. |

Under it, `font.heading.xxsmall` at 11 / 14, uppercase, is the Eyebrow. Four are enough here because a page is a title, its sections and their cards.

## Modifiers

- **`size`**: required. The design's choice.
- **`as`**: the page's choice. `h2` for a section at the card size in a rail; `h4` for a subsection at the section size; `div` for a title-sized line where the outline already has its `h1`.
- **`color`**: `color.text`, `color.text.inverse`, `color.text.warning.inverse`. Left off, it follows the surface.
- **`id`**, for a section's `aria-labelledby`.
- **No `style`.** A heading has no computed dimension.

## Content

- **One `h1`.** The page's title; every other title is `as="h2"` or below, whatever its size.
- **The outline in order.** No `h3` under an `h1` without an `h2` between, and no level chosen for its size.
- **A title is a noun phrase**, sentence case, no full stop: "Assessment results", "Schedule assessment".
- **`large` is a number**, not a title. The 28px size is a Stat's.
- **A tone goes on the fact beside the title**, never on the title.

## Style

| Element | Token                                                                                                      |
| ------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Size    | `font.heading.large` · `.medium` · `.small` · `.xsmall`, family, size, leading, weight and tracking in one |
| Colour  | `color.text` · `color.text.inverse` · `color.text.warning.inverse`                                         |

## Accessibility

- **The level is the element**, and the element is the page's decision through `as`. The size says nothing to a screen reader.
- **A section is named by its heading.** `<Box as="section" aria-labelledby>` pointing at the Heading's `id`.
- **The outline is a map.** A screen reader's user jumps by heading; two `h1`s are two pages, a skipped level is a missing floor.
- **`large` is a `div`** so a displayed number is not a heading in the outline. A Stat's label is its heading, if it needs one.
- **Contrast is the token's.** `color.text` on every surface and `color.text.inverse` on every bold fill are measured on the Color sheet.

## Props

_Props: generated from `Heading`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._

### Playground

_Example: story `Stories.Playground`._

_Rendered in the Storybook: Controls._

## Related

- [Text](?path=/docs/primitives-text--docs): everything that is not a title.
- [Typography](?path=/docs/components-typography--docs): the Eyebrow, the heading under `xsmall`.
- [PageHeader](?path=/docs/layout-pageheader--docs) and [PageHeader](?path=/docs/layout-pageheader--docs): where the `h1` is drawn.
- [Section](?path=/docs/layout-section--docs) and [Card](?path=/docs/components-card--docs): where the `h2` and the `h3` are drawn.
- [Stat](?path=/docs/components-stat--docs): where `large` is drawn.
- [Typography tokens](?path=/docs/tokens-typography--docs): the ramp.

## Don't

_Example: story `Stories.Dont`._

<!-- page: Primitives/Inline (src/stories/primitives/Inline.mdx) -->

# Inline

A row with one gap. Children sit start to end with one space token between them, aligned on the block axis as the row says, wrapping when told to with a row space of their own. A separator is drawn between children and hidden from a screen reader. A separator does not belong on a list element. Here it also renders inline-level, as a `span` with `display="inline-flex"`, so a chip and a word can sit inside a sentence.

_Example: story `Stories.InlineMatrix`._

## Anatomy

| Part      | What it is                                                                                                      |
| --------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Container | A flex row: a `div`, a `span`, a list or a list item, as `as` names. `display="inline-flex"` keeps it inline-level. |
| Space     | `space`, one token between every pair of children on the inline axis; `rowSpace` between rows when wrapping, `space` if unset. |
| Alignment | `alignBlock`, where the children sit on the block axis: `start`, `center`, `end`, `baseline`, `stretch`; `alignInline`, where they sit along the row. |
| Spread    | `spread="space-between"`: a label at the start and a count at the end.                                          |
| Separator | A string or node drawn between children, `aria-hidden`: the dot of a meta line, the slash of a path.           |
| Wrap      | `shouldWrap`, rows of chips; off, the children overflow.                                                        |
| Grow      | `grow="fill"` takes the parent's inline space; `hug` is as wide as the children.                                 |

## Variants

| Inline       | Use                                                                                                   |
| ------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Row          | An id beside a title beside a status: one token between each, on the baseline or centred.             |
| Wrapping row | Chips, tags, filters: `shouldWrap` with a `rowSpace` tighter than `space`.                            |
| Meta line    | Facts separated by a dot: `separator="·"` on subtle small text.                                        |
| Spread       | A label and a count, a title and its action: `spread="space-between"`.                                 |
| In text      | `as="span" display="inline-flex"`: a chip inside a sentence, the sentence's line height kept.          |
| List         | `as="ul"` with `as="li"` children: a list of chips, a set of links.                                    |

Not built, and why: a reverse order (the tab order would run against the eye); a `separator` that is read (the dot is decoration; a list that needs its items separated for a screen reader is a list, `as="ul"`); a per-child alignment (a child that sits differently is in its own Inline, or is a Flex); a truncating row (the children truncate themselves with Text's `maxLines`; the row does not know which one should).

## Sizes

`space` on the inline axis, `rowSpace` between wrapped rows:

| Token       | px  | Where                                                    |
| ----------- | --- | -------------------------------------------------------- |
| `space.050` | 4   | An icon and its word, a dot and its label.               |
| `space.075` | 6   | A small control and its neighbour.                       |
| `space.100` | 8   | Chips, buttons in a group, facts on a line.              |
| `space.150` | 12  | Facts under a title, a control cluster.                  |
| `space.200` | 16  | Actions at a header's end, columns of a header.          |
| `space.300` | 24  | A header's title from its actions.                        |

When wrapping, `rowSpace` is one step tighter than `space`: `space.100` across, `space.050` down.

## Modifiers

- **`space`** and **`rowSpace`**.
- **`alignBlock`**: `center` for controls of one height; `baseline` for text of two sizes, a title beside its id; `start` for a mark beside two lines.
- **`alignInline`**: `start`, `center`, `end`, where the children sit along the row when it is wider than they are.
- **`spread`**: `space-between`.
- **`shouldWrap`**.
- **`separator`**: a string or a node. Not with `as="ul"`, `"ol"` or `"dl"`.
- **`grow`**: `fill` for the Inline that takes the space between a fixed start and a fixed end.
- **`display`**: `inline-flex` for a row that sits in a run of text.
- **`as`**: `span` in text; `ul`, `ol`, `li` for a list; the layout elements.
- **No `style`.** A row of a fixed width sits in a Box with the width.

## Content

- **The dot is the separator.** Never a child: it would be read, and it would take a gap on each side.
- **Text of two sizes sits on the baseline.** A title beside an id is `alignBlock="baseline"`; controls beside each other are `center`.
- **A row that can grow wraps.** Chips, tags and filters get `shouldWrap`; a row that cannot wrap (a header's actions) has a count that is fixed.
- **A list is a list.** Chips that are a set are `as="ul"` with `li` children, and no separator.

## Style

| Element   | Token                                                        |
| --------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Space     | `space.*`, as `gap-x-*`; `rowSpace` as `gap-y-*`             |
| Alignment | `items-*` for `alignBlock`, `justify-*` for `alignInline` and `spread` |
| Separator | The children's font and colour; the row's `space` on each side |
| Grow      | `flex-1` for `fill`                                          |

## Accessibility

- **The separator is hidden.** It is `aria-hidden`; a screen reader hears the children, one after the other.
- **Not on a list.** A span between `li` elements is not a valid child of a list, so a list with a separator is no longer a list.
- **Visual order is DOM order.** No reverse: what is first on the line is first in the tab order.
- **A row in text is a `span`.** `as="span" display="inline-flex"` keeps a chip inside a paragraph's flow, so the paragraph is one paragraph to a screen reader.

## Props

_Props: generated from `Inline`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._

### Playground

_Example: story `Stories.Playground`._

_Rendered in the Storybook: Controls._

## Related

- [Stack](?path=/docs/primitives-stack--docs): the column.
- [Flex](?path=/docs/primitives-flex--docs): the row an Inline cannot say.
