- [Grid](?path=/docs/primitives-grid--docs): columns of a fixed template, when the children should line up across rows.
- [ButtonGroup](?path=/docs/components-buttongroup--docs): a row of buttons with the row's own rules.
- [Fact](?path=/docs/components-fact--docs): the facts a meta line is made of.
- [Space](?path=/docs/tokens-space--docs): the scale.

_Example: story `Stories.Dont`._

<!-- page: Primitives/Overview (src/stories/primitives/Primitives.mdx) -->

# Primitives

Layout and text, modelled on `@atlaskit/primitives`. Every prop that carries a design value is typed to a token, so an invalid value is a type error and a valid one is a literal class the scanner sees. Every layout primitive renders a container, a landmark or a list element, never a link or a button.

- [Box](?path=/docs/primitives-box--docs)
- [Stack](?path=/docs/primitives-stack--docs)
- [Inline](?path=/docs/primitives-inline--docs)
- [Flex](?path=/docs/primitives-flex--docs)
- [Grid](?path=/docs/primitives-grid--docs)
- [Bleed](?path=/docs/primitives-bleed--docs)
- [Text](?path=/docs/primitives-text--docs)
- [Heading](?path=/docs/primitives-heading--docs)

| Primitive   | For                                                                                                                          | Key props                                                                                                    |
| ----------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| **Box**     | Padding and a fill. No margins, ever. A bold fill paints its text inverse; a surface publishes itself to sticky children.    | `padding`, `paddingInline`, `paddingBlock` (space tokens), `backgroundColor` (a background or surface token), `as` |
| **Stack**   | A column with one gap.                                                                                                       | `space`, `alignInline`, `alignBlock`, `spread`, `grow`, `as`                                                 |
| **Inline**  | A row with one gap, optionally wrapping. `display="inline-flex"` keeps it inline-level for a chip or a count beside a label. | `space`, `rowSpace`, `alignBlock`, `alignInline`, `spread`, `shouldWrap`, `separator`, `grow`, `display`     |
| **Flex**    | The escape hatch when Stack and Inline are not enough. No reverse.                                                           | `direction`, `gap`, `alignItems`, `justifyContent`, `wrap`                                                   |
| **Grid**    | Columns or rows on a template. `templateColumns` takes a string, or one per breakpoint (`{ base, sm, md, lg, xl }`).         | `templateColumns`, `templateRows`, `templateAreas`, `gap`, `alignItems`, `justifyContent`                    |
| **Bleed**   | The one place a negative margin is written: pulling a child out to the edge of its parent's padding, by the padding's token. | `all`, `inline`, `block` (`space.025` to `space.400`)                                                        |
| **Text**    | Interface text on the body ramp.                                                                                             | `size` (large, medium, small, xsmall), `weight`, `color` (a text token), `align`, `maxLines`, `as`           |
| **Heading** | A title: the size from the design, the level from the page.                                                                  | `size` (large, medium, small, xsmall), `as`, `color` (text, inverse, warning inverse)                        |

## Rules of thumb

- A component decides its inside; its parent decides the space around it. That is why Box has no margin props and Stack and Inline own the gaps.
- Reach for Stack and Inline first. Flex and Grid are for the layouts those cannot express.
- Visual order is DOM order. No primitive reverses, reorders or floats its children.
- Text and Heading take colour tokens, not classes. `color="color.text.subtle"` is checked by the compiler.
- When a Box paints a surface it records that surface, so a child that needs "the surface I am on" can read `bg-surface-current`. When it paints a bold fill, the text inside is inverse.
- A link is a TextLink and a button is a Button. `as` on a primitive will not render either: the layout primitives take a `LayoutElement`, Text a `TextElement`, Heading a `HeadingElement`.
- `style` is for runtime values, on Box and Grid only. A Stack, an Inline or a Text of a fixed width sits in a Box with the width.

<!-- page: Primitives/Stack (src/stories/primitives/Stack.mdx) -->

# Stack

A column with one gap. Children sit top to bottom with one space token between them, and the children carry no margin of their own: the parent owns the distance, so the rhythm of a form, a rail or a page body changes in one place. `space`, `alignBlock`, `alignInline`, `spread` and `grow`, on a `div`, a `span` or a list element. The child has no margin; the container has the distance. Here the orientation is the primitive's name; a row is an Inline.

_Example: story `Stories.StackMatrix`._

## Anatomy

| Part      | What it is                                                                                                                      |
| --------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Container | A flex column: a `div`, or the container, landmark or list element `as` names.                                                  |
| Space     | `space`, one token between every pair of children. No first or last exception: a Stack has no outer space.                      |
| Alignment | `alignInline`, where the children sit across the column; `alignBlock`, where they sit along it when it is taller than they are. |
| Spread    | `spread="space-between"`, the free block space divided between the children: a footer pinned to a panel's bottom.               |
| Grow      | `grow="fill"`, the Stack takes the block space its parent offers; `hug`, the default, it is as tall as its children.            |

## Variants

| Stack         | Use                                                                                                       |
| ------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Column        | Rows of a form, sections of a rail, paragraphs of a body: one token between each.                         |
| Spread column | A panel's content over its footer: `spread` with the Stack filling the panel's height.                    |
| List          | `as="ul"` or `"ol"` with `li` children, when the rows are a list: steps, linked records, a menu of links. |

Not built, and why: a horizontal orientation (a row is an Inline, which has what a row needs: wrapping, a separator, baseline alignment); dividers between children (a Separator is a child, and rows that want hairlines are an Item.Group); a responsive space (one token at every width; the layout that changes at a breakpoint is a Grid); a `space` per child (a different distance is a different Stack, or a Section).

## Sizes

One space token between every child:

| Token       | px  | Where                                             |
| ----------- | --- | ------------------------------------------------- |
| `space.025` | 2   | A label over its control's helper line.           |
| `space.050` | 4   | A title over its description, lines of one thing. |
| `space.075` | 6   | Rows of facts in a rail.                          |
| `space.100` | 8   | Rows of a compact list, chips' rows.              |
| `space.150` | 12  | Fields of a dense form, cards in a rail.          |
| `space.200` | 16  | Fields of a form, cards in a body.                |
| `space.300` | 24  | Sections of a rail, a header over its body.       |
| `space.400` | 32  | Sections of a page body.                          |
| `space.600` | 48  | Page sections with their own headings.            |

## Modifiers

- **`space`**: the one token. Leave it off for children that touch: rows with their own hairlines.
- **`alignInline`**: `start`, `center`, `end`, `stretch`. `stretch` is the browser's default for a flex column, so a Button in a Stack is as wide as the Stack unless the Stack says `start`.
- **`alignBlock`**: `start`, `center`, `end`, when the Stack is taller than its children.
- **`spread`**: `space-between`, the free block space between the children.
- **`grow`**: `fill` to take the parent's block space, the case for `spread` and `alignBlock` to have any effect.
- **`as`**: `ul` or `ol` for rows that are a list; `section` or `aside` for a region; the layout elements.
- **No `style`.** A Stack of a fixed width sits in a Box with the width; the Stack has no computed dimension of its own.

## Content

- **Reading order is the order.** A Stack renders its children as written; there is no reverse. What is first is first to the eye and to a screen reader.
- **Two things, two Stacks.** A card's title over its description is one Stack at `space.050`; the cards themselves are another at `space.200`. Nesting is the way to two distances.
- **One child needs no Stack.** The primitive is for the distance between children; a Stack around one child spaces nothing.
- **Steps are a list.** `as="ol"` with `li` children, so a screen reader says how many and where it is.

## Style

| Element   | Token                                                                  |
| --------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Space     | `space.*`, as `gap-*`                                                  |
| Alignment | `items-*` for `alignInline`, `justify-*` for `alignBlock` and `spread` |
| Grow      | `flex-1` for `fill`                                                    |

## Accessibility

- **Visual order is DOM order.** No reverse, no `order`: the tab order and the reading order are the order the children are written in.
- **A list is `as="ul"` or `"ol"`** with `li` children, so the count and the position are announced. Rows that are not a list stay a `div`.
- **A region is `as="section"`** with a name, or `"aside"` for a rail. The Stack's element is the semantics; the space is not.
- **`stretch` is not a size.** A full-width Button from `alignInline="stretch"` is still one target; its label sits at its start.

## Props

_Props: generated from `Stack`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._

### Playground

_Example: story `Stories.Playground`._

_Rendered in the Storybook: Controls._

- [Inline](?path=/docs/primitives-inline--docs): the row.
- [Box](?path=/docs/primitives-box--docs): the inset around a Stack, which the Stack never sets.
- [Flex](?path=/docs/primitives-flex--docs): the column a Stack cannot say.
- [Section](?path=/docs/layout-section--docs): a Stack's child with a heading of its own.
- [Item](?path=/docs/components-item--docs): rows with hairlines, which are not a Stack.
- [Space](?path=/docs/tokens-space--docs): the scale.

<!-- page: Primitives/Text (src/stories/primitives/Text.mdx) -->

# Text

Body text on the body ramp. The size is a composite type token, so the family, the size, the leading and the tracking always agree; the weight is one of three; the colour is a text token, or inherited, so a Text inside a bold Box is inverse without being told. `as`, `size`, `weight`, `color`, `align`, `maxLines`, and a colour that inverts inside a bold fill. `font.body` at 13px is the UI size; `small` at 12px is a label's and a hint's. The rules on colour and weight: running text is neutral, colour is functional, semibold is for a heading and not a paragraph.

_Example: story `Stories.TextMatrix`._

## Anatomy

| Part    | What it is                                                                                                                      |
| ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Element | A `span` by default, or the `TextElement` `as` names: `p`, `div`, `strong`, `em`, `small`, `label`, `legend`, `figcaption`, `dt`, `dd`, `li`. Never a heading, a link or a button. |
| Size    | `large`, `medium`, `small`, `xsmall`: the four `font.body` tokens.                                                              |
| Weight  | `regular`, `medium`, `semibold`. Over the token's own weight.                                                                    |
| Colour  | A `color.text` token, or inherited: `color.text` from the page, `color.text.inverse` from a bold Box.                            |
| Clamp   | `maxLines` 1, 2 or 3, with an ellipsis.                                                                                          |

## Variants

| Text      | Use                                                                                                         |
| --------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Paragraph | `as="p"`: a statement, a description, a note, at `medium` or `large`, at the reading measure.                |
| Run       | The default `span`: a value in a cell, a word in a row, a count beside a label.                              |
| Label     | `as="label"` with `htmlFor`, or `as="dt"` in a pair: `small` medium, subtle.                                |
| Meta      | `small` or `xsmall`, `subtle` or `subtlest`: a date, an id, a count.                                         |
| Emphasis  | `weight="medium"` on a word in a sentence; `as="strong"` when the emphasis is for a screen reader too.       |

Not built, and why: a `bold` weight (the ramp's top is `semibold`, the page title's weight, and a paragraph above it shouts); italic (for the titles of works and technical terms, and the product has neither in running text); an underline (a link is a TextLink; an underline that is not a link reads as one); a `truncate` with a tooltip (`maxLines` clamps, and the parent gives the full text a `title` or a Tooltip when it matters); an escape below the ramp (`xsmall` is the floor, and nothing is set below 11px); a text transform (an Eyebrow sets its own uppercase; nothing else is transformed).

## Sizes

| Size     | Token              | Size / leading | Where                                                                  |
| -------- | ------------------ | -------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `large`  | `font.body.large`  | 15 / 22        | Reading text: a statement, a dialog's body, a note at the measure.     |
| `medium` | `font.body`        | 13 / 18        | The UI size: controls, cells, tabs, menu items, descriptions. The default, inherited from the page. |
| `small`  | `font.body.small`  | 12 / 16        | Table headers, field labels, badges, KeyValue, meta lines.             |
| `xsmall` | `font.body.xsmall` | 11 / 14        | Counts, dates, ids beside something. Never a sentence.                 |

The UI size is 13, a point under the usual 14, because a register's rows are the page.

## Modifiers

- **`size`**, **`weight`**, **`color`**, **`align`**, **`maxLines`**, **`as`** as in Anatomy.
- **`color`** is left off where the text should follow its surface: inside a bold Box, inside a Button.
- **`maxLines`** is 1, 2 or 3. A longer clamp is a Section with a "Show more".
- **No `style`.** A width for a label column is a Box's, or a Grid's template.

## Content

- **Running text is neutral.** `color.text` for a paragraph, `subtle` for a description, `subtlest` for meta.
- **Colour says something.** `danger` on an overdue count, `success` on a passed check, `brand` on nothing that is not a link.
- **Sentence case, one idea per sentence.** A description ends with a full stop; a label and a meta line do not.
- **Emphasis is a weight, and rare.** One word in `medium`; never a sentence in `semibold`.
- **A title is a Heading.** A Text in `large` `semibold` is not in the outline and is not on the heading ramp.
- **The reading measure.** A paragraph at `large` or `medium` is capped at `dimension.layout.measure`, 720px, by its parent.

## Style

| Element | Token                                                                                              |
| ------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Size    | `font.body.large` · `font.body` · `font.body.small` · `font.body.xsmall`, the family, size, leading and tracking in one |
| Weight  | `font.weight.regular` · `.medium` · `.semibold`                                                    |
| Colour  | `color.text` · `.subtle` · `.subtlest` · `.disabled` · `.brand` · `.selected` · `.danger` · `.warning` · `.success` · `.information` · `.inverse` · `.warning.inverse` |
| Clamp   | `truncate` for one line; `line-clamp-2`, `line-clamp-3`                                             |
| Measure | `dimension.layout.measure`, set by the parent                                                       |

## Accessibility

- **A clamped text is still all there.** `maxLines` hides with CSS; a screen reader reads the whole. The eye needs the rest too: the parent gives a `title`, or a Tooltip, or the row opens the record.
- **`as="strong"` for emphasis that must be heard**; `weight="medium"` for emphasis that is only seen.
- **A label is a `label`** with `htmlFor`, so the control is named. Text as a label without the element names nothing.
- **Colour is never the only signal.** A red count has the word beside it: "2 past due", not "2".
- **Contrast is the token's.** Every `color.text.*` on every `color.background.*` it is paired with is measured on the Color sheet; a Text inherits the pair its Box chose.

## Props

_Props: generated from `Text`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._

### Playground

_Example: story `Stories.Playground`._

_Rendered in the Storybook: Controls._

## Related

- [Heading](?path=/docs/primitives-heading--docs): titles, on the heading ramp.
- [Typography](?path=/docs/components-typography--docs): Eyebrow, Absent and Prose, the three parts between Text and Heading.
- [TextLink](?path=/docs/components-textlink--docs): a link in text.
- [Box](?path=/docs/primitives-box--docs): the fill that sets a Text's colour.
- [Typography tokens](?path=/docs/tokens-typography--docs): the ramp, with every token's value.

## Don't

_Example: story `Stories.Dont`._

<!-- page: Components/Accordion (src/stories/components/Accordion.mdx) -->

# Accordion

A coordinated set of expandable sections, implemented with the shadcn Base UI composition. Use Collapsible for one independent disclosure.

## Anatomy

Compose the flat `Accordion`, `AccordionItem`, `AccordionTrigger`, and `AccordionContent` exports. Each item needs a stable value; values are always arrays, and `multiple` allows more than one open item.

```tsx
<Accordion defaultValue={["delivery"]}>
  <AccordionItem value="delivery">
    <AccordionTrigger>What delivery options are available?</AccordionTrigger>
    <AccordionContent>Delivery information.</AccordionContent>
  </AccordionItem>
</Accordion>
```

## Variants and states

_Example: story `Stories.Examples`._

Use `value` with `onValueChange` for controlled state and `defaultValue` otherwise. Use `disabled` on the root or an item. `keepMounted` preserves panel state while closed; `hiddenUntilFound` additionally lets browser find-in-page reveal closed content.

_Example: story `Stories.ControlledAndRetained`._

## Accessibility

Triggers are native buttons with Enter, Space, and normal Tab behavior. Base UI follows current APG guidance and does not add arrow-key roving focus. The trigger wrapper supplies the heading and associates every panel with its trigger.

## Related

[Collapsible](?path=/docs/components-collapsible--docs), [shadcn Accordion](https://ui.shadcn.com/docs/components/base/accordion), and [Base UI Accordion](https://base-ui.com/react/components/accordion).

<!-- page: Components/Alert (src/stories/components/Alert.mdx) -->

# Alert

Inline feedback with explicit title, description and action parts. Use record-specific language that tells the reader what happened and what they can do.

## Anatomy

```tsx
<Alert variant="destructive">
  <AlertTitle>Import failed</AlertTitle>
  <AlertDescription>The file is missing record identifiers.</AlertDescription>
  <AlertAction>
    <a href="#format">Read the required format</a>
  </AlertAction>
</Alert>
```

A decorative SVG may sit directly inside Alert, or beside text inside AlertTitle. Content and icons are caller-owned. Ledger keeps actions in normal flow so long recovery links fit narrow panels.

## Variants and states

`variant="default"` uses a neutral tone; `destructive` uses danger. Ledger's optional `tone` overrides either visual tone. Tone does not choose announcement behavior.

_Example: story `Stories.Variants`._
_Example: story `Stories.Tones`._

The application owns action handlers and feedback.

_Example: story `Stories.WithAction`._

## Accessibility

Alert defaults to `role="alert"`, following shadcn. Use `role="status"` for polite updates or `role="note"` for static contextual information. Explicitly associate titles and descriptions with `aria-labelledby` and `aria-describedby` when needed. Hide decorative icons from assistive technology. Buttons and links retain their native behavior.

## Props

_Props: generated from `Alert`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._

All parts accept native div attributes and refs. `title` is now the native HTML tooltip attribute.

### Migration

Replace `Alert.Title`, `Alert.Description`, and `Alert.Action` with flat exports. Move shorthand `title`, `action`, and `icon` content into children. Existing callers explicitly retain their previous tones and announcement roles. New callers receive shadcn's neutral default appearance and alert role.

## Related

[Banner](?path=/docs/components-banner--docs), [Toaster](?path=/docs/components-toaster--docs), [AlertDialog](?path=/docs/components-alertdialog--docs).

Sources: [shadcn Alert](https://ui.shadcn.com/docs/components/base/alert), [implementation](https://github.com/shadcn-ui/ui/blob/main/apps/v4/registry/bases/base/ui/alert.tsx).

<!-- page: Components/AlertDialog (src/stories/components/AlertDialog.mdx) -->

# AlertDialog

Based on [shadcn’s Base UI source](https://ui.shadcn.com/docs/components/base/alert-dialog) and [Base UI](https://base-ui.com/react/components/alert-dialog). Ledger retains its tokens and application layouts.

## Anatomy

A confirmation that requires an explicit decision. Compose AlertDialog, Trigger, Content, Header, Title, Description, Footer, Cancel and Action. Flat export names include the AlertDialog prefix. Media supplies an optional icon region; Portal and Overlay allow custom composition.

## Variants

_Example: story `Stories.ConfirmationAndPending`._

_Example: story `Stories.SmallConfirmation`._

_Example: story `Stories.CustomPortal`._

## Accessibility

Base UI prevents outside-click dismissal and supplies the alertdialog role. Put the consequences in Description. Set Content initialFocus to the least destructive action when appropriate. Escape requests a close unless the caller cancels it; Cancel is an explicit native Close part.

## Props

Root exposes generic Base UI AlertDialog props, payloads, handles and cancellable onOpenChange. Content supports native popup props plus default/sm size. Action is a Ledger Button, matching shadcn: the caller performs the action and closes only when it succeeds. Cancel composes Base UI Close with Button.

### Migration and API

- Replace configured title, description, confirmLabel and onConfirm with explicit Title, Description and Action children/onClick.
- Replace onClose with onOpenChange and pending with caller-owned cancellation, disabled buttons and loading state. Action does not automatically dismiss the confirmation.
- Move returnFocusRef to Content finalFocus. Existing app confirmations retain their 440px maximum and top placement.

## Related

- [Dialog](?path=/docs/components-dialog--docs)
- [Button](?path=/docs/components-button--docs)

<!-- page: Components/Attachment (src/stories/components/Attachment.mdx) -->

# Attachment

One file or image with its name, metadata and optional actions. Experimental; owner: Ledger maintainers. A base component for file presentation. The application owns file selection, uploading, retries, removal and preview dialogs.

## Anatomy

Compose only the parts the file needs:

| Part                   | Responsibility                                                        |
| ---------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Attachment             | Surface, size, orientation and upload state.                          |
| Attachment.Media       | Icon or image preview.                                                |
| Attachment.Content     | Groups the name, metadata and optional progress.                      |
| Attachment.Title       | Truncated filename; native `title` can expose the full name on hover. |
| Attachment.Description | File type, size, status or a wrapping failure explanation.            |
| Attachment.Trigger     | Optional card-wide action button.                                     |
| Attachment.Actions     | Independent controls above the trigger.                               |
| Attachment.Action      | IconButton with a required `label` and `icon`.                        |
| Attachment.Group       | Horizontally scrollable row.                                          |

```tsx
<Attachment>
  <Attachment.Media aria-hidden="true">
    <FileText />
  </Attachment.Media>
  <Attachment.Content>
    <Attachment.Title>quarterly-report.pdf</Attachment.Title>
    <Attachment.Description>PDF · 2.4 MB</Attachment.Description>
  </Attachment.Content>
  <Attachment.Trigger aria-label="Preview quarterly-report.pdf" onClick={openPreview} />
  <Attachment.Actions>
    <Attachment.Action label="Remove quarterly-report.pdf" icon={<X />} onClick={removeFile} />
  </Attachment.Actions>
</Attachment>
```

## Variants

`orientation="horizontal"` places media beside metadata; `vertical` places it above. `Media variant="image"` crops a caller-rendered image into a square preview. Supply `alt=""` when it repeats the filename without adding useful information; otherwise describe the image. The caller owns unavailable-image fallbacks and object URL cleanup.

_Example: story `Stories.Images`._

## Sizes

`medium` is the default, with 12px padding and 40px media. `small` uses 8px padding and 32px media; `xsmall` uses 6px padding and 24px media. Small sizes use the small body token. Metadata remains visible at every size. Action buttons keep their minimum 28px target. Vertical media fills the card width. Override width on the root or constrain its container.

_Example: story `Stories.AttachmentMatrix`._

## States

`idle` uses a dashed border; `uploading` and `processing` set `aria-busy`; `error` changes the border and description to danger; `done` is the default resting surface. These are caller-supplied states, with no internal transitions. Write the status or error in Description so color is never its only signal. Compose Spinner or Progress when useful; filename animation is not imposed. Spinner respects reduced motion.

_Example: story `Stories.UploadStates`._

## Modifiers

Native attributes, event handlers, `className`, `style` and refs reach each part's own element. Title and Description are spans; structural parts are divs. The root's native `title` remains a tooltip attribute. Set explicit `aria-busy` if the default busy mapping does not fit the composition.

Trigger is an action button with `type="button"` by default. Use `render` to compose a custom button that forwards its props and ref. For navigation or downloads, style an ordinary anchor with `buttonVariants` and the same overlay geometry. It retains native link keyboard behavior and browser actions. A native disabled Trigger represents an unavailable action. A root upload state does not disable actions automatically; removing or cancelling an upload may still be useful.

```tsx

<a
  href={file.url}
  download
  aria-label={`Download ${file.name}`}
  className={buttonVariants({
    variant: "subtle",
    className:
      "absolute inset-0 z-10 h-full w-full rounded-medium bg-transparent p-0 hover:bg-transparent active:bg-transparent",
  })}
/>;
```

Existing `Attachment.Trigger asChild` navigation migrates to this anchor. Trigger follows Button's action contract, so links no longer pass through its button interaction behavior.

## Content

Keep the filename recognizable, including its extension. Description supports multiple lines so failure reasons and recovery instructions remain visible. Place all interactive content in Actions when using the card-wide Trigger; avoid wrapping the whole card in a button or link. Actions accepts ordinary Button, IconButton, menus or links when its icon-button shortcut does not fit.

_Example: story `Stories.WithActions`._

## Style

Ledger surface, border, text, spacing, icon, radius and focus tokens. Horizontal cards fit their content; vertical cards default to the rail width. Actions remain in normal flow even on images so they do not cover the preview or its metadata. Group preserves the scrollbar and uses proximity snapping. No external stylesheet, uploader dependency or runtime media inference is required.

_Example: story `Stories.Group`._

## Accessibility

Every Trigger needs `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`; it is an empty overlay with no text of its own. Icon actions require a descriptive `label`, such as “Remove quarterly-report.pdf”. Trigger and actions are sibling controls with independent focus and activation. Put Trigger before Actions in the DOM for preview-then-actions tab order. Return focus to a surviving control after removal; the With Actions example offers Undo.

No live region is imposed. `aria-busy` identifies in-progress content but does not announce completion; the application can use a separate polite status region for upload results. Give Progress a label. Hide decorative icons explicitly. For a group containing no interactive attachments, add `tabIndex={0}`, `role="group"` and an accessible name to make horizontal scrolling available from the keyboard. Interactive attachments are reached by Tab, which scrolls them into view.

## Props

_Props: generated from `Attachment`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._

All compound part prop types are exported. `Attachment.Action` accepts IconButton props; Trigger supports Button's native attributes, ref and `render` composition. The app's old shadcn copy uses different size and action APIs; import the Ledger component from `@ledger/design-system`.

### Playground

_Example: story `Stories.Playground`._
_Rendered in the Storybook: Controls._

## Related

[Button](?path=/docs/components-button--docs), [Progress](?path=/docs/components-progress--docs), [Dialog](?path=/docs/components-dialog--docs), [Composer](?path=/docs/patterns-composer--docs). Reference: [shadcn Attachment](https://ui.shadcn.com/docs/components/base/attachment).

## Don't

Do not build upload orchestration or infer preview behavior inside Attachment. Do not nest a remove button inside the card's trigger. Do not communicate upload failure through a red border alone, hide recovery copy with truncation, or force every group into a carousel with hidden scrollbars.

<!-- page: Components/Avatar (src/stories/components/Avatar.mdx) -->

# Avatar

Represent a person or entity with Base UI image loading and shadcn's flat Avatar parts. Ledger retains its sizes, shapes and accent treatments.

## Anatomy

```tsx
<Avatar role="img" aria-label="Dana Whitfield" size="medium">
  <AvatarImage src="/dana.png" alt="" />
  <AvatarFallback>DW</AvatarFallback>
  <AvatarBadge tone="success" />
</Avatar>
```

Compose overlapping avatars with `AvatarGroup` and `AvatarGroupCount`. The caller chooses members and writes the overflow count. `Person` remains the small avatar plus visible name used in record rows.

## Variants and states

Sizes are `xsmall`, `small` (default), `medium`, `large` and `xlarge`. Shapes are `circle` and `square`; treatments are `neutral`, `tinted`, `bold` and `gradient`. Use `avatarHue(name)` when a person's accent should stay stable and `avatarInitials(name, count)` to produce fallback text.

_Example: story `Stories.AvatarMatrix`._
_Example: story `Stories.People`._

Base UI shows the fallback while the image loads or fails. `AvatarFallback.delay` can delay its appearance. Changing Image's `src` retries loading.

_Example: story `Stories.ImageLoading`._

## Accessibility

Name an informative avatar with `role="img"` and `aria-label`, including meaningful presence information. When a visible name already identifies the person, set `aria-hidden="true"` on the avatar. A named group can hide its avatars and count when its accessible name already describes the entire group. Give Image an empty alt when the root supplies the name.

## Props

Root, Image and Fallback preserve their native Base UI props, refs, `render`, and state-based classes/styles. Badge accepts native span props and Ledger's `tone`. Group and GroupCount accept native div props. Ref targets follow each part.

Replace `Avatar name/src` with explicit Image and Fallback children; replace `isDecorative` with native `aria-hidden`. Replace `Avatar.Stack names/max` with caller-owned `AvatarGroup` children and `AvatarGroupCount`. There is one composition API.

_Example: story `Stories.Playground`._

## Related

[shadcn Avatar](https://ui.shadcn.com/docs/components/base/avatar) · [Base UI Avatar](https://base-ui.com/react/components/avatar) · [Badge](?path=/docs/components-badge--docs)

<!-- page: Components/Badge (src/stories/components/Badge.mdx) -->

# Badge

A compact label built on the shadcn Base UI Badge foundation and adapted to Ledger. One Badge combines six visual treatments with semantic tones, subtle or bold emphasis, two density sizes, optional icons, and rendered-link composition. Every combination uses the same pill anatomy.

`variant` chooses the treatment and its defaults; `tone` chooses the palette; `appearance` adjusts the emphasis of filled treatments; `size` adjusts density. With no props, Badge is the standard brand-filled `default` variant. A record status commonly uses `variant="secondary"` with its tone.

_Example: story `Stories.Matrix`._

## Anatomy

| Export or part  | Responsibility                                                                                                              |
| --------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Badge`         | A `span` by default, or the element supplied through Base UI's `render` prop.                                               |
| `badgeVariants` | The shared class recipe for treatment, tone, emphasis, and size. Consumers composing their own element can use it directly. |
| Label           | Concise children that remain meaningful without color or an icon.                                                           |
| Icon            | An optional leading `icon`, or explicit icon children with `data-icon="inline-start"` / `"inline-end"`.                     |

Badge emits `data-slot="badge"` and its resolved `data-variant`, `data-tone`, `data-appearance`, and `data-size`. Palette choices do not select a different component or change the shape.

```tsx

<Badge>Featured</Badge>;
<Badge variant="secondary" tone="neutral">
  Draft
</Badge>;
<Badge variant="secondary" tone="success" icon={<CircleCheck aria-hidden="true" />}>
  Verified
</Badge>;
<Badge variant="secondary" tone="danger" appearance="bold" size="xsmall">
  Overdue
</Badge>;
<Badge variant="outline" tone="success" render={<a href="/evidence" />}>
  Verified evidence
  <ArrowUpRight aria-hidden="true" data-icon="inline-end" />
</Badge>;

<span className={badgeVariants({ variant: "secondary", tone: "success", size: "xsmall" })}>
  Verified
</span>;
```

The recipe supplies classes only. A consumer using `badgeVariants` directly owns its element, attributes, refs, semantics, and composition.

_Example: story `Stories.Recipe`._

## Variants

All six treatments accept the same tone and size axes.

| `variant`     | Default palette / emphasis | Treatment                                                                                      |
| ------------- | -------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `default`     | Brand / bold               | Filled. A rendered anchor uses the palette's hover fill. The default.                          |
| `secondary`   | Neutral / subtle           | Filled. A rendered anchor uses the palette's hover fill.                                       |
| `destructive` | Danger / subtle            | Filled. Its default danger tone uses the danger focus outline.                                 |
| `outline`     | Neutral                    | Transparent with a visible border; a rendered anchor gains the palette's subtle fill on hover. |
| `ghost`       | Neutral                    | Transparent, with the palette's subtle fill on hover.                                          |
| `link`        | Brand                      | Palette-colored text, underlined on hover. Render an anchor to give it link behavior.          |

`appearance="subtle"` or `"bold"` overrides the filled treatments' default emphasis. Outline, ghost, and link retain their treatment when an appearance is supplied. `tone` overrides the palette across every variant, including outline borders and link text. Semantic colors adapt to light and dark modes; bold warning badges use the dark `color.text.warning.inverse` text token.

| Tone          | Meaning                                                                      |
| ------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `brand`       | Branding or a featured label. The default palette for `default` and `link`.  |
| `neutral`     | A category, kind, or state without a judgment: Inspection, Draft, Inherited. |
| `information` | In progress: In review, In remediation.                                      |
| `success`     | Done and good: Verified, Satisfied, Closed.                                  |
| `warning`     | Needs attention soon: Due soon, Partial, Suspect.                            |
| `danger`      | Wrong or late: Overdue, Other than satisfied, Invalidated.                   |

_Example: story `Stories.SemanticMatrix`._

The next matrix applies every status tone to all six variants at the compact size. Outline and link examples render actual anchors. The radius, icon anatomy, and density are shared across the matrix.

_Example: story `Stories.SemanticVariants`._

## Sizes

| `size`   | Height / text | Use                                                 |
| -------- | ------------- | --------------------------------------------------- |
| `small`  | 20px / 12px   | Default. Beside a title, in a rail, or in a header. |
| `xsmall` | 16px / 11px   | A table row, a tab, or a dense list item.           |

Both sizes use the same pill radius and 12px icons. Small badges use 8px horizontal padding, reduced to 6px beside a marked icon; xsmall badges keep 4px padding for density. The width follows the label, which stays on one line. Containers should wrap separate badges when space is limited; keep long labels readable.

_Example: story `Stories.InRows`._

_Example: story `Stories.DenseAndLongContent`._

## States

| State           | Behavior                                                                                            |
| --------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Plain label     | Native span semantics. No default tab stop or action.                                               |
| Rendered anchor | Native link semantics, Tab focus, Enter activation, and treatment-specific hover styling.           |
| Focus visible   | Focus border and Ledger's 2px outline with a 2px offset. A danger tone uses the danger outline.     |
| Invalid         | Caller-owned `aria-invalid` selects the danger border and outline color. It does not validate data. |

Badge manages no selection, dismissal, loading, or disabled state. Use an appropriate interactive control for those behaviors. A variant supplies presentation; a rendered element supplies its native interaction semantics.

_Example: story `Stories.States`._

## Composition

### Links

Keep the destination on the rendered anchor or router element. A router adapter must forward every received prop and its ref to the actual anchor so that styles, handlers, and accessibility attributes reach the same element.

```tsx

type RouterLinkProps = Omit<ComponentProps<"a">, "href"> & { to: string };

const RouterLink = forwardRef<HTMLAnchorElement, RouterLinkProps>(function RouterLink(
  { to, ...props },
  ref,
) {
  return <a ref={ref} href={to} {...props} />;
});

<Badge variant="outline" tone="information" render={<RouterLink to="/programs" />}>
  Programs
</Badge>;
```

Base UI merges attributes, classes, styles, event handlers, and both refs onto the same rendered element.

_Example: story `Stories.RenderLink`._

### Icons and conditional content

Use `icon={<CircleCheck aria-hidden="true" />}` for a leading icon, or place icons explicitly among the children. Explicit leading and trailing icons use `data-icon="inline-start"` and `data-icon="inline-end"` to select the corresponding padding. An icon element supplied through the shorthand receives the leading marker. Keep the label meaningful whether an optional icon is present or absent.

_Example: story `Stories.ConditionalIcons`._

## Content

- Use one or two words that remain useful without color: Verified, In review, Overdue.
- Use the state rather than the tone name: Overdue, not Danger.
- Keep categories neutral; their words distinguish them.
- Use one vocabulary for each state throughout the product.
- Keep bold emphasis for the status that needs the most attention.
- Give rendered links labels that make their destinations understandable.

_Example: story `Stories.Categories`._

_Example: story `Stories.OneBold`._

_Example: story `Stories.Dont`._

_Example: story `Stories.StatusGuidance`._

## Accessibility

- A plain Badge is inline text. A click handler does not make it a keyboard control.
- A link requires an actual anchor with a destination through `render`; `variant="link"` supplies presentation only.
- Native attributes and refs reach the actual element. Custom router adapters must forward them.
- Pair semantic colors with visible words and hide decorative icons from assistive technology.
- Use native controls for selection or dismissal. Badge does not implement those behaviors.

_Example: story `Stories.NativeAttributes`._

## Props

`BadgeProps` combines native span props and Base UI's `render` composition with the shared recipe's variant, tone, appearance, and size axes, plus the optional icon. `React.ComponentProps<typeof Badge>` derives the same component props. The ref receives the actual rendered element; anchor-specific props such as `href` belong on the anchor supplied through `render`.

_Props: generated from `Badge`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._

### Playground

_Example: story `Stories.Playground`._

_Rendered in the Storybook: Controls._

## Migration

| Previous use                                        | Updated use                                                                                            |
| --------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `<Badge tone="success">Verified</Badge>`            | `<Badge variant="secondary" tone="success">Verified</Badge>` preserves subtle status emphasis.         |
| Neutral `<Badge>Draft</Badge>`                      | `<Badge variant="secondary" tone="neutral">Draft</Badge>`. The unconfigured default is now brand/bold. |
| `appearance="bold"`, `size="xsmall"`, or `icon={…}` | Keep these conveniences on Badge. Use `secondary` for existing status compositions.                    |
| A clickable span                                    | Supply a real anchor through `render` for navigation.                                                  |
| `BadgeProps`                                        | Continue using the same export; it now also includes variants and Base UI render composition.          |

All Badge uses now share the shadcn-derived pill shape, including semantic tones. Existing semantic palettes and compact heights remain, while small labels adopt the shared padding and border anatomy. `Count`, `Dot`, `Indicator`, `Tone`, `tones`, and `toneClasses` keep their existing contracts. `Avatar.Badge` and `AvatarGroupCount` remain separate Avatar parts with their existing APIs. The checked-in shadcn reference and the unrelated reui Badge remain separate code.

## Related

- [Count](?path=/docs/components-count--docs): numeric counts.
- [Indicator](?path=/docs/components-indicator--docs): a status dot and a word.
- [FilterChip](?path=/docs/components-filterchip--docs): a filter the reader can change.
- Reference: [shadcn Base UI Badge](https://ui.shadcn.com/docs/components/base/badge). The checked-in application reference is the foundation for this adaptation.

<!-- page: Components/Banner (src/stories/components/Banner.mdx) -->

# Banner

A message about the whole site, at the top of the screen in the shell's Banner area: the loss of data or a function, or something site-wide that changes what the reader can do. One at a time, never dismissible, gone when no longer true. It is one line and truncates rather than wraps; the action is one link or button drawn in the banner's own colour. The kit's inline message is the [Alert](?path=/docs/components-alert--docs).

An Alert is about the record; a Banner is about the site. Feedback after an act is a toast. If the message would be true for one reader and not the next, it is not a banner.

_Example: story `Stories.BannerMatrix`._

## Anatomy

| Part    | What it is                                                                                                  |
| ------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Bar     | 48px, `dimension.layout.banner`, the tone's bold fill, its content centred, `space.200` inside at each end. |
| Icon    | The tone's icon at `dimension.icon.small`: Info, TriangleAlert, CircleAlert. `icon` replaces it.            |
| Message | One line in `font.body` medium and the inverse text colour. It truncates.                                   |
| Action  | One link or button after the message, underlined, in the banner's own text colour.                          |

## Variants

Banner has one appearance; the tone is what varies, and there are three.

| Tone          | Use                                                                                                      |
| ------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `information` | Something changed for everyone: the catalogue moved to a new revision, a maintenance window is booked.   |
| `warning`     | The default. Something is about to change what the reader can do: the audit window closes, uploads lock. |
| `danger`      | Something is lost: the connection to the evidence store, the session's writes. Announced at once.        |

There is no success banner and no neutral one: a banner is gone when it is no longer true, and good news is feedback, which is a toast. The kit has the bold fill only, no low-contrast form, since a banner is by definition the one thing on the screen that outranks the page.

Where it lives: `Shell.Banner` is the area, above the top navigation. It holds the Banner and pushes the page down by the banner's height while one is rendered; see [Shell](?path=/docs/layout-shell--docs).

## Sizes

One: the width of the screen at 48px. On a narrow screen the message truncates and the action stays; the message should be short enough that a phone shows most of it.

## States

Present or absent. A banner is rendered while its condition holds and unmounted when it stops; there is no dismissed state, no hover, and no collapsed form. Its action has the kit's focus outline.

## Modifiers

- **`tone`** as in Variants; `warning` when unsaid.
- **`action`** for the one link or button: an anchor, a button, or the router's Link. The Banner colours it and underlines it; it keeps its own `onClick` or `to`.
- **`icon`** to replace the tone's icon with a more specific one, rarely.
- **`className`** for the shell's layout, not for colour.

_Example: story `Stories.Banners`._

## Content

- **One sentence: the fact and what it changes.** "The audit window closes in three days; evidence uploads lock after that."
- **Present tense, plain.** No "Please note", no "Attention".
- **The action names where it goes:** "See what changed", "Ask for an extension". One.
- **Not feedback, not a greeting, not a record.** Those are a toast, nothing, and an Alert.

## Style

| Element | Token                                                                                                  |
| ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Bar     | `dimension.layout.banner` 48px · `color.background.<tone>.bold` · `space.200` inline · `space.100` gap |
| Text    | `font.body` medium · `color.text.inverse`, `color.text.warning.inverse` on warning                     |
| Icon    | `dimension.icon.small` 14px in the text colour                                                         |
| Action  | Underlined, `radius.xsmall` for its focus outline                                                      |

The bold fills are Badge's bold appearance, so a danger banner and a danger bold Badge are the same red.

## Accessibility

- **A danger Banner is `role="alert"`**, announced at once; the rest are `role="status"`. The shell's Banner area is a region named "Banner".
- **Truncation hides words from sighted readers only;** a screen reader hears the whole line. Keep it short so both get the same message.
- **The action is in the tab order; the banner is not.** It sits first in the page, before the top navigation, so it is the first thing a keyboard reader meets, which is the point.
- **The bold fills pass 4.5:1** with the inverse text in both modes; the contrast test covers them.

## Props

Native `div` props and refs target the outer message. IDs, ARIA, data attributes, styles and handlers are forwarded; `className` merges with the default layout. The default role remains `status`, or `alert` for danger. An explicit `role` or live-region attribute controls delivery when the enclosing page needs different announcement behavior.

The `action` keeps its own element, ref, ID, attributes, styles and handlers while receiving the banner’s action classes. A root click handler receives the action’s bubbled click. Default icons are decorative.

_Props: generated from `Banner`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._

### Playground

_Example: story `Stories.Playground`._

_Rendered in the Storybook: Controls._

## Related

- [Alert](?path=/docs/components-alert--docs): the message about a record.
- [Toaster](?path=/docs/components-toaster--docs): feedback after an act.
- [Shell](?path=/docs/layout-shell--docs): the Banner area.
- [Badge](?path=/docs/components-badge--docs): the tone table.

## Don't

_Example: story `Stories.Dont`._

<!-- page: Components/Breadcrumb (src/stories/components/Breadcrumb.mdx) -->

# Breadcrumb

Show where the reader is in the record tree and provide links to its parent levels. Breadcrumb follows the shadcn Base UI component structure, with Ledger's typography, color, spacing, icon, focus, and motion tokens.

Compose the list, items, links, separators, and current page explicitly. The list wraps when space is limited. The component does not generate separators, infer the current page, truncate labels, or manage overflow for you.

_Example: story `Stories.BreadcrumbMatrix`._

## Anatomy

All seven parts are named exports from `@ledger/design-system`.

| Part                  | Default element and responsibility                                                       |
| --------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Breadcrumb`          | A `nav` with `aria-label="breadcrumb"`. Contains the list.                               |
| `BreadcrumbList`      | An `ol` that wraps its children and labels.                                              |
| `BreadcrumbItem`      | An inline-flex `li` for one level. Contains a link, page, or composed control.           |
| `BreadcrumbLink`      | An `a`, or the element supplied through Base UI's `render` prop.                         |
| `BreadcrumbPage`      | A `span` with `role="link"`, `aria-disabled="true"`, and `aria-current="page"`.          |
| `BreadcrumbSeparator` | A decorative `li` between items. A chevron by default; accepts custom children.          |
| `BreadcrumbEllipsis`  | A decorative `span` containing a horizontal ellipsis. Provides no interaction by itself. |

```tsx

<Breadcrumb aria-label="Program hierarchy">
  <BreadcrumbList>
    <BreadcrumbItem>
      <BreadcrumbLink href="/programs">Programs</BreadcrumbLink>
    </BreadcrumbItem>
    <BreadcrumbSeparator />
    <BreadcrumbItem>
      <BreadcrumbLink href="/programs/atlas">Atlas payments platform</BreadcrumbLink>
    </BreadcrumbItem>
    <BreadcrumbSeparator />
    <BreadcrumbItem>
      <BreadcrumbPage>Controls</BreadcrumbPage>
    </BreadcrumbItem>
  </BreadcrumbList>
</Breadcrumb>;
```

_Example: story `Stories.Basic`._

## Variants

The component has one appearance. Its parts support different compositions without adding variant props.

| Composition       | How to build it                                                                                                                      |
| ----------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Standard trail    | Place `BreadcrumbLink` in each parent item and `BreadcrumbPage` in the final item.                                                   |
| Custom separator  | Pass text or an icon to `BreadcrumbSeparator`, such as `<BreadcrumbSeparator>/</BreadcrumbSeparator>`.                               |
| Collapsed parents | Put `BreadcrumbEllipsis` inside a named button or menu trigger. The application owns which levels are hidden and how to reveal them. |
| Local hierarchy   | Render an actual button through `BreadcrumbLink` for a level that changes state in place.                                            |
| Single page       | One `BreadcrumbItem` containing `BreadcrumbPage`, without separators.                                                                |

_Example: story `Stories.CustomSeparator`._

### Collapsed parents

Ellipsis is hidden from assistive technology, including its internal "More" text. Give the enclosing control its own accessible name and implement its behavior. This example uses a disclosure button with `aria-expanded`, reveals the parents inline, and retains keyboard focus on the button.

```tsx

<BreadcrumbItem>
  <button
    type="button"
    aria-label={expanded ? "Hide parent levels" : "Show parent levels"}
    aria-expanded={expanded}
    onClick={() => setExpanded((value) => !value)}
  >
    <BreadcrumbEllipsis />
  </button>
</BreadcrumbItem>;
```

_Example: story `Stories.Collapsed`._

## Sizes

One default size: `font.body.small`. The ordered list uses wrapping flex layout, and long labels can wrap within an item. There is no automatic single-line truncation or maximum number of levels.

A constrained header must allow room for additional lines. If a product requires a compact trail, compose a disclosure or overflow menu and keep the hidden levels accessible.

_Example: story `Stories.LongWrappingTrail`._

_Example: story `Stories.AboveTitle`._

## States

| State             | Behavior                                                                                             |
| ----------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Parent link       | Subtle text, default text color on hover; native Tab and Enter behavior.                             |
| Keyboard focus    | Ledger's focus outline on the rendered link or button.                                               |
| Current page      | Regular-weight default text. Announced as the current, disabled link; no `href` or default tab stop. |
| Collapsed parents | Application-owned state on the enclosing control. Ellipsis remains decorative.                       |

`BreadcrumbPage` preserves shadcn's accessible semantics: it is a noninteractive span exposed as a disabled current link. Its role does not make it an anchor or add keyboard behavior.

## Modifiers

- **`aria-label`** on `Breadcrumb` names the navigation landmark. The default is lowercase `breadcrumb`.
- **`render`** on `BreadcrumbLink` composes a router link or another suitable element through Base UI's `useRender` and `mergeProps`.
- **`children`** on `BreadcrumbSeparator` replaces the default chevron.
- **Native props and `ref`** reach each part's rendered DOM element. Use `className` and `style` on the relevant part for a deliberate layout adjustment.

### Router link composition

The custom component must forward its received props and ref to its actual anchor. This allows Base UI to compose event handlers, classes, attributes, and both refs on the same element.

```tsx

type RouterLinkProps = Omit<ComponentProps<"a">, "href"> & { to: string };

const RouterLink = forwardRef<HTMLAnchorElement, RouterLinkProps>(function RouterLink(
  { to, ...props },
  ref,
) {
  return <a ref={ref} href={to} {...props} />;
});

<BreadcrumbItem>
  <BreadcrumbLink render={<RouterLink to="/programs" />}>Programs</BreadcrumbLink>
</BreadcrumbItem>;
```

The example below verifies that props and both refs reach the anchor, and that mouse and keyboard activation each invoke the adapter and breadcrumb handlers. Its adapter prevents navigation to keep the demonstration in the canvas.

_Example: story `Stories.RenderLink`._

### In-place state

Use an anchor for page navigation. For a hierarchy that updates local state, supply a native button explicitly:

```tsx
<BreadcrumbItem>
  <BreadcrumbLink render={<button type="button" onClick={() => selectLevel("programs")} />}>
    Programs
  </BreadcrumbLink>
</BreadcrumbItem>
```

The rendered control remains a button, including its Enter and Space behavior. This is a local record hierarchy; use [Stepper](?path=/docs/components-stepper--docs) for sequential tasks.

_Example: story `Stories.InPlaceButtons`._

### Migration from the previous Ledger API

This is a breaking API change. Update complete breadcrumb compositions, including their surrounding layout.

| Previous API or behavior                            | New composition                                                                                             |
| --------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Breadcrumb.Item`                                   | Import `BreadcrumbItem` as a named export.                                                                  |
| Root automatically supplied `ol`                    | Place `BreadcrumbList` inside `Breadcrumb`.                                                                 |
| Item automatically supplied its leading chevron     | Place `BreadcrumbSeparator` between items.                                                                  |
| `<Breadcrumb.Item isCurrent>Page</Breadcrumb.Item>` | `<BreadcrumbItem><BreadcrumbPage>Page</BreadcrumbPage></BreadcrumbItem>`                                    |
| `Breadcrumb.Item asChild` around an anchor          | Put `BreadcrumbLink href="…"` inside `BreadcrumbItem`.                                                      |
| `Breadcrumb.Item asChild` around a router link      | Put `BreadcrumbLink render={<RouterLink to="…" />}` inside `BreadcrumbItem`.                                |
| Item `onClick` implicitly created a button          | Explicitly render a button through `BreadcrumbLink`, or compose a suitable control inside `BreadcrumbItem`. |
| Root `label="Program hierarchy"`                    | Root `aria-label="Program hierarchy"`.                                                                      |
| Item `className` styled its link or page            | Apply that class to `BreadcrumbLink` or `BreadcrumbPage`; item props now target the `li`.                   |
| Current page used medium weight                     | `BreadcrumbPage` uses regular weight, following shadcn's structure and styling intent.                      |
| Every crumb truncated to keep one line              | The list and long labels wrap. Review narrow headers and use an explicit overflow composition where needed. |

`BreadcrumbProps` and `BreadcrumbItemProps` remain exported as aliases for their native `nav` and `li` props. They no longer contain the old custom props. For any part, `React.ComponentProps<typeof BreadcrumbLink>` (or the corresponding component) derives its public props.

## Content

- Use the level's actual name: "Programs", "Atlas payments platform", "Controls".
- Order the trail from the highest relevant parent to the current page.
- Include the record's identifier when it is needed to distinguish that record.
- Keep tabs and browsing history out of the hierarchy.
- Retain readable names at narrow widths; reveal omitted parents through a labeled, working control.

## Style

| Element                     | Ledger tokens and classes                                                             |
| --------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| List typography             | `font.body.small` / `font-body-small`                                                 |
| Parent links and separators | `color.text.subtle` / `text-subtle`; links use `color.text` / `text-default` on hover |
| Current page                | `color.text` / `text-default`, `font-regular`                                         |
| List gap                    | `space.075` / `gap-075`                                                               |
| Item gap                    | `space.050` / `gap-050`                                                               |
| Chevron                     | `dimension.icon.small` / `size-icon-small`                                            |
| Ellipsis                    | `size-250` container with a `dimension.icon.medium` / `size-icon-medium` icon         |
| Focus                       | `radius.xsmall` / `rounded-xsmall`, `focus-visible:outline-focused`                   |
| Link transition             | `duration-fast`, `ease-standard`                                                      |

These defaults use the same semantic tokens in light and dark modes. Customize presentation through Ledger tokens while retaining the component anatomy and prop contract.

## Accessibility

- `Breadcrumb` creates a named navigation landmark containing an ordered list supplied by `BreadcrumbList`.
- Use distinct `aria-label` values for distinct breadcrumb landmarks on one page. The matrix does this without disabling the landmark uniqueness check.
- Parent anchors are reached by Tab and activated by Enter. Keep their real destinations so users can open them in another tab.
- `BreadcrumbPage` identifies the current page through `aria-current="page"`, with `role="link"` and `aria-disabled="true"`. It has no default tab stop.
- Separators and ellipsis have `role="presentation"` and `aria-hidden="true"`. Do not put interactive content inside a separator.
- Ellipsis alone is not an accessible control. Its button or menu trigger needs a name, keyboard behavior, and appropriate state attributes.
- Custom render components must forward props and refs to preserve native attributes and keyboard behavior.

## Props

Each part accepts its native element's props, including DOM attributes, event handlers, `className`, `style`, and `ref`. `BreadcrumbLink` additionally accepts Base UI's `render` prop.

| Export                | Native props                    | Ref target                                                  |
| --------------------- | ------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Breadcrumb`          | `React.ComponentProps<"nav">`   | `HTMLElement` (`nav`)                                       |
| `BreadcrumbList`      | `React.ComponentProps<"ol">`    | `HTMLOListElement`                                          |
| `BreadcrumbItem`      | `React.ComponentProps<"li">`    | `HTMLLIElement`                                             |
| `BreadcrumbLink`      | `useRender.ComponentProps<"a">` | Anchor by default; the composed element when using `render` |
| `BreadcrumbPage`      | `React.ComponentProps<"span">`  | `HTMLSpanElement`                                           |
| `BreadcrumbSeparator` | `React.ComponentProps<"li">`    | `HTMLLIElement`                                             |
| `BreadcrumbEllipsis`  | `React.ComponentProps<"span">`  | `HTMLSpanElement`                                           |

_Props: generated from `Breadcrumb`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._

### BreadcrumbList

_Props: generated from `BreadcrumbList`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._

### BreadcrumbItem

_Props: generated from `BreadcrumbItem`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._

### BreadcrumbLink

_Props: generated from `BreadcrumbLink`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._

### BreadcrumbPage

_Props: generated from `BreadcrumbPage`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._

### BreadcrumbSeparator

_Props: generated from `BreadcrumbSeparator`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._

### BreadcrumbEllipsis

_Props: generated from `BreadcrumbEllipsis`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._
