<!-- page: Components/Button (src/stories/components/Button.mdx) -->

# Button

Button starts an action. Use a short label that names what happens, such as “Save changes” or “Export report.” For navigation, style a real anchor or router Link with `buttonVariants`; for a text link, use [TextLink](?path=/docs/components-textlink--docs).

_Example: story `Stories.Matrix`._

Leading and trailing icons use a smaller inset on their own side; icon-only controls stay centered. Open popup triggers retain their pressed surface through `aria-expanded` while the popup is open. Toggle selection continues to use `aria-pressed`.

## Variants and sizes

| Variant | Use |
| --- | --- |
| `secondary` | Default raised action: Export, Edit, Open. |
| `primary` | The main action in a header, form or dialog. |
| `subtle` | Low emphasis actions in toolbars, rows and footers. |
| `danger` | Destructive actions, with confirmation when appropriate. |
| `link` | A text styled action, such as Show more. |

| Size | Height | Typical placement |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `medium` | 32px | Default for forms, headers and footers. |
| `small` | 28px | Toolbars and rows. |
| `xsmall` | 24px | Dense inline actions. |

The `link` variant has no fixed height. `iconBefore` and `iconAfter` take an icon element; Button sizes it to 14px and keeps a 6px gap. `isSelected` applies the selected palette and `aria-pressed`.

_Example: story `Stories.Emphasis`._

## Loading and forms

Button defaults to `type="button"`. Set `type="submit"` for a form's submit action. Native form attributes, event handlers and refs reach the button element. `isFullWidth` fills its container.

`isLoading` replaces the leading icon with a decorative spinner and retains the label. It sets `aria-busy`, blocks activation and preserves focus while work is pending. An explicitly `disabled` button remains disabled and leaves the normal tab order. Base UI's `focusableWhenDisabled` is available when a disabled action needs to remain focusable.

_Example: story `Stories.Loading`._

## Composition

`render` accepts an element or a render function for an action control. Render elements merge native props, handlers, refs, classes and styles. Render functions receive the props and state and must apply those props to their result. Custom components must forward them to their DOM element. Button's root ref describes a native button; put a ref for another target on the render element itself.

Use `nativeButton={false}` when the rendered action is not a native button; it receives button semantics and Enter/Space activation. `className` and `style` also accept callbacks with Base UI's `{ disabled }` state, including while loading.

Navigation uses a real anchor or the application's router Link, with the same styling recipe. [Base UI Button enforces button semantics](https://base-ui.com/react/components/button#rendering-links-as-buttons), so styling the link directly preserves its navigation behavior:

```tsx
<a href="/requirements" className={buttonVariants({ variant: "primary" })}>
  View requirements
</a>
```

`buttonVariants` accepts `variant`, `size`, `isSelected`, `isFullWidth` and `className`. It supplies classes without adding ARIA or disabled behavior. Existing `Button asChild` and `IconButton asChild` usages must move to a styled link for navigation, or to `render` for an action control.

_Example: story `Stories.AsLink`._

## Accessibility

- Tab reaches an enabled button. Enter and Space activate it; the focus outline appears on keyboard focus.
- Disabled buttons are skipped by Tab by default. Explain unavailable actions nearby; for form validation, keep the submit action available so the form can report errors.
- Loading blocks click, Enter and Space activation, including handlers on the rendered action. It keeps the accessible name stable.
- Use [IconButton](?path=/docs/components-iconbutton--docs) for an icon only action with a required accessible label, and [Toggle](?path=/docs/components-toggle--docs) for an on/off control.

## Props

_Props: generated from `Button`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._

_Example: story `Stories.Playground`._

_Rendered in the Storybook: Controls._

## Related

[IconButton](?path=/docs/components-iconbutton--docs) · [ButtonGroup](?path=/docs/components-buttongroup--docs) · [TextLink](?path=/docs/components-textlink--docs) · [DropdownMenu](?path=/docs/components-dropdownmenu--docs) · [AlertDialog](?path=/docs/components-alertdialog--docs) · [Forms](?path=/docs/patterns-forms--docs)

<!-- page: Components/ButtonGroup (src/stories/components/ButtonGroup.mdx) -->

# ButtonGroup

Join related actions, split buttons or controls. Each child keeps its own behavior and accessible name.

## Anatomy

```tsx
<ButtonGroup aria-label="Export">
  <Button>Export</Button>
  <ButtonGroupSeparator isDecorative />
  <Button>Print</Button>
</ButtonGroup>
```

ButtonGroup joins the outer corners of children with `data-slot` attributes. ButtonGroupText adds a label, value or prefix. ButtonGroupSeparator adds a visible rule. Nested groups may separate related sets of actions.

_Example: story `Stories.Composition`._

## Variants and states

`orientation` accepts `horizontal` (default) or `vertical`. Horizontal joins use logical edges in RTL. Child controls choose their size, disabled state and loading behavior. The separator's orientation describes its own line; use a horizontal separator between vertically stacked controls.

_Example: story `Stories.Orientations`._

## Accessibility

Name the group with `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`. Each enabled control remains in the normal tab order. A group does not add arrow-key navigation or selection behavior. Use ToggleGroup for a selection among options. Decorative separators may use `isDecorative`.

ButtonGroupText supports Base UI `render`, including a native label with `htmlFor`. Rendered elements must accept merged attributes, events and refs.

## Props

_Props: generated from `ButtonGroup`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._
_Props: generated from `ButtonGroupText`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._
_Props: generated from `ButtonGroupSeparator`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._

The root forwards native div attributes and refs. Text uses Base UI useRender/mergeProps; Separator uses the existing Base UI Separator. `buttonGroupVariants` exports the same orientation classes for composition.

### Migration

Rename `label` to `aria-label`. Compose text and separators with the flat exports. The root is now a div and accepts native props, refs and orientation.

## Related

[Button](?path=/docs/components-button--docs), [DropdownMenu](?path=/docs/components-dropdownmenu--docs), [ToggleGroup](?path=/docs/components-togglegroup--docs), [InputGroup](?path=/docs/components-inputgroup--docs).

Sources: [shadcn ButtonGroup](https://ui.shadcn.com/docs/components/base/button-group), [implementation](https://github.com/shadcn-ui/ui/blob/main/apps/v4/registry/bases/base/ui/button-group.tsx).

<!-- page: Components/Calendar (src/stories/components/Calendar.mdx) -->

# Calendar

A day or range picker following [shadcn’s Calendar](https://ui.shadcn.com/docs/components/base/calendar), built on React DayPicker. Ledger provides token styling and provider-localized date labels.

## Anatomy

```tsx
const [date, setDate] = useState<Date>();
<Calendar mode="single" selected={date} onSelect={setDate} />;
```

Calendar exposes DayPicker’s native props. Navigation uses the shared Button recipe; `CalendarDayButton` uses Button while preserving DayPicker’s focus, selection and event contracts. Days remain 32px cells.

_Example: story `Stories.Single`._

## Variants and states

Use native single, multiple or range selection, disabled matchers and month bounds. `numberOfMonths` supports a range across months, stacking on narrow screens. `captionLayout="dropdown"` and `showWeekNumber` use the same token styling.

_Example: story `Stories.CalendarRange`._
_Example: story `Stories.DropdownsAndWeekNumbers`._

Custom `components`, `formatters`, `labels` and `classNames` merge with Calendar’s defaults. Use the exported CalendarDayButton when customizing a day. `buttonVariant` controls the navigation buttons; selected days keep their selection treatment.

## Accessibility

DayPicker owns keyboard movement and disabled-day behavior. The day button forwards native attributes and moves focus when DayPicker marks it focused. Give standalone pickers a visible context or accessible name. Ledger supplies localized month/day labels; explicit locale, labels and formatters remain caller overrides. Timestamp timezone settings do not shift date-only labels. Native `timeZone` remains available for callers that supply timezone-aware Date values.

## Props

Existing DayPicker callers keep their selection contract. CalendarDayButton is a new flat export. Custom component overrides now preserve unrelated defaults, and dropdown chevrons point down rather than inheriting the next-month icon.

_Props: generated from `Calendar`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._
_Props: generated from `CalendarDayButton`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._

## Related

[DatePicker](?path=/docs/components-datepicker--docs), [Popover](?path=/docs/components-popover--docs), [Dialog](?path=/docs/components-dialog--docs).

<!-- page: Components/Card (src/stories/components/Card.mdx) -->

# Card

A raised container for a table, chart, form or set of facts. Compose its header, content and footer as needed.

## Anatomy

```tsx
<Card>
  <CardHeader>
    <CardTitle>
      <h2>Evidence</h2>
    </CardTitle>
    <CardDescription>Three linked artifacts</CardDescription>
    <CardAction>
      <Button size="small">Add evidence</Button>
    </CardAction>
  </CardHeader>
  <CardContent>Assessment details</CardContent>
  <CardFooter className="border-t">
    <Button>Save</Button>
  </CardFooter>
</Card>
```

CardHeader arranges the title, description and optional action. CardContent supplies the horizontal inset. CardFooter holds actions or secondary content. The root supplies vertical padding and spacing between parts, and records its raised surface so sticky table headers remain opaque.

Headers and footers are undivided by default. Add `className="border-b"` to CardHeader or `className="border-t"` to CardFooter when a rule separates distinct work areas; the part adds padding beside that rule. Form titles usually need spacing only, while a footer with submission actions can earn a divider.

_Example: story `Stories.Playground`._

## Variants and states

The default size uses Ledger's standard inset; `size="sm"` reduces the inset and gaps. Tables and charts that own their spacing can sit directly inside Card. For a table flush against a divided header and the bottom edge, use `className="gap-0 pb-0"` on Card and `className="border-b"` on CardHeader. Loading, empty and error behavior belongs to the content.

_Example: story `Stories.Sizes`._
_Example: story `Stories.EdgeToEdge`._

## Accessibility

All parts are native divs. CardTitle does not choose a heading level: compose an h2 or h3 when the card should appear in the document outline. Existing callers retain their h2 headings. Name a region with `role="region"` and `aria-labelledby` when a landmark is useful. Links and buttons inside the card keep their own semantics and focus.

## Props

_Props: generated from `Card`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._
_Props: generated from `CardHeader`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._
_Props: generated from `CardTitle`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._
_Props: generated from `CardDescription`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._
_Props: generated from `CardAction`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._
_Props: generated from `CardContent`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._
_Props: generated from `CardFooter`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._

Every part accepts native div props and refs. Root `style` overrides merge with the raised-surface default.

### Migration

Replace `Card.Header title/description/action` with CardHeader containing CardTitle, CardDescription and CardAction. Replace `Card.Body` with CardContent. Add a heading inside CardTitle to preserve the original outline. Card now lives in the components layer; application imports still come from the package root.

## Related

[Section](?path=/docs/layout-section--docs), [Table](?path=/docs/components-table--docs), [Empty](?path=/docs/components-empty--docs), [Related](?path=/docs/patterns-related--docs).

Sources: [shadcn Card](https://ui.shadcn.com/docs/components/base/card), [Base UI catalog implementation](https://github.com/shadcn-ui/ui/blob/main/apps/v4/registry/bases/base/ui/card.tsx).

<!-- page: Components/Checkbox (src/stories/components/Checkbox.mdx) -->

# Checkbox

An independent boolean choice, using the shadcn Base UI root and indicator. The 16px control supplies the check or mixed-state dash; labels and descriptions are composed outside it.

```tsx
<label className="inline-flex items-center gap-100">
  <Checkbox name="pii" value="yes" defaultChecked />
  Handles PII
</label>
```

Use [RadioGroup](?path=/docs/components-radiogroup--docs) for one selected answer from visible choices, or [Switch](?path=/docs/components-switch--docs) for an on/off setting. The caller decides when to save a change.

_Example: story `Stories.CheckboxMatrix`._

## Selection and mixed state

Use boolean `checked` with `onCheckedChange(checked, details)`, or `defaultChecked` for local state. `details.cancel()` rejects a change. `disabled` prevents interaction and removes the control from the tab order; `readOnly` keeps it focusable without allowing changes.

Mixed state uses a separate boolean `indeterminate` prop. A select-all control can derive `checked={allSelected}` and `indeterminate={someSelected && !allSelected}`, then update every child in `onCheckedChange`. [Table.Selection](?path=/docs/components-table--docs) uses the same two booleans.

The existing Base UI `CheckboxGroup` can also own the selected values and derive a `parent` checkbox's mixed state. Import that grouping primitive from `@base-ui/react/checkbox-group` when using this composition:

_Example: story `Stories.Parent`._

## Labels, Field and forms

A wrapping label names the checkbox and toggles it when clicked. A sibling label uses `htmlFor` with the checkbox's `id`. Use `aria-label` for a control with no visible label. Put supporting text in an element referenced by `aria-describedby`.

Compose [Field](?path=/docs/components-field--docs) with FieldLabel and FieldDescription/FieldError. Associate the checkbox through `htmlFor`/`id` and `aria-describedby`; pass `aria-invalid` and `aria-required` explicitly. For several checkboxes, use FieldSet/FieldLegend and give each choice its own label. Requiring the group does not require every checkbox. Native `required` enables browser validation.

`name`, `value` and `form` control native submission. A checked checkbox submits its value (or `on` when omitted); an unchecked checkbox is omitted unless `uncheckedValue` is supplied. Native form reset is caller-owned in Base UI 1.7: restore controlled `checked` state in `onReset`.

_Example: story `Stories.InField`._

## Native props and keyboard

The default root is a span with `role="checkbox"`, plus a hidden input. `ref` targets the visible control; `inputRef` and `id` target the input. For a native button root, use `nativeButton` with `render={<button />}`; `id` then belongs to that button. The render element's props, classes, styles, handlers and refs are merged. `className` and `style` accept Base UI state callbacks.

Each enabled checkbox is a Tab stop. Space toggles it. Enter does not toggle it; inside a form it activates the default submitter. Mixed state is announced as `aria-checked="mixed"` and drawn with a dash.

## Migration

Move label children into an external label and replace `description` with supporting content linked by `aria-describedby` or FieldDescription. Replace `checked="indeterminate"` with `checked={false} indeterminate`; callbacks now receive a boolean and cancellable event details. Use `render` for composition. The root follows Base UI's default span and input structure.

## Props

_Props: generated from `Checkbox`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._

_Example: story `Stories.Playground`._

_Rendered in the Storybook: Controls._

## Related

[Field](?path=/docs/components-field--docs) · [Forms](?path=/docs/patterns-forms--docs) · [Table](?path=/docs/components-table--docs) · [shadcn Checkbox](https://ui.shadcn.com/docs/components/base/checkbox) · [Base UI Checkbox](https://base-ui.com/react/components/checkbox)

<!-- page: Components/CodeBlock (src/stories/components/CodeBlock.mdx) -->

# CodeBlock

Source shown as source: a configuration excerpt, a serialised record, a log, a command the reader will paste. One row per line in the code face, a line-number gutter that stays put when the block scrolls sideways, a cap on the height so a long document scrolls inside the block and not the page, and a Copy when the reader will take the text away. The caller owns highlighting and passes rendered lines.

It is not a field: a value the reader edits is a [Textarea](?path=/docs/components-textarea--docs). It is not prose: a paragraph is [Text](?path=/docs/primitives-text--docs). A single identifier in a sentence is an [Id](?path=/docs/components-id--docs).

_Example: story `Stories.Code`._

## Anatomy

| Part   | What it is                                                                                                                                                                 |
| ------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Frame  | A box in `elevation.surface.sunken` with a 1px `color.border` and `radius.medium`. It scrolls both ways inside itself; it is a tab stop so the keyboard can scroll it.        |
| Gutter | The line numbers, `color.text.subtlest`, tabular, right-aligned, on a column that sticks to the start edge when the lines scroll sideways, with a 1px rule at its end.        |
| Line   | One row per entry of `lines`, `space.150` from the gutter, in `font.code`. A string, or the caller's spans.                                                                  |
| Copy   | With `copy`, a subtle IconButton at the top end that puts the text on the clipboard and says Copied for a moment.                                                            |

## Variants

One. What changes is what the lines are: a string per line, or nodes the caller has coloured, because a kit tokenizer for every format the product meets is not the kit's job. The export page splits its JSON and colours the keys; a log is strings.

_Example: story `Stories.Highlighted`._

Not built, and why: a highlighted line (the one a validation error points at, the changed lines of a revision), because no screen asks for it yet; a diff, which is two documents and a decision; a language picker or a tokenizer.

## Sizes

One face, `font.code`, at the body size. The block is as wide as its container and as tall as its lines up to `maxHeight`, 560px by default; a short excerpt never scrolls. The gutter is as wide as the last line number needs, three digits at least.

## States

| State     | Look                                                                                                         |
| --------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Rest      | The lines, the gutter, the frame.                                                                            |
| Focus     | The kit's focus outline on the frame, on keyboard focus, so a keyboard reader can scroll it.                 |
| Scrolled  | Sideways, the gutter stays and the lines pass under it. Down, the gutter goes with the lines.                |
| Copied    | The Copy's icon is a check in `color.icon.success` and its label reads Copied, for a moment.                 |

_Example: story `Stories.CodeBlockMatrix`._

## Modifiers

- **`start`**: the number of the first line, for an excerpt of a longer file.
- **`maxHeight`**: pixels before the block scrolls inside itself.
- **`wrap`**: long lines fold at the block's edge. Off by default so code keeps its columns; on for a log or a value with no columns to keep.
- **`copy`**: the text a Copy puts on the clipboard, usually the lines joined. Unsaid, there is no button.
- **`label`**: the block's accessible name, the file or the format. "Code" by default; say which.

_Example: story `Stories.Wrapped`._

_Example: story `Stories.Capped`._

## Content

- **Lines are the source as it is,** indentation included. Do not trim, reflow or re-indent for the page.
- **`label` names the thing:** "control.json", "Ingest log", "Router configuration". Not "Code".
- **`start` is the real line number** when the block is an excerpt, so a reader can find the line in the file.
- **A Copy where the reader will paste:** a command, a configuration, a document. Not on a log they read.
- **Highlighting colours the grammar, in the kit's text colours:** keys in `color.text.brand`, strings subtle, comments subtlest. Never a rainbow.

## Style

| Element | Token                                                                                                   |
| ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Frame   | `elevation.surface.sunken` · 1px `color.border` · `radius.medium` · `space.050` block inside              |
| Gutter  | `font.code` · `color.text.subtlest` · tabular · `space.100` inline · 1px `color.border` at its end        |
| Line    | `font.code` · `color.text` · `space.150` from the gutter                                                  |
| Copy    | IconButton `subtle` `small` at `space.100` from the top and the end · `color.icon.success` when copied    |
| Focus   | The kit's focus outline, `color.border.focused`                                                           |

## Accessibility

- **The frame is a group named by `label`** and a tab stop, so a keyboard reader can reach a block that scrolls and move it with the arrows. A block with a bare "Code" name is a block the screen reader cannot tell from the next one.
- **Line numbers are not selectable,** so a copied selection is the code alone.
- **The Copy is an IconButton:** named, with the kit's tooltip, and a status region says Copied.
- **Contrast:** the gutter's `color.text.subtlest` passes on the sunken surface in both modes; the caller's highlight colours are the kit's text tokens, which do too.
- **The a11y gate** checks the name, the tab stop and the contrast in the matrix.

## Props

_Props: generated from `CodeBlock`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._

### Playground

_Example: story `Stories.Playground`._

_Rendered in the Storybook: Controls._

## Related

- [Textarea](?path=/docs/components-textarea--docs): code the reader edits.
- [Id](?path=/docs/components-id--docs): one identifier in running text.
- [Text](?path=/docs/primitives-text--docs): prose.
- [IconButton](?path=/docs/components-iconbutton--docs): the Copy.
- [ScrollArea](?path=/docs/components-scrollarea--docs): a region that scrolls with the kit's bar; the CodeBlock uses the platform's, so the gutter can stick.

## Don't

_Example: story `Stories.Dont`._

# Collapsible

Based on [shadcn’s Base UI source](https://ui.shadcn.com/docs/components/base/collapsible) and [Base UI](https://base-ui.com/react/components/collapsible). Ledger retains its tokens and application layouts.

## Anatomy

An independent boolean disclosure using Collapsible, CollapsibleTrigger and CollapsibleContent. Use Accordion for a coordinated set. Labels, counts and icons are ordinary trigger children.

## Variants

_Example: story `Stories.RetainedState`._

_Example: story `Stories.IndependentAndDisabled`._

_Example: story `Stories.SearchableContent`._

## Accessibility

Base UI owns expanded state, trigger/panel association, disabled behavior and keyboard activation. Retained closed panels stay hidden and unfocusable. hiddenUntilFound lets supported browser find-in-page reveal closed content. Nested disclosures keep independent state.

## Props

The three parts expose native Base UI props, refs, render, state classes/styles and cancellable onOpenChange. Content uses the measured --collapsible-panel-height for Ledger motion and respects reduced motion.

### Migration and API

- Replace Collapsible.Trigger/Content with the flat exports. Replace asChild with render and forceMount with keepMounted.
- Use data-open/data-closed instead of Radix data-state selectors. Item, Section, Stepper, Inspector and DataTable metrics use the same Base UI disclosure behavior.
- The unused LegacyAccordion/LegacyCollapsible adapters are removed; use the current flat Accordion and Collapsible parts.

<!-- page: Components/Combobox (src/stories/components/Combobox.mdx) -->

# Combobox

Search and select predefined values using shadcn's Base UI Combobox composition. Root owns selection, filtering, popup state and form serialization. ComboboxInput composes the shared InputGroup and its trigger/clear controls.

## Anatomy

```tsx
const frameworks = ["React", "Vue", "Svelte"];

<Field>
  <FieldLabel htmlFor="combobox">Framework</FieldLabel>
  <Combobox items={frameworks}>
    <ComboboxInput id="combobox" placeholder="Choose a framework" showClear />
    <ComboboxContent>
      <ComboboxEmpty>No frameworks found.</ComboboxEmpty>
      <ComboboxList>
        {(item: string) => (
          <ComboboxItem key={item} value={item}>
            {item}
          </ComboboxItem>
        )}
      </ComboboxList>
    </ComboboxContent>
  </Combobox>
</Field>;
```

Root renders no DOM wrapper. Content includes Portal, Positioner and Popup. List renders filtered items inside a [Scroller](?path=/docs/components-scroller--docs), so long results show hover arrows at each overflowed edge. Group, Label, Collection and Separator compose categorized results.

## Variants and states

_Example: story `Stories.Searchable`._
_Example: story `Stories.Groups`._

For multiple selection, use an array value with ComboboxChips, ComboboxValue, ComboboxChip and ComboboxChipsInput. Chips include removal controls unless `showRemove={false}`. Use `useComboboxAnchor()` to anchor the popup to the whole chips container.

_Example: story `Stories.Multiple`._

For remote results, own loading/query state and pass `filter={null}` when the server filters. ComboboxStatus presents loading feedback outside the list of options. Disabled options cannot be selected; read-only selection stays submitted without allowing changes.

_Example: story `Stories.AsyncResults`._

## Accessibility

Connect FieldLabel to ComboboxInput with `htmlFor`/`id`; put description IDs, invalid state and required announcements on the editable input. Root’s `required` enables native constraint validation separately. Typing filters, arrows highlight, Enter selects, and Escape closes the popup before the surrounding dialog. Base UI controls focus and nested popup behavior.

_Example: story `Stories.InDialog`._

## Props

`ComboboxProps<Value, Multiple>` is the generic Base UI root contract, with Ledger locale/direction defaults. Root's `value` is one value/null or an array; `onValueChange(value, details)` supports cancellation. Use `name`, `form`, `inputRef`, serialization and equality callbacks on Root. The installed Base UI version is 1.7; reset controlled selections in the owning form's `onReset`.

ComboboxInput forwards native input refs, events, render composition, classes and styles; Ledger retains small/medium sizing. `showTrigger` defaults true and `showClear` defaults false. Its children follow the control addons. Content forwards popup props plus positioning, `portalContainer` and `keepMounted`; the latter two preserve existing advanced integrations. Clear, ChipRemove and Status are additional flat native parts.

Replace `Combobox options/onChange` and `Combobox.Root` with the single root API. Move placeholder, ref, blur and input ARIA to ComboboxInput. Replace the old separate InputGroup/Trigger composition with ComboboxInput, and use ComboboxChipsInput inside chips. Layout owns widths. NativeSelect has been removed; use Select for choices that do not need search.

_Example: story `Stories.NativeForms`._

## Related

[Select](?path=/docs/components-select--docs) · [InputGroup](?path=/docs/components-inputgroup--docs) · [Field](?path=/docs/components-field--docs) · [Forms](?path=/docs/patterns-forms--docs) · [shadcn Combobox](https://ui.shadcn.com/docs/components/base/combobox) · [Base UI Combobox](https://base-ui.com/react/components/combobox)
