# Command

Based on [shadcn’s Base UI source](https://ui.shadcn.com/docs/components/base/command) and [cmdk](https://cmdk.paco.me). Ledger retains its tokens and application layouts.

## Anatomy

Keyboard-filtered actions using cmdk, as in shadcn’s Base UI implementation. CommandDialog uses the shared Base UI Dialog. Compose Command, CommandInput, CommandList, CommandGroup, CommandItem, CommandEmpty, CommandSeparator and CommandShortcut.

## Variants

_Example: story `Stories.Filtering`._

_Example: story `Stories.Palette`._

_Example: story `Stories.Loading`._

## Accessibility

Give Command a descriptive `label` (cmdk uses it to name the search input), and give CommandDialog a title. cmdk handles filtering, disabled choices, option navigation and selection. Base UI Dialog handles focus, modality and dismissal. CommandSeparator is presentational within the listbox. Put CommandLoading alongside CommandList, with aria-busy on the list while fetching. Item onSelect owns the action and any palette closing. When showCloseButton is false, compose a DialogClose so touch and screen-reader users have a dismissal control; the palette and record picker make their Escape footer hint a close button.

## Props

Command parts forward their native cmdk props and refs. CommandDialog accepts the native generic Dialog root contract plus title, description, className, style, showCloseButton and finalFocus. CommandLoading, CommandFooter and CommandCount retain their existing loading and result-count roles.

### Migration and API

- Replace Command.Input/List/Group/Item/etc. with flat exports. Put trailing content in children, using CommandShortcut for key hints.
- Replace Command.Dialog with CommandDialog. Compose an explicit Command inside it; command filtering/value props belong on Command.
- Replace onClose with onOpenChange and label with title on the dialog. Use style or className for palette width; finalFocus replaces returnFocusRef.
- Command continues to use cmdk; its modal shell no longer imports Radix Dialog directly.

## Related

- [Dialog](?path=/docs/components-dialog--docs)
- [Combobox](?path=/docs/components-combobox--docs)

<!-- page: Components/Count (src/stories/components/Count.mdx) -->

# Count

A number in a pill: unread items, rows in a group, results behind a filter, findings on a control. It sits after the name of what it counts and is named by it. Anything above `max`, 99 by default, renders as `99+`. Not the notification circle on a corner.

_Example: story `Stories.CountMatrix`._

## Anatomy

| Part   | What it is                                                                                             |
| ------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Pill   | 20px tall, at least 20px wide, round, `space.075` at each end: the neutral fill or one of four others. |
| Number | `font.body.small` medium, tabular, centred. Never a word.                                              |

## Variants

| Appearance  | Use                                                                                           |
| ----------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `default`   | Rows in a group, results behind a filter, items in a section. The neutral fill.               |
| `primary`   | The one count on the screen that must be seen: unread, new since you last looked. Brand fill. |
| `important` | What needs attention now: overdue, blocked. Danger fill.                                      |
| `added`     | Rows a change adds. Success fill, subtle.                                                     |
| `removed`   | Rows a change removes. Danger fill, subtle.                                                   |

Not built, and why: a corner placement on an avatar or an icon (a notification circle); the shell's navigation has no unread counts yet, and when it does the Count will sit after the item's label, not on its icon. No count in a tone's text colour without a fill; the number alone is a Stat.

## Sizes

One size, 20px, the height of a small Badge, so the two sit on one line. The width grows with the digits and stops at three and a plus.

## States

A Count has one state. A count of zero is usually not shown: a section with nothing in it says so in words, and the consumers that take a `count` hide it at zero.

_Example: story `Stories.InContext`._

## Modifiers

- **`value`** as a number, or a string when the text is not a number the pill should cap ("12 of 40" is not a Count).
- **`max`** for the ceiling: 99 by default; 999 or 9999 on a tab that counts rows.
- **`appearance`** as in Variants; `default` when unsaid.

## Content

- **A number.** Digits only; the word before it says what they count.
- **Named by its label.** "Findings 3", "Evidence 7": the Count follows the label at `space.100`.
- **Capped, not exact.** Past the ceiling the reader needs the order of magnitude; the exact number is a Stat.

## Style

| Element   | Token                                                                                        |
| --------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Pill      | `dimension.control.xsmall` 20px tall and at least as wide · `radius.full` · `space.075` ends |
| Number    | `font.body.small` medium · tabular                                                           |
| default   | `color.background.neutral` · `color.text.subtle`                                             |
| primary   | `color.background.brand.bold` · `color.text.inverse`                                         |
| important | `color.background.danger.bold` · `color.text.inverse`                                        |
| added     | `color.background.success` · `color.text.success`                                            |
| removed   | `color.background.danger` · `color.text.danger`                                              |

## Accessibility

- **It is text**, read in the flow after its label: "Findings, 3". The label names it; a Count on its own says only a number.
- **`99+` is read as "99 plus"**, which is the meaning.
- **The appearance is not the only signal.** An important count sits beside a label that says why; the red ranks it.
- **Nothing to focus.** A Count inside a Tab or a Collapsible is part of that control's name.

## Props

_Props: generated from `Count`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._

### Playground

_Example: story `Stories.Playground`._

_Rendered in the Storybook: Controls._

## Related

- [Badge](?path=/docs/components-badge--docs): the tone table, and which of Badge, Count, Indicator and Dot to use.
- [Stat](?path=/docs/components-stat--docs): the exact number, big.
- [Tabs](?path=/docs/components-tabs--docs), [Collapsible](?path=/docs/components-collapsible--docs), [Related](?path=/docs/patterns-related--docs): the controls that take a `count`.

## Don't

_Example: story `Stories.Dont`._

<!-- page: Components/DatePicker (src/stories/components/DatePicker.mdx) -->

# DatePicker

A single date stored as an ISO day (`yyyy-MM-dd`). This is Ledger’s form convenience built from [shadcn’s Popover + Calendar pattern](https://ui.shadcn.com/docs/components/base/date-picker); shadcn has no separate DatePicker root primitive.

## Anatomy

```tsx
const id = useId();
<Field>
  <FieldLabel htmlFor={id}>Scheduled completion</FieldLabel>
  <DatePicker id={id} name="due" value={due} onChange={setDue} />
</Field>;
```

The visible control is Button composed through Base UI PopoverTrigger. A hidden input carries the ISO value for native submission. The popup contains Calendar and Today/Clear actions.

_Example: story `Stories.Playground`._

## Variants and states

Use `value`/`onChange` for controlled state or `defaultValue` for uncontrolled state. Selection reports an ISO day; clearing reports an empty string. `size` is small or medium. Disabled pickers cannot open and omit their hidden input from FormData.

A range uses Calendar inside an explicit Popover. Keep application-specific range behavior at that composition.

## Accessibility

Use FieldLabel with a stable ID, or give the button an aria-label. Native refs, onFocus, onBlur, ARIA and data attributes reach the visible trigger. Hint/error IDs belong in aria-describedby. A button cannot carry aria-required; announce required state in the label or hint and validate in the owning form.

Calendar receives initial focus when opened. Selection, Clear and Escape restore focus to the visible trigger. Base UI coordinates the popup within Dialog and Drawer. Native form reset closes the popup and restores an uncontrolled default; controlled callers reset their own value. External owning forms are supported through `form`.

## Props

The existing ISO value and form contracts are retained. Button now supplies the trigger’s native behavior and shared composition, while Ledger keeps field styling and localized date-only formatting. No timezone conversion is applied to the submitted day.

_Props: generated from `DatePicker`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._

## Related

[Calendar](?path=/docs/components-calendar--docs), [Field](?path=/docs/components-field--docs), [Forms](?path=/docs/patterns-forms--docs), [Popover](?path=/docs/components-popover--docs).

<!-- page: Components/Density (src/stories/components/Density.mdx) -->

# Density

Row density belongs to each table. `default` gives rows 40px of height; `compact` gives them 36px. Headers, controls and typography keep their sizes.

## Usage

Set `density` on a plain Table. The frame sets `data-density="compact"`, which changes the row-height token for its contents. Keep that attribute on the table frame so nearby lists and cards retain their spacing.

_Example: story `Stories.Tables`._

## Reader preference

A DataTable's Columns menu offers Compact rows. With a `view` name, the choice persists with its column settings; Reset view restores the author's default.

_Example: story `Stories.RegisterStory`._

For a compact default, pass `density: "compact"` to `useDataTable`. The reader can still change it.

_Example: story `Stories.ByDesign`._

## Accessibility

Changing row height preserves labels, focus order and control targets. The Columns menu exposes the current choice as a checkbox item. Offer density per table, so a choice in one view does not change unrelated content.

## Migration

The former global density provider, switch, hook, storage helpers and scripts are removed. Remove their imports and unwrap the provider's children. Use `Table density` or the DataTable view setting; no document-wide storage key or before-paint script is needed. The `Density` type remains exported.

## Related

- [Table](?path=/docs/components-table--docs): native table structure and density prop.
- [DataTable](?path=/docs/patterns-datatable--docs): view preferences, Columns menu and reset.

<!-- page: Components/Dialog (src/stories/components/Dialog.mdx) -->

# Dialog

Based on [shadcn’s Base UI source](https://ui.shadcn.com/docs/components/base/dialog) and [Base UI](https://base-ui.com/react/components/dialog). Ledger retains its tokens and application layouts.

## Anatomy

A modal task, composed from Dialog, DialogTrigger, DialogContent, DialogHeader, DialogTitle, DialogDescription, DialogFooter and DialogClose. Content includes its portal, backdrop and optional close button; DialogPortal and DialogOverlay are available for custom composition.

## Variants

_Example: story `Stories.Form`._

_Example: story `Stories.PendingAndNestedPopup`._

_Example: story `Stories.Scrollable`._

_Example: story `Stories.CustomPortal`._

## Accessibility

Use a named title and a close control. Base UI owns focus trapping, Escape, outside dismissal and nested dialog coordination. Content exposes native initialFocus and finalFocus. A supplied description is associated automatically. For triggerless tasks opened by disappearing actions, supply a stable finalFocus target.

## Props

Root exposes the native generic Base UI contract, including controlled/uncontrolled state, trigger payloads, handles, modality and cancellable onOpenChange. Native refs, render and state-based styles/classes reach their matching parts. Content adds showCloseButton; Footer can add a close button too.

### Migration and API

- Replace configured title, description and footer props with their explicit parts; body and aside layouts are ordinary children.
- Replace onClose with onOpenChange. Cancel a close request through details.cancel() while saving, and disable the caller-composed Close control.
- Move returnFocusRef to Content finalFocus, and width to Content style/className. Existing app dialogs retain their 520/860px widths and top placement.
- The default Content is centered, 520px maximum, with bounded height. Ledger Header/Footer own their padding; place scrolling body padding in children.

## Related

- [Sheet](?path=/docs/components-sheet--docs)
- [AlertDialog](?path=/docs/components-alertdialog--docs)
- [Command](?path=/docs/components-command--docs)

<!-- page: Components/Drawer (src/stories/components/Drawer.mdx) -->

# Drawer

A gesture-driven panel using [shadcn’s Base UI composition](https://ui.shadcn.com/docs/components/base/drawer) and [Base UI Drawer](https://base-ui.com/react/components/drawer). Use Sheet for a side panel that needs no swipe gestures.

## Anatomy

```tsx
<Drawer showSwipeHandle>
  <DrawerTrigger render={<Button />}>Quick actions</DrawerTrigger>
  <DrawerContent>
    <DrawerHeader>
      <DrawerTitle>Control actions</DrawerTitle>
      <DrawerDescription>For the selected control.</DrawerDescription>
    </DrawerHeader>
    <div className="min-h-0 flex-1 overflow-y-auto p-250">Actions</div>
    <DrawerFooter>
      <DrawerClose render={<Button />}>Done</DrawerClose>
    </DrawerFooter>
  </DrawerContent>
</Drawer>
```

Content composes Portal, the modal Overlay, Base UI Viewport/Popup and the text-selectable Content region. Header, Title, Description, Footer and Close are explicit parts. Portal, Overlay and SwipeHandle are also exported for custom native compositions.

_Example: story `Stories.Actions`._

## Variants and states

`swipeDirection` is `down` by default; `up`, `left` and `right` use physical edges. `showSwipeHandle` defaults to false. Root supports controlled or uncontrolled open state, native snap points and modal modes. Give long content its own scrolling body. Side drawers default to 75% of the viewport, capped at 24rem; vertical drawers leave space above the panel.

_Example: story `Stories.Positions`._
_Example: story `Stories.SnapPoints`._

For pending work, cancel the native `onOpenChange` event details when dismissal is unavailable. The same callback receives Escape, outside press, close button and swipe requests.

_Example: story `Stories.NestedPopups`._

## Accessibility

Supply a Title or an accessible name. Description is optional and creates its relationship only when rendered. Include an accessible Close action; the swipe handle is decorative. Base UI handles focus trapping, restoration, Escape, scroll locking and nested popups. Content accepts native `initialFocus`, `finalFocus`, refs, render and state callbacks. Specify a surviving finalFocus target if the opener disappears.

Nested drawers must be nested in the React tree. Ledger’s CSS follows Base UI’s measured swipe, snap and stack variables and honors reduced motion.

_Example: story `Stories.NestedDrawers`._

## Props

Replace the old configured `title`, `description`, `footer` and `onClose` props with children and Root `onOpenChange`. Move `returnFocusRef` to Content `finalFocus`, and surface dimensions/className to Content. The Vaul dependency and its portal/Escape/focus bridge are removed from the package.

_Props: generated from `Drawer`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._
_Props: generated from `DrawerContent`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._
_Props: generated from `DrawerTrigger`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._
_Props: generated from `DrawerClose`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._

## Related

[Sheet](?path=/docs/components-sheet--docs), [Dialog](?path=/docs/components-dialog--docs), [Popover](?path=/docs/components-popover--docs).

<!-- page: Components/DropdownMenu (src/stories/components/DropdownMenu.mdx) -->

# DropdownMenu

Actions and view options anchored to a button, using shadcn's Base UI Menu composition. Ledger supplies the menu surface, row geometry, colors and motion.

```tsx
<DropdownMenu>
  <DropdownMenuTrigger render={<Button variant="secondary" />}>Actions</DropdownMenuTrigger>
  <DropdownMenuContent style={{ width: 200 }}>
    <DropdownMenuItem onClick={edit}>Edit</DropdownMenuItem>
    <DropdownMenuSeparator />
    <DropdownMenuItem variant="destructive" onClick={archive}>
      Archive
    </DropdownMenuItem>
  </DropdownMenuContent>
</DropdownMenu>
```

## Composition and states

Root owns controlled or uncontrolled open state, modality, generic trigger payloads and cancellable `onOpenChange(open, details)`. Trigger defaults to a native button and composes existing buttons through `render`. Custom rendered components must accept merged props and refs; use `nativeButton={false}` only when replacing a button with a non-button action target.

Content includes its portal and positioner. It defaults to bottom/start, with a 4px side offset and zero alignment offset. Its width fits its contents and is at least the trigger width or 128px, within the available viewport. A narrow trigger never forces action labels to wrap. It scrolls when the available space is smaller than its contents, inside a [Scroller](?path=/docs/components-scroller--docs) whose hover arrows mark each overflowed edge. Native `style`, `className`, `render` and refs target the popup; classes and styles accept state callbacks. Content's `dir` overrides Ledger's inherited positioning direction.

Use Group around related items and Label inside that Group. Items compose icons, text and Shortcut as children. Destructive actions use `variant="destructive"`; `inset` aligns labels and items without icons. The row uses Ledger's 28px menu height. Action labels stay on one line.

_Example: story `Stories.DropdownMenuMatrix`._

## Choices and closing

Use CheckboxItem with `checked` and `onCheckedChange` for independent options. Use RadioGroup with `value` and `onValueChange`, and RadioItem with `value`, for exclusive options. A change callback's `details.cancel()` rejects the change. The installed Base UI radio value contract is not generic; callers can validate values against their own options.

Ordinary Item actions use `onClick` and close by default. CheckboxItem and RadioItem stay open by default; set `closeOnClick` when selecting should close the menu. Columns keep the menu open while toggling visibility; saved views and sorting close after a choice. Essential form values still belong in labeled form controls.

_Example: story `Stories.Toggles`._

## Submenus and links

Sub, SubTrigger and SubContent create a nested menu. SubContent defaults to start alignment, -3px alignment offset, zero side offset and a 96px minimum. Its logical `inline-end` side and chevron follow the locale. Escape closes the submenu first; Root's `closeParentOnEsc` can change that behavior.

LinkItem is Base UI's native anchor part. Give it `href`, or `render` a router Link, to retain navigation and modified clicks. It stays open by default; `closeOnClick` closes after navigation. Item with a rendered action button instead uses `nativeButton`. The public Portal part is available for custom Base UI compositions; Content already includes one.

_Example: story `Stories.Submenus`._

## Accessibility and dialogs

The trigger exposes `aria-haspopup="menu"` and expanded state. Items use `menuitem`, `menuitemcheckbox` or `menuitemradio`, with checked state where appropriate. Enter, Space or ArrowDown opens from the trigger; arrows, Home, End and typeahead navigate; Enter or Space activates an action. Disabled items remain focusable and announce their disabled state, but cannot activate. Root defaults to modal with looping keyboard navigation.

A row-action button must remain keyboard-reachable. Use `opacity-0 focus-visible:opacity-100 group-hover/row:opacity-100 data-popup-open:opacity-100` for visual concealment, rather than `visibility: hidden`, which removes it from keyboard navigation.

Content owns `finalFocus`. Ledger's modal wrappers resolve an activating menu item to its stable menu trigger, so closing the dialog returns there. For custom modal compositions, give the dialog an explicit return ref and use `finalFocus={false}` if menu focus return must be suppressed. A menu inside a current Radix dialog shares its portal boundary; Escape dismisses the menu before its parent dialog.

_Example: story `Stories.Dialogs`._

## Migration and API

Replace the configured `trigger` prop with Trigger's `render`; move placement and width into Content. Replace `DropdownMenu.Item`, `.Label` and `.Separator` with the flat exports. `onSelect` becomes `onClick` for actions; `isSelected` becomes CheckboxItem or RadioGroup state; `closeOnSelect` becomes `closeOnClick`; `tone="danger"` becomes `variant="destructive"`; `trailing` becomes Shortcut children. Remove children-as-`close` callbacks: items close through Base UI, and Root exposes controlled state or `actionsRef` for imperative dismissal.

See [shadcn Dropdown Menu](https://ui.shadcn.com/docs/components/base/dropdown-menu) and [Base UI Menu](https://base-ui.com/react/components/menu) for the native APIs. Content adds the four positioning props to Popup. Ledger adds token styling and locale/dialog integration; reference catalogs remain independently refreshable.

## Related

[Popover](?path=/docs/components-popover--docs) · [Dialog](?path=/docs/components-dialog--docs) · [Editable](?path=/docs/patterns-editable--docs) · [DataTable](?path=/docs/patterns-data-table--docs) · [IconButton](?path=/docs/components-iconbutton--docs) · [Overlays](?path=/docs/components-overlays--docs)

<!-- page: Components/Empty (src/stories/components/Empty.mdx) -->

# Empty

A region with nothing in it says why, and offers the next step. The picture, the message and the actions sit at the centre of the region; the caller composes them from the parts. A [DataTable](?path=/docs/patterns-data-table--docs) draws its own, so a register never needs to.

_Example: story `Stories.Playground`._

## Anatomy

```tsx
<Empty>
  <EmptyMedia aria-hidden>
    <EmptyIllustration kind="records" />
  </EmptyMedia>
  <EmptyHeader>
    <EmptyTitle>No programs yet</EmptyTitle>
    <EmptyDescription>Create one to define its systems and their work.</EmptyDescription>
  </EmptyHeader>
  <EmptyContent>
    <Button variant="primary" iconBefore={<Plus />}>New program</Button>
    <Button variant="secondary">Import</Button>
  </EmptyContent>
</Empty>
```

| Part                | What it is                                                                                                                                                                   |
| ------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Empty`             | The region: a column, centred, on a dashed frame. `size="compact"` for the rail's row; `frame="none"` on a surface that already bounds it.                                     |
| `EmptyMedia`        | The picture. Holds an `EmptyIllustration`, or `variant="icon"` draws a Lucide icon in the neutral circle. Anything else fits: an avatar, a chart's ghost.                    |
| `EmptyIllustration` | The kit's picture, on the surface tokens: a scene of ghost records the shape of what the region will hold, sometimes with a badge that says why it is empty. Twelve kinds, below. Decorative. |
| `EmptyHeader`       | The title and its description, at a readable measure.                                                                                                                        |
| `EmptyTitle`        | A heading in the default size, body text in compact.                                                                                                                         |
| `EmptyDescription`  | One or two lines: why there is nothing, what creates it.                                                                                                                     |
| `EmptyContent`      | The actions, centred, wrapping. A second `EmptyContent` holds a quieter row: a link, suggested searches.                                                                     |

## Variants

Which empty this is decides the picture and the action. The picture is the shape of what the region will hold, so a reader who has never seen a record still learns what one is:

| The region                          | `kind`     | Action                                       |
| ----------------------------------- | ---------- | -------------------------------------------- |
| Nothing exists yet                  | `records`  | The primary: create the first, import        |
| A search or a filter left nothing   | `search`   | Clear filters; suggestions under it          |
| Empty because the work is finished  | `done`     | A link to the closed items, or none          |
| Nothing assigned or waiting for you | `inbox`    | None, or a link to everything                |
| The reader may not see this         | `locked`   | Request access                               |
| No controls or requirements yet     | `shield`   | Allocate, map, import a catalog              |
| No files, evidence or documents     | `document` | Upload, attach                               |
| No tasks or work items              | `tasks`    | Add a task                                   |
| No people, owners or assignees      | `people`   | Assign, invite                               |
| No systems, components or parts     | `tree`     | Add the first node                           |
| No data to chart                    | `chart`    | None; the records make the chart             |
| Nothing scheduled                   | `calendar` | Schedule                                     |
| A tab or a card body with no items  | an icon    | One small action                             |
| A rail's related list               | compact    | One link                                     |

A [DataTable](?path=/docs/patterns-data-table--docs) with no records at all is only its Empty: the toolbar, the header and the hairline go, the frame stays, and the action in it creates the first record. While a search or a filter is what emptied it, the toolbar and header stay and the Empty sits under them without a frame.

_Example: story `Stories.NoMatches`._

_Example: story `Stories.Illustrations`._

_Example: story `Stories.Icon`._

_Example: story `Stories.Compact`._

## Sizes

`default` is the hero: the picture, a small heading, body copy, medium buttons, `space.300` between the three, `space.600` above and below. `compact` is the rail's row: `EmptyMedia` beside the message, a medium-weight body title, small body copy, a small link. In compact, place `EmptyMedia` before `EmptyHeader` and keep `EmptyContent` a direct child, so the grid puts media in the first column and the message and actions in the second.

## States

Empty has no states of its own. Loading is [Skeleton](?path=/docs/components-skeleton--docs) or [Spinner](?path=/docs/components-spinner--docs); an error is an [Alert](?path=/docs/components-alert--docs). A DataTable chooses between its two empties itself: the caller's message when there are no records, the kit's **Nothing matches** with **Clear filters** while a search or a column filter is active.

## Modifiers

- **`size`**: `default` or `compact`.
- **`frame`**: `dashed` (the default region) or `none`, for a table cell, a page body, a panel that has its own edges. Compact never draws a frame.
- **`kind`** on `EmptyIllustration`: the twelve above. Every scene is 128 by 84px, so empty states sit at one height across a page.

_Example: story `Stories.OnAPage`._

## Content

- **The title says what is missing, in the reader's words**: "No programs yet", "Nothing matches", "Nothing open". Not "Empty", not "No data".
- **The description says why, or what creates it**, in one or two lines. Never advice that points at another control ("Choose another tab").
- **One primary action**, the same verb as the page's own; a secondary beside it at most. In a filtered table the action is **Clear filters**.
- **Suggestions are small secondary buttons** in a second row, after a "Try" in `color.text.subtlest`.

## Style

| Element       | Token                                                                                       |
| ------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Frame         | `color.border` dashed · `radius.large` · `space.300` × `space.600`                          |
| Gaps          | `space.300` between picture, message and actions · `space.100` between title and description |
| Title         | `font.heading.small` · `color.text`                                                         |
| Description   | `font.body` · `color.text.subtle` · 400px measure                                           |
| Icon circle   | `dimension.control.large` · `color.background.neutral` · `color.icon.subtle`                |
| Illustration  | 128 × 84px · `elevation.surface.raised` and `.sunken` · `color.border` and `.bold` · `color.skeleton` · `color.background.neutral` |
| Badge         | `dimension.control.medium` · `color.background.neutral.bold`, `.success.bold` or `.brand.bold` · `color.icon.inverse` · `elevation.shadow.raised` |
| Compact       | no frame · `space.150` between media and message · `font.body` medium · `font.body.small`   |

## Accessibility

The parts are divs with no automatic landmark or announcement. Give the root `role="region"` and `aria-labelledby` the title when the region is a page's main content; inside a table the cell is enough. The illustration and the icon circle are decorative: `EmptyIllustration` hides itself, and `EmptyMedia` takes `aria-hidden`. Text precedes the actions in reading order, so a screen reader hears why before what.

## Props

_Props: generated from `Empty`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._
_Props: generated from `EmptyMedia`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._
_Props: generated from `EmptyIllustration`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._
_Props: generated from `EmptyHeader`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._
_Props: generated from `EmptyTitle`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._
_Props: generated from `EmptyDescription`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._
_Props: generated from `EmptyContent`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._

Every part accepts native div attributes, events, styles and refs. Icon children retain their own props, classes and refs.

### Migration

The default was left-aligned with a body-weight title; it is now centred with a heading, the description at a measure, and the actions under it. A caller that wanted the old row keeps `size="compact"`. `Related`, `Item.Group` and `DataTable` compose the parts themselves; a DataTable's `empty` now takes `illustration`, `secondary` and `filtered`, and draws **Nothing matches** with **Clear filters** on its own while a search or a filter is active.

_Example: story `Stories.EmptyMatrix`._

## Related

[DataTable](?path=/docs/patterns-data-table--docs), [Related](?path=/docs/patterns-related--docs), [Card](?path=/docs/components-card--docs), [Skeleton](?path=/docs/components-skeleton--docs).

Sources: [shadcn Empty](https://ui.shadcn.com/docs/components/base/empty), [ReUI empty state](https://reui.io/blocks/empty-state), [Atlassian Empty state](https://atlassian.design/components/empty-state), [Carbon empty states pattern](https://carbondesignsystem.com/patterns/empty-states-pattern).

## Don't

_Example: story `Stories.Dont`._

<!-- page: Components/Fact (src/stories/components/Fact.mdx) -->

# Fact

An inline label and value on one baseline: Owner Dana Whitfield, Frequency Quarterly. A row of them is a `Fact.Group`, the facts strip under a record's title: the four to six facts the reader acts on, above the fold, so that needing to open a panel to find out who owns a thing is never the problem. The rest belong in the rail as [KeyValue](?path=/docs/components-keyvalue--docs) rows. The strip most page headers write by hand.

_Example: story `Stories.FactMatrix`._

## Anatomy

| Part  | What it is                                                                                                                   |
| ----- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Label | `dt` in `font.body.small` and `color.text.subtle`, one or two words.                                                         |
| Value | `dd` after it, `space.075` away, `font.body` medium in `color.text`: a word, a number, a date, a Person, a Badge, an Absent. |
| Group | A `dl` that wraps: `space.300` between facts, `space.075` between lines, every fact whole on its line.                       |

## Variants

Fact has one appearance. What varies is where the strip is:

| Where                  | What it holds                                                         |
| ---------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Under a record's title | The facts the reader acts on: owner, due, method, count. At most six. |
| In a Sheet's header    | The same, for the record the sheet shows.                             |
| In a Glance            | Three or four, for the record previewed.                              |

Not built, and why: a stacked label-over-value grid (the prototype draws one by hand on several pages), because that shape is a decision still open; a Fact that edits in place, because the value is an [Editable](?path=/docs/patterns-editable--docs) and the Fact only frames it.

## Sizes

One size: the label `font.body.small`, the value `font.body`. The strip is as wide as its header and wraps when narrower; a fact never breaks across lines.

_Example: story `Stories.UnderHeader`._

## States

A Fact has one state. Its value may: a Badge is a state, a Person is a person, an Editable value opens. The Fact does not.

## Modifiers

- **The value** is the modifier: text, a Person, a Badge at `xsmall`, an Id, an Absent, an Editable.
- **Group `className`** for the rule above the strip under a header.

## Content

- **The label is one or two words, a noun:** "Owner", "Next due", "Open findings".
- **The value is one thing that fits on a line:** a name, a number, a date, a state. A sentence is Prose or a wrapping KeyValue.
- **Four to six facts, the ones acted on.** Reference joins (created by, framework, family) go in the rail.
- **A missing value stays, as an Absent**, so the strip says what is missing.

## Style

| Element | Token                                                                     |
| ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Label   | `font.body.small` · `color.text.subtle`                                   |
| Value   | `font.body` medium · `color.text` · `space.075` after the label           |
| Group   | `space.300` between facts · `space.075` between wrapped lines · baselines |

## Accessibility

- **A group is a definition list** and each Fact a `dt` and `dd`, so a screen reader hears "Owner, Dana Whitfield" as a pair. A Fact belongs inside a Fact.Group; the headers and sheets that take a `facts` slot wrap it.
- **The strip is read in order**, so the order is the order of importance.
- **An Absent is read as a dash**, which says "nothing here" in one character.
- **Contrast:** the label in `color.text.subtle` passes 4.5:1; the gate runs the matrix.

## Props

_Props: generated from `Fact`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._

### Fact.Group

_Props: generated from `Fact.Group`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._

### Playground

_Example: story `Stories.Playground`._

_Rendered in the Storybook: Controls._

## Related

- [KeyValue](?path=/docs/components-keyvalue--docs): the row, for the rail.
- [PageHeader](?path=/docs/layout-pageheader--docs), [Sheet](?path=/docs/components-sheet--docs), [Glance](?path=/docs/patterns-glance--docs): the `facts` slots.
- [Typography](?path=/docs/components-typography--docs): `Absent`, and `Prose` for the sentence that is not a fact.

## Don't

_Example: story `Stories.Dont`._

<!-- page: Components/Field (src/stories/components/Field.mdx) -->

# Field

Compose labels, controls and validation messages with shadcn's Base UI Field parts and Ledger tokens. Field owns layout; the form owns values, validation and native associations.

## Anatomy

```tsx
const id = useId();
<Field data-invalid={invalid}>
  <FieldLabel htmlFor={id}>Owner</FieldLabel>
  <Input id={id} aria-invalid={invalid} aria-describedby={`${id}-message`} />
  {invalid ? (
    <FieldError id={`${id}-message`} errors={errors} />
  ) : (
    <FieldDescription id={`${id}-message`}>Use the full name.</FieldDescription>
  )}
</Field>;
```

`FieldSet` and `FieldLegend` group related controls. `FieldGroup` spaces fields; `FieldContent` groups text beside a control; `FieldTitle` supplies visual text when a wrapping label already provides the association. `FieldSeparator` divides sections, with optional text.

_Example: story `Stories.Composition`._

## Variants and states

Field supports `vertical` (default), `horizontal` and `responsive` orientations. Responsive fields change direction inside a FieldGroup container. Mark the wrapper with `data-invalid` or `data-disabled` and pass the actual state to the control. An asterisk belongs in label content; `aria-required` describes the requirement, while native `required` enables browser validation.

Invalid labels and messages use the same error color; a focused invalid input retains its error border and a separate focus outline. Disabled labels use the disabled text token. A FieldLabel wrapping a Field becomes a choice card with hover, checked and keyboard-focus feedback; disabled choices keep a quiet surface. These styles do not disable a control or validate a value.

Labeled FieldSeparator rules stop on either side of the text instead of painting over the parent surface, so they work inside a page, Card or dialog without a background override.

_Example: story `Stories.Validation`._

FieldError accepts children or an `errors` array of message objects. It deduplicates messages and renders nothing for an empty result. Children take precedence.

_Example: story `Stories.Errors`._

## Accessibility

Use `htmlFor` and a matching control `id` for individual fields. Reference hint/error IDs with `aria-describedby`, and pass `aria-invalid` to the control. Use FieldSet/FieldLegend for checkbox groups and explicitly name a RadioGroup with `aria-labelledby`. Choice controls keep their individual labels. A group requirement does not make every checkbox required.

Native associations work through wrappers and custom components that forward their props. Generate IDs with `useId` when a form can appear more than once. TanStack Form continues to own touched state, validation and submission; focus the first invalid control on failed submission.

## Props

_Props: generated from `Field`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._
_Props: generated from `FieldError`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._
_Props: generated from `FieldLegend`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._

Every part forwards the native attributes and ref of its element: Field/Group/Content/Title/Error/Separator use divs, FieldLabel a label, FieldDescription a paragraph, FieldSet a fieldset, and FieldLegend a legend.

### Migration

Replace `label`, `hint`, `error`, `isRequired`, `isGroup` and `controlId` with composed parts and native attributes. `useFieldControl` and automatic child binding are removed. Move group content to FieldSet/FieldLegend; preserve the control's accessible name, description, invalid state and required announcement. Shadcn's Base UI Field uses semantic HTML; it is separate from the optional Base UI Field primitive.

## Related

[Input](?path=/docs/components-input--docs), [Textarea](?path=/docs/components-textarea--docs), [Select](?path=/docs/components-select--docs), [Combobox](?path=/docs/components-combobox--docs), and [Forms](?path=/docs/patterns-forms--docs).

Sources: [shadcn Field](https://ui.shadcn.com/docs/components/base/field), [implementation](https://github.com/shadcn-ui/ui/blob/main/apps/v4/registry/bases/base/ui/field.tsx), [TanStack integration](https://base-ui.com/react/handbook/forms#tanstack-form).

<!-- page: Components/FilterChip (src/stories/components/FilterChip.mdx) -->

# FilterChip

A filter the reader adds to a [Toolbar](?path=/docs/patterns-toolbar--docs): dashed with a plus until it is on, then solid and selected, with the chosen value after its label. A chip is one question of the register, Owner or Status or Gaps; the chips together are the question the table answers.

A chip asks; a [Badge](?path=/docs/components-badge--docs) tells. A coordinated set of single or multiple choices is a [ToggleGroup](?path=/docs/components-togglegroup--docs); a thing to do is a [Button](?path=/docs/components-button--docs).

_Example: story `Stories.FilterChipMatrix`._

## Anatomy

| Part   | What it is                                                                                                          |
| ------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Plus   | "+" before the label while the chip is off: add this filter. Hidden from a screen reader; gone once the chip is on. |
| Label  | The column or the question, `font.body`, `color.text.subtle` at rest and `color.text.selected` on.                  |
| Value  | After the label, `font.weight.medium` in `color.text`: the value chosen, or "3 chosen".                             |
| Border | Dashed `color.border.bold` at rest; solid `color.border.selected` on `color.background.selected` once on.           |

## Variants

FilterChip has one appearance. What varies is what a click does:

| The question                                   | Use                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| ---------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Yes or no about the rows: Gaps, Hide closed    | A toggle: `isActive` flips, no value.                                                                                                                                                          |
| A column with a value: Owner, Status, Due      | The trigger of a [Popover](?path=/docs/components-popover--docs); the DataTable's `Filter` builds one from the column (checkboxes, a range, a contains field) and the value reads on the chip. |
| Three values the reader steps through          | A toggle that cycles, the value showing which. Past three, a popover.                                                                                                                          |
| Exclusive choices: All, High, Medium | A ToggleGroup, not chips.                                                                                                                                                                      |
| A saved question with its count                | The DataTable's `Presets`, a ToggleGroup with Count children.                                                                                                                                          |

There is no remove cross on the chip: a click on an active toggle turns it off, and a popover chip has Clear. There is no chip with an icon, and no chip with a count: the rows a question would leave belong to a preset's Count.

## Sizes

One: `dimension.control.small` 28px, the Toolbar's height, `space.100` each side.

_Example: story `Stories.InToolbar`._

## States

| State        | What changes                                                                                                  |
| ------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Rest         | Dashed `color.border.bold`, the plus, `color.text.subtle`.                                                    |
| Hover        | The border to `color.border`, the text to `color.text`.                                                       |
| Active       | Solid `color.border.selected` on `color.background.selected`, `color.text.selected`; no plus; pressed.        |
| With a value | The value after the label in `color.text` at `font.weight.medium`.                                            |
| Open         | As a Popover's trigger, `aria-expanded`; the chip is active only while it holds a value.                      |
| Focus        | The focus outline.                                                                                            |
| Disabled     | `color.border.disabled`, `color.text.disabled`, no pointer: a filter with nothing to choose. Better left out. |

## Modifiers

- **`label`** and **`value`**.
- **`isActive`** paints the chip on and says pressed.
- **`disabled`**.
- **`onClick`** and the rest of a button's props. A Popover passes `aria-expanded` to its trigger, and the chip stops saying pressed.

## Content

- **The label is the column or the question as a noun**, sentence case: Owner, Status, Gaps, Hide closed. Not "Filter by owner".
- **The value is what was chosen, as the cell shows it**: "Dana Whitfield", "Overdue", "≥ 10", "3 chosen". Never a count of rows.
- **A toggle reads as what it turns on**: Gaps shows the gaps, Hide closed hides them; both are true while the chip is on.
- **Four or five chips** in a toolbar. Past that the table has too many questions, and the answers are presets.

## Style

| Element  | Token                                                                                           |
| -------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Chip     | `dimension.control.small` · `radius.medium` · `space.100` sides · gap `space.075` · `font.body` |
| Rest     | border dashed `color.border.bold` · `color.text.subtle` · hover `color.border`, `color.text`    |
| Active   | border `color.border.selected` · `color.background.selected` · `color.text.selected`            |
| Value    | `font.weight.medium` `color.text`                                                               |
| Disabled | `color.border.disabled` · `color.text.disabled`                                                 |
| Focus    | The focus outline                                                                               |
| Motion   | `motion.duration.fast` on the colours                                                           |

## Accessibility

- **A button.** On its own it is a toggle: `aria-pressed` follows `isActive`, so a screen reader hears "Gaps, toggle button, pressed". As a Popover's trigger it takes the popover's `aria-expanded` and does not say pressed; the value in its text says what is applied.
- **Named by its text**, label and value together: "Owner Dana Whitfield".
- **Keyboard.** Tab reaches it; Space or Enter flips it or opens the popover; Escape closes the popover and returns focus to the chip.
- **Not colour alone.** The plus and the dashed border say off; the solid border and the pressed state say on.
- **Disabled is the last resort.** A filter with nothing to choose is left out of the row.

## Props

Native button props, including `ref`, pass through to the button. Refs target `HTMLButtonElement`;
when composed with `PopoverTrigger render={<FilterChip label="Status" />}`, both parts' refs and
event handlers reach the same button. The Popover owns opening, dismissal and focus return.

_Props: generated from `FilterChip`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._

### Playground

_Example: story `Stories.Playground`._

_Rendered in the Storybook: Controls._

## Related

- [Toolbar](?path=/docs/patterns-toolbar--docs): where chips live.
- [DataTable](?path=/docs/patterns-data-table--docs): `Filter` builds a chip and its popover from a column; `Presets` are saved questions.
- [ToggleGroup](?path=/docs/components-togglegroup--docs): single or multiple toggle buttons. [Popover](?path=/docs/components-popover--docs): what a value chip opens.
- [Badge](?path=/docs/components-badge--docs): a status told, not asked.

## Don't

_Example: story `Stories.Dont`._

<!-- page: Components/HoverCard (src/stories/components/HoverCard.mdx) -->

# HoverCard

A supplementary preview of a link's destination, built from shadcn's Base UI PreviewCard composition. The trigger stays a link; the preview can contain a [Glance](?path=/docs/patterns-glance--docs) or other supporting content available at that destination.

```tsx
<HoverCard>
  <HoverCardTrigger href="/controls/CTRL-0412">CTRL-0412</HoverCardTrigger>
  <HoverCardContent style={{ width: 300 }}>
    <Glance id="CTRL-0412" title="Segregation of duties, payables" />
  </HoverCardContent>
</HoverCard>
```

## Composition and placement

`HoverCard` owns the open state. `HoverCardTrigger` renders an anchor and accepts native link props, a ref, state callbacks and `render` for a custom link. `HoverCardContent` includes the portal and positioner; its native props, ref and `render` target the popup.

An action trigger can use `render={<button type="button" />}`. Its native button owns click and keyboard activation; Trigger has no `nativeButton` prop.

Content is 256px wide by default. Override its width through `style`, including a state callback. Placement defaults to `side="bottom"`, `sideOffset={4}`, `align="center"` and `alignOffset={4}`. These four props belong to Content. The positioner handles collisions; logical sides and alignment follow the Ledger locale, with Content's `dir` available as an override.

The surface uses Ledger's overlay, border, text, radius, spacing and motion tokens. Content `className` and `style` callbacks receive Base UI popup state; render props, classes, styles and refs are merged.

_Example: story `Stories.HoverCardMatrix`._

## Interaction

The trigger opens the preview after pointer hover or keyboard focus. `delay` defaults to 600ms and `closeDelay` to 300ms, both on Trigger. Pointer passage from trigger to popup keeps the preview open. Leaving both, moving focus away, an outside press or Escape dismisses it. Escape leaves focus where it was.

Clicking or pressing Enter on the trigger follows the link. A trigger press does not itself guarantee dismissal; navigation or caller-controlled state may close the card. Touch follows the link without the mouse-hover behavior.

Use Root's `defaultOpen`, or controlled `open` with `onOpenChange(open, details)`. `details.cancel()` rejects a change. Multiple triggers can share one Root: pass `payload` on each trigger and render the active payload through Root's children function.

_Example: story `Stories.OnAnId`._

## Accessibility

Keep the preview supplementary. Essential information and actions belong at the linked destination or in a [Popover](?path=/docs/components-popover--docs). Opening the preview does not move focus or add a popup Tab stop, and it is not a dialog announcement. The link remains the way to navigate for keyboard, touch and assistive-technology users.

## Migration

Replace the wrapper's `content` prop with `HoverCardContent` children. Compose an existing link through `HoverCardTrigger render`, or pass `href` and link text directly to Trigger. Move `delay` to Trigger; move placement to Content and replace `width` with `style={{ width }}`. Root retains controlled open state and now provides Base UI event details. The old 280px width and 400ms/120ms timing defaults become 256px and 600ms/300ms.

## Props

HoverCard inherits Base UI's [Root props](https://base-ui.com/react/components/preview-card#root), and HoverCardTrigger inherits its [Trigger props](https://base-ui.com/react/components/preview-card#trigger). HoverCardContent inherits [Popup props](https://base-ui.com/react/components/preview-card#popup) plus the four positioning props described above.

_Example: story `Stories.Playground`._

## Related

[Glance](?path=/docs/patterns-glance--docs) · [PreviewSheet](?path=/docs/patterns-previewsheet--docs) · [Tooltip](?path=/docs/components-tooltip--docs) · [Overlays](?path=/docs/components-overlays--docs) · [shadcn Hover Card](https://ui.shadcn.com/docs/components/base/hover-card) · [Base UI Preview Card](https://base-ui.com/react/components/preview-card)

<!-- page: Components/IconButton (src/stories/components/IconButton.mdx) -->

# IconButton

A square [Button](?path=/docs/components-button--docs) with an icon, a required `label` and a tooltip. Name the action, such as “Search” or “Close.” Use a labelled Button when the icon alone would be unclear.

_Example: story `Stories.IconButtonMatrix`._

## Variants and sizes

| Variant | Use |
| --- | --- |
| `secondary` | Default raised action. |
| `subtle` | Toolbars, rows and header controls. |
| `primary` | Emphasized actions, including the options beside a primary split action. |

| Size | Button | Icon |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `small` | 28px square, the default | 14px |
| `medium` | 32px square | 16px |

Pass the icon element with `icon`. IconButton sizes it and hides it from assistive technology; `label` provides the accessible name. `isSelected` applies the selected palette and `aria-pressed`. `isLoading` replaces the icon with a decorative spinner while retaining the label and focus.

_Example: story `Stories.InPlace`._

## Composition and accessibility

IconButton shares Button's native props, form behavior, refs and Base UI `render` support. The rendered component must forward props and refs to its DOM element. Use `nativeButton={false}` for a custom action that is not a native button. For navigation, use a real anchor or router Link with `buttonVariants`, as shown on the [Button page](?path=/docs/components-button--docs).

- The tooltip shows `label` on hover and focus. Escape closes it.
- `isTooltipDisabled` suppresses the tooltip when a parent supplies one or the label is already visible; the accessible name remains.
- Tab reaches an enabled control; Enter and Space activate it. Disabled controls leave the normal tab order unless `focusableWhenDisabled` is set.
- Loading sets `aria-busy`, blocks activation and retains focus. An explicitly disabled control stays disabled.
- Keep sufficient space around compact controls; choose a larger labelled Button when a touch interaction needs a larger target.

## Props

_Props: generated from `IconButton`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._

_Example: story `Stories.Playground`._

_Rendered in the Storybook: Controls._

## Related

[Button](?path=/docs/components-button--docs) · [ButtonGroup](?path=/docs/components-buttongroup--docs) · [Tooltip](?path=/docs/components-tooltip--docs) · [Toggle](?path=/docs/components-toggle--docs) · [DropdownMenu](?path=/docs/components-dropdownmenu--docs)

<!-- page: Components/Id (src/stories/components/Id.mdx) -->

# Id

An identifier: CTRL-0412, AC-2(3), FND-2231, a hash. One typeface app-wide, so an Id inherits the font, the size and the colour of wherever it sits and adds only tabular numerals, which is what makes a column of ids line up. It is kept as a component for the semantics, and so every id in the product can be found. A code snippet is for code, which an id is not.

_Example: story `Stories.IdMatrix`._

## Anatomy

| Part | What it is                                                                                                             |
| ---- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Id   | A span with tabular numerals. Nothing else: no fill, no face, no colour of its own.                                    |
| List | `Id.List`: a wrapping run of ids at `font.body.xsmall` in `color.text.subtle`, `space.050` apart; or the `empty` word. |

## Variants

| Variant   | Use                                                                           |
| --------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Id`      | One id, in text, in a title, in a link, in a cell.                            |
| `Id.List` | Several ids: the controls a requirement traces to, the CCIs a package covers. |

Not built, and why: a monospace face (the old habit; the kit has one typeface and tabular numerals do the aligning); a copy button, because an id is selected like any word; a link inside the Id, because the link is outside it, a TextLink whose text is an Id.

## Sizes

None of its own. An Id is the size of its line: `font.body` in a sentence, `font.body.small` in a row, `font.heading` in a title. `Id.List` is `font.body.xsmall`, the size of a list of references.

_Example: story `Stories.InRows`._

## States

None. An Id is text. The link around it hovers; the cell around it is selected; the Id does neither.

## Modifiers

- **`className`** for the colour or the size it takes from its place: `text-subtle` in a row's id column, `font-body-small` in a rail, `break-all` for a hash that must break anywhere.
- **List `empty`** for the word that stands where there are no ids; a muted dash by default.

## Content

- **The id as the record writes it:** "CTRL-0412", "AC-2(3)". Never a prose rendering ("Control 412", "AC 2.3").
- **One id per Id.** Several are an `Id.List`, never a comma-joined string.
- **A hash is an Id** too, with `break-all` so it wraps inside its column.
- **Subtle beside a name, default alone.** In a row the id column is `color.text.subtle` and the name is `color.text`; in a sentence the Id takes the sentence's colour.

## Style

| Element | Token                                                              |
| ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Id      | Tabular numerals; the surrounding font, size and colour            |
| List    | `font.body.xsmall` · `color.text.subtle` · `space.050` between ids |
| Empty   | `font.body.small` · `color.text.subtlest`                          |

## Accessibility

- **An Id is text**, read as its characters. Nothing to focus, nothing to operate.
- **A screen reader spells an id as it reads it.** Punctuation inside it, the parentheses in AC-2(3), is read or skipped by the reader's own rules; the kit does not rewrite an id to help.
- **The colour is not the meaning.** An Id in `color.text.subtle` is an id; an Id in the link colour is a link, because a TextLink is around it.
- **`break-all` is for a hash**, so a long id never widens its column past the viewport.

## Props

_Props: generated from `Id`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._

### Id.List

_Props: generated from `Id.List`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._

### Playground

_Example: story `Stories.Playground`._

_Rendered in the Storybook: Controls._

## Related

- [TextLink](?path=/docs/components-textlink--docs): the link an Id sits inside.
- [Item](?path=/docs/components-item--docs), [Table](?path=/docs/components-table--docs): the id column.
- [PageHeader](?path=/docs/layout-pageheader--docs): the id above a title.

## Don't

_Example: story `Stories.Dont`._

<!-- page: Components/Indicator (src/stories/components/Indicator.mdx) -->

# Indicator

A Dot with a word: severity or health beside a label, in a row or a rail. High, Medium, Low; Healthy, Degraded. Never a pill, so the status column stays the only pill in the row and the eye can tell the rank from the state. The Dot alone is a 6px circle in the tone's icon colour, tuned to read at small sizes, for a status in a spot too small for a word. A status indicator is usually an icon per state; this uses the Dot.

_Example: story `Stories.IndicatorMatrix`._

## Anatomy

| Part | What it is                                                                                                                |
| ---- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Dot  | 6px, round, `color.icon.<tone>`. It never shrinks.                                                                        |
| Word | `font.body` after the Dot, `space.075` away: `color.text`, or `color.text.subtle` when the tone is neutral. It truncates. |

## Variants

| Variant     | Use                                                                                                        |
| ----------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Indicator` | Severity or health with its word: a column in a table, a fact in a rail.                                   |
| `Dot`       | The status alone: a cell 24px wide, a name in a tree, a mark in a timeline. With `label` it says its name. |

The tone is a rank, not a state: `danger` High, `warning` Medium, `neutral` Low, `success` Healthy, `information` Informational. Neutral mutes the word as well as the Dot, so a scale reads from loud to quiet. A record's state, Verified or Overdue, is a [Badge](?path=/docs/components-badge--docs).

Not built, and why: an icon per tone (failed, warning, in progress), because the Dot is the kit's one status mark and the word says the rest; a large Dot; an Indicator in a pill.

## Sizes

One size. The Dot is 6px whatever the text beside it; the word is `font.body`, the row's size, and in a `font.body.small` line it takes that size from the parent. An Indicator is as wide as its word and truncates when the column is narrower.

_Example: story `Stories.Truncation`._

## States

An Indicator has one state and does not hover, focus or disable. The tone is the whole variation.

_Example: story `Stories.InRows`._

## Modifiers

- **`tone`** as in Variants; `neutral` when unsaid.
- **Dot `label`** for a Dot with no text beside it: the status as a word, spoken and not shown.
- **`className`** for placement, never for colour.

## Content

- **The word is the rank:** High, Medium, Low; Healthy, Degraded, Down. One word, two at most.
- **The same scale everywhere.** A severity is High, Medium or Low on every screen, never Critical on one and Severe on another.
- **A Dot's label is the same word** the Indicator would show: "Suspect", "Blocked".

## Style

| Element | Token                                                                         |
| ------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Dot     | 6px · `color.icon.<tone>` · `color.icon.subtlest` at neutral                  |
| Word    | `font.body` · `color.text` · `color.text.subtle` at neutral · `space.075` gap |

The icon colours are Badge's, so a danger Dot and a danger Badge's text are one red, and the icon colour is the step tuned for a 6px mark.

## Accessibility

- **The word carries the rank**; the Dot reinforces it and is hidden from a screen reader, so "High" is read once.
- **A Dot alone is colour alone.** Give it `label`: it becomes an image named "Suspect", and the cell is no longer silent. Without a label it is hidden, which is right only when text beside it says the same thing.
- **Neutral is muted, not disabled.** `color.text.subtle` passes the contrast test; the gate runs every tone.
- **Nothing to focus.** An Indicator is a span in the row's reading order.

## Props

_Props: generated from `Indicator`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._

### Dot

_Props: generated from `Dot`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._

### Playground

_Example: story `Stories.Playground`._

_Rendered in the Storybook: Controls._

## Related

- [Badge](?path=/docs/components-badge--docs): the tone table, and which of Badge, Count, Indicator and Dot to use.
- [Gates](?path=/docs/patterns-gates--docs): the Dot on an unmet gate.
- [Timeline](?path=/docs/components-timeline--docs): the Dot as a mark.
- [Alert](?path=/docs/components-alert--docs): the Dot before a title.
