_Example: story `Stories.Dont`._

<!-- page: Components/Input (src/stories/components/Input.mdx) -->

# Input

One line of free text, using shadcn's Base UI Input implementation with Ledger control styling. Labels and validation messages belong to Field.

## Anatomy

```tsx
<Field>
  <FieldLabel htmlFor="input">Program name</FieldLabel>
  <Input
    id="input"
    aria-describedby="input-help"
    name="program"
    value={name}
    onValueChange={setName}
  />
  <FieldDescription id="input-help">As it appears on the authorization package.</FieldDescription>
</Field>
```

Use `InputGroupInput` inside InputGroup when the field has addons. Input itself remains a single input element.

## Variants and states

`medium` is 32px; `small` is 28px beside toolbar actions. Native `type`, `inputMode`, `readOnly`, `disabled`, `maxLength` and form attributes retain their meanings. The layout sets width. Disabled controls leave the tab order; read-only values remain focusable and copyable.

Focus draws one continuous 2px edge over the field border, without a gap or a second ring. Invalid fields keep that edge in the error color. The field and its text stay in place when focus changes; InputGroup owns the edge when the input has addons.

_Example: story `Stories.InputMatrix`._
_Example: story `Stories.InField`._
_Example: story `Stories.Kinds`._

## Accessibility

Use FieldLabel with `htmlFor` and the input’s `id`, or another explicit accessible name. Reference hint/error IDs with `aria-describedby`, and pass `aria-invalid` and `aria-required` to the input. Native `required` enables browser validation. A placeholder gives an example and never replaces the label.

Native `onChange` remains supported. Search clearing and application shortcuts are caller-owned; Input does not install an Escape handler. Use an accessible InputGroupButton when a clear action is needed.

## Props

`InputProps` extends Base UI Input with Ledger's `size`. Refs and events target the native input; `render`, state callbacks for `className`/`style`, and `onValueChange(value, details)` are forwarded. A value change may be cancelled with `details.cancel()`.

_Example: story `Stories.NativeComposition`._
_Example: story `Stories.Playground`._

## Related

[InputGroup](?path=/docs/components-inputgroup--docs) · [Textarea](?path=/docs/components-textarea--docs) · [Field](?path=/docs/components-field--docs) · [Select](?path=/docs/components-select--docs) · [shadcn Input](https://ui.shadcn.com/docs/components/base/input) · [Base UI Input](https://base-ui.com/react/components/input)

<!-- page: Components/InputGroup (src/stories/components/InputGroup.mdx) -->

# InputGroup

Compose an input or textarea with icons, units and actions using shadcn's InputGroup parts. The group supplies the shared border and focus/invalid appearance.

## Anatomy

```tsx
<Field>
  <FieldLabel htmlFor="inputgroup">Retention</FieldLabel>
  <InputGroup>
    <InputGroupInput id="inputgroup" type="number" defaultValue="90" />
    <InputGroupAddon align="inline-end">
      <InputGroupText>days</InputGroupText>
    </InputGroupAddon>
  </InputGroup>
</Field>
```

Replace `leading` and `trailing` props with InputGroupAddon children. Replace a direct Input/Textarea child with InputGroupInput/InputGroupTextarea. Set width through native style or the surrounding layout.

## Variants and states

Addon alignment is `inline-start` (default), `inline-end`, `block-start` or `block-end`. Inline positions follow text direction. Block addons create a header or footer around the control. InputGroupButton supports `xs`, `sm`, `icon-xs` and `icon-sm`, with Ledger Button variants.

The actual input or textarea supplies focus, invalid, read-only and disabled surface states. Disabling an addon button does not disable or dim the editable field. Focused invalid groups keep their error border and a separate focus outline, matching Input and Textarea.

_Example: story `Stories.Units`._
_Example: story `Stories.Multiline`._
_Example: story `Stories.States`._

## Accessibility

Label the control with Field or an explicit accessible name. Decorative icons use `aria-hidden`; explanatory text and actions remain available to assistive technology. Give icon buttons accessible names. Addon buttons are real keyboard stops and default to `type="button"`. Clicking non-interactive addon space focuses the input or textarea; custom click handlers can cancel this.

_Example: story `Stories.SearchBox`._

## Props

Group and Addon accept native div props and refs; Text accepts span props. Input and Textarea parts preserve their control contracts and refs. Button preserves Ledger Button's native Base UI composition, loading and disabled behavior. There are no configured content slots.

## Related

[Input](?path=/docs/components-input--docs) · [Textarea](?path=/docs/components-textarea--docs) · [Combobox](?path=/docs/components-combobox--docs) · [shadcn InputGroup](https://ui.shadcn.com/docs/components/base/input-group)

<!-- page: Components/Item (src/stories/components/Item.mdx) -->

# Item

A compact record row with aligned identifiers, descriptions, dates and independent actions. Item retains Ledger's record-list layout; Base UI owns link composition and disclosure behavior.

## Anatomy

Item.Group renders an ordered list inside a div. Rows share a six-column grid: disclosure, leading mark, record id, title/body, trailing value and actions. Expanded content starts under the title. A group can supply its heading, count, trailing action and empty message.

_Example: story `Stories.Lists`._

## Variants and states

Use `link` to navigate, `onSelect` for an action, or neither for a plain row. `isActive` marks the selected record. A link takes precedence over onSelect. Secondary actions and disclosure buttons remain outside the title link/button.

`children` display below the row; add `isCollapsible` to fold them. Use `defaultOpen` or controlled `open` with Base UI's `onOpenChange(open, details)`. Call `details.cancel()` to reject a change.

Group `size="compact"` reduces vertical padding. `flush` extends separators and hover backgrounds to the card edges. `idWidth` defaults to 72px; align it across related rows.

_Example: story `Stories.ItemMatrix`._
_Example: story `Stories.Nested`._

## Accessibility

The title is a real anchor or button. Enter follows links; Space activates buttons. Disclosure buttons announce expanded state and reference the linked title's id. Actions are independent tab stops. Plain rows stay out of the tab order unless the caller explicitly supplies tabIndex for programmatic focus.

A group title names the list. Use `labelledBy` when a surrounding section already provides the heading. Keep link titles descriptive; meta and trailing values are separate from the link's accessible name.

_Example: story `Stories.NativeIntegration`._

## Props

_Props: generated from `Item`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._
_Props: generated from `Item.Group`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._

Item forwards native li attributes, styles, events and refs. Its existing `id`, `title` and `onSelect` props keep their record-content/action meanings. Item.Group forwards native div attributes and refs to the outer wrapper; its `title` remains the visible group heading. Styles merge with the standalone row grid.

`link={<Link to="/record" />}` uses Base UI useRender to preserve the supplied link's attributes, ref, handlers and id. Leave the link empty to use Item's configured title. Explicit link children follow Base UI's rendered-element precedence. No router dependency is added.

_Example: story `Stories.Playground`._
_Rendered in the Storybook: Controls._

## Related

[Table](?path=/docs/components-table--docs) for comparing rows, [Tree](?path=/docs/components-tree--docs) for deeper hierarchy, [Related](?path=/docs/patterns-related--docs) for a record card, and [Collapsible](?path=/docs/components-collapsible--docs) for a whole section.

Sources: [shadcn Item](https://ui.shadcn.com/docs/components/base/item), [Base UI useRender](https://base-ui.com/react/utils/use-render). Ledger keeps its aligned record rows and separate actions as a product extension.

<!-- page: Components/Kbd (src/stories/components/Kbd.mdx) -->

# Kbd

Keyboard input displayed as a keycap, in text, tooltips and menu hints. Use `KbdGroup`
to show the keys of a shortcut together. The existing `Kbd.Group` alias also works.

_Example: story `Stories.KbdMatrix`._

## Anatomy

Both parts render native `<kbd>` elements and accept their native props and refs.
`Kbd` draws a 16px-tall cap, at least 16px wide, using the sunken surface, default
border, extra-small radius and small text tokens. `KbdGroup` spaces its caps 4px apart.

```tsx

<KbdGroup>
  <Kbd label="Command">⌘</Kbd>
  <Kbd>K</Kbd>
</KbdGroup>
```

Use separate caps when that makes a multi-key shortcut easier to read. Choose the
platform's keys in the calling application. There is no platform detection or shortcut
handler inside these components.

## Accessibility

`<kbd>` marks up keyboard input. Caps and groups have no built-in focus or activation
behavior; the surrounding button or menu item owns the action. Keep the action's name
in the surrounding text, such as “Press Command K to search.”

Use `label` to supply a glyph's `aria-label`; an explicit `aria-label` takes precedence.
Screen-reader handling of glyphs and labels varies, so the shortcut should remain
understandable from its visible text and context.

## Props

`className`, `style`, attributes, events and `ref` target each part's own `<kbd>`.
Both refs use `HTMLElement`. Parts expose `data-slot="kbd"` and `data-slot="kbd-group"`.

_Props: generated from `Kbd`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._

### Playground

_Example: story `Stories.Playground`._
_Rendered in the Storybook: Controls._

## Migration

Existing `Kbd`, `label`, and `Kbd.Group` callers need no edits. Native attributes and
refs are now supported on both parts; use the flat `KbdGroup` export for new compositions.
Geometry and token styling are unchanged.

## Related

- [Tooltip](?path=/docs/components-tooltip--docs): show a shortcut beside an action's name.
- [DropdownMenu](?path=/docs/components-dropdownmenu--docs): put a shortcut in an item's `trailing` slot.
- [Command](?path=/docs/components-command--docs): keyboard hints in the palette.

<!-- page: Components/KeyValue (src/stories/components/KeyValue.mdx) -->

# KeyValue

One rail row: a label column and a value. Owner, Frequency, Last verified, each on its own line with the label in a fixed column so the values make a column too. It is a definition list of one pair, valid wherever it sits. The shape every rail writes by hand.

It is one of two ways to write a fact. A [Fact](?path=/docs/components-fact--docs) is inline, label then value on one baseline, for the strip under a record's title; a KeyValue is a row, for the rail and the inspector.

_Example: story `Stories.KeyValueMatrix`._

## Anatomy

| Part  | What it is                                                                                                                             |
| ----- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Label | `dt` in the label column, `labelWidth` wide (104 by default), `font.body` in `color.text.subtle`, truncating.                          |
| Value | `dd` in the rest, `font.body` in `color.text`: text, a Badge, a Person, a TextLink, an Absent. Truncates with its title unless `wrap`. |
| Row   | `space.050` above and below, `space.150` between label and value, baselines aligned.                                                   |

## Variants

KeyValue has one appearance. What varies is the value:

| The value              | Use               |
| ---------------------- | ----------------- |
| A word, a name, a date | Text.             |
| A state                | A Badge.          |
| A person               | A Person.         |
| A record               | A TextLink.       |
| A statement            | Text with `wrap`. |
| Nothing                | An Absent.        |

Not built, and why: a group component, because each KeyValue is its own definition list so it is valid inside any pattern, and the rail's group is the Inspector's; a label-over-value layout, because that shape is a decision still open; an editable value, because that is an [Editable](?path=/docs/patterns-editable--docs) inside the value.

## Sizes

One size, `font.body`. The row is as wide as its rail; the label column is `labelWidth`, the same for every row in one rail, and the value takes the rest. The Glance uses 88, a rail 104; a rail with long labels ("Authorizing official") sets 160 on every row.

_Example: story `Stories.InRail`._

## States

A KeyValue has one state. Its value may: a Badge is a state, a TextLink hovers. The row does not.

## Modifiers

- **`labelWidth`**: the label column, the same down one rail.
- **`wrap`** for a value that is a sentence.
- **The value** as in Variants.

## Content

- **The label is a noun**, one or two words, no colon: "Owner", "Last verified", "Next due". The column is the colon.
- **The value is one thing.** Two facts are two rows.
- **Nothing there is an Absent**, not an empty row and not "N/A", which is a different fact.
- **The order is the order the reader asks:** who, how often, when last, when next, then the rest.

## Style

| Element | Token                                                               |
| ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Label   | `font.body` · `color.text.subtle` · `labelWidth` column             |
| Value   | `font.body` · `color.text`                                          |
| Row     | `space.050` block · `space.150` between columns · baselines aligned |

## Accessibility

- **It is a definition list**: `dl`, `dt`, `dd`, so a screen reader hears "Owner, Dana Whitfield" as a pair, and a rail of them as a series of pairs.
- **A truncated string value carries its full text as the title**, so a hover reads it; a value that matters whole takes `wrap` so no one has to hover.
- **The label is text, not a heading.** A rail's sections are headed by an Eyebrow or a Collapsible; the label names one fact.
- **Contrast:** the label in `color.text.subtle` passes 4.5:1; the gate runs the matrix.

## Props

Native `dl` props and refs target the definition-list root. Use IDs, data attributes and event handlers directly; `className` merges with the default row classes, and caller `style` can override the columns computed from `labelWidth`. The inner `dt`/`dd`, wrapping behavior and title on a truncated string value are preserved.

_Props: generated from `KeyValue`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._

### Playground

_Example: story `Stories.Playground`._

_Rendered in the Storybook: Controls._

## Related

- [Fact](?path=/docs/components-fact--docs): the inline pair, and the strip under a title.
- [Typography](?path=/docs/components-typography--docs): `Eyebrow` to head a group of rows, `Prose` for a paragraph, `Absent` for nothing.
- [Glance](?path=/docs/patterns-glance--docs), [Panel](?path=/docs/layout-shell--docs): where rails of KeyValues live.

## Don't

_Example: story `Stories.Dont`._

<!-- page: Components/Mode (src/stories/components/Mode.mdx) -->

# Mode

The colour mode: light, dark, or whatever the machine says. It is one attribute on the root, `data-color-mode`, and every token reads it, so the whole product flips at once and no component knows. The choice is the reader's, per browser, in `localStorage` under `ledger.color-mode`; never per account, so a shared machine keeps each person's choice. **`modeScript`** applies the stored choice before the first paint, **`ModeProvider`** owns it, **`ModeSwitch`** is the control.

It is the one setting that belongs to the document. Row [density](?path=/docs/components-density--docs) is a table's; the shell's widths are the shell's.

_Example: story `Stories.Live`._

## Anatomy

| Part           | What it is                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| -------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Attribute      | `data-color-mode="light"` or `"dark"` on the root pins a mode; no attribute lets `prefers-color-scheme` decide. `tokens.css` and `base.css` read it.                                                                        |
| Script         | `modeScript`: a string for the document head, above the stylesheet. It applies the stored choice before the first paint so nothing flashes. `modeScriptFor(key)` for another storage key.                                    |
| Provider       | `ModeProvider`: owns the choice. On mount it reads storage and applies it (a no-op after the script); every change is stored and applied at once. `useMode()` returns `{ mode, setMode, resolved }`, `resolved` being what is on screen. |
| Switch         | `ModeSwitch`: a ToggleGroup of three, sun, moon and monitor, `sm`. Icons only in chrome; `showLabels` in a settings form.                                                                                                |

## Variants

One control, in two forms. **Icons only**, in the top navigation's end, where the reader expects it and a label would be noise. **With labels**, `showLabels`, in a settings form, where the three words sit in a row of other settings.

There is no two-state form. A light-or-dark toggle has no answer for a machine that changes at dusk, and it pins a choice the reader never made; system is the default and the third state.

_Example: story `Stories.ControlledStory`._

## Sizes

One: the ToggleGroup's `sm`, 28px, the height of the chrome it sits in.

## States

| State    | Look                                                                                                                       |
| -------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Light    | The root pinned light; the sun is the selected item.                                                                       |
| Dark     | The root pinned dark; the moon.                                                                                            |
| System   | No attribute; the monitor. What is on screen follows the machine, and `resolved` says which.                               |
| Hover, focus, selected | The ToggleGroup's: the item tints, takes the kit's focus outline, and the selected one carries the selected fill. |

_Example: story `Stories.ModeMatrix`._

## Modifiers

- **`value` and `onChange`** on the switch override the provider, for a settings form that commits later, or for a story.
- **`showLabels`**, as in Variants.
- **`storageKey`** on the provider and **`modeScriptFor(key)`**, when a product keeps its own key. The two must agree.
- **`aria-label`** on the switch: "Appearance" by default.

## Content

- **The three words are Light, Dark and System.** Not "Match system", not "Auto", not "Night".
- **The switch's name is Appearance.** The reader is choosing how the product looks, not a "theme".
- **Never a colour by hand.** A hex value written into a component does not flip; every colour is a token, and the mode flips the tokens.
- **Never a mode-specific screen.** A page does not know which mode it is in; if a figure needs a different colour in dark, that colour is a token with two values.

## Style

| Element   | Token                                                                                              |
| --------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Switch    | The ToggleGroup, `sm`: `dimension.control.small` 28px · `dimension.icon.small` 14px              |
| Attribute | `data-color-mode` on `html` · every `color.*` and `elevation.*` token has a light and a dark value  |
| Motion    | None. A mode changes at once; a fade across every surface reads as a fault.                        |

## Accessibility

- **The switch is a group of toggle buttons** named Appearance. Each button has `aria-pressed` and an accessible name, including Light, Dark and System when only icons are visible.
- **Keyboard:** Tab enters and leaves the group as one stop; Left and Right move focus, and Space or Enter selects. The switch retains a selected mode when it is pressed again.
- **System honours the reader's machine,** including `prefers-color-scheme` set for a vision reason, so it is the default and never overridden by the product.
- **Contrast is tested in both modes:** every pairing on the Colour sheet, and the a11y gate runs each matrix in the mode the toolbar sets.
- **No flash:** the script marks the root before the first paint, so a reader who chose dark never sees a light page load.

## Props

_Props: generated from `ModeSwitch`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._

The provider and the script, by hand:

| Export          | What it is                                                                                                  |
| --------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `ModeProvider`  | Wraps the app; `storageKey` for a key of the product's own. Renders nothing itself.                         |
| `useMode()`     | `{ mode, setMode, resolved }`. Throws outside a provider.                                                   |
| `modeScript`    | The before-paint script for the default key; `modeScriptFor(key)` for another.                              |
| `readMode`, `writeMode`, `applyMode` | The three steps the provider takes, for a product that wires them itself.                  |

### Wiring it

Plain HTML: put the script in the head, above the stylesheet.

```html
<script>
  (function () {
    try {
      var m = localStorage.getItem("ledger.color-mode");
      if (m === "light" || m === "dark") document.documentElement.dataset.colorMode = m;
    } catch (e) {}
  })();
</script>
```

A framework with a `head()` hook renders the same string inline:

```tsx

head: () => ({ scripts: [{ children: modeScript }] });
// …
<ModeProvider>
  <Shell>
    <Shell.TopNav>
      …
      <Shell.TopNav.End>
        <ModeSwitch />
      </Shell.TopNav.End>
    </Shell.TopNav>
    …
  </Shell>
</ModeProvider>;
```

Do not also pin `data-color-mode` on the root in markup: the pin wins over the script and the switch cannot move it. Put `suppressHydrationWarning` on the `<html>` element: the script marks it before React hydrates, and React would otherwise report the mismatch.

### Playground

_Example: story `Stories.Playground`._

_Rendered in the Storybook: Controls._

## Related

- [Colour](?path=/docs/tokens-color--docs): every token's two values.
- [ToggleGroup](?path=/docs/components-togglegroup--docs): the control the switch is.
- [Shell](?path=/docs/layout-shell--docs): where the switch sits, in the top navigation's end.
- [Density](?path=/docs/components-density--docs): the setting that is a table's, not the document's.

## Don't

_Example: story `Stories.Dont`._

<!-- page: Components/Overlays (src/stories/components/Overlays.mdx) -->

# Overlays

Everything that floats over the page, from the smallest label to a full task. Four are anchored to the thing that opened them and four cover the page under a blanket. The anchored and modal overlays all use Base UI. Modal overlays manage focus and page scrolling; anchored previews keep focus on their trigger. The surfaces share one recipe, `elevation.surface.overlay`, `elevation.shadow.overlay`, the large radius, the enter and exit motion, so a product's overlays read as one family.

Each part has its own page: [Tooltip](?path=/docs/components-tooltip--docs), [HoverCard](?path=/docs/components-hovercard--docs), [Popover](?path=/docs/components-popover--docs), [DropdownMenu](?path=/docs/components-dropdownmenu--docs), [Dialog](?path=/docs/components-dialog--docs), [Sheet](?path=/docs/components-sheet--docs), [Drawer](?path=/docs/components-drawer--docs), [AlertDialog](?path=/docs/components-alertdialog--docs).

## Variants

| Need                                                             | Use              | Opens on                            | Closes on                              |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------- | ----------------------------------- | -------------------------------------- |
| A short label                                                    | **Tooltip**      | Hover or focus, after 300ms         | Leaving, Escape                        |
| A peek at a record: a few facts, no actions                      | **HoverCard**    | Hover or focus, after 600ms         | Leaving, Escape                        |
| A small task at its button: a filter, a reason, a picker         | **Popover**      | Click                               | Escape, outside click, Done            |
| A list of actions                                                | **DropdownMenu** | Click, Enter, Space, the down arrow | Choosing, Escape, outside click        |
| A focused task over the page                                     | **Dialog**       | The caller's state                  | Escape, the blanket, Cancel, the verb  |
| A modal selection, review or explicitly scoped parent-draft task | **Sheet**        | The caller's state                  | Escape, the blanket, the footer's verb |
| The bottom sheet, for a narrow screen and a quick task           | **Drawer**       | The caller's state                  | A drag down, Escape, the blanket       |
| A decision that needs a word before it happens                   | **AlertDialog**  | The caller's state                  | Cancel, Escape, the verb               |

_Example: story `Stories.Anchored`._

_Example: story `Stories.Modal`._

## Anatomy

- **The anchored four** sit beside their trigger, 4 to 6px off it, flipping when there is no room, with Tooltip adding a small arrow. A Tooltip is the dark one, `color.background.neutral.bold` with inverse text; the other three are the overlay surface with a hairline border.
- **The blanketed four** paint `color.blanket` over the page; nothing else paints it. Their surface is `elevation.surface.overlay` with `radius.xxlarge` (a Sheet has square corners, since it is an edge), a header with the title in `font.heading.xsmall`, a body that scrolls, a footer on `elevation.surface.sunken` with the buttons at the end.
- **The close** is one shared icon button at the top end, `dimension.control.small`. AlertDialog and Drawer compose explicit action buttons; a Drawer’s optional swipe handle is decorative.

## Accessibility

- **Focus moves in** when a blanketed overlay opens (Drawer focuses its popup by default; initialFocus can target an action or field) and **returns** to what opened it when it closes. The page behind is hidden from assistive technology and does not scroll.
- **Escape closes** every overlay. An outside click closes the anchored ones and the blanket closes a Dialog, a Sheet and a Drawer; an AlertDialog ignores it.
- **Pending holds.** The caller blocks `onOpenChange` while saving and disables repeated actions: Escape, the blanket and Close do nothing until the save returns.
- **A tooltip never holds a control**, a hover card never holds an action, a popover never holds a task the reader must finish.

## Style

- **One blanket at a time.** An AlertDialog may open over a Sheet or a Dialog, for the decision the task ends in; that is the only stack. Independent stacked record workflows should navigate or replace the current frame. A selection workflow owns its internal preview.
- **A sheet's next record is its next frame**, not a second sheet: the same surface, the chevron before the title, `onBack`, the stack in the URL so the browser's back agrees.
- **Anchored overlays stack on anything.** A Tooltip in a Dialog, a DropdownMenu in a Sheet, a Popover in a Drawer are fine; a Popover in a Popover is not.

_Example: story `Stories.Stacked`._

## Props

- **Trigger composition follows each component's API**: Popover uses `PopoverTrigger render={<Button />}`; DropdownMenu uses `DropdownMenuTrigger render` and `DropdownMenuContent`; Tooltip uses `TooltipTrigger render` and `TooltipContent`. HoverCard uses `HoverCardTrigger`, an anchor by default, with `render` for a custom link. Custom trigger components must forward their props and ref.
- **The blanketed four are opened by state**: `open` and `onOpenChange`. An act sets it; the caller clears it. Nothing opens a Dialog for the reader who did not ask.
- **Where the task lives decides the overlay.** At the button: Popover. An independent focused form: Dialog. Beside a usable list: Shell.Panel. A specifically modal selection or review task: Sheet. Under the thumb: Drawer.

## Content

- The blanket is `color.blanket`; nothing else paints it.
- A blanketed overlay's title is the act's verb (a Dialog), the record's name (a Sheet), or the question (an AlertDialog). Its primary button says the verb, never OK.
- What the reader must know is on the page or in the body, never only in a tooltip or a hover card.
- An overlay is never the record. The record has a page; the overlay is the way to it or the task on it.

## Sizes

Choose the smallest surface that fits the task. Content must reflow at a 320 CSS pixel viewport; the body scrolls independently when a header and footer must remain available. Check long titles, translated buttons, and browser zoom. A large task with navigation belongs on a page.

## States

Closed, open, pending, failed and completed are separate states. Keep the surface and draft open on failure and explain how to retry. A pending operation must settle or expose a recovery path. Close only after a successful command or an explicit cancel.

## Modifiers

Controlled modal surfaces accept `returnFocusRef` for asynchronous opening, a removed trigger, or a deliberate replacement target. Without it, they capture the active opener before moving focus into the surface. The target must remain connected and focusable after closing. `pending` prevents dismissal while supported saves are in flight.

## Related

See Forms for validation and focus on error, Button for activation semantics, and Toaster for nonblocking completion feedback. Each overlay's page documents its exact dismissal contract.

## Don't

Do not rely on a toast as the only record of a failure, hide required instructions in a tooltip, nest independent modal tasks, or remove the opener without specifying a meaningful focus destination. Do not make a hover-only surface the sole route to an action.

<!-- page: Components/Pagination (src/stories/components/Pagination.mdx) -->

# Pagination

Navigation between pages using [shadcn’s flat Pagination parts](https://ui.shadcn.com/docs/components/base/pagination). The caller owns page state, URLs and result counts.

## Anatomy

```tsx
<Pagination aria-label="Control pages">
  <PaginationContent>
    <PaginationItem>
      <PaginationPrevious href="?page=1" />
    </PaginationItem>
    <PaginationItem>
      <PaginationLink href="?page=2" isActive>
        2
      </PaginationLink>
    </PaginationItem>
    <PaginationItem>
      <PaginationEllipsis />
    </PaginationItem>
    <PaginationItem>
      <PaginationNext href="?page=3" />
    </PaginationItem>
  </PaginationContent>
</Pagination>
```

Root is a nav, Content a list and Item a list item. Link uses a real anchor with the shared Button recipe. Base UI 1.7 Button adds button semantics even when rendered as an anchor, so Ledger preserves native link semantics here. Previous and Next are links with localized names, optional `text` and direction-aware icons.

_Example: story `Stories.Links`._

## Variants and states

`isActive` sets `aria-current="page"` and the selected appearance. All links accept native anchor attributes, events and refs, including href, target and rel. Ellipsis is decorative.

For in-memory tables, compose Button inside PaginationItem with native disabled and aria-current attributes. The internal DataTable pagination pattern owns page calculation, empty results and row-range text, using those same parts.

_Example: story `Stories.InMemoryTable`._
_Example: story `Stories.ManyPages`._

## Accessibility

Name each navigation region distinctly. Use links for URLs and buttons for local state changes. An unavailable link needs caller-owned semantics and activation handling; anchors have no native disabled attribute. Prefer omitting unavailable navigation links or rendering a disabled Button for an in-memory pager. RTL arrows follow the enclosing direction.

## Props

The configured `page`, `pageCount`, `onPageChange`, `total`, `pageSize` and `label` API is removed. Use native `aria-label` and explicit children. DataTable retains its page-size and table-state API; its internal composition preserves result counts and page controls.

_Props: generated from `Pagination`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._
_Props: generated from `PaginationLink`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._
_Props: generated from `PaginationPrevious`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._
_Props: generated from `PaginationNext`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._

## Related

[DataTable](?path=/docs/patterns-datatable--docs), [Table](?path=/docs/components-table--docs), [Button](?path=/docs/components-button--docs).

<!-- page: Components/Popover (src/stories/components/Popover.mdx) -->

# Popover

An anchored dialog for controls, forms and supporting content. It follows shadcn's Base UI composition, with Ledger's surface, spacing and motion tokens.

```tsx
<Popover>
  <PopoverTrigger render={<Button />}>Review schedule</PopoverTrigger>
  <PopoverContent>
    <PopoverHeader>
      <PopoverTitle>Review schedule</PopoverTitle>
      <PopoverDescription>Reviews occur every quarter.</PopoverDescription>
    </PopoverHeader>
    <PopoverClose render={<Button />}>Done</PopoverClose>
  </PopoverContent>
</Popover>
```

## Composition

Root owns open state. Trigger and Close render native buttons by default; use `render` to compose Button, IconButton or FilterChip. Trigger's `nativeButton={false}` supports a custom element with button semantics. Custom components must forward their props and ref.

Content includes the portal and positioner. Native props, `ref`, `render`, and state callbacks for `className` or `style` apply to the popup. Title and Description connect their content to the dialog's accessible name and description; Header supplies their layout. When no visible title fits, give Content an `aria-label`.

Content defaults to 288px wide, `side="bottom"`, `sideOffset={4}`, `align="center"` and `alignOffset={0}`. Override width with `style={{ width: 300 }}` or match the trigger with `style={{ width: "var(--anchor-width)" }}`. The positioner handles collisions. Logical sides and alignment follow the Ledger locale; Content's `dir` can override it.

_Example: story `Stories.PopoverMatrix`._

## Focus and dismissal

Click, Enter or Space activates the trigger. Focus moves to the first tabbable control, or the popup if it has none. Touch opening focuses the popup to avoid opening a virtual keyboard. Content's `initialFocus` and `finalFocus` support explicit focus destinations.

The default `modal={false}` leaves the page reachable. Tab moves through controls and can leave the popup, dismissing it. Escape and Close dismiss it and return focus to the trigger; an outside press dismisses it while allowing the clicked control to receive focus.

For focus trapping, use Root's `modal="trap-focus"` and include `PopoverClose` inside Content. `modal={true}` additionally restricts outside interaction; see the upstream API for its scrolling behavior. Base UI 1.7 requires the Close part inside the popup to enable its focus trap.

Inside an existing Dialog, Sheet or Drawer, the popup stays within that surface's focus scope. Escape closes the popup first and returns focus to its trigger; a subsequent Escape can dismiss the enclosing surface.

_Example: story `Stories.Options`._

## Controlled tasks

Use `defaultOpen` for local initial state, or `open` and `onOpenChange(open, details)` for caller-owned state. `details.cancel()` rejects an open-state change. Keep form drafts in caller state when they should survive dismissal, and close after the task succeeds.

_Example: story `Stories.Task`._

## Migration and API

Replace the old `trigger` prop with `PopoverTrigger render`, move the body into `PopoverContent`, and replace `Popover.Close` with `PopoverClose render`. Move `label` to a Title or Content's `aria-label`; move placement and sizing onto Content. `width` becomes `style.width`, and `matchTriggerWidth` becomes `width: "var(--anchor-width)"`. State attributes follow Base UI, including `data-open`.

The flat parts retain their upstream props: [Root](https://base-ui.com/react/components/popover#root), [Trigger](https://base-ui.com/react/components/popover#trigger), [Popup](https://base-ui.com/react/components/popover#popup), [Title](https://base-ui.com/react/components/popover#title), [Description](https://base-ui.com/react/components/popover#description), and [Close](https://base-ui.com/react/components/popover#close). Content additionally exposes the four positioning props above; Header accepts native div props. See [shadcn's composition examples](https://ui.shadcn.com/docs/components/base/popover).

## Related

[FilterChip](?path=/docs/components-filterchip--docs) · [DatePicker](?path=/docs/components-datepicker--docs) · [Combobox](?path=/docs/components-combobox--docs) · [Dialog](?path=/docs/components-dialog--docs) · [Overlays](?path=/docs/components-overlays--docs)

# Progress

Based on [shadcn’s Base UI source](https://ui.shadcn.com/docs/components/base/progress) and [Base UI](https://base-ui.com/react/components/progress). Ledger retains its tokens and application layouts.

## Anatomy

Task completion using Base UI Progress. Progress supplies its default Track and Indicator; ProgressLabel and ProgressValue are optional children. ProgressTrack and ProgressIndicator expose the corresponding native parts for custom composition under Base UI’s root. ProgressStacked remains the separate proportional coverage bar.

## Variants

_Example: story `Stories.ValuesAndRanges`._

_Example: story `Stories.LabelAndValue`._

_Example: story `Stories.StackedCoverage`._

_Example: story `Stories.CustomTrack`._

## Accessibility

Name meaningful bars through ProgressLabel or aria-label. Mark redundant decorative bars aria-hidden. Base UI keeps the indicator width, bounded value and accessible value in sync for min/max; null or a nonfinite value is indeterminate. Interactive stacked segments keep individual button names.

## Props

Progress exposes Base UI native root props and ref, including value, min/max, formatting, locale, render and state callbacks. Ledger tone and small/medium/large track sizes remain. Label, Value, Track and Indicator expose their corresponding native contracts.

### Migration and API

- Replace label with aria-label or ProgressLabel; valueText with aria-valuetext; showValue with ProgressValue children.
- Replace Progress.Stacked with ProgressStacked. Existing tone, size and coverage segment APIs remain.
- ProgressValue defaults to the formatted percentage; its children callback can display counts. Base UI performs clamping; the wrapper no longer calculates a second percentage.

## Related

- [Gates](?path=/docs/patterns-gates--docs)
- [Chart](?path=/docs/patterns-chart--docs)

<!-- page: Components/RadioGroup (src/stories/components/RadioGroup.mdx) -->

# RadioGroup

One selected value from a set of visible choices, using the shadcn Base UI composition. `RadioGroupItem` includes the circular indicator; labels and supporting content are composed outside it.

```tsx
<RadioGroup aria-label="Frequency" defaultValue="quarterly">
  <label className="inline-flex items-center gap-100">
    <RadioGroupItem value="monthly" /> Monthly
  </label>
  <label className="inline-flex items-center gap-100">
    <RadioGroupItem value="quarterly" /> Quarterly
  </label>
</RadioGroup>
```

_Example: story `Stories.RadioGroupMatrix`._

## Selection and layout

Use `defaultValue` for local state, or `value` and `onValueChange(value, details)` for controlled state. Selecting an item clears the previous selection; selecting it again keeps it selected. `details.cancel()` rejects a change. `disabled` blocks interaction; `readOnly` allows focus while keeping the selected value unchanged. Both props can apply to the group or an individual item.

The indicator is a 16px circle with an 8px dot. The selected circle uses Ledger's brand fill and a contrasting dot. The group defaults to a grid with an 8px gap. Use classes such as `flex flex-row flex-wrap gap-200` for a horizontal layout; there is no `orientation` prop.

Tab enters and leaves the group as one stop. All four arrow keys move focus and select, skipping disabled items and wrapping at the ends. Horizontal arrows follow the Ledger locale direction, which `dir` on the group can override. Space selects the focused item; Enter does not select it. Home/End and configurable focus wrapping are not part of the installed API.

_Example: story `Stories.Orientation`._

## Labels, Field and forms

Name the group with `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`, which can point to a [FieldLegend](?path=/docs/components-field--docs) inside FieldSet. A wrapping label or a sibling label with `htmlFor` names each item and selects it when clicked. Put descriptions in ordinary elements and reference them with the item's `aria-describedby`.

Compose FieldSet/FieldLegend and reference description/error IDs on the group with `aria-describedby`. Pass `aria-invalid` and `aria-required` explicitly. Pass `aria-invalid` to individual items when their indicators should show the error treatment. Native `required` on RadioGroup makes its hidden radio inputs participate in browser validation; `aria-required` supplies the accessible required state.

`name` and `form` associate the hidden inputs with native submission. The selected item's value is submitted. Native form reset is caller-owned in Base UI 1.7: restore controlled `value` in the form's `onReset` handler.

_Example: story `Stories.InField`._

## Native props and composition

The group renders a div with `role="radiogroup"`. Each item renders a span with `role="radio"` and `aria-checked`, plus a hidden input. Item `ref` targets the visible control; `inputRef` and `id` target its hidden input. Group `inputRef` follows the selected input, or an enabled input when none is selected.

`render` composes a custom element and merges props, classes, styles and refs. An item rendered as a button uses `nativeButton` with `render={<button />}`; its `id` then targets the visible button. `className` and `style` accept Base UI state callbacks.

## Migration

Replace `RadioGroup.Item` with `RadioGroupItem`. Move label children and `description` into external labels and description elements. Replace `orientation="horizontal"` with layout classes. Selection values and callbacks use Base UI's generic value API, including the cancellable event details argument.

## Props

_Props: generated from `RadioGroup`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._

_Props: generated from `RadioGroupItem`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._

_Example: story `Stories.Playground`._

_Rendered in the Storybook: Controls._

## Related

[Field](?path=/docs/components-field--docs) · [Forms](?path=/docs/patterns-forms--docs) · [Checkbox](?path=/docs/components-checkbox--docs) · [shadcn Radio Group](https://ui.shadcn.com/docs/components/base/radio-group) · [Base UI Radio](https://base-ui.com/react/components/radio)

# Resizable

User-sized panes following [shadcn’s Resizable source](https://ui.shadcn.com/docs/components/base/resizable), built on react-resizable-panels. A plain dividing rule is a Separator.

## Anatomy

```tsx
<ResizablePanelGroup>
  <ResizablePanel defaultSize="30%" minSize="20%">
    List
  </ResizablePanel>
  <ResizableHandle aria-label="Resize the list" withHandle />
  <ResizablePanel>Detail</ResizablePanel>
</ResizablePanelGroup>
```

Give the group a sized parent. Panels clip their contents; put ScrollArea inside a scrolling pane. `withHandle` adds a visible grip.

_Example: story `Stories.Panes`._

## Variants and states

`orientation="vertical"` stacks panes. Native panel props include minimum/maximum sizes, collapse behavior and resize callbacks. The library owns layout, pointer resizing and keyboard behavior.

_Example: story `Stories.Vertical`._
_Example: story `Stories.Collapsible`._

Persist layouts where the composition needs it. Use the upstream `useDefaultLayout` hook, stable group/panel IDs and the hook’s `defaultLayout`/`onLayoutChanged` pair. Preserve an existing ID to read its saved layouts. Supply server-safe storage when rendering the hook on the server; the story demonstrates this explicitly.

_Example: story `Stories.Persisted`._

## Accessibility

The handle is a focusable separator with the orientation of the rule: a horizontal group has a vertical separator. Arrow keys resize; Home/End reach bounds; Enter toggles a collapsible panel. Name handles with `aria-label`, especially when several splits are present. Group and Panel expose native `elementRef`, `groupRef` and `panelRef` instead of translating them into a generic ref.

## Props

Replace `Resizable` with `ResizablePanelGroup`, `.Panel` with `ResizablePanel`, and `.Handle` with `ResizableHandle`. Replace handle `label` with `aria-label`; move `persist` into the native hook at the caller. **Numeric sizes now mean pixels.** Change old percentage numbers such as `minSize={20}` to `minSize="20%"`. Existing PreviewSplit proportions are preserved.

_Props: generated from `ResizablePanelGroup`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._
_Props: generated from `ResizablePanel`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._
_Props: generated from `ResizableHandle`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._

## Related

[Shell.Panel](?path=/docs/layout-pages--docs), [ScrollArea](?path=/docs/components-scrollarea--docs), [Separator](?path=/docs/components-separator--docs).

# ScrollArea

Based on [shadcn’s Base UI source](https://ui.shadcn.com/docs/components/base/scroll-area) and [Base UI](https://base-ui.com/react/components/scroll-area). Ledger retains its tokens and application layouts.

## Anatomy

A bounded scrolling region following shadcn’s ScrollArea and ScrollBar composition. ScrollArea includes the viewport, a vertical scrollbar and corner. Add ScrollBar with orientation="horizontal" for horizontal overflow.

## Variants

_Example: story `Stories.Vertical`._

_Example: story `Stories.HorizontalAndRTL`._

## Accessibility

Base UI manages keyboard scrolling, scrollbar geometry and dragging. Its viewport becomes keyboard-reachable when it overflows. Use viewportProps to name the scrolling region and expose its native ref/events. Direction follows LedgerProvider or explicit dir.

## Props

Root exposes Base UI ScrollArea props, native refs, render and state callbacks; viewportProps forwards the corresponding viewport contract. ScrollBar exposes native scrollbar props, including orientation and keepMounted. Bars appear when there is overflow, following the source behavior.

### Migration and API

- Replace label with viewportProps containing role="region" and aria-label. Put sizing classes on ScrollArea.
- Replace root orientation="horizontal"/"both" with a horizontal ScrollBar child; overflow determines which bars are needed.
- The old bar visibility shortcut and fixed hide delay are removed. Native state attributes and classes can style hovering/scrolling if needed.

<!-- page: Components/Scroller (src/stories/components/Scroller.mdx) -->

# Scroller

A bounded scrolling region with an arrow at each edge that can still scroll. Select, DropdownMenu, Combobox and horizontal line Tabs compose it, so a long list and a wide strip scroll alike.

## Anatomy

`Scroller` is the bounded box: it sets `orientation`, how an arrow scrolls (`scrollOn`) and the `surface` the arrows sit on. `ScrollerViewport` is the element that scrolls; `render` substitutes a list (Combobox does), and `viewport` on the root points at an element the Scroller does not render (Tabs passes its ScrollArea viewport). `ScrollerArrow` renders one edge: `start` or `end`.

An arrow appears only when the viewport overflows, only at an edge that can still scroll, and only where the pointer can hover (`hover: hover` and `pointer: fine`); touch readers swipe and see none. While arrows show they replace the native scrollbar, and the viewport keeps their thickness clear as scroll padding, so a focused or highlighted item scrolls out from under them.

## Vertical

Vertical scrollers scroll on hover unsaid: the arrow is a hover zone, hidden from assistive technology, and keyboard readers already move through the content. Menus use the `overlay` surface.

_Example: story `Stories.Vertical`._

## Horizontal

Horizontal scrollers step a page on click unsaid: the arrow is a labelled button outside the tab order that reads as one (a pointer cursor, a hover tint and a hairline on its inner edge), and it follows the locale's direction. Pass `scrollOn` to change either default.

_Example: story `Stories.Horizontal`._

## Composition

Select keeps Base UI's own scroll arrows, which step item by item and know the open method; they wear the Scroller arrow classes so the two cannot drift apart. Tabs sizes its arrows to the strip and gives them the strip's hairline. Do not add a second scroller, an overflow utility or a fade inside a part that already composes one.

## Props

_Props: generated from `Scroller`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._

_Props: generated from `ScrollerViewport`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._

_Props: generated from `ScrollerArrow`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._

## Related

- [ScrollArea](?path=/docs/components-scrollarea--docs)
- [Select](?path=/docs/components-select--docs)
- [Tabs](?path=/docs/components-tabs--docs)

<!-- page: Components/Select (src/stories/components/Select.mdx) -->

# Select

Choose predefined values with shadcn's Base UI Select parts. Ledger supplies control geometry, menu styling, locale direction and Field integration. Use Combobox when the list needs filtering.

```tsx
const statuses = { draft: "Draft", review: "In review" };

<Field>
  <FieldLabel htmlFor="select">Status</FieldLabel>
  <Select name="status" items={statuses} defaultValue="draft">
    <SelectTrigger id="select" className="w-full">
      <SelectValue placeholder="Choose a status" />
    </SelectTrigger>
    <SelectContent>
      <SelectItem value="draft">Draft</SelectItem>
      <SelectItem value="review">In review</SelectItem>
    </SelectContent>
  </Select>
</Field>;
```

## Composition and states

Root owns selected values, open state, form props and modality. Trigger owns native button props, refs, render composition, layout and size: `default` is 32px and `sm` is 28px. It fits its contents by default; use `className="w-full"` in a form or native `style` for a fixed width. Value owns the placeholder and displayed value.

Supply Root's `items` label map/array, object-value label conversion, or Value's children to format the selected value. Item children alone do not label the closed trigger. A label can contain the same Dot or Badge shown on the record. Group and Label identify sections; Separator divides them.

`disabled` prevents interaction and omits the value from submission. `readOnly` keeps the value submitted and the trigger focusable while preventing selection. Item's `disabled` state prevents activation but remains reachable with arrows. For decorated option children, provide Item's plain-text `label` for typeahead. Classes, styles, render props and refs follow each Base UI part's native contract.

_Example: story `Stories.SelectMatrix`._

## Forms and selection

Connect FieldLabel to Trigger with `htmlFor`/`id`; put `aria-describedby`, `aria-invalid` and `aria-required` on Trigger. Root’s `required` enables native constraint validation. Native form props (`name`, `form`, `autoComplete`, `inputRef`) belong on Root. Root’s ID supplies the default trigger ID; an explicit Trigger ID takes precedence. `inputRef` targets the hidden form input.

Single selection accepts a value or `null`; `onValueChange(value, details)` can reject a change with `details.cancel()`. Cancellation preserves the value, but an item activation still closes a single-select popup. Add a `null` item when the reader needs to clear from the list. Value's placeholder appears when no value is selected.

`multiple` uses arrays and keeps the list open while toggling options. FormData contains one entry per selected value under the same name. Object values can supply `itemToStringLabel`, `itemToStringValue` and `isItemEqualToValue` for display, submission and identity. Root preserves generic single/multiple inference; Item and Value use the installed Base UI value contracts.

With installed Base UI 1.7, form reset is caller-owned: reset controlled values in the form's `onReset`. The example covers required values, cancelled changes, multiple numeric values and object identity.

_Example: story `Stories.InField`._

## Positioning and scrolling

Content includes Portal, Positioner, Popup, List and both scroll arrows. It defaults to trigger width, a 144px minimum, bottom/center placement, a 4px side offset and zero alignment offset. Native style/className/render/ref props target Popup; `finalFocus` controls focus return.

Following shadcn, `alignItemWithTrigger` defaults to true: when space and input modality allow it, the selected item overlaps and aligns with the trigger value. Side/alignment offsets apply in fallback positioning or when `alignItemWithTrigger={false}`. Existing consumers explicitly retain below-trigger placement with that setting. Content's `dir` overrides inherited positioning direction as well as text direction.

The inner List owns bounded scrolling so hover arrows work in both alignment modes with Base UI 1.7. ScrollUpButton and ScrollDownButton wrap Base UI's hover scroll arrows, including their native props and refs, and wear the [Scroller](?path=/docs/components-scroller--docs) arrow look across the popup's inner box. They appear when scrolling is available and are omitted for touch input. Content includes them automatically; the example composes them directly for custom list geometry, beside the standard Content in RTL.

_Example: story `Stories.Scrolling`._

## Accessibility and dialogs

Trigger is a native button with combobox semantics, expanded state and a listbox association. Options announce selected and disabled state. Enter, Space and ArrowDown open; arrows, Home and End move focus; typing matches labels; Enter/Space select. Closed single-select typeahead changes the selected value. Keep a visible Field label or an explicit accessible name on Trigger. Name Content’s list with `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` when a specific list name is needed. These name the listbox as well as passing through to Popup.

Base UI coordinates nested Select, Dialog and Drawer popups. Escape dismisses Select before the dialog, returning focus to the trigger. Closing the dialog then returns to its opener.

_Example: story `Stories.Dialogs`._

## Migration and API

Replace the configured root with Select, SelectTrigger, SelectValue and SelectContent. Move trigger refs, ARIA, size, styles and event handlers to Trigger; replace `width` with native style and `small`/`medium` with `sm`/`default`. Move the placeholder to Value. Replace compound Item/Group/Separator with flat exports and put SelectLabel inside SelectGroup. Supply labels through `items` or Value; handle nullable single values explicitly.

The implementation follows [shadcn Select](https://ui.shadcn.com/docs/components/base/select) and [Base UI Select](https://base-ui.com/react/components/select), using the installed Base UI version. Content adds shadcn's five positioning props to Popup; Ledger adds token styling and locale/Field/dialog integration.

## Related

[Combobox](?path=/docs/components-combobox--docs) · [Field](?path=/docs/components-field--docs) · [Forms](?path=/docs/patterns-forms--docs) · [DropdownMenu](?path=/docs/components-dropdownmenu--docs)

<!-- page: Components/Separator (src/stories/components/Separator.mdx) -->

# Separator

A hairline between siblings: two blocks in a stack or two groups in a toolbar. Built on the shadcn Base UI Separator, with Ledger's `color.border` and parent-owned spacing. Rows, menus and tables already draw their own rules.

_Example: story `Stories.SeparatorMatrix`._

## Anatomy

One `div` by default, with `data-slot="separator"` and `data-orientation`. The rule is one pixel: a top border spanning the container horizontally, or an inline-start border stretching to the height of a flex row vertically. Stack or Inline supplies the gap around it.

Ledger retains its existing border paint instead of the reference's background-filled line. Both orientations use `color.border`; the component requires no shadcn theme or state-selector aliases.

## Variants and composition

| Option | Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| `orientation="horizontal"` | Default. Spans its container between stacked blocks. |
| `orientation="vertical"` | Stretches inside a flex row, such as an Inline or toolbar. |
| `isDecorative` | Hides a purely visual rule from assistive technology. Defaults to `false`. |
| `render` | Replaces the default element or composes a custom component. |
| `className` / `style` | Accept a value or a callback receiving `{ orientation }`. |

Native props and refs reach the rendered element. Base UI merges props, event handlers, classes, styles and refs from a rendered element. A render callback or custom component must forward the supplied props and ref.

_Example: story `Stories.NativeComposition`._

```tsx
<Separator
  orientation="vertical"
  aria-label="Editing actions"
  className={({ orientation }) =>
    orientation === "vertical" ? "border-bold" : undefined
  }
/>
```

## Accessibility

- By default the element has `role="separator"` and an `aria-orientation` matching its orientation.
- `isDecorative` supplies `role="none"`, `aria-hidden="true"` and no `aria-orientation`. Explicit native role and ARIA props override those defaults; keep them consistent with the intended semantics.
- The default separator has no tab stop. Use Resizable for a keyboard-operable resize handle.
- Place a separator between related groups. Avoid redundant rules around containers or between rows that already draw their own borders.

## Props

`SeparatorProps` includes the Base UI primitive props and Ledger's optional `isDecorative`. See the [Base UI API](https://base-ui.com/react/components/separator#api-reference) for native composition and state callbacks.

_Props: generated from `Separator`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._

_Example: story `Stories.Playground`._

_Rendered in the Storybook: Controls._

## Migration

Existing `orientation`, `isDecorative` and string `className` callers continue to work. Separator now uses Base UI and also accepts native div props, refs, `render`, and callback classes/styles. No consumer rename is required.

`data-slot="separator"` and `data-orientation` are available for integration. The existing one-pixel `color.border` appearance and parent-owned spacing remain. Decorative separators retain their previous hidden semantics.

## Related

- [Stack](?path=/docs/primitives-stack--docs) and [Inline](?path=/docs/primitives-inline--docs): the gap around the rule.
- [Toolbar](?path=/docs/patterns-toolbar--docs): groups separated vertically.
- [Item](?path=/docs/components-item--docs): rows with their own separators.
- [Resizable](?path=/docs/components-resizable--docs): an interactive resize handle.

_Example: story `Stories.Dont`._

<!-- page: Components/Sheet (src/stories/components/Sheet.mdx) -->

# Sheet

Based on [shadcn’s Base UI source](https://ui.shadcn.com/docs/components/base/sheet) and [Base UI](https://base-ui.com/react/components/dialog). Ledger retains its tokens and application layouts.

## Anatomy

An edge panel using Base UI Dialog. Compose Sheet, SheetTrigger, SheetContent, SheetHeader, SheetTitle, SheetDescription, SheetFooter and SheetClose.

## Variants

_Example: story `Stories.EdgesAndScrolling`._

_Example: story `Stories.NestedAndRTL`._

## Accessibility

Base UI provides modal focus trapping, nested dismissal and focus return. Give the panel a title. Keep a close control available; Content includes one by default. Put scrolling on a body child so the header and footer remain reachable.

## Props

Root exposes the generic Base UI Dialog contract. Content accepts native popup props, refs, render, initialFocus and finalFocus, plus side and showCloseButton. The four physical sides follow shadcn; Ledger also accepts start/end for locale-relative edges.

### Migration and API

- Replace title/subtitle/footer shortcuts with Title, Description and Footer children. Eyebrow, facts, back actions and toolbars are ordinary header/body composition.
- Replace onClose with onOpenChange; returnFocusRef becomes Content finalFocus; width becomes Content style.maxWidth.
- Content defaults to physical right and a 420px maximum width for side panels. Migrated callers explicitly use logical end to preserve RTL behavior.
