<!-- page: Components/Skeleton (src/stories/components/Skeleton.mdx) -->

# Skeleton

A placeholder that holds the space of loading content. It follows shadcn's native div contract, with Ledger's line, heading, circle and block options. Use [PageSkeleton](?path=/docs/layout-pageskeleton--docs) for a page's first paint and [Spinner](?path=/docs/components-spinner--docs) for an action in progress.

_Example: story `Stories.SkeletonMatrix`._

## Anatomy

The outer element is a `div` with `data-slot="skeleton"`, hidden from assistive technology by default. A single shape paints this element in `color.skeleton`. With `shape="line"` and `lines > 1`, the outer div groups the generated lines with `space.100` between them.

Native attributes, events and refs always belong to the outer div. IDs, labels and handlers are never copied to each generated line.

## Shapes and sizing

| Shape     | Default geometry                       | Use                                                                          |
| --------- | -------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `line`    | 12px tall, full width, `radius.small`  | Body text. Use `lines` for a paragraph.                                      |
| `heading` | 20px tall, full width, `radius.small`  | A title or record name.                                                      |
| `circle`  | 32px square, `radius.full`             | An avatar or icon. `width` also sets its height unless `height` is supplied. |
| `block`   | 96px tall, full width, `radius.medium` | A card, chart or image.                                                      |

`width` and `height` accept a number in pixels or a CSS length. On a single shape, explicit `style` values override those dimensions. Existing className overrides continue through the package's class merger.

For generated lines, `width` and `height` apply to **each line**; `className` and `style` apply to **the wrapper**. The last line is two thirds wide when `width` is omitted. An explicit `width` sizes every line equally, including the last.

## Native props and content

_Example: story `Stories.NativeAttributes`._

```tsx
<Skeleton
  ref={placeholderRef}
  id="record-placeholder"
  shape="block"
  height={120}
  data-record="preview"
/>
```

Native children render once. In multiline mode, supplied children replace the automatic lines; omitting children generates them. Explicit `null`, `false` or `0` are supplied content. Native HTML content also replaces automatic lines and follows React's normal content rules.

Skeleton uses a native div, as the shadcn reference does. It has no `render` or `asChild` prop. Compose a more specific loading layout with several Skeletons inside a normal container.

## Accessibility and motion

- `aria-hidden` defaults to `true` so placeholders do not announce meaningless shapes. Explicit native ARIA props can override the default.
- Put `aria-busy` and any loading message on the region that is waiting; clear its busy state when content arrives.
- Keep placeholders noninteractive. Use a nearby status message for meaningful loading information.
- Shapes pulse while waiting. The existing reduced-motion stylesheet stops the pulse and keeps the layout in place.
- Match the size and amount of expected content, then replace the placeholders when it arrives.

## Props

`SkeletonProps` includes native div props plus `shape`, `lines`, `width` and `height`.

_Props: generated from `Skeleton`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._

_Example: story `Stories.Playground`._

_Rendered in the Storybook: Controls._

## Migration

Existing shapes, line counts, dimensions and style overrides retain their behavior. Skeleton now forwards native attributes, events, children and refs and exposes `data-slot="skeleton"` on the outer div. Multiline refs point to the wrapper, not an individual line. No existing consumer changes are required.

## Related

- [PageSkeleton](?path=/docs/layout-pageskeleton--docs): the page's first paint.
- [Spinner](?path=/docs/components-spinner--docs): progress for an action.
- [Chart](?path=/docs/patterns-chart-overview--docs): loading layouts for plots.
- [Empty](?path=/docs/components-empty--docs): a region with no content to load.

_Example: story `Stories.Dont`._

<!-- page: Components/Spinner (src/stories/components/Spinner.mdx) -->

# Spinner

An indeterminate wait such as saving, exporting or refreshing. Use Skeleton when the loading content has a known shape.

## Anatomy

Spinner renders Lucide's Loader2 SVG with `data-slot="spinner"`. Native SVG attributes, events and refs reach that element.

_Example: story `Stories.Playground`._

## Variants and states

Sizes are small (12px, default), medium (16px) and large (24px). Appearance is subtle, inverse on a bold fill, or inherit for the surrounding text color.

_Example: story `Stories.SizesAndAppearance`._

`delay` waits before revealing the spinner. Changing a pending delay restarts the timer; once visible, it stays visible until unmounted. A new operation can reset it with a new key. Non-positive delays reveal immediately.

_Example: story `Stories.Delay`._

## Accessibility

The default is a status named by the provider's localized Loading text. Use `label` or native `aria-label` to describe the operation; explicit native attributes take precedence. Use `aria-labelledby` to associate visible text.

`isDecorative` hides a spinner when its parent already owns the busy announcement. Button does this for its loading indicator. Reduced motion stops the animation while retaining the accessible status.

## Props

_Props: generated from `Spinner`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._

Native SVG props include `ref`, `id`, `strokeWidth`, `style`, `className`, ARIA and events. Ledger retains `size`, `appearance`, `label`, `isDecorative` and `delay`. Class overrides can adjust dimensions.

### Migration

Existing Spinner calls keep working. Native SVG props and refs no longer need an enclosing element.

## Related

[Button](?path=/docs/components-button--docs), [Skeleton](?path=/docs/components-skeleton--docs), [Progress](?path=/docs/components-progress--docs).

Sources: [shadcn Spinner](https://ui.shadcn.com/docs/components/base/spinner), [implementation](https://github.com/shadcn-ui/ui/blob/main/apps/v4/registry/bases/base/ui/spinner.tsx).

<!-- page: Components/Stat (src/stories/components/Stat.mdx) -->

# Stat

A number with its name. `Stat.Tile` is a label, a big tabular number and a one-line note, one cell of a `Stat.Grid`: the headline numbers at the top of a record, framed as a card, or a band between two sections. A bare `Stat` is the number over its label for an unframed row inside a Section. Zero reads muted.

_Example: story `Stories.StatMatrix`._

## Anatomy

| Part  | What it is                                                                                                                                  |
| ----- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Label | `font.body.small` in `color.text.subtle`: what the number counts. Above the number in a Tile, below it in a bare Stat.                      |
| Value | `font.heading.small` semibold, tabular. `color.text`, or the tone's text colour when the number is a status; zero in `color.text.subtlest`. |
| Note  | `font.body.small` in `color.text.subtle`, one line under the value. Tile only.                                                              |
| Grid  | Two to six cells across, hairline gutters painted with `color.border`. `card` is bordered and rounded; `band` runs between two rules.       |

## Variants

| Variant               | Use                                                                                                    |
| --------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `Stat.Tile` in a Grid | The headline numbers of a record or a screen: at the top as a card, or as a band between two sections. |
| `Stat`                | A summary row inside a Section, where a framed grid would be a card inside a card.                     |

Not built, and why: no trend arrow, delta or sparkline ("+3 this week"), because a number on a record is a state, not a series, and a series is a [Chart](?path=/docs/patterns-chart-overview--docs); no icon in the tile; no tinted tile. The prototype has a stat with a bar under it on the dashboard and tinted counts on two pages, and both are parked as decisions rather than added here.

## Sizes

One type size, `font.heading.small`. What varies is the grid: `cols` from two to six, two below the small breakpoint, and six is three on a small screen.

_Example: story `Stories.SixAcross`._

## States

| State   | What changes                                                                     |
| ------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Neutral | The number in `color.text`. The default, and most numbers.                       |
| Toned   | The number in the tone's text colour, because the number is a status.            |
| Zero    | The number in `color.text.subtlest`, whatever the tone: nothing is not a status. |

A Stat does not hover, focus or disable. A tile that takes the reader somewhere is a link around the tile, and the tile does not change.

## Modifiers

- **`tone`** when the number is a status: overdue in `danger`, verified in `success`, held in `warning`. Most numbers stay neutral, so the one that is a status stands out.
- **`note`** for the one line under the number: what it is out of, the oldest, the next.
- **`cols`** and **`frame`** on the grid: `card` at the top of a record, `band` between sections.

_Example: story `Stories.Frames`._

## Content

- **The label is a noun phrase**, under three words when it can be: "Open findings", "Re-tests owed", "Verified".
- **The value is a number**, or a short string that reads as one: "80%", "41/80". Tabular, so a row of tiles aligns.
- **The note is one line** that qualifies the number: "298 of 372", "Oldest 12 days", "Nothing waiting on you". A note that decomposes a number belongs on the tile that holds the whole, not on a part.
- **Zero's note says what the zero means.** "Nothing waiting on you" is worth more than a muted 0.

## Style

| Element | Token                                                                                                             |
| ------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Tile    | `elevation.surface` · `space.200` inline · `space.150` block · `space.025` between lines                          |
| Value   | `font.heading.small` semibold · tabular · `color.text` / `color.text.<tone>` / `color.text.subtlest` at zero      |
| Label   | `font.body.small` · `color.text.subtle`                                                                           |
| Note    | `font.body.small` · `color.text.subtle`                                                                           |
| Grid    | `gap-px` painted `color.border` · `card`: `color.border`, `radius.large` · `band`: `color.border` above and below |
| Stat    | `space.100` block · `space.050` between value and label                                                           |

The toned value is Badge's text colour for the tone, so a danger count and a danger Indicator are the same red.

## Accessibility

- **Reading order is label then value in a Tile,** so a screen reader hears "Open findings, 17". A bare Stat reads value then label, "17, Open findings", which is how a summary row is scanned.
- **Zero is muted, not disabled.** `color.text.subtlest` still passes the contrast test; the a11y gate runs the zero row of the matrix.
- **The tone is not the only signal.** The label says what the number is, and the note says what it means; the colour ranks it.
- **A grid is a `div`**, not a table or a list: the tiles are read in order and there is nothing to navigate.

## Props

Stat, Stat.Tile and Stat.Grid forward native `div` props and refs to their outer elements. IDs, ARIA, data attributes and events are preserved; `className` merges with each part’s defaults. Styles override the Grid’s default gutter background and accept ordinary sizing on all three parts.

Stat and Stat.Tile keep their configured `label`/`value`/`note` slots. Compose tiles through Stat.Grid’s children. Zero remains muted, and tones, responsive columns and frames retain their existing defaults.

_Props: generated from `Stat`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._

### Stat.Tile

_Props: generated from `Stat.Tile`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._

### Stat.Grid

_Props: generated from `Stat.Grid`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._

### Playground

_Example: story `Stories.Playground`._

_Rendered in the Storybook: Controls._

## Related

- [Progress](?path=/docs/components-progress--docs): the bar a number often has beside it.
- [Chart](?path=/docs/patterns-chart-overview--docs): a number over time.
- [KeyValue](?path=/docs/components-keyvalue--docs): a fact that is not a headline.
- [Badge](?path=/docs/components-badge--docs): the tone table.

## Don't

_Example: story `Stories.Dont`._

<!-- page: Components/Stepper (src/stories/components/Stepper.mdx) -->

# Stepper

Progress through an ordered path: the RMF steps, a program's milestones, a wizard. One step is `current`, the steps behind it are `done`, the ones ahead `upcoming`, and `blocked` is the step that failed. The list knows each step's place and its neighbour's state, so the rail is bold behind every completed step and a hairline ahead.

A path is fixed and has three or more steps. Two steps are a [Badge](?path=/docs/components-badge--docs); a percentage is a [Progress](?path=/docs/components-progress--docs) bar; a set of conditions that are met or not is [Gates](?path=/docs/patterns-gates--docs); events in time are a [Timeline](?path=/docs/components-timeline--docs).

_Example: story `Stories.StepperMatrix`._

## Anatomy

| Part   | What it is                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| ------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Marker | A 16px circle: a check on `color.background.success.bold` when done, a cross on `color.background.danger.bold` when blocked, a `color.border.selected` ring at the focused width when current, a hairline ring when upcoming. `numbered` writes the step's number in it. |
| Rail   | The line between markers. `color.border.selected` behind a completed step, `color.border` ahead. It stops at the first and last markers.                                                                                                                                 |
| Label  | One or two words, `font.body.small`: semibold in `color.text` when current, medium otherwise, `color.text.subtle` when upcoming, `color.text.danger` when blocked. Under the marker horizontally, beside it vertically.                                                  |
| Meta   | Under the label, `font.body.xsmall` in `color.text.subtle`: the date, the owner, why it is blocked.                                                                                                                                                |
| Step   | The marker and its text together, one `li`: a button when it can be moved to, a plain block when it only reports.                                                                                                                                                        |

## Variants

| Variant      | Use                                                                                                                                                                              |
| ------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `horizontal` | Labels under markers on one line: a record's milestone header, the top of a form.                                                                                                |
| `vertical`   | Markers down the left with labels beside them: a wizard's rail, a panel. Preferred wherever it fits, because the labels and metas can wrap.                              |
| `numbered`   | The marker shows the step's number; done and blocked keep their icon: numbers make the order plain on a long path.                            |
| Interactive  | A step with `onSelect` is a button the reader can move to; a step without one only reports. Mix them: done steps open, the rest do not. |

Not built, and why: a disabled state, because a step the reader cannot reach is `upcoming` without `onSelect`; a skeleton, because the steps are known before the data is.

A vertical step takes `children`: under the label, with the rail running past it, a Collapsible with the owner and the open task, a sentence, a Badge. That is a rail of milestones, where each step carries its record. A wizard's step carries nothing, because its content is the page it opens.

_Example: story `Stories.Milestones`._

## Sizes

One size: the marker 16px, the label `font.body.small`, the meta `font.body.xsmall`. Horizontally each step is one equal column of the list, which is 420px wide at least; give a longer path a wider minimum or let its container scroll. Vertically the list is as wide as its longest label and meta allow, and a step is `space.200` above the next.

_Example: story `Stories.Paths`._

## States

| State      | What changes                                                                                                                              |
| ---------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `done`     | The check on the success fill; the rail behind and ahead of it bold; the label medium.                                                    |
| `current`  | The selected ring at the focused width; the label semibold; `aria-current="step"`. The rail behind it is bold if the step before is done. |
| `upcoming` | A hairline ring; the label in `color.text.subtle`; a hairline rail.                                                                       |
| `blocked`  | The cross on the danger fill; the label in `color.text.danger`; the meta says why.                                                        |
| Hover      | On a step with `onSelect`: the label underlines.                                                                                          |
| Focus      | On a step with `onSelect`: the focus outline around the whole step.                                                                       |

## Modifiers

- **`orientation`**, **`numbered`** as in Variants; **`label`** names the list.
- **`meta`** for the date, the owner or the reason under the label. It may wrap; the label does not.
- **`title`** for the full text when a label truncates.
- **`children`** for what a milestone carries under its label. Anything interactive in it is its own stop beside the step's button.
- **`onSelect`** on the steps the reader may move to. On a wizard that is every done step and the next one; on a milestone header, every step, to open the milestone.

## Content

- **Labels are one or two words** in sentence case, sixteen characters at most: "Categorize", "Select controls", "MS-C". A noun, or verb and noun. Never "Processing".
- **The meta is a date, a person or a reason**, in the product's date format: "3 Aug", "Priya Natarajan", "Baseline not approved".
- **A blocked step says why** in its meta. The marker alone is a red dot with no story.
- **Numbers on a long path.** Six RMF steps read better as 1 to 6; three steps do not need them.

## Style

| Element | Token                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| ------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Marker  | 16px · `radius.full` · done `color.border.success` on `color.background.success.bold` · blocked `color.border.danger` on `color.background.danger.bold` · current `color.border.selected` at `border.width.selected` on `elevation.surface` · upcoming `color.border` on `elevation.surface` |
| Number  | `font.body.xsmall` medium · `color.text.selected` when current, `color.text.subtle` when upcoming                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| Rail    | 1px · `color.border.selected` behind a done step · `color.border` otherwise                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| Label   | `font.body.small` · current semibold `color.text` · done medium `color.text` · upcoming medium `color.text.subtle` · blocked medium `color.text.danger`                                                                                                                                      |
| Meta    | `font.body.xsmall` · `color.text.subtle` · tabular                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| Spacing | horizontal: label `space.075` under the marker, `space.050` inline · vertical: `space.150` between marker and text, `space.200` under each step                                                                                                                                              |
| Hover   | Label underline on a selectable step                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| Focus   | The focus outline, `radius.medium`, around the step                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| Motion  | Marker colours in `motion.duration.fast`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |

Here done is green and blocked is red, the product's status tones, because on a milestone header the states are the story and colour carries it alongside the icon.

## Accessibility

- **The list is an ordered list**, named by `label`; a screen reader hears "RMF steps, list, 6 items" and moves step by step.
- **The state is in the name.** Each label is prefixed, visually hidden, with "Completed", "Not started" or "Blocked", and the current step carries `aria-current="step"`, so the label includes the state of each step.
- **One button per step.** A step that can be moved to is a single button holding its marker and text, so it is one tab stop with one name. A step that only reports is not focusable.
- **Keyboard:** Tab moves between the selectable steps, Enter or Space moves to one. Each reachable step is its own stop, not one stop with arrows inside it, which is what a wizard's rail of three or four wants.
- **Colour is never alone.** Done and blocked have their icon, current its weight and ring, and the words are read.
- **Contrast:** the inverse check and cross pass on their fills; the danger label passes on the surface. The gate runs both orientations.

## Props

Native `ol` props and refs target Stepper; native `li` props and refs target Stepper.Item. IDs, data attributes, styles, classes and events reach those elements. An explicit `aria-label` overrides the root’s `label` shorthand, and caller styles override the horizontal minimum width. Item’s native `title` now belongs to the `li`, so it also applies when hovering its label.

`onSelect` remains the existing step-action callback. Use `onClickCapture` on the item or list and call `event.preventDefault()` to cancel selection before its button runs. A bubble-phase `onClick` runs after the button, following normal DOM event order. Step state still owns `aria-current`; step actions remain native buttons with Enter/Space activation.

_Props: generated from `Stepper`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._

### Stepper.Item

_Props: generated from `Stepper.Item`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._

### Playground

_Example: story `Stories.Playground`._

_Rendered in the Storybook: Controls._

## Related

- [Progress](?path=/docs/components-progress--docs): how much, as a bar.
- [Gates](?path=/docs/patterns-gates--docs): conditions met or not, in no order.
- [Timeline](?path=/docs/components-timeline--docs): what happened, in order, with no fixed end.
- [Tabs](?path=/docs/components-tabs--docs): sections the reader may take in any order.

## Don't

_Example: story `Stories.Dont`._

<!-- page: Components/Switch (src/stories/components/Switch.mdx) -->

# Switch

An on/off setting built on Base UI with the shadcn composition API. The thumb is included; compose the setting's label and supporting text outside the switch.

```tsx
<label className="inline-flex items-center gap-100">
  <Switch id="switch" aria-describedby="switch-help" defaultChecked />
  Notify the owner
</label>
```

_Example: story `Stories.SwitchMatrix`._

## Sizes and state

| Size      | Track     | Thumb |
| --------- | --------- | ----- |
| `default` | 32 × 20px | 16px  |
| `sm`      | 24 × 16px | 12px  |

These dimensions use Ledger spacing tokens. The thumb moves toward the inline end when checked, follows RTL direction, and stops animating when reduced motion is requested.

Use `defaultChecked` for local state or `checked` and `onCheckedChange(checked, details)` for controlled state. `details.cancel()` rejects a change. `disabled` blocks activation and removes the switch from the tab order; `readOnly` retains focusability while preventing state changes.

## Labels, Field and forms

A wrapping `<label>` or a sibling `<label htmlFor={id}>` names the setting and toggles it when clicked. Keep the name stable across on/off states. [Field](?path=/docs/components-field--docs) provides label and message parts. Associate them with the control using native IDs and ARIA:

```tsx
<Field>
  <FieldLabel htmlFor="switch">Notify the owner</FieldLabel>
  <Switch checked={notify} onCheckedChange={setNotify} />
  <FieldDescription id="switch-help">Send an email when a finding changes status.</FieldDescription>
</Field>
```

`name`, `value`, `uncheckedValue`, `form` and `required` configure the hidden checkbox used for native submission and validation. Without `uncheckedValue`, an unchecked switch contributes no entry. `aria-required` on Switch describes the requirement; use Switch's native `required` when browser validation is intended.

In installed Base UI 1.7, native form reset is caller-owned: restore controlled `checked` state in the form's `onReset` handler.

_Example: story `Stories.Settings`._

## Native props and composition

The default visible root is a `<span role="switch">`, with a hidden checkbox beside it. `ref` targets the visible root; `inputRef` and `id` target the hidden input. Native event handlers and state-based `className`/`style` callbacks apply to the root.

For a native button root, pass `nativeButton` and `render={<button />}`. In that mode `id` targets the button, and refs and event handlers merge with those on the rendered element. Every switch needs a visible label, `aria-label`, or `aria-labelledby`.

_Example: story `Stories.InRows`._

## Migration

Replace label children and the `description` prop with a wrapping label, sibling label or Field. The track is now 32px wide by default instead of 40px; `sm` adds a 24px option. A root ref now receives the visible span by default, and `inputRef` accesses the form input. Native `checked`, `defaultChecked` and `onCheckedChange` usage remains supported.

## Props

_Props: generated from `Switch`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._

_Example: story `Stories.Playground`._

_Rendered in the Storybook: Controls._

## Related

[Field](?path=/docs/components-field--docs) · [Forms](?path=/docs/patterns-forms--docs) · [Checkbox](?path=/docs/components-checkbox--docs) · [Toggle](?path=/docs/components-toggle--docs) · [shadcn Switch](https://ui.shadcn.com/docs/components/base/switch) · [Base UI Switch](https://base-ui.com/react/components/switch)

<!-- page: Components/Table (src/stories/components/Table.mdx) -->

# Table

The register, by hand: a header row, a row per record, a hairline between them. `Table` is the markup and its parts; it sorts, pages or selects only when the caller wires the state. A table with state to keep, sort, filters, pages, selection, pinned columns, nested or reordered rows, is a [DataTable](?path=/docs/patterns-data-table--docs), which draws these same parts from a TanStack instance. No route sorts, filters or pages by hand.

A few facts about one thing are a [KeyValue](?path=/docs/components-keyvalue--docs), not a two-column table; a list with one line per record is an [Item](?path=/docs/components-item--docs) list; a hierarchy without columns is a [Tree](?path=/docs/components-tree--docs).

_Example: story `Stories.TableMatrix`._

## Anatomy

| Part       | What it is                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| ---------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Frame      | The wrapper that scrolls: sideways always, and down past `maxHeight`, so the header sticks to it and not to the page. While it is scrolled sideways it carries `data-scrolled-start` and `data-scrolled-end`, and the pinned column at the edge shows its border. |
| Header     | `Table.Header`: `dimension.row.header` 32px, sticky at the top of the frame, `font.body.small` at `font.weight.medium` in `color.text.subtle` on the current surface, a hairline under. Sortable, it holds a button that reports `aria-sort` and shows the arrow. |
| Row        | `Table.Row`: the record, `dimension.row` 40px with a hairline under. It lights on hover and paints `color.background.selected` when chosen; `isStatic` for a row that is not a record.                                                                            |
| Cell       | `Table.Cell`: `space.150` each side, one line, truncated; a plain string is also the cell's title, so the whole shows on hover.                                                                                                                                   |
| Id         | `Table.Id`: the id in `Id`, `color.text.brand` on the row's hover, with the eye at the end of the cell, there at rest, that opens the record in the preview.                                                                                                       |
| List       | `Table.List`: several values on one line, the first by name and the rest as a count, every one in a hover card with its meta line; the click is the row's preview when it has one, else the line is text. |
| Selection  | `Table.Selection`: the checkbox column, 32px; in the header it chooses every row and reads mixed when only some are.                                                                                                                                              |
| Group      | `Table.Group`: a band on the sunken surface with a chevron, a title and a Count, holding its rows in a `tbody`.                                                                                                                                                   |
| Tree cell  | `Table.Tree`: the name cell of a treegrid, one `space.200` indent per level, the chevron on rows with children, a hint after the name.                                                                                                                            |
| Disclosure | `Table.Disclosure`: the chevron as a leading cell of its own, centred, one narrow column whatever the depth. The disclosure is always the first column, never moves when a column is reordered, hidden or pinned, and never changes width as rows open and close; the indent belongs to the row's first value. What DataTable draws in tree mode. |
| Detail row | `Table.Detail`: the row a record opens into, one cell across every column on the sunken surface.                                                                                                                                                                  |
| Handle     | `Table.Handle`: the grip cell of a row that drags into a new order.                                                                                                                                                                                               |

## Variants

Table has one appearance. What varies is the parts a register takes:

| The register                                          | Use                                                                                           |
| ----------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Records with nothing to sort, filter or page          | `Table` with `Table.Header`, `Table.Row`, `Table.Cell` and `Table.Id`.                        |
| Rows the reader chooses for a batch action            | `Table.Selection` in the header and in each row; the bar above names the count and the verbs. |
| Records under headings                                | `Table.Group`, one per heading, opened and closed.                                            |
| A hierarchy with columns                              | `role="treegrid"`, `Table.Disclosure` as the leading cell (or `Table.Tree` as the name cell); the caller flattens and folds. |
| A record that opens into more                         | `Table.Detail` under its row, a chevron in the row.                                           |
| Rows in an order the reader sets                      | `Table.Handle` as the first cell.                                                             |
| Sort, filters, pages, pinned columns, a thousand rows | `DataTable`.                                                                                  |
| A few facts about one thing                           | `KeyValue`.                                                                                   |

There is no zebra striping: the hairline and the row's hover carry the eye across, and stripes fight the selected and the sunken surfaces. There is no radio selection of one row: the row's click opens the record, and one chosen row is that click. There is no expand-all chevron: a detail row loads what it needs when it opens, and opening every row at once gives that up. There is no row size prop; see Sizes.

## Sizes

One row height, `dimension.row` 40px, and the header `dimension.row.header` 32px. The reader's density setting, beside the mode switch, resolves the row to `dimension.row.compact` 36px on every table at once; a table never takes a density prop, so two tables on a page never disagree. One density setting for the reader, not a row height per table.

Column widths are content. `width` in pixels on the header fixes a column (on the cells, in a table with no header row); one column takes the slack. The frame scrolls sideways when the columns are wider than the page, and a pinned column keeps its place.

_Example: story `Stories.FrameStory`._

## States

| State              | What changes                                                                                                                           |
| ------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Header, sortable   | The up-down chevron appears on hover and on focus; the text turns `color.text`.                                                        |
| Sorted             | The arrow up or down stays and the text is `color.text`; `aria-sort` says which.                                                       |
| Row hover          | `color.background.surface.hovered`; the id turns `color.text.brand`; the eye, there at rest in `color.icon.subtlest`, sharpens.       |
| Selected           | `color.background.selected`, `color.background.selected.hovered` on hover; `data-selected` on the row.                                 |
| Active id          | The id in `color.text.brand` and the eye on `color.background.selected`: the row open in the preview.                                  |
| Static             | No hover: a totals row, a form laid out as a table.                                                                                    |
| Scrolled           | The frame carries `data-scrolled-start` or `-end`; the pinned column at the edge draws `color.border.bold` in place of `color.border`. |
| Group open, closed | The chevron turns; closed, the rows are not rendered.                                                                                  |
| Expanded           | In a treegrid, `aria-expanded` on the row; the chevron turns; the folded count goes.                                                   |
| Disabled selection | The checkbox disabled; the row still opens.                                                                                            |

Loading, empty and error belong to the DataTable, which keeps the header and draws skeleton rows, an Empty or the error inside the frame. A bare Table shows what it is given: an empty register is an [Empty](?path=/docs/components-empty--docs) in its Section, not a table with no rows.

## Modifiers

- **`label`** names the table when no heading above does. A DataTable takes the same.
- **`maxHeight`** makes the frame scroll down inside itself; the header sticks to the frame.
- **`fill`** makes the frame take the rest of a bounded flex column and scroll inside it, the companion of Stack's `grow="fill"`; the DataTable's `fill` builds that column.
- **`sort` and `onSort`** on a header. `useSort` gives a plain table `dir(key)` and `toggle(key)`; `usePage` with [Pagination](?path=/docs/components-pagination--docs) pages it.
- **`sticky`, `pinned`, `offset`, `edge`** on a header and its cells: `pinned="start"` or `"end"`, `offset` the widths of the pinned columns before it, `edge` on the one that touches the middle. `sticky` is `pinned="start"` with no offset.
- **`width`** in pixels on the header, or on the cells of a table with no header row.
- **`resize` and `trailing`** on a header are the DataTable's: a handle on the trailing edge, a control on hover. By hand only in a header the DataTable cannot draw.
- **`isSelected` and `isStatic`** on a row.
- **`tone="subtle"`** on `Table.Id` where the id is not the link, in a grouped listing; `onPreview` and `isActive` for the eye.
- **`role="treegrid"`** with `aria-level` and `aria-expanded` on the rows, and `Table.Disclosure` as the leading cell or `Table.Tree` as the name cell.

_Example: story `Stories.SortedAndPaged`._

_Example: story `Stories.Groups`._

_Example: story `Stories.TreeStory`._

## Content

- **Headers are one or two words**, sentence case, no trailing colon, no units when the cells carry them: Due, not "Due date:". A header that would wrap is a shorter word.
- **The id first, the name second, actions last.**
- **Text starts; a number ends**, in tabular numerals, and so does its header. A number never centres.
- **A status is a Badge, a severity an Indicator, a person a Person**; a date is `d MMM yyyy`.
- **An absent value is `Absent`**, never a blank, a dash typed by hand or "N/A".
- **Cells hold one line.** A column that must wrap wraps as a column, and it is never the one sorted by eye. Long prose lives on the record.
- **The register is named** by the Section above it, or by `label`.

## Style

| Element     | Token                                                                                                                                                             |
| ----------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Frame       | full width · scrolls sideways · scrolls down past `maxHeight` or, with `fill`, inside the height its column gives it                                              |
| Header      | `dimension.row.header` 32px · `font.body.small` `font.weight.medium` `color.text.subtle` · `elevation.surface.current` · `color.border` under, the cell's own so it stays while the frame scrolls · `space.150` sides |
| Sort button | `dimension.control.xsmall` · `radius.small` · arrow 12px · hover `color.text`                                                                                     |
| Row         | `dimension.row` 40px, `dimension.row.compact` 36px · `color.border` hairline · hover `color.background.surface.hovered`                                           |
| Selected    | `color.background.selected` · hover `color.background.selected.hovered`                                                                                           |
| Cell        | `space.150` sides · `font.body` · one line, truncated                                                                                                             |
| Id          | `Id` · hover and active `color.text.brand` · the eye `dimension.icon.small` in a 20px button over the cell's end, revealed on the row's hover, active on `color.background.selected` |
| Group band  | `elevation.surface.sunken` · `font.body` `font.weight.medium` · `space.100` × `space.075` · hover `color.background.surface.hovered`                              |
| Detail row  | `elevation.surface.sunken` · `space.200` × `space.150`                                                                                                            |
| Tree indent | `space.200` 16px per level · a 20px chevron button                                                                                                                |
| Pinned edge | `color.border`, `color.border.bold` while the frame is scrolled                                                                                                   |
| Motion      | `motion.duration.fast` on the row's colours and the chevrons' turn                                                                                                |

## Accessibility

- **It is a table**: `table`, `thead`, `tbody`, `th`, `td`. `role="treegrid"` for a hierarchy with columns; `grid` only when cells are editable, which is the DataTable's editing mode.
- **The name.** `label` sets `aria-label` when no heading names the table.
- **Sorting.** The header's button reports `aria-sort`; Space or Enter sorts; the chevron shows on hover and on focus, so a keyboard user sees which headers sort. There is no persistent sign that a table sorts, which is why the chevron follows focus.
- **Keyboard.** Tab moves through the interactive elements in reading order: sort buttons, checkboxes, the eye, links. That is enough for a table; only a treegrid takes arrow keys, and the DataTable's tree mode wires them. A bare treegrid's caller does.
- **Selection is a checkbox with a name**: "Select CTRL-0412", and the header's "Select all". The row's click opens the record and does not select.
- **Every control is named.** The eye is "Preview row" with a Tooltip; the group's chevron says Expand or Collapse; the tree's names its row, "Expand Ground segment"; a detail row's chevron carries `aria-controls`.
- **Truncated text is the cell's title**, so it shows whole on hover; the record has it in full.
- **Not colour alone.** Hover and selection have the checkbox and the id's colour beside the fill; the sort has its arrow and `aria-sort`; the header text at `color.text.subtle` passes 4.5:1.

## Props

Table, Table.Header, Table.Row and Table.Cell accept native element props and refs. Table's ref targets the table; frameRef targets its scroll container and supports React 19 callback cleanup. Sorting, pinning and sizing keep their existing contracts. The frame tracks size changes in both itself and its table, so keyboard scroll access and pinned edges update when content grows or shrinks.

_Example: story `Stories.DynamicFrame`._

_Example: story `Stories.FillFrame`._

_Props: generated from `Table`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._

### Table.Header

_Props: generated from `Table.Header`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._

### Table.Row

_Props: generated from `Table.Row`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._

### Table.Cell

_Props: generated from `Table.Cell`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._

### The other parts

| Part              | Does                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| ----------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `Table.Id`        | `id`, `onPreview`, `isActive`, `tone` (`brand` or `subtle`), `width`, and the pinned props. The row opens the record; the eye opens the same row in the preview. It takes no room in the cell and shows on the row's hover, on focus, and while that row's preview is open. |
| `Table.Selection` | `header`, `checked` and `indeterminate` (booleans), `onCheckedChange(checked)`, `label`, `disabled`, `pinned`. The click does not reach the row.                                                        |
| `Table.Group`     | `colSpan`, `open`, `onToggle`, `title`, `count`, `trailing`. It renders a `tbody`, so several stack in one Table.                                                                                      |
| `Table.Tree`      | `depth`, `hasChildren`, `expanded`, `onToggle`, `label` (the row's plain name, for the chevron), `hint`. The Table takes `role="treegrid"`, each Row `aria-level` and, with children, `aria-expanded`. |
| `Table.Disclosure` | `hasChildren`, `expanded`, `onToggle`, `label`, `width`, and the pinned props. One width for every depth, so the columns do not move as rows open and close; a leaf keeps the space, and the caller indents the row's first value. |
| `Table.Detail`    | `id`, `colSpan`. The chevron that opens it carries `aria-controls` with this row's `id`.                                                                                                               |
| `Table.Handle`    | `label`, `isDragging`; `ref` and the drag props come from the drag context. The cell is the handle, so the row's own controls keep their clicks.                                                       |

<!-- page: Components/Tabs (src/stories/components/Tabs.mdx) -->

# Tabs

Related views within one page, using [shadcn's Base UI Tabs](https://ui.shadcn.com/docs/components/base/tabs) and [Base UI Tabs](https://base-ui.com/react/components/tabs). Use short view names; use a ToggleGroup or filters to narrow the same rows.

## Anatomy

Compose `Tabs`, `TabsList`, `TabsTrigger` and `TabsContent`. Match each Trigger's `value` to its Content. Put counts, badges and icons in the Trigger's children. Name the List with `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`.

```tsx
<Tabs defaultValue="controls">
  <TabsList variant="line" activateOnFocus aria-label="Record views">
    <TabsTrigger value="controls">
      Controls <Count value={340} max={9999} />
    </TabsTrigger>
    <TabsTrigger value="history">History</TabsTrigger>
  </TabsList>
  <TabsContent value="controls">Control register</TabsContent>
  <TabsContent value="history">Change history</TabsContent>
</Tabs>
```

Routes compose Tabs, TabsList and TabsContent directly; route state controls the selected value. Supporting context can be contributed separately with Shell.Aside.

## Variants

`TabsList` supports shadcn's `default` filled strip and `line` underline. Ledger retains its color, spacing and focus tokens; line tabs remain 32px tall on a border, with a 2px brand underline. One Base UI Indicator follows the selected tab, sliding and resizing over the moderate motion duration (240ms). The filled strip moves its raised selection surface in the same way. Horizontal line tabs fill the available width and align to the start. Their border continues across the container even when only a few tabs exist.

Horizontal line tabs use the kit's `ScrollArea` and horizontal `ScrollBar` inside a horizontal [Scroller](?path=/docs/components-scroller--docs), whose click arrows mark the overflowed edge for pointer readers and replace the scrollbar while they show; touch readers swipe with the bar. They stay on one row at every container width, including narrow preview panels. Touch, trackpad, scrollbar dragging and arrow-key focus can reach the overflowed tabs. Do not add `flex-wrap`, an overflow utility or another scroller to `TabsList`. Size the `Tabs` container when a bounded example is needed; the List handles its own width and scrolling.

The default filled strip fits its content. Record pages and previews explicitly use `variant="line"`; `activateOnFocus` remains an independent choice. Vertical lists retain their vertical layout and do not receive a horizontal scroller. The exported `tabsListVariants` recipe supplies list styling; the `TabsList` component also supplies the horizontal scrolling composition.

_Example: story `Stories.Variants`._

_Example: story `Stories.ResponsiveWidths`._

Set `orientation="vertical"` on Tabs for a vertical strip and Up/Down navigation. Direction follows LedgerProvider; `dir="ltr"` or `dir="rtl"` overrides both layout and keyboard direction.

_Example: story `Stories.Orientation`._

## Accessibility

Base UI owns the tablist, tab and tabpanel roles, selection, focus and panel associations. Keep a panel for the selected tab. Each strip is one Tab stop; arrows move within it and Home/End reach the ends. Focus wraps unless `loopFocus={false}` is set on the List.

Activation is **manual by default**: arrows move focus, then Enter or Space selects. `activateOnFocus` on the List selects as focus moves; use it when the panel can appear immediately. Disabled tabs remain arrow-focusable in the installed Base UI 1.7 contract and cannot activate.

A navigation tab uses `nativeButton={false}` and `render={<Link ... />}` or an anchor. It keeps its href and native modified-click navigation while receiving the tab role. The caller owns synchronization between route state and the controlled value.

_Example: story `Stories.Links`._

Inactive panels unmount by default. `keepMounted` retains their state; hidden panels remain hidden even with a display class, and Base UI makes their controls inert. The arriving panel fades from 0.65 opacity and rises 4px over the medium duration (150ms). The outgoing panel hides immediately so two views never occupy layout together. A controlled route that reuses one panel with a changing value replays its entrance without remounting children or resetting retained input state.

Reduced motion disables both indicator movement and panel entrance. The Motion story samples rendered frames for filled, line, RTL, vertical and reused-panel examples; the dark test project uses reduced motion. Keyboard, link and retained-state stories run in both color modes.

_Example: story `Stories.Motion`._

## Props

The four parts expose their corresponding Base UI props, native refs, `render`, events, and state-based `className`/`style`. `TabsList` props and its ref still target the element with `role="tablist"`, inside the horizontal line scroller. The scroller adds no separate Tab stop; keyboard users enter the tablist and arrows or Home/End reveal the focused tab. Public types are `TabsProps`, `TabsListProps`, `TabsTriggerProps` and `TabsContentProps`.

Root accepts `value`/`onValueChange` or `defaultValue`, including numeric values; `null` means no selection. `onValueChange(value, details)` can cancel user activation with `details.cancel()`. Uncontrolled selection falls back when a selected tab disappears or becomes disabled; those automatic notifications are not cancellable. For predictable server rendering, give an explicit enabled initial value.

_Example: story `Stories.EditingAndMounting`._

### Migration and API

| Previous API                                                       | Current API                                                                                   |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Tabs.List`, `Tabs.Tab`, `Tabs.Panel`                              | `TabsList`, `TabsTrigger`, `TabsContent`                                                      |
| Root `activation="automatic"`                                      | List `activateOnFocus` (omit for manual activation)                                           |
| List `label`                                                       | `aria-label`                                                                                  |
| Trigger `count` / `trailing`                                       | Compose `Count`, `Badge` or other children; use `max={9999}` to preserve the former count cap |
| `asChild`                                                          | `render`; add `nativeButton={false}` for a link trigger                                       |
| `TabListProps`, `TabProps`, `TabPanelProps`                        | `TabsListProps`, `TabsTriggerProps`, `TabsContentProps`                                       |
| Line styling by default                                            | List `variant="line"`; the new default is a filled strip                                      |
| Line List `w-full justify-start`, `overflow-x-auto` or `flex-wrap` | Remove these overrides; horizontal line tabs fill and scroll through ScrollArea               |

## Related

- [ToggleGroup](?path=/docs/components-togglegroup--docs): view options or filters over the same rows.
- [Badge](?path=/docs/components-badge--docs): counts and state labels inside tabs.
- [Pages](?path=/docs/layout-pages--docs): record page composition and controlled routing.

<!-- page: Components/Textarea (src/stories/components/Textarea.mdx) -->

# Textarea

Several lines of free text: a note, description or implementation statement. This follows shadcn's native textarea implementation with Ledger styling.

## Anatomy

```tsx
<Field>
  <FieldLabel htmlFor="textarea">Review note</FieldLabel>
  <Textarea
    id="textarea"
    aria-describedby="textarea-help"
    name="note"
    value={note}
    onChange={(event) => setNote(event.target.value)}
    rows={4}
  />
  <FieldDescription id="textarea-help">
    Explain the evidence supporting this decision.
  </FieldDescription>
</Field>
```

## Variants and states

`rows` sets the expected initial answer length. Textarea has a 64px minimum height and can be resized vertically. Native read-only, disabled and invalid states use the shared control styling. Use InputGroupTextarea when the editor has header or footer addons.

_Example: story `Stories.TextareaMatrix`._
_Example: story `Stories.Rows`._
_Example: story `Stories.InField`._

## Accessibility

Use FieldLabel with `htmlFor` and the textarea’s `id`, or another accessible name. Reference hint/error IDs with `aria-describedby`; pass invalid and required announcements explicitly. Keep labels and instructions visible. Native keyboard editing, selection and form submission remain available.

## Props

`TextareaProps` is the native textarea contract, including `ref`, `rows`, `name`, `value`, `defaultValue`, `onChange`, `onBlur`, `required` and ARIA attributes. Ref and event targets are HTMLTextAreaElement. Styling and layout pass through native className and style.

_Example: story `Stories.Playground`._

## Related

[Input](?path=/docs/components-input--docs) · [InputGroup](?path=/docs/components-inputgroup--docs) · [Field](?path=/docs/components-field--docs) · [shadcn Textarea](https://ui.shadcn.com/docs/components/base/textarea)

<!-- page: Components/TextLink (src/stories/components/TextLink.mdx) -->

# TextLink

Navigation that reads as text, with Ledger's brand color, hover underline and keyboard focus outline. Use `Button variant="link"` for actions.

## Anatomy

TextLink renders an anchor by default. Compose a router link through Base UI `render`; the package has no router dependency.

```tsx
<TextLink href="/records">Records</TextLink>
<TextLink render={<Link to="/records" />}>Records</TextLink>
```

The rendered component must forward merged props and its ref. Supply its label as TextLink children.

## Variants and states

Omitted size inherits surrounding text. `small` and `medium` set the body scale; `weight="medium"` emphasizes a standalone destination. Hover adds an underline; keyboard focus adds the focus outline. Use plain text for unavailable destinations.

_Example: story `Stories.TextLinkMatrix`._
_Example: story `Stories.InProse`._

## Accessibility

A real anchor retains Enter activation, copy-link and open-in-new-tab behavior. Space does not activate a link. Name the destination, such as “Full timeline”, rather than “Click here”. Add a persistent underline in prose where color alone would not distinguish the link.

_Example: story `Stories.RenderComposition`._

## Props

_Props: generated from `TextLink`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._

Native anchor attributes, events and refs pass through. `render` merges rendered-element refs and handlers; put element-specific props on the rendered component.

Migration: replace implicit child composition or `asChild` with `render`. Remove `asChild={false}` from native anchors. Size, weight and Ledger styles are preserved.

_Example: story `Stories.Playground`._
_Rendered in the Storybook: Controls._

## Related

[Button](?path=/docs/components-button--docs), [Breadcrumb](?path=/docs/components-breadcrumb--docs), [Item](?path=/docs/components-item--docs).

Sources: [shadcn's native link composition](https://github.com/shadcn-ui/ui/blob/main/apps/v4/registry/bases/base/ui/breadcrumb.tsx), [Base UI useRender](https://base-ui.com/react/utils/use-render).

<!-- page: Components/Timeline (src/stories/components/Timeline.mdx) -->

# Timeline

Events in order along one rail: a record's activity, a scope's history, an audit trail, a pipeline, a line of releases, a feed of what people did. Each event is a marker on the rail, what happened, who and when, and under it what the event carries: a sentence, a file, a note, two buttons. Vertical reads down, newest first, with sticky group labels over a week or a month; horizontal reads across, oldest first. The anatomy follows [Item](?path=/docs/components-item--docs): a row that opens is its title stretched over the row, and everything beside it is a separate stop.

A timeline is for events; things with a date are an Item list, and a fixed path with a current step is a [Stepper](?path=/docs/components-stepper--docs).

_Example: story `Stories.TimelineMatrix`._

## Anatomy

| Part        | What it is                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| ----------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Rail        | A hairline, `color.border`, through the centre of every marker. Each row draws its own piece of it in the marker column, so it runs from the first marker to the last whatever the rows hold and wherever the time sits.                                                                       |
| Marker      | On the rail, at the list's size: a bare Dot in the tone at `small`; a ring on `elevation.surface.raised` holding a Dot at `medium` and `large`. With `icon`, a disc in the tone with the icon on it (a check, a cross, a play). Anything the slot holds as `marker`: an Avatar for who did it. |
| Title       | What happened, `font.body` in `color.text`, one line unless the list says `wrap`; medium weight when emphasised. It may be a sentence: the name in medium weight, the verb subtle, the record as a link. On a row that opens, this is the link or button, stretched over the row.          |
| Time        | `font.body.xsmall` in `color.text.subtle`, as the reader would say it, where the list puts it: at the end of the title's line, above the title as a dated line, first in the footer, or in a column before the rail. Across, above or below the marker. A `<time>` when `dateTime` is given.   |
| Meta        | Under the title, one line, `font.body.xsmall` in `color.text.subtle`: who, and the kind.                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| Description | Under the meta, `font.body.small` in `color.text.subtle`, wrapping: what the event amounts to, in a sentence.                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| Body        | Under the description, `font.body`: the note, the diff, what was said; a file; two buttons; who is on it; a collapsible detail.                                                                                                                                                                |
| Footer      | The last line: Badges for the kind and the state, or who did it; the time first, when it sits below.                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| Trailing    | At the end of the title's line, beside the row's control: an unread Count, a chevron, a menu button.                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| Group       | A run of events under a sticky Eyebrow with a count, on the current surface and on the title's column; the rail runs to its edge.                                                                                                                                                              |

## Variants

| Variant      | Use                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| ------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `vertical`   | The default. Reads down, newest first, the rail on the left: a feed, a history, a log, a pipeline. Groups live here.                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `horizontal` | Reads across, oldest first, the rail on top: releases, a project's journey, a workflow's stages on a record header. `center`, the default, puts each marker mid-column with the time above, like a Stepper; `start` puts it at the column's start with the time below and the text under it, for stages with a body. |

Where the time sits, `timePosition` on the list:

| Position | Use                                                                                                                           |
| -------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `end`    | The default: at the end of the title's line. A history, an audit trail, anywhere the rows are one or two lines.               |
| `above`  | A dated line above the title: a log where the date is the point, and the rows carry a sentence and a file.                    |
| `below`  | First in the footer, with the kind and the state: a feed of people, where the title is who did what and the when is a detail. |
| `start`  | A column before the rail, on the title's line: releases by month, a changelog, where the reader scans the dates.              |

What a row does:

| The row        | Use                                                                                              |
| -------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Opens a record | `link` with the router's Link: the title is the link, stretched over the row.                    |
| Opens in place | `onSelect`: the title is a button over the row; `isActive` marks the event open beside the list. |
| Only reads     | Neither: a plain row.                                                                            |
| Is unread      | `emphasis`: the title in medium weight, and an unread mark in `trailing`.                        |

_Example: story `Stories.People`._

_Example: story `Stories.Log`._

Not built, and why: alternating sides, because the rail is a list, not a poster; a collapsed "show more", because the group's count says how many and the page scrolls; a rating on an event, because a rating is a record's fact, not an event's; markers in the accent hues, a colour per row to tell rows apart, because the marker's colour is the tone and a colour that says nothing is a colour the reader tries to read.

## Sizes

| Size     | Slot | Marker                                                  | Row                         | Where                                                                                  |
| -------- | ---- | ------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `small`  | 16px | A bare 8px Dot; an `xsmall` Avatar; a 16px disc         | `space.050` above and below | A dense log, a changelog, a rail's recent activity.                                    |
| `medium` | 20px | A 12px ring with a Dot; an `xsmall` Avatar; a 20px disc | `space.075` above and below | The default: a record's history, an audit trail, a pipeline.                           |
| `large`  | 24px | A 16px ring with a Dot; a `small` Avatar; a 24px disc   | `space.100` above and below | A feed of people, where the avatar is the marker; a workflow's stages across a header. |

The size is the list's, not the row's: every marker in a list sits on the same rail. The title stays `font.body` at every size; what scales is the marker and the room around it. A vertical timeline is as wide as its container; in a rail it is the rail's width, on a record page a measure. A horizontal one gives each event an equal column, 420px in all at least, like a Stepper; in a scrolling area it can be as wide as its stages need.

_Example: story `Stories.Releases`._

_Example: story `Stories.Runs`._

_Example: story `Stories.Activity`._

## States

| State          | What changes                                                                                         |
| -------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Plain          | No hover. Text on the surface.                                                                       |
| Link or button | `color.background.neutral.subtle.hovered` on hover across the row; the focus outline around the row. |
| Active         | `color.background.selected`, and its hovered step on hover: the event open beside the list.          |
| Emphasised     | The title medium: unread, or the current one.                                                        |

The feed in a Sheet, the count in its title, is the [In a sheet](?path=/story/components-timeline--in-a-sheet) story.

## Modifiers

- **`orientation`**, **`size`**, **`timePosition`** and, across, **`align`**, as in Variants and Sizes. All four are the list's, so every row agrees. **`wrap`**, also the list's, lets every title wrap: a feed whose sentences name a task or a file.
- **`tone`** colours the default marker's dot by the event's kind; **`icon`**, passed bare, turns the marker into a disc in the tone with the icon on it; **`marker`** replaces it.
- **`time`** as said, **`timeTitle`** as the full stamp on hover, **`dateTime`** as the machine stamp, which makes it a `<time>`.
- **`meta`** for who and the kind, one line; **`description`** for the sentence under it; **`children`** for what the event carries; **`footer`** for the Badges and the name last.
- **`link`**, **`onSelect`**, **`isActive`**, **`emphasis`**, **`trailing`** as in Variants.
- **Group `label`** and **`count`**; the label sticks to the top of the scrolling surface.
- **`label`** on the list names it: "Activity", "History", "Releases".

## Content

- **Newest first** down a page; oldest first across. The reader wants what just happened; the beginning is at the bottom.
- **The title says what happened**, in one line: "Verified", "Due date moved", "Evidence linked". As a sentence, who first: "Nadia Flores approved payout batch ACH-4182", the name in medium weight, the verb subtle, the record a link.
- **The meta says who and what changed**: "Dana Whitfield · 14 Sep → 18 Sep". **The description says why**, in one sentence.
- **The footer is the kind, then the state**: "Payout · Same day", "Risk · High". Or the name, when the title is the thing done: "Maya Brooks · Done".
- **The time matches its place**: "2h ago" and "Yesterday" at the end of the line or in the footer; "6 May 2026" above; "May 2025" in the column. The full stamp is the tooltip.
- **Group by period**: "This week", "August", "Earlier". A count on the group when there are more than a few.

## Style

| Element     | Token                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| ----------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Rail        | 1px · `color.border` · through the marker column's centre, each row its own piece, the first row's top and the last row's bottom hidden                                                                                                             |
| Marker      | slot 16, 20 or 24px · ring 12 or 16px `color.border` on `elevation.surface.raised` · Dot in the tone · disc the slot's size in `color.background.{tone}.bold` with a 12 or 16px icon in `color.text.inverse`, neutral in `color.background.neutral` |
| Row         | `space.050`, `space.075` or `space.100` block by size · `space.050` inline · `space.100` between marker and text · `space.150` between the time column and the marker · `radius.medium` when it clicks                                              |
| Across      | rail 1px `color.border` between markers, from the marker when start-aligned · time `space.050` above the marker or first under it · text `space.075` below · equal columns, 420px in all at least                                                   |
| Title       | `font.body` · `color.text` · medium when emphasised                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| Time        | `font.body.xsmall` · `color.text.subtle` · tabular · right-aligned in the column                                                                                                                                                                    |
| Meta        | `font.body.xsmall` · `color.text.subtle` · one line                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| Description | `font.body.small` · `color.text.subtle`                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| Footer      | `font.body.xsmall` · `color.text.subtle` · `space.075` between its parts · `space.025` above                                                                                                                                                        |
| Group       | Eyebrow · on the title column · `space.050` below, `space.150` above after the first · `elevation.surface.current` behind                                                                                                                           |
| Hover       | `color.background.neutral.subtle.hovered`                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| Active      | `color.background.selected` · `color.background.selected.hovered`                                                                                                                                                                                   |

Down the page the list is one CSS grid the rows share, time · marker · body, and each row a subgrid of it: the time column is as wide as its widest stamp, the marker column as wide as the size's slot, and the rail is drawn inside the marker column, so it is centred by construction.

## Accessibility

- **The list is an ordered list**, named by `label`, and every event an `li`; a group is an `li` holding a heading and its own list, labelled by the heading.
- **The title is the control.** A row that opens is a link or a button named by the title alone and stretched over the row; the time, the meta, the description and the footer are read as the text beside it. Nothing interactive sits inside it: the trailing slot, a file's download, a menu and the buttons in the body are their own stops beside it.
- **The time is a `<time>`** when `dateTime` is given, so the machine stamp travels with the words; the full stamp is the tooltip.
- **Tone is never alone.** The marker's colour says the kind; the title says what happened. A footer Badge says the state in a word.
- **An Avatar as the marker is decorative** when the name is in the title, so the name is read once.
- **A plain row is not focusable.**

## Props

_Props: generated from `Timeline`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._

_Props: generated from `Timeline.Item`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._

_Props: generated from `Timeline.Group`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._

The existing Timeline.Item accepts a marker, icon, tone, sentence, metadata, timestamp, body and footer. Feed event taxonomies and their mappings stay in the consuming application; no separate shared Activity.Item wrapper is required.

_Example: story `Stories.FeedComposition`._

## Related

- [Item](?path=/docs/components-item--docs): rows that are things, not events.
- [Stepper](?path=/docs/components-stepper--docs): a fixed path with a current step, which a horizontal timeline resembles and is not; with a record under each milestone.
- [Collapsible](?path=/docs/components-collapsible--docs): a detail folded under a row.

_Example: story `Stories.Dont`._
