<!-- page: Components/Toaster (src/stories/components/Toaster.mdx) -->

# Toaster

Short feedback after an action. This family follows shadcn's Base UI Toast implementation, with Ledger surfaces, typography, motion and localized labels.

## Anatomy

Mount one Toaster near the application root. It composes ToastProvider, ToastPortal, ToastViewport and a stack of Toast / ToastContent / ToastTitle / ToastDescription / ToastAction / ToastClose parts. The default stack is at the bottom end edge, bounded on narrow screens.

```tsx
<Toaster />;
// After the provider mounts, from a workflow:
const id = toast.add({ title: "Evidence linked", type: "success" });
toast.update(id, { description: "Bank reconciliation, July" });
toast.close(id);
```

## Variants and states

Set `type` to success, info, warning, error or loading for the standard icons. Toaster defaults to a 4000ms timeout and four visible toasts. Set `timeout: 0` for persistent feedback. Application errors explicitly use 8000ms; the native manager does not infer timeouts from type.

_Example: story `Stories.Playground`._

Supply `actionProps` with `children` and `onClick`. The action does not close automatically: call `close(id)` when it should dismiss. This lets an action update a toast or keep it visible while work continues.

_Example: story `Stories.WithAction`._

`promise` replaces loading feedback with the resolved or rejected result and returns a promise with the original value. Await or handle its rejection as usual.

_Example: story `Stories.Working`._

## Accessibility

Base UI owns announcements, timers, stack focus and swipe dismissal. F6 focuses the notification viewport; Shift+Tab from that viewport returns to the previous element. Hover and focus pause timers. Each default toast includes a localized Close button. Loading icons are decorative because the toast already announces the work.

Keep essential record state in persistent page content. Toast portals participate in Base UI popup accessibility, including while a dialog is open.

_Example: story `Stories.InDialog`._

## Props

Toaster accepts native Provider props: `children`, `timeout`, `limit` and `toastManager`. It is state-only and has no DOM ref. For custom placement or presentation, compose the exported parts; ToastViewport owns native div props/ref, direction and accessible name. Styled parts retain native `render`, refs and class/style state callbacks. `createToastManager` isolates stacks, and `useToastManager` reads the nearest provider's toasts and actions.

_Example: story `Stories.NativeOptions`._

Migration: replace `toast.success(message, options)` with `toast.add({ title: message, type: "success", ...options })`; use `close` instead of `dismiss`, `timeout` instead of `duration`, zero instead of Infinity, and `actionProps.children` instead of `action.label`. The callable Sonner adapter and Sonner Toaster options are removed. Independent stacks use separate managers. A manager must have a mounted provider before feedback can be shown.

## Related

[Alert](?path=/docs/components-alert--docs), [Banner](?path=/docs/components-banner--docs), [AlertDialog](?path=/docs/components-alertdialog--docs), [Spinner](?path=/docs/components-spinner--docs).

Sources: [shadcn Toast](https://ui.shadcn.com/docs/components/base/toast), [implementation](https://github.com/shadcn-ui/ui/blob/main/apps/v4/registry/bases/base/ui/toast.tsx), [Base UI Toast](https://base-ui.com/react/components/toast).

<!-- page: Components/Toggle (src/stories/components/Toggle.mdx) -->

# Toggle

A two-state button built on Base UI with the shadcn composition API. Put icons and labels in `children`; give an icon-only toggle an `aria-label`.

```tsx
<Toggle aria-label="Bold">
  <Bold aria-hidden />
</Toggle>
```

_Example: story `Stories.ToggleMatrix`._

## Variants and state

`variant="default"` is unbordered; `variant="outline"` adds a border. Sizes are `sm` (28px), `default` (32px) and `lg` (36px). The default size is `default`.

Use `defaultPressed` for local state, or `pressed` and `onPressedChange(pressed, details)` for controlled state. Calling `details.cancel()` rejects a change. `disabled` blocks activation and removes the toggle from the normal tab order.

Native attributes, event handlers and refs reach the button. `render` composes another action element; it must forward props and refs. Set `nativeButton={false}` for a non-button action. `className` and `style` accept callbacks with `{ pressed, disabled }`. `toggleVariants({ variant, size, className })` exposes the shared styling recipe.

## Accessibility

The native button reports `aria-pressed`. Enter and Space toggle it; Tab moves to the next control. Keep its name stable when the pressed state changes. Icons supplied as children should be decorative when the label already names the action.

For coordinated selection, use [ToggleGroup](?path=/docs/components-togglegroup--docs). It provides one tab stop and arrow-key navigation among its items.

## Migration

Replace `icon={<Bold />}` with `<Bold aria-hidden />` inside the toggle. Size names are now `sm`, `default` and `lg`; use `sm` for a former 28px `small` toggle and `default` for a former 32px `medium` toggle. There is no 24px size preset. The appearance follows the shared shadcn toggle recipe rather than the previous recessed control.

## Props

_Props: generated from `Toggle`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._

_Example: story `Stories.Playground`._

_Rendered in the Storybook: Controls._

## Related

[ToggleGroup](?path=/docs/components-togglegroup--docs) · [Switch](?path=/docs/components-switch--docs) · [Button](?path=/docs/components-button--docs) · [Base UI Toggle](https://base-ui.com/react/components/toggle)

<!-- page: Components/ToggleGroup (src/stories/components/ToggleGroup.mdx) -->

# ToggleGroup

A group of toggle buttons with shared selection and keyboard navigation. Compose each choice with `ToggleGroupItem`, using a unique `value` and explicit children for its label, icon or count.

```tsx
<ToggleGroup aria-label="View" defaultValue={["table"]} variant="outline">
  <ToggleGroupItem value="table">Table</ToggleGroupItem>
  <ToggleGroupItem value="board">Board</ToggleGroupItem>
</ToggleGroup>
```

_Example: story `Stories.ToggleGroupMatrix`._

## Selection and layout

Selection is an array in both modes. By default, at most one item can be pressed; pressing it again clears the selection. Add `multiple` to allow several pressed items. `defaultValue` initializes local state; `value` and `onValueChange(values, details)` control it. Call `details.cancel()` to reject a change, such as clearing a required view.

Group `variant` and `size` pass to its items. Variants are `default` and `outline`; sizes are `sm` (28px), `default` (32px) and `lg` (36px). Default `spacing={2}` leaves an 8px gap; `spacing={0}` joins the items. `orientation="vertical"` stacks them and changes arrow navigation.

The group and items support native attributes, refs, `render`, and state callbacks for `className` and `style`. Use `disabled` on an item or the whole group to block selection.

_Example: story `Stories.ViewsStory`._

## Accessibility

- The root has `role="group"`; each item is a button with `aria-pressed`. Name the group with `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`, and give icon-only items an accessible name.
- Tab enters and leaves the group as one stop. Arrow keys move focus; Enter or Space changes selection. Disabled items are skipped.
- Horizontal arrows follow the Ledger locale direction; `dir` on the group overrides it. Vertical groups use Up and Down. Home and End reach the first and last enabled items.
- Focus wraps by default. Set `loopFocus={false}` to stop at the ends.
- Add [Tooltip](?path=/docs/components-tooltip--docs) explicitly when an icon needs a visible explanation.

## Migration

Replace `items` with `ToggleGroupItem` children, scalar `value` with an array, and `onChange` with `onValueChange`. The old required single-selection rule now belongs to the consumer: ignore or cancel an empty selection when one choice must remain active. `small` becomes `sm`; `medium` becomes `default`. Counts are explicit Count children, and icons are ordinary children. `isIconOnly` and automatic item tooltips are removed.

This uses the installed Base UI array API with `multiple`; it does not use Radix's `type="single"` or `type="multiple"` API.

## Props

_Props: generated from `ToggleGroup`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._

_Props: generated from `ToggleGroupItem`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._

_Example: story `Stories.Playground`._

_Rendered in the Storybook: Controls._

## Related

[Toggle](?path=/docs/components-toggle--docs) · [Count](?path=/docs/components-count--docs) · [shadcn Toggle Group](https://ui.shadcn.com/docs/components/base/toggle-group) · [Base UI Toggle Group](https://base-ui.com/react/components/toggle-group)

<!-- page: Components/Tooltip (src/stories/components/Tooltip.mdx) -->

# Tooltip

A supplementary visual label on hover or keyboard focus, using shadcn's Base UI composition. IconButton already draws one from its `label`; only compose a separate tooltip when its content differs, such as a keyboard shortcut.

```tsx
<TooltipProvider delay={300} timeout={300}>
  <Tooltip>
    <TooltipTrigger render={<IconButton label="Search" icon={<Search />} isTooltipDisabled />} />
    <TooltipContent>Search <Kbd>K</Kbd></TooltipContent>
  </Tooltip>
</TooltipProvider>
```

## Composition

Root owns open state. Trigger renders a button by default; `render` composes an existing button, link or span with its native props, handlers and ref. It does not give a rendered link or span button semantics, and has no `nativeButton` prop. A custom trigger must accept merged props and its ref.

Content includes the portal, positioner and decorative arrow. Native props, `ref`, `render`, and state callbacks for `className` and `style` target the popup. Placement defaults to top/center with `sideOffset={4}` and `alignOffset={0}`; those four positioning props belong on Content. Logical sides follow the Ledger locale or Content's explicit `dir`.

The surface retains Ledger's bold neutral fill, inverse text, small body text and spacing tokens. Its maximum width is 320px, constrained by available space; use native `style` to override it. The arrow uses Ledger's 8px size and small radius. Content stays inside an enclosing dialog's portal boundary so it remains visible and hoverable there.

_Example: story `Stories.TooltipMatrix`._

## Timing and interaction

TooltipProvider shares hover timing across a group. Its shadcn default is `delay={0}`; Base UI's `timeout` defaults to 400ms. Shell and Storybook explicitly use `delay={300}` and `timeout={300}` to preserve the product's timing. Without a provider, Base UI uses a 600ms trigger delay and no shared group; no local fallback provider is created.

Trigger accepts `delay`, `closeDelay` and `closeOnClick`. An adjacent tooltip opens immediately during the provider's timeout. Keyboard focus opens without the hover delay. Pointer passage into the popup keeps it open; leaving both, moving focus away, clicking the trigger or pressing Escape dismisses it. Trigger clicks close by default; `closeOnClick={false}` changes that behavior. Touch retains the trigger's action without opening a hover tooltip.

Use Root's `defaultOpen`, or controlled `open` with `onOpenChange(open, details)`. `details.cancel()` rejects a state change. Generic payloads let several triggers share one Root and provide content through its children function.

_Example: story `Stories.IconButtons`._

## Accessibility and disabled actions

Give the trigger its own accessible name and keep essential instructions visible. Base UI 1.7 does not automatically add `role="tooltip"` or `aria-describedby`; the popup is a visual supplement, not the control's accessible name or description. Keep controls and links out of the popup; use Popover for content the reader needs to interact with.

Trigger's `disabled` disables tooltip interaction; it does not disable the rendered button. Put the native `disabled` prop on the rendered Button. To explain an unavailable action on hover and keyboard focus, render a focusable span around its disabled button, and expose the reason independently in text or the wrapper's accessible name. The application uses this composition in UnavailableAction.

Inside a Dialog, Escape dismisses an open tooltip first while keeping focus on its trigger. A subsequent Escape can dismiss the dialog.

_Example: story `Stories.Unavailable`._

## Migration and API

Move `content` into TooltipContent, the old child trigger into `TooltipTrigger render`, timing onto Trigger or Provider, and placement/styles onto Content. The old 260px maximum and 6px offset become 320px and 4px, with an arrow. Remove redundant outer tooltips around IconButton; use `isTooltipDisabled` when composing custom content.

Props follow Base UI's [Provider](https://base-ui.com/react/components/tooltip#provider), [Root](https://base-ui.com/react/components/tooltip#root), [Trigger](https://base-ui.com/react/components/tooltip#trigger) and [Popup](https://base-ui.com/react/components/tooltip#popup), with the four positioning props added to Content. See [shadcn Tooltip](https://ui.shadcn.com/docs/components/base/tooltip) for its source composition.

## Related

[IconButton](?path=/docs/components-iconbutton--docs) · [Kbd](?path=/docs/components-kbd--docs) · [HoverCard](?path=/docs/components-hovercard--docs) · [Popover](?path=/docs/components-popover--docs) · [Overlays](?path=/docs/components-overlays--docs)

<!-- page: Components/Tree (src/stories/components/Tree.mdx) -->

# Tree

A hierarchy the reader opens and closes: control families, a system's composition, a folder of evidence. The caller owns the data, the open set and the selection and renders one row per visible node; the tree draws the indent guides, the chevron on rows that have children, and owns the keyboard: one tab stop, the arrows move and open, Enter selects. The ARIA tree pattern is the model.

A tree is for two or more levels. One level is a collapsible [Item](?path=/docs/components-item--docs) list; a hierarchy with columns is [Table.Tree](?path=/docs/components-table--docs).

_Example: story `Stories.TreeMatrix`._

## Anatomy

| Part     | What it is                                                                                                                              |
| -------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Row      | One visible node, 32px (`small`) or 24px (`xsmall`), the tree item itself: focusable, selected on a click.                              |
| Guides   | One 16px column per ancestor level, a hairline down it while that ancestor's branch continues (`lines`).                                |
| Chevron  | On a branch: right while closed, down while open. A click on it opens or closes without selecting. A leaf has a small dot in its place. |
| Icon     | Optional, before the label, 16px: a folder for a branch, a document for a leaf. On every row, or on none.                               |
| Label    | `font.body` in `color.text`, one line. It is the row's accessible name.                                                                 |
| Trailing | At the end: a Count of what is beneath, a Badge for the row's state, a Dot.                                                             |

## Variants

Tree has one appearance. What varies:

| Variant    | Use                                                                                                                                                          |
| ---------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Selectable | Rows with `onSelect` and one `isSelected`: the tree is a navigator, and the selected row is where the reader is. The composition browser, the families rail. |
| Read-only  | No `onSelect`: the tree only shows shape. Rare; a hierarchy worth drawing is usually worth opening.                                                          |
| With icons | An icon on every row, so labels at one level align; see Don't.                                                                                               |

Not built, and why: multi-select with checkboxes, because bulk work on nodes is a table; drag to reorder, because nothing here is rearranged by hand; a tree that owns its data, because the callers already flatten a tree with rolled-up posture on every row.

## Sizes

| Size     | Row  | Where                                                           |
| -------- | ---- | --------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `small`  | 32px | The default: a composition browser, a families rail.            |
| `xsmall` | 24px | A deep tree that must show more at once; a tree inside a panel. |

Rows stack with no space between them. The indent is 16px per level, the guide down its middle.

_Example: story `Stories.Families`._

## States

| State    | What changes                                                                                                                                   |
| -------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Plain    | Text on the surface.                                                                                                                           |
| Hover    | `color.background.neutral.subtle.hovered` across the row.                                                                                      |
| Selected | `color.background.selected`; `aria-selected`. The row is the initial tab stop; focus can move independently. If its branch is closed, the parent shows the selection instead. |
| Focus    | The focus outline around the row, on keyboard focus.                                                                                           |
| Open     | The chevron down; `aria-expanded="true"`; the children rendered under it by the caller.                                                        |
| Closed   | The chevron right; `aria-expanded="false"`; a Count in `trailing` says how many are beneath.                                                   |

## Modifiers

- **`depth`** and **`lines`**: how deep, and which ancestors' guides to draw. A last child under each ancestor clears that ancestor's line.
- **`hasChildren`**, **`expanded`**, **`onToggle`** on a branch; **`isSelected`**, **`onSelect`** on a selectable row.
- **`trailing`** for a Count, a Badge or a Dot. A button there is a tab stop of its own, outside the tree's keyboard model.
- **`size`** on the tree; **`label`** names it.

## Content

- **Branch labels say what kind of children they hold**: "Finance", "Payables", "Ground segment".
- **Leaf labels say what the node is**: "CTRL-0412 Segregation of duties", "mission-api:2.1.4".
- **Icons on every row or none**: a folder and a document, and nothing else.
- **The count beneath a closed branch goes in `trailing`**, so a closed tree still says how big it is.

## Style

| Element  | Token                                                                                                                                                      |
| -------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Row      | `dimension.control.medium` 32px `small` · `dimension.control.xsmall` 24px `xsmall` · `radius.medium` · `space.100` end padding · `space.075` between parts |
| Guide    | 16px column (`space.200`) · 1px `color.border`                                                                                                             |
| Chevron  | 20px · `color.icon.subtle`, `color.icon` on hover · `radius.small` · rotates in `motion.duration.fast`                                                     |
| Leaf dot | 4px · `color.background.neutral.pressed`                                                                                                                   |
| Label    | `font.body` · `color.text`                                                                                                                                 |
| Hover    | `color.background.neutral.subtle.hovered`                                                                                                                  |
| Selected | `color.background.selected`                                                                                                                                |
| Focus    | The focus outline                                                                                                                                          |

No left border marks the selected row: the selected fill is the same one a table row and a list row take, so a selection reads the same everywhere.

The tree retains one entry tab stop as rows are selected, removed or collapsed. Typing a label prefix moves focus without selecting. Flat visible rows receive inferred `aria-posinset` and `aria-setsize`; for partial or virtualized sibling sets, supply `posInSet` and `setSize` with the complete sibling position and count.

## Accessibility

- **It is a tree**: `role="tree"` named by `label`, every row a `treeitem` with `aria-level`, `aria-selected`, and `aria-expanded` on a branch: the ARIA pattern.
- **One entry tab stop per tree.** Initially the selected row is tabbable, or the first row when none is. Arrow navigation moves that tab stop without selecting; returning to the tree retains the last focused row. Removing that row restores focus to a preceding visible row when focus would otherwise be lost.
- **Keyboard:** Down and Up move between visible rows; Right opens a closed branch, or moves into an open one; Left closes an open branch, or moves to the parent; Home and End go to the ends; Enter or Space selects.
- **The chevron is for the mouse.** It focuses and toggles the branch without selecting it. It is hidden from the keyboard and screen readers, which have Right and Left.
- **Trailing controls are outside the model.** A button in `trailing` is its own tab stop; keep to a Count, a Badge or a Dot where the tree is long.
- **The selection is never hidden.** When the selected row's branch is closed, the caller selects the parent, so the reader does not lose their place.

_Example: story `Stories.Keyboard`._

Tree and Tree.Item accept native div attributes, styles, events and refs. Caller handlers run before their built-in handler; `preventDefault()` cancels that behavior. Use `onKeyDownCapture` on the root to reserve keys before row handling. Item’s `onSelect` is the existing node-selection callback, not the native text-selection event. Tree roles and row levels stay component-owned. An explicit `aria-label` overrides the root’s `label` shorthand; `posInSet`/`setSize` or native sibling metadata overrides inferred counts.

Embedded trees keep separate arrow navigation, typeahead and entry tab stops. Trailing controls keep their own actions and do not select the containing row.

_Example: story `Stories.NestedTrees`._

The keyboard behavior follows the [WAI-ARIA tree view pattern](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/treeview/). Root refs compose through [Base UI useRender](https://base-ui.com/react/utils/use-render#merging-refs).

## Props

_Props: generated from `Tree`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._

### Tree.Item

_Props: generated from `Tree.Item`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._

### Playground

_Example: story `Stories.Playground`._

_Rendered in the Storybook: Controls._

## Related

- [Table](?path=/docs/components-table--docs): `Table.Tree`, a hierarchy with columns.
- [Item](?path=/docs/components-item--docs): one level of nesting, as a collapsible list.
- [Collapsible](?path=/docs/components-collapsible--docs): one section that opens.

## Don't

_Example: story `Stories.Dont`._

<!-- page: Components/Typography (src/stories/components/Typography.mdx) -->

# Typography

The small text parts a record page is made of, beyond body copy and titles. `Eyebrow` is the uppercase micro-label on `font.heading.xxsmall`: a section's name in a rail, a record's kind above its title, a callout's label. `Absent` is the muted dash where a value would be. `Prose` is a labelled paragraph: an Eyebrow over body text. For body copy and titles, the [Text](?path=/docs/primitives-text--docs) and [Heading](?path=/docs/primitives-heading--docs) primitives; this page is the three parts between them.

_Example: story `Stories.TypographyMatrix`._

## Anatomy

| Part    | What it is                                                                                                     |
| ------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Eyebrow | `font.heading.xxsmall`, uppercase, `color.text.subtle`; a tone colours it. A `div`, or the element `as` names. |
| Absent  | An em dash in `color.text.subtlest`, the size of its line.                                                     |
| Prose   | An Eyebrow, then a paragraph in `font.body` and `color.text`, `space.050` between them, `space.075` above.     |

## Variants

| Part    | Use                                                                                                                                                                   |
| ------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Eyebrow | The name of a group of rows in a rail (`as="h3"`), the kind above a record's title, the label of a callout (with a tone), the label of a value in a grid (`as="dt"`). |
| Absent  | Any value that is not there: in a KeyValue, a Fact, a cell.                                                                                                           |
| Prose   | A paragraph with a name: Rationale, Objective, Condition. In a rail or a detail body.                                                                                 |

Not built, and why: a description-list primitive, because KeyValue and Fact are the two shapes of a pair; a "no data" word in place of the dash, because the dash is the product's one absent mark and reads in a column; an Eyebrow with an icon or a count, because it is a label and a count is a Count beside it.

## Sizes

One size each. The Eyebrow is `font.heading.xxsmall` whatever it heads; the Absent is its line's size; the Prose paragraph is `font.body`. A rail's Prose is as wide as the rail, a detail body's is the reading measure.

_Example: story `Stories.InRail`._

## States

None. The three are text. The tone on an Eyebrow or a Prose is a colour for a callout, not a state.

## Modifiers

- **Eyebrow `tone`** for a callout's label: `warning` over a condition, `danger` over a finding. `neutral`, the default, is `color.text.subtle`.
- **Eyebrow `as`**: `h3` or `h4` when it heads a section, so the page's outline has it; `dt` when it labels a value; `span` inline.
- **Prose `label`** and **`tone`**: the paragraph's name, and its colour when it is a callout.

## Content

- **An eyebrow is one to three words**, a noun: "Schedule", "By supplier origin", "Rationale". Uppercase is set by the component; write it in sentence case.
- **Prose is one paragraph** under its name. Two paragraphs are two Prose, or a section.
- **The dash means nothing here.** "N/A" means not applicable, "Unknown" means unknown; those are values and are written as words.

## Style

| Element | Token                                                                                     |
| ------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Eyebrow | `font.heading.xxsmall` · uppercase · `color.text.subtle` · `color.text.<tone>` when toned |
| Absent  | `color.text.subtlest` · the line's font                                                   |
| Prose   | `font.body` · `color.text` · `space.050` under the eyebrow · `space.075` above            |

The eyebrow moved from `color.text.subtlest` to `color.text.subtle` in this walk: a label is secondary text, and the prototype had written forty-five of its own eyebrows in subtle against eight in subtlest. The Shell's section headings and the Preview eyebrow took the step with it.

## Accessibility

- **An eyebrow that heads a section is a heading**, with `as="h3"` or `h4`, so the page's outline lists it and a screen reader can jump to it. As a `div` it is a label and is read in place.
- **Uppercase is styling**, so a screen reader reads the words, not the letters; write the text in sentence case.
- **The dash is read as a dash**, which is enough for "nothing"; it is not hidden, because an empty cell would be read as nothing at all and the reader could not tell a gap from a skip.
- **Contrast:** `color.text.subtle` at 11px uppercase passes 4.5:1, and `color.text.subtlest` does for the dash; the gate runs every tone.

## Props

### Eyebrow

_Props: generated from `Eyebrow`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._

### Absent

_Props: generated from `Absent`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._

### Prose

_Props: generated from `Prose`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._

### Playground

_Example: story `Stories.Playground`._

_Rendered in the Storybook: Controls._

## Related

- [Text](?path=/docs/primitives-text--docs), [Heading](?path=/docs/primitives-heading--docs): body copy and titles.
- [KeyValue](?path=/docs/components-keyvalue--docs), [Fact](?path=/docs/components-fact--docs): the two shapes of a labelled value.
- [Alert](?path=/docs/components-alert--docs): the callout an eyebrow with a tone often heads.

## Don't

_Example: story `Stories.Dont`._

<!-- page: Layout/PageHeader (src/stories/layout/PageHeader.mdx) -->

# PageHeader

One composable page header for collections and records. Two columns: Heading, what names the page, on the left; Actions on the right; Lead across both above them. Native header, heading, paragraph and div props and refs pass through every part.

_Example: story `Stories.Collection`._
_Example: story `Stories.Record`._
_Example: story `Stories.Constrained`._

Compose a Heading with a Title, an optional Lead and one primary action or Actions menu. A breadcrumb is the Lead through `render={<Breadcrumb />}`; a category line is a Lead with text. Record fields, owner/status editors and property strips belong in the work area or Aside, not in PageHeader or a preview header. Description is optional and wraps without hiding content behind a tooltip.

Use PageHeader.Title once for the page's h1. Panel and dialog headings use their own h2 semantics. Actions always occupy a fixed column beside the title, including at phone widths; titles wrap to their left. Keep action groups on one line; use a dropdown when several actions compete for space.

No part has props of its own: the root is a `header`, Heading and Actions are `div`s, Title an `h1`, Description a `p`, and Lead a `div` or the element given to `render`; each takes its element's native props and ref.

<!-- page: Layout/Pages (src/stories/layout/Pages.mdx) -->

# Page composition

Mount the application shell once around the router outlet. Routes compose normal primitives and components inside Main and contribute optional Aside or Panel content. There are no collection-page or record-page wrapper APIs. A collection page is a PageHeader and a DataTable with `fill`, which takes the rest of the window; see Register.

The record example brings the visual conventions together: an Actions menu beside the title, a descriptive method selector, a standard input, and inline status and owner editors. App and Storybook load Geist and Geist Mono. Select and Combobox share row spacing, persistent choice indicators and neutral keyboard highlights; descriptions grow the row instead of clipping.

_Example: story `Stories.Record`._
_Example: story `Stories.Register`._
_Example: story `Stories.QueueWithPanel`._
_Example: story `Stories.CompactQueue`._

## Regions and behavior

- **Main** contains the page header, filters, tabs and work area. Keep these visible controls in the route.
- **Aside** provides supporting context, such as properties. It follows Main below the `aside` breakpoint (`dimension.breakpoint.aside`, 75rem: 1200px at the default root size) and sits beside it above that. When a Panel is also open, Aside follows Main until the `wide` breakpoint (110rem, 1760px). The breakpoints are tokens; [Metrics](?path=/docs/tokens-metrics--docs) lists them.
- **Panel** holds a selected record or task. From the `panel` breakpoint (80rem, 1280px) it is a resizable column beside Main that runs the full height of the window; the banner and the top nav stop at its edge. Below that it replaces the visible work area under the top nav while Main stays mounted. Close or Escape returns focus to the opener when it still exists.
- **Sheet** is the modal surface for a workflow that needs focus containment. Compose it with the existing Base UI components.

A route contributes at most one Aside and one Panel. Their portal destinations remain stable across route updates. Route React context travels with the contribution, and unmounting the route removes it. Slots appear after mounting; server rendering does not render portaled region content. The application restores its browser workspace before rendering routes.

## Tabs and accessibility

Keep each tab's primary content inside its TabsContent. Supporting context is a separate labelled landmark and is conditional on the selected tab. Give pages one h1, panels an h2, and contextual regions meaningful names. Avoid placing modal semantics on a panel that leaves global navigation available.

The examples test route cleanup, retained context, tab relationships, queue state, resizing and focus return. Responsive behavior is also checked in the application.

## Extending

Compose a new route from Stack, Inline, Grid, PageHeader and the controls it needs. Add a pattern when a repeated interaction earns one—for example record selection, coordinated filtering, or calendar scheduling. Layout ownership stays in Shell.

<!-- page: Layout/PageSkeleton (src/stories/layout/PageSkeleton.mdx) -->

# PageSkeleton

What a screen looks like before its data arrives: a title and a line, a tab strip, then a table's worth of rows, in the [Skeleton](?path=/docs/components-skeleton--docs)'s shapes. The router shows it for every route that is still loading, so it is the shape most pages share, an index. A page loads progressively; a section that loads on its own draws its own Skeleton inside a page that has already landed.

_Example: story `Stories.PageSkeletonMatrix`._

## Anatomy

| Part | What it is                                                                                     |
| ---- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Head | A heading shape 240px wide and a line 440px wide, where a PageHeader's title and line will be. |
| Tabs | Four short lines over a rule, where a Tabs strip or a filter row will be.                      |
| Rows | `rows` lines of a table: an id, a title that fills, two values; `space.200` apart.             |

## Variants

One skeleton. Not built, and why: a record variant with a facts strip and a rail, because the router shows one skeleton before it knows the route's shape, and a record's first paint lands within the same 150ms; per-section skeletons, because those are the sections' own, drawn from Skeleton where they load.

## Sizes

`rows` sets how many rows to draw, 8 by default, about a screen at the register's row height. The skeleton is as wide as the page.

## States

One state: waiting. The whole is a `status` region marked busy and named "Loading", so a screen reader hears one announcement and not a hundred grey bars.

## Modifiers

- **`rows`** as in Sizes.

## Content

- **The shape of an index.** A page that is not one still lands on the same title line, so the swap is small.
- **Shown after 150ms**: the router's pending delay, so a fast route never flashes it.
- **Never beside content.** It replaces the page; a section that loads later draws its own.

## Style

| Element | Token                                                                             |
| ------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Head    | Skeleton heading and line · `space.150` between                                   |
| Tabs    | four Skeleton lines · `space.250` apart · `color.border` rule · `space.150` under |
| Rows    | Skeleton lines · `space.200` between rows and cells                               |
| Layout  | `space.300` between the three parts                                               |

## Accessibility

- **A `role="status"` marked `aria-busy`** and named "Loading", so the wait is announced once.
- **The bars are hidden**; the region carries the meaning.
- **Reduced motion stops the pulse**; the shapes stay.

## Props

_Props: generated from `PageSkeleton`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._

### Playground

_Example: story `Stories.Playground`._

_Rendered in the Storybook: Controls._

## Related

- [Skeleton](?path=/docs/components-skeleton--docs): the shapes it is drawn from.
- [Pages](?path=/docs/layout-pages--docs): the index it stands in for.
- [Spinner](?path=/docs/components-spinner--docs): a wait on an action, not a page.

## Don't

_Example: story `Stories.Dont`._

<!-- page: Layout/Section (src/stories/layout/Section.mdx) -->

# Section

Optional presentation for a titled content region. `title`, `count`, `description` and `action` render the built-in header; leave `title` out and compose Section.Header, Section.Heading, Section.Title, Section.Description and Section.Actions yourself when the heading needs another level, a badge, or two actions. The Title names the region either way. Native section props and refs pass through every part. A rule is opt-in with `divided`.

_Example: story `Stories.Presentation`._
_Example: story `Stories.Composed`._
_Example: story `Stories.Untitled`._

Use Stack or Grid directly when no titled region is needed. Compose Collapsible when disclosure helps the workflow. Section imposes no distinction between work, reference, forms or narrative.

_Props: generated from `Section`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._
_Props: generated from `Section.Header`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._

Heading, Description and Actions take only their element's native props; Title takes `render` for another heading level.

<!-- page: Layout/Shell (src/stories/layout/Shell.mdx) -->

# Shell

The persistent application frame, inspired by [Atlassian's navigation layout](https://atlassian.design/components/navigation-system/layout/). It owns navigation, page gutters, responsive placement and panel scrolling. Product code supplies navigation links and route content.

_Example: story `Stories.Frame`._
_Example: story `Stories.ComposedPanel`._

Mount Shell once in a shared router layout. Place Banner, TopNav, SideNav and Main there. Child routes render Shell.Aside or Shell.Panel to contribute to the frame's stable region slots. Contributions preserve route React context and disappear when their route unmounts. They mount on the client after slot destinations exist.

Every part renders one element and forwards its native props and its ref to it; AppLogo, Profile, SideNav.Item and Panel.Title take Base UI `render` where the element may change, so Profile is a menu's trigger through `render` and a side nav item is a router link. The SideNav.ToggleButton is a child of TopNav.Start and places itself; TopNav.End is a named group that renders its children as given, and a product that needs them to fold on a phone renders its own menu there.

Aside contains supporting context. Panel contains dismissible selected-record or task content. With `title` (and `actions`) it renders its built-in header, close and resizer; without them compose Panel.Header, Panel.Title, Panel.Actions, Panel.Close, Panel.Body and Panel.Splitter yourself, as Composed panel shows, to change the heading's level, the labels or the padding. Panel.onClose is required either way and the Title names the landmark. From the `panel` breakpoint (`dimension.breakpoint.panel`, 80rem: 1280px at the default root size; see [Metrics](?path=/docs/tokens-metrics--docs)) the panel is the last column for the whole height of the window: the banner and the top nav stop at its edge, so opening it narrows everything and covers nothing. Below it the panel replaces the visible Main area under the top nav while retaining Main's state, and it returns focus on close. Global navigation remains available; use Sheet for modal work.

Every default name (Banner, Top navigation, Side navigation, Main content, Page context, Details, Actions, Switch product, the toggle's two labels, the splitters' and the skip links') is a locale message, so a product translates them once with `LedgerLocaleProvider`; a `label` prop overrides one instance. The splitters take the arrow keys, Home for the minimum and End for the maximum. What `persist` restores is validated and clamped to the screen it is restored on.

SideNav retains its existing collapse, persistence, keyboard and resize behavior. Main uses document scrolling; Panel scrolls inside the available viewport. A register that is the page fills the rest of the window with DataTable `fill`: Main publishes its bottom inset as `--shell-inset-bottom`, and the layout otherwise owns placement, so content patterns do not add sticky rails or nested page frames.

Set `collapsedSideNav="icons"` on Shell to keep a 56px navigation rail when collapsed on desktop. The default, `"hidden"`, hides the side nav and retains the hover flyout. Supply meaningful icons for top-level items and expandable groups. In icon mode, destination names remain accessible and appear in tooltips on hover or focus; the active destination and profile avatar remain visible. Section headings and nested destinations are visually hidden. Custom SideNav.Header content, such as navigation search, is hidden in the rail and returns when expanded. Activating an expandable group expands the shell and opens that group. Hovering the toggle does not open a flyout in this mode. With the default app mark, the collapsed expand control occupies the mark’s existing position and appears on hover or keyboard focus. The mark is visible at rest, and the product name keeps its position through collapse and expansion. Phone navigation keeps its separate visible toggle. The splitter returns with the remembered width when expanded, and phone navigation continues to use the existing overlay. `shellScript` and `shellScriptFor` preserve the compact rail before hydration when collapse state is stored. See [Icon rail](?path=/story/layout-shell-icon-rail--desktop) for keyboard, RTL, phone and first-paint examples.

`Shell.Panel.actions` places route-owned controls immediately before Close in the built-in header. Collection previews compose `Panel.Header`, `Panel.Actions` and `Panel.Close` for a navigation-only outer bar: previous/next through the displayed rows, a native full-record link and, for nested frames, Back. Put the visible record name and domain commands in a `PageHeader` at the beginning of `Panel.Body`, using an h2 and `PageHeader.Actions`. Give the panel an accessible `label` when its outer bar has no `Panel.Title`. The route owns row order, destinations and endpoint availability; Shell only supplies placement. The Record header narrow story exercises both headers at the minimum panel width.

See [page composition](?path=/docs/layout-pages--docs) for route and tab examples.

## Props

The parts with props of their own. The others (SideNav.Header, Body and Footer, TopNav.Middle, Mark, Panel.Header, Actions and Body) take only their element's native props; Panel.Title takes `render`.

_Props: generated from `Shell`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._

_Props: generated from `Shell.Profile`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._

### Panel

_Props: generated from `Shell.Panel`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._
_Props: generated from `Shell.Panel.Close`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._
_Props: generated from `Shell.Panel.Splitter`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._

### Narrow panel headers

Panel header slots respond to the panel container, including a manually resized desktop panel. Below 400px, a title with actions occupies a full row and navigation/Close share the row beneath; title-only headers keep Close beside the title. Below 320px, a PageHeader inside the panel also puts its action slot below its heading. The normal desktop header remains one row. See the 240px, 320px and 640px Panel header stories, composed-slot forwarding and Panel record header examples.

<!-- page: Layout/Shell/Icon rail (src/stories/layout/ShellIconRail.mdx) -->

# Shell icon rail

Set `collapsedSideNav="icons"` on Shell to retain destination icons, the active destination and the profile avatar in a 56px rail on desktop. Names remain accessible and appear in tooltips on hover or focus. Activating an expandable group restores the full navigation and opens its children. The default collapsed mode remains `"hidden"`. With the default app mark, the collapsed expand control occupies the mark’s existing position and appears on hover or keyboard focus. The mark is visible at rest, and the product name keeps its position through collapse and expansion. Phone navigation keeps its separate visible toggle.

_Example: story `Stories.Desktop`._

Expand and minimize animate the sidebar width over Ledger's moderate duration. The page follows the sidebar while the app mark stays fixed; resizing follows the pointer immediately. Reduced motion and restoring a remembered layout skip the transition.

_Example: story `Stories.WidthMotion`._

On phones, navigation slides in and out with a fading scrim, and returns focus to its toggle when dismissed. Closing navigation stops accepting input immediately, and reversing the action continues from its current position. The rail does not take space from the page.

_Example: story `Stories.Mobile390`._

The RTL and persisted first-paint stories verify logical placement and restoration before hydration. See [Shell](?path=/docs/layout-shell--docs) for composition, persistence, keyboard behavior and the complete API.

<!-- page: Patterns/Chart/Overview (src/stories/patterns/Chart.mdx) -->

# Chart

Data drawn on the chart tokens. `Chart` is the Frame: the figure that names a plot, keys it, holds its states, keeps the way back from a drill-down, and lays the same numbers out as a table one toggle away. Each kind of plot is its own part with its own page: [Bar](?path=/docs/patterns-chart-bar--docs), [Line](?path=/docs/patterns-chart-line--docs), [Area](?path=/docs/patterns-chart-area--docs), [Donut](?path=/docs/patterns-chart-donut--docs), [Sparkline](?path=/docs/patterns-chart-sparkline--docs), [Scatter](?path=/docs/patterns-chart-scatter--docs), [Treemap](?path=/docs/patterns-chart-treemap--docs) and [Heatmap](?path=/docs/patterns-chart-heatmap--docs). Recharts draws; the kit decides the paint, the marks, the grid, the tooltip, the legend and the motion, so a chart reads like the rest of the page in both modes. The colour rules follow the data-visualization method, and the categorical order is validated, not eyeballed.

_Example: story `Stories.Framed`._

## Kinds

The data's job picks the kind, and sometimes the right kind is not a chart: one number is a [Stat](?path=/docs/components-stat--docs), one ratio against a limit is a [Progress](?path=/docs/components-progress--docs) bar, and more than seven classes that all carry meaning is a [Table](?path=/docs/components-table--docs).

| The reader must                            | Part                                                            | Colour job                              |
| ------------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------- |
| Compare sizes across categories            | [`Chart.Bar`](?path=/docs/patterns-chart-bar--docs)             | One hue; `horizontal` for long names    |
| See parts of each whole                    | `Chart.Bar` stacked                                             | Status tones, or the categorical set    |
| Read actual against planned                | `Chart.Bar` with `target`                                       | The series' tone; the target is ink     |
| See when things happen                     | `Chart.Bar` horizontal with `[from, to]` values                 | One hue                                 |
| Follow a trend                             | [`Chart.Line`](?path=/docs/patterns-chart-line--docs)           | `brand`, or a tone per series           |
| Follow parts of a whole over time          | [`Chart.Area`](?path=/docs/patterns-chart-area--docs) stacked   | Status tones, or the categorical set    |
| See one number against its whole           | [`Chart.Donut`](?path=/docs/patterns-chart-donut--docs)         | The parts' tones on the track           |
| Read a score against a scale               | `Chart.Donut` `arc="half"`                                      | The tone the score earns                |
| See a trend beside a number                | [`Chart.Sparkline`](?path=/docs/patterns-chart-sparkline--docs) | One tone                                |
| Place things on two measures               | [`Chart.Scatter`](?path=/docs/patterns-chart-scatter--docs)     | `brand`, or at most three groups        |
| See how a total splits, and splits again   | [`Chart.Treemap`](?path=/docs/patterns-chart-treemap--docs)     | The categorical set, one hue per branch |
| Read how much across two dimensions        | [`Chart.Heatmap`](?path=/docs/patterns-chart-heatmap--docs)     | `sequential`: one hue, light to dark    |
| Read above and below across two dimensions | `Chart.Heatmap` `scale="diverging"`                             | Two hues around grey                    |
| Read status by place                       | `Chart.Heatmap` with a tone function                            | The Badge's fills, values printed       |

Not built, and why: no pie (a ring with the number in the middle says more, and a two-slice pie is a Stat); no second value axis (two measures of different scale are two charts, or one indexed; a dual axis invents a correlation); no gauge with a needle (the half ring reads the same and its number is text); no radar, boxplot, histogram, lollipop, alluvial, word cloud, circle pack or map (none of the four products has asked, and a histogram is a bar chart of bins the data layer makes); no zoom, brush or export toolbar (a range is a control in the Frame's `actions`, a drill-down is the Frame's `path`, and export is the register's).

## Anatomy

| Part        | What it is                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| ----------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Title       | `font.body` medium in `color.text`, a noun phrase: what the chart shows. It names the plot to a screen reader.                                                                                                                                |
| Description | `font.body.small` in `color.text.subtle`, one line under the title: the period, the unit, the source.                                                                                                                                         |
| Path        | A [Breadcrumb](?path=/docs/components-breadcrumb--docs) under the description while a drill-down is open: every level so far, every crumb but the last a way back.                                                                            |
| Legend      | Swatch and label per series, `font.body.small` in `color.text.subtle`, at the end of the header. A square for a fill, a stroke for a line, a dot for a point. Present for two or more series; a single series needs none, the title names it. |
| Actions     | Controls at the end of the header: a range, a filter, a Retry. Then the tools: the Table toggle, the Download menu (the table twin as CSV, the plot as PNG), the Expand button.                                                               |
| Plot        | The part's marks on a hairline grid. Ticks are `font.body.xsmall` in `color.text.subtlest`; grid lines and the axis line are `color.border`, solid, 1px. Focusable when named, with the kit's focus ring on the keyboard only.                |
| Tooltip     | The overlay surface. The category first, then every series at that point: the name, then the value in `font.body.small` medium, keyed by the mark's swatch. A stack adds its total.                                                           |
| Card        | The details on a chosen mark: a Popover anchored to it, the kit's head (swatch, name, category, value; or every series at a category), then whatever the caller adds.                                                                         |
| Table       | The same numbers as a [Table](?path=/docs/components-table--docs), one toggle away: the category column, then a column per series.                                                                                                            |

## Variants

| Variant                              | Use                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| ------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `Chart` (the Frame)                  | Every chart on a page. Title, description, legend, actions, the states, the path, the table twin, the legend's interaction.                                                                                                                                              |
| `legend="top"`, `"bottom"`, `"none"` | The legend at the end of the header (the default for two or more series), under the plot when the header is busy, or nowhere for one series.                                                                                                                             |
| `path`                               | The Frame of a drill-down: the levels so far as crumbs, the last being the current one.                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `download`, `expandable`             | The tools: a Download menu with the table twin as CSV and the plot as a PNG at twice the pixel density; an Expand button that opens the same chart in a large Dialog.                                                                                                    |
| `columns`                            | Columns for the table twin and the CSV beyond the series, each a key in the datum: a name beside the category (`place: "before"`), a total, a share, an owner after the series. Facts the plot does not draw, so the twin is the record's table and not only the plot's. |
| `syncId`                             | Charts that share their hover: small multiples, one hover across them, on one `domain`.                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `texture`                            | Every series wears a pattern as well as its colour, in the plot, the legend, the tooltip and the card.                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `Chart.Legend`                       | The key on its own, outside a Frame: beside a Donut, under a stacked bar. Inside a Frame it is the interactive one.                                                                                                                                                      |
| The parts                            | One per kind, each on its own page. A part inside the Frame inherits its name, its formats, its loading state and its legend's state.                                                                                                                                    |

_Example: story `Stories.Drilldown`._
_Example: story `Stories.Details`._
_Example: story `Stories.Filtering`._
_Example: story `Stories.Linked`._
_Example: story `Stories.Downloads`._
_Example: story `Stories.Textured`._
_Example: story `Stories.Legends`._

## Sizes

| Size     | Height | Where                                                                         |
| -------- | ------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `small`  | 120px  | A rail, a card in a grid of them, a cell of the matrix.                       |
| `medium` | 200px  | A Section. The default.                                                       |
| `large`  | 320px  | The one chart a page is about: the scatter of risks, the treemap of findings. |

The height is the whole plot, axis band included, so a card never scrolls inside itself. `height` takes pixels when a layout must. The Frame's states stand in at the same height, so nothing moves when the data arrives. A Donut and a Sparkline are sized in pixels, since they sit inline; a Heatmap's `size` is its cell's height.

The width is the container's. Below about 480px the header wraps: the legend and the tools drop under the title, and the plot keeps its height. An expanded chart is the same Frame at `large` in a Dialog.

_Example: story `Stories.Narrow`._

## States

| State      | What changes                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| ---------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Hover      | The tooltip, for every series at that point; a hovered bar and a hovered slice take the tone's `hovered` step, a slice grows 2px, a line's marker appears. Synced charts show their tooltips together. A hovered legend item dims the other series to `opacity.disabled`, faded over `motion.duration.fast`. |
| Isolated   | A clicked legend item hides its series; the swatch hollows. Clicking the last visible one shows everything again.                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| Chosen     | A clicked mark, or the category Enter chose on the focused plot: the other marks dim, the card opens on it. Escape or a click outside closes the card and focus returns to the plot.                                                                                                                         |
| Loading    | The plot's own silhouette in `color.skeleton`, pulsing, at the plot's height: columns, a line, a ring, dots, tiles. The header stays.                                                                                                                                                                        |
| Refreshing | The last plot stays, dimmed to `opacity.loading`, with a Spinner beside the title. For a refetch, so the reader keeps what they had.                                                                                                                                                                         |
| Empty      | A dashed frame at the plot's height: "Nothing to show yet" and one line of why.                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| Error      | The same frame, the title in `color.text.danger`, and a Retry in `actions`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| Table      | The Table toggle swaps the plot for the same numbers as a Table; the legend and the actions stay.                                                                                                                                                                                                            |

_Example: story `Stories.States`._

## Modifiers

- **`legend`**, **`swatch`**, **`actions`**, **`status`**, **`statusTitle`**, **`statusText`** on the Frame.
- **`path`** on the Frame for a drill-down; each crumb's `onSelect` goes back.
- **`download`** (`["csv", "png"]`) and **`expandable`** for the tools; **`summary`** for the sentence a screen reader hears; **`syncId`** to share the hover; **`texture`** for the patterns.
- **`data`**, **`x`**, **`xLabel`** on the Frame, so it can lay the table out.
- **`format`** and **`formatX`** for the numbers and the categories, set once on the Frame and inherited by the part, the tooltip, the card and the table.
- **`size`** and **`height`** on the Frame, for the states that stand in for the plot; the same on the part.
- On every part: **`label`** to name a plot outside a Frame, **`loading`** to draw its skeleton, **`onSelect`** to hear a choice, **`details`** to open a card on it. Each part's page lists its own.

## Choosing a mark

A chart that answers "what is this?" and "show me more" is the point of a platform's charts, and the kit does it one way everywhere:

- **`onSelect`** hears a choice: a bar, a point, a slice, a tile, a cell. It filters what is under the chart, or drills down.
- **`details`** opens a card on the choice: the kit renders its head (the swatch, the name, the category, the value; for a whole category, every series' value) and the caller renders the rest under it, facts and a way to the record. The card is a Popover anchored to the mark: Escape and a click outside close it, and focus returns to the plot.
- **A drill-down** is a Frame whose `path` grows: the click redraws the same plot one level down, the marks moving to their new places, and the path holds the way back. Two or three levels is the ceiling; past that the reader wants a table with filters.
- **The keyboard gets the same.** A named plot is focusable; the arrow keys move across the categories with the tooltip; Enter chooses the one under the tooltip. A Heatmap's cells are buttons and do it themselves.
- **A pointer over a mark that chooses is a pointer.** A plot with neither `onSelect` nor `details` shows the default cursor and no focus ring on a click, so nothing promises what it cannot do.

## Small multiples

Two measures of different scale, or more than six series, are several small charts, not one big one. The Frame makes them honest: give every chart the same `domain`, so a bar's height means the same thing on each, and the same `syncId`, so a hover on one shows the same category on all. A cumulative that needs its own scale says so in its description and keeps `baseline="auto"`.

## Textures

Colour is never the only channel, and in print, under colour-vision loss and in a forced-colours mode it is not a channel at all. `texture` on the Frame gives every series a pattern in its own colour, in a fixed order the legend and the tooltip repeat: the first series solid, then hatch, back-hatch, dots, cross, lines, columns. The pattern is the colour at 30% under 1.5px marks in the colour, 8px across, so the series still reads as its hue. Bars, areas and rings take it; a line's stroke stays solid, since a 2px line has no room for a pattern and its marker and end label already set it apart. Turn it on for a chart that will be printed or exported, or everywhere in a product that must meet a print or high-contrast requirement.

## Motion

Marks arrive once, over `motion.duration.slow` (400ms) on the standard curve: bars grow from the baseline, lines draw in, a ring sweeps round. A change of data moves the marks the same way, which is what makes a drill-down read as the same chart one level down rather than a new one. The tooltip follows the pointer over `motion.duration.fast`; a legend hover fades the other series over the same. Under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` the marks draw in place and nothing fades. Nothing loops, nothing pulses but a skeleton, and no number counts up.

_Example: story `Stories.Motion`._

## Series and tones

Every series names a `color.chart.*` token through its `tone`. A status tone on a chart is data, the same rule as a Badge or a Stat, and a series that is not a status never wears one.

| Tone                                          | Use                                                                                                                      |
| --------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `success`, `warning`, `danger`, `information` | The series carries a status: satisfied, at risk, overdue, in progress.                                                   |
| `brand`                                       | The one series the reader is asked to look at.                                                                           |
| `neutral`                                     | Context: totals, the remainder, last period, the plan. Also a target line and Other.                                     |
| `categorical.1` to `categorical.6`            | Categories with no status, in this order: blue, orange, teal, red, purple, green. The default when a series has no tone. |
| `categorical.7`                               | Other: the fold for everything past the sixth. Grey.                                                                     |

The order is not cosmetic. It was chosen by enumerating every order of the six hues and keeping the ones whose neighbours stay apart under deutan and protan vision: the worst neighbouring pair sits at ΔE 12.7 in both modes, above the floor of 8, and the first three validate against each other in every pairing, which is why a Scatter takes three groups at most. Assign in order, never by rank: a filter that hides a series must not repaint the survivors. Past six, fold the tail into Other, split into small charts, or make a table; never a seventh hue.

Two more scales exist for a Heatmap: `color.chart.sequential.1` to `5`, blue from light to dark for how much; and `color.chart.diverging.negative.bold`, `negative`, `midpoint`, `positive`, `positive.bold`, red against blue around grey for above and below.

_Example: story `Stories.Emphasis`._

## Content

- **The title is a noun phrase**: "Coverage by control family", "Findings over time". Not a sentence, not a verb.
- **The description is the period, the unit or the source**, one line: "Opened in the month", "Sized by exposure in $K". While a drill-down is open it says the level: "Components of Payments".
- **A crumb is the level's name**: "All systems", then "Payments".
- **A series label is what the legend, the tooltip, the card and the table call it**: "Other than satisfied", not "other". Sentence case, no acronyms the reader would not say.
- **The numbers are formatted once**, on the Frame: grouped, two decimals at most, compact from ten thousand. A unit goes in `format`, so the axis, the tooltip, the labels, the card and the table agree.
- **A card's body is facts and one way onward**: two or three KeyValues and a button to the record. Not a form, not a second chart.
- **A reference says what it is**: "Target", "Limit", "Today", "Milestone C"; a date band says what happened in it: "Assessment window".
- **A summary is one sentence with the numbers in it**: "Open findings fell from 14 in January to 5 in September." A screen reader hears it after the description; nobody sees it.

## Style

| Element      | Token                                                                                                                                                |
| ------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Series       | `color.chart.<tone>` · the same step in both modes                                                                                                   |
| Grid, axis   | `color.border` · 1px solid                                                                                                                           |
| Ticks        | `font.body.xsmall` · `color.text.subtlest` · tabular                                                                                                 |
| Axis titles  | `font.body.xsmall` · `color.text.subtle`                                                                                                             |
| Labels       | `font.body.xsmall` · `color.text.subtle` · tabular                                                                                                   |
| Tooltip      | `elevation.surface.overlay` · `color.border` · `radius.medium` · `elevation.shadow.overlay` · `space.150` inline, `space.100` block                  |
| Card         | `elevation.surface.overlay` · `color.border` · `radius.large` · `elevation.shadow.overlay` · `space.150` · 280px · the value in `font.heading.small` |
| Hover cursor | `color.background.neutral.subtle.hovered` behind a bar · `color.border.bold` across a line chart                                                     |
| Reference    | `color.chart.<tone>` · 1px dashed 4 3 · label `font.body.xsmall` in `color.text.subtlest`, above the plot for a vertical line                        |
| Hovered mark | `color.chart.<tone>.hovered`: one step darker in light, one lighter in dark                                                                          |
| Texture      | The series colour at 30% under 1.5px marks in the colour · 8px repeat · `radius` 2px on a swatch                                                     |
| Dimmed       | `opacity.disabled`, over `motion.duration.fast`                                                                                                      |
| Refreshing   | `opacity.loading`                                                                                                                                    |
| Skeleton     | `color.skeleton` and `color.skeleton.subtle`, pulsing                                                                                                |
| Focus        | `color.border.focused` on the plot, keyboard only                                                                                                    |
| Motion       | `motion.duration.slow` on `motion.easing.standard` for the marks · `motion.duration.fast` for the tooltip and the dimming                            |

Every chart colour clears 3:1 on `elevation.surface` in both modes. Text never wears a chart colour: values, labels and legends stay in the text tokens, and a coloured mark beside them carries identity. The one place text sits on a chart colour is a status Heatmap cell, which is the Badge's fill and text, already in the contrast test.

## Accessibility

- **The Frame is a figure named by its title.** A screen reader hears "Coverage by control family, figure", then the description, then the path as a Breadcrumb, then the legend as a list of toggle buttons, then the plot.
- **The table is one toggle away, for everyone.** Every chart in a Frame given `data` and `x` lays the same numbers out as a Table when the Table toggle is pressed; the toggle is a button like any other, and the plot's markup is not the only copy of the data. The tooltip enhances; it never gates.
- **The plot is a group named by the title**, or by its own `label` outside a Frame. It is focusable, the arrow keys move the tooltip across the categories, and Enter chooses the one under it, opening its card when the plot has one. The focus ring shows on the keyboard, not on a click. A plot with no name is decoration: hidden from a screen reader and not focusable, so a sparkline beside a number says nothing twice.
- **The card is a dialog** named "[the plot's name], details"; focus moves into it and back to the plot when it closes; Escape closes it.
- **Loading says so.** A loading plot is `aria-busy` and named "[the plot's name], loading"; a refreshing one is `aria-busy` over the last plot.
- **A summary is the chart in a sentence.** With `summary`, the figure is described by it, so a screen reader hears the trend without walking the table.
- **Textures are the second channel.** With `texture`, a series is its colour and its pattern, in the plot and in the legend, so a stack reads in greyscale print and in a forced-colours mode where fills are flattened. The categorical order is still validated for colour vision; textures are the belt to that brace.
- **The tools are buttons.** Download is a menu of two items, Expand opens a Dialog that returns focus when it closes, and both are disabled while the plot is loading, empty or failed.
- **Colour is never the only channel.** Two or more series have a legend; a status series has its word in the legend, the tooltip and the table; a Heatmap's status cells print their value; a target is ink, not a hue; a gap in a line is a gap.
- **The categorical order is validated** for deutan and protan vision (Machado 2009, severity 1.0) and for normal vision, both modes. A Scatter's groups stop at three for the same reason.
- **Motion respects the reader.** Under reduced motion the marks draw in place and nothing fades.
- **The axe gate runs every kind's matrix** in both modes.

## Props

The Frame, `Chart`, accepts native figure attributes, events, styles and refs. `title` remains the visible chart title. Native DOM ids, refs and handlers belong to the original figure; expanding creates a separately named figure without duplicating those attributes or moving the caller's ref. Internal PNG export still reads the same figure.

_Props: generated from `Chart.Frame`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._

_Props: generated from `Chart.Legend`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._
