<!-- page: Patterns/Chart/Area (src/stories/patterns/ChartArea.mdx) -->

# Area

A [Line](?path=/docs/patterns-chart-line--docs) with a wash under it: the hue at 12%, so the plot says "how much" where a line alone says "which way". Stacked, the washes are parts of a whole over time, and the top edge is the total. Everything a Line takes, an Area takes; the difference is the fill and `stacked`. It lives in a [Chart](?path=/docs/patterns-chart-overview--docs) Frame.

_Example: story `Stories.AreaMatrix`._

## Anatomy

| Part     | What it is                                                                                                                                                       |
| -------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Line     | 2px in the series' tone, round joins, as on a Line.                                                                                                              |
| Wash     | The series' tone at 12% from the line to the baseline; in a stack, from the line to the series below. With `texture`, the series' pattern in its colour instead. |
| Marker   | 8px ringed, on hover, or on every point with `dots`.                                                                                                             |
| The rest | End labels, bands, references, gaps and axes as on a Line.                                                                                                       |

## Variants

| Variant                                                                                                      | Use                                                                                                      |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| One series                                                                                                   | A count whose size matters: open findings, month by month. The wash gives it weight.                     |
| `stacked`                                                                                                    | Parts of a whole over time: open and closed as parts of the month's total. The tooltip totals the stack. |
| `texture`                                                                                                    | Each wash its pattern: four assessors stacked read apart in print.                                       |
| `curve="smooth"`, `labels="end"`, `baseline="auto"`, `domain`, `scale="time"`, `delta`, `bands`, `reference` | As on a Line.                                                                                            |

_Example: story `Stories.Single`._
_Example: story `Stories.Stacked`._
_Example: story `Stories.Textured`._

## Sizes

`size` is the plot's height: `small` 120px, `medium` 200px (the default), `large` 320px, or `height` in pixels.

## States

| State    | What changes                                                                                                                                                                            |
| -------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Hover    | A hairline across the plot at the category, a marker on every line there, the tooltip.                                                                                                  |
| Isolated | A series hidden from the Frame's legend leaves the plot; a stack closes up.                                                                                                             |
| Chosen   | With `onSelect` or `details`: a click in a category's column, or Enter on the focused plot, chooses it; the card opens on the point. On an unstacked area every series is ringed there. |
| Loading  | A skeleton line with a `color.skeleton.subtle` wash, pulsing, at the plot's height.                                                                                                     |
| Entering | The areas draw in over `motion.duration.slow`.                                                                                                                                          |

_Example: story `Stories.Details`._

## Modifiers

- **`stacked`** for parts of a whole; **`texture`** for the patterns.
- **`curve`**, **`dots`**, **`labels`**, **`baseline`**, **`bands`**, **`reference`**, **`connectNulls`**, **`xLabel`**, **`yLabel`**, **`format`**, **`formatX`**, **`onSelect`**, **`details`**, **`loading`**, **`label`** as on a Line.

## Content

- **Stack only parts of one whole.** Series that are not parts (three assessors' counts) are lines.
- **Two series that cross are lines**, not two washes: where washes overlap they mix into a colour on nobody's legend.
- **One series or a stack**; never several unstacked areas.
- The rest as on a Line: label the end, declare a cropped axis, keep a gap.

## Style

| Element  | Token                                                                             |
| -------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Line     | `color.chart.<tone>` · 2px · round joins                                          |
| Wash     | `color.chart.<tone>` at 12% · or its pattern: the colour at 30% under 1.5px marks |
| Marker   | 8px · 2px `elevation.surface` ring                                                |
| Skeleton | `color.skeleton` path over a `color.skeleton.subtle` wash                         |
| The rest | As on a Line                                                                      |

## Accessibility

- **As a Line**: named by the Frame or `label`, focusable, arrow keys and Enter, the table one toggle away, a legend for two or more series, `aria-busy` while loading.
- **A stack's total is a column in the table**, since the top edge is the only place the plot shows it.
- **The wash is decoration**: the line carries the value, so a wash at 12% that fails 3:1 against the surface costs nothing.

## Props

_Props: generated from `Chart.Area`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._

_Example: story `Stories.Playground`._

- [Bar](?path=/docs/patterns-chart-bar--docs) stacked: parts of a whole per category, when the categories are not ordered.

<!-- page: Patterns/Chart/Bar (src/stories/patterns/ChartBar.mdx) -->

# Bar

Bars per category: the size of each thing, compared. Several series sit side by side or stack into parts of a whole; a bar runs down the side when its name is long; a value that is a `[from, to]` pair floats, which is how a phase window is drawn. Simple, grouped, stacked, horizontal and bullet bar charts are all this one part; a histogram is a bar chart of bins the data layer makes. It lives in a [Chart](?path=/docs/patterns-chart-overview--docs) Frame, which names it, keys it and lays it out as a table.

_Example: story `Stories.BarMatrix`._

## Anatomy

| Part         | What it is                                                                                                                                                           |
| ------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Bar          | 24px thick at most, the data end rounded 2px and the baseline end square; `barCategoryGap` a quarter of the slot. Grouped bars sit 2px apart.                        |
| Segment      | In a stack, a part of the bar in its series' tone, with a 2px `elevation.surface` gap from the next, so the parts count.                                             |
| Floating bar | A `[from, to]` value: the bar starts at `from`. For windows in time.                                                                                                 |
| Negative bar | A value below zero hangs from the zero line, which is drawn in `color.border.bold`; its rounded end and its label are at the data end, below.                        |
| Texture      | With `texture`, each series' fill is its pattern in its colour; the first series stays solid.                                                                        |
| End label    | The value at the bar's end in `font.body.xsmall` and `color.text.subtle`, outside the bar. `labels="end"`, for a few bars and no stack.                              |
| Target       | A 2px mark in `color.text` across the bar at the datum's `target` value: actual reads against planned.                                                               |
| Line         | A series drawn as a 2px line over the bars on the same axis: a cumulative, a rate, a plan.                                                                           |
| Axes         | The category axis with a hairline; the value axis from zero, no line, ticks in `color.text.subtlest`. Titles in `color.text.subtle` when the keys do not say enough. |
| Tooltip      | The category, every series at it keyed by a square, and the total when stacked. A hovered bar lightens to 80%.                                                       |

## Variants

| Variant             | Use                                                                                                                        |
| ------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| One series          | Findings by source. `brand` when the reader is asked to look, `neutral` when it is context. No legend; the title names it. |
| Grouped             | Two or three series side by side, in the categorical set. Past three the groups blur: stack, or emphasise one as a Line.   |
| `stacked`           | Parts of each whole, in the status tones or the categorical set. The tooltip totals them.                                  |
| `horizontal`        | Long names, or many categories: the names read whole down the side.                                                        |
| `target`            | A mark across each bar at its target: a bullet chart, without the qualitative bands.                                       |
| `[from, to]` values | Floating bars: phase windows, with `horizontal` and a `reference` for today.                                               |
| `line`              | One series as a line over the bars, on the same axis: closed against the plan.                                             |
| Below zero          | Variance, change, balance: the bars hang from the zero line. The axis reaches below zero on its own.                       |
| `domain`            | The value axis pinned, so charts side by side share a scale: small multiples.                                              |
| `texture`           | Patterns as well as colours, for print and colour-vision loss.                                                             |

_Example: story `Stories.Single`._
_Example: story `Stories.Grouped`._
_Example: story `Stories.Stacked`._
_Example: story `Stories.Horizontal`._
_Example: story `Stories.Targets`._
_Example: story `Stories.Windows`._
_Example: story `Stories.Combo`._
_Example: story `Stories.Negatives`._
_Example: story `Stories.Rates`._
_Example: story `Stories.Textured`._

## Sizes

`size` is the plot's height: `small` 120px, `medium` 200px (the default), `large` 320px, or `height` in pixels. A bar never grows past 24px however wide the plot; the slots grow instead, so a wide chart of four bars still reads as four bars and not four slabs. A horizontal chart gives its category axis the width its longest name needs, to 160px, and cuts the rest with the whole name in a title.

## States

| State    | What changes                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Hover    | The tooltip for the category; a `color.background.neutral.subtle.hovered` band behind the slot; the bar under the pointer in its tone's `hovered` step (a textured bar at 85%). Synced charts hover together. |
| Isolated | A series hidden from the Frame's legend leaves the plot; the others keep their places.                                                                                                                        |
| Chosen   | With `onSelect` or `details`: the bars take the pointer, a click on one chooses it and the other categories dim; Enter on the focused plot chooses the category under the tooltip. The card opens on the bar. |
| Loading  | Eight skeleton columns on a hairline, pulsing, at the plot's height; five skeleton bars when `horizontal`.                                                                                                    |
| Entering | The bars grow from the baseline over `motion.duration.slow`; a change of data moves them.                                                                                                                     |

_Example: story `Stories.Details`._

## Modifiers

- **`stacked`**, **`horizontal`**, **`labels="end"`**, **`target`**, **`line`** as in Variants.
- **`xLabel`**, **`yLabel`** print axis titles: the unit on the value axis when the title does not say it.
- **`domain`** pins the value axis, `[0, "auto"]` when unsaid; a value below zero extends it on its own. **`texture`** and **`syncId`** as on the Frame. A series' own **`format`** wins over the plot's in the tooltip, the card and the table: a fraction printed as a percentage.
- **`reference`** draws dashed lines: a target across every bar, a milestone on the category axis, labelled at the end. A `y` reference on a horizontal chart is a vertical line, labelled above the plot.
- **`format`**, **`formatX`** for the numbers and the categories, inherited from the Frame.
- **`onSelect`** and **`details`** as in States; the selection is `{ datum, series?, index }`, and `series` is absent when Enter chose the whole category.
- **`loading`** draws the skeleton; the Frame sets it from `status="loading"`.
- **`label`** names the plot outside a Frame.

## Content

- **Categories are short**: a code, a name, a month. A long name goes down the side with `horizontal`.
- **Print a value only at the end** of a few unstacked bars. A stack's parts are the tooltip's and the table's.
- **A target is a fact about the datum**, in its own key, not a series: the mark is ink.
- **The value axis starts at zero.** A bar's length is its meaning; there is no `baseline="auto"` here on purpose. Below zero is allowed, and the zero line is drawn, because a negative bar's length still means something.

## Style

| Element   | Token                                                                                                      |
| --------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Bar       | `color.chart.<tone>` · 24px at most · `radius` 2px at the data end · hover in `color.chart.<tone>.hovered` |
| Zero line | `color.border.bold` · 1px                                                                                  |
| Texture   | The colour at 30% under 1.5px marks · 8px repeat                                                           |
| Stack gap | 2px `elevation.surface`                                                                                    |
| Group gap | 2px                                                                                                        |
| End label | `font.body.xsmall` · `color.text.subtle` · tabular · 4px off the end                                       |
| Target    | `color.text` · 2px · 24px across                                                                           |
| Line      | `color.chart.<tone>` · 2px · round joins · a ringed 8px marker on hover                                    |
| Cursor    | `color.background.neutral.subtle.hovered` behind the slot                                                  |
| Dimmed    | `opacity.disabled`, over `motion.duration.fast`                                                            |
| Skeleton  | `color.skeleton` columns on a `color.border` hairline                                                      |

## Accessibility

- **Named by the Frame**, or by `label`: the plot is a group, focusable, and the arrow keys move the tooltip across the categories. Enter chooses the category when the plot has `onSelect` or `details`; the card that opens is a dialog, and focus returns to the plot after.
- **The table is the other copy** of the same numbers, one toggle away in the Frame; a stack's parts and its total are columns there.
- **A status series says its status** in the legend, the tooltip and the table; the tone reinforces.
- **The target is a mark in ink**, not a colour, so it reads under every vision.
- **Loading is `aria-busy`** and named "[the plot's name], loading".
- **`texture` gives a stack a second channel**, so its parts read in print and where fills are flattened.

## Props

_Props: generated from `Chart.Bar`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._

_Example: story `Stories.Playground`._

- [Line](?path=/docs/patterns-chart-line--docs): the same categories over time, when the change matters more than the size.
- [Progress](?path=/docs/components-progress--docs): one stacked bar of a register's parts, without axes.
- [Treemap](?path=/docs/patterns-chart-treemap--docs): parts of a whole with a hierarchy.

<!-- page: Patterns/Chart/Donut (src/stories/patterns/ChartDonut.mdx) -->

# Donut

A ring of slices on a `color.chart.track`, with a number in the middle: one number against its whole, the parts around it. Half a ring is a gauge, a score against a scale with the number at its base. It sits inline, sized in pixels, beside a Stat or in a tile; in a [Chart](?path=/docs/patterns-chart-overview--docs) Frame it inherits the name and the legend's interaction. There is no pie: the number in the middle is what a pie could not say, and a ring of two slices for one number is a Stat.

_Example: story `Stories.DonutMatrix`._

## Anatomy

| Part    | What it is                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Track   | The full ring in `color.chart.track`, under the slices, so a single slice reads against its whole.                                                                                                |
| Slice   | An arc in its tone, clockwise from the top, with a 2px `elevation.surface` gap from the next. A hovered slice grows 2px and takes its tone's `hovered` step; with `texture` it wears its pattern. |
| Label   | The number in the middle, `font.heading.xsmall` in `color.text`: the total, the share, the one that matters.                                                                                      |
| Caption | One word under the number in `font.body.xsmall` and `color.text.subtle`: what it counts.                                                                                                          |
| Tooltip | The slice's name and value, keyed by a square.                                                                                                                                                    |
| Card    | On a chosen slice: the slice, its value and its share of the whole, then the caller's facts.                                                                                                      |

## Variants

| Variant       | Use                                                                                                                |
| ------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Ring          | Parts of a whole with the whole in the middle: coverage, with the satisfied share printed.                         |
| One slice     | One value against its whole: 62% assessed, the rest the track. The slice's tone is the value's status, or `brand`. |
| `arc="half"`  | A gauge: a score from 0 to 100, the number at the base, the slice in the tone the score earns.                     |
| Beside a Stat | The ring at 120 with its legend as a `Chart.Legend`, the Stat carrying the words.                                  |

_Example: story `Stories.BesideStat`._
_Example: story `Stories.Gauge`._

## Sizes

| `size` | `thickness` | Where                                                   |
| ------ | ----------- | ------------------------------------------------------- |
| 64     | 8           | A cell, a list row, a card's corner: done against left. |
| 120    | 12          | Beside a Stat. The default.                             |
| 160    | 16          | A tile of its own, with a number and a caption inside.  |
| 200    | 20          | A gauge that is a section's point.                      |

A gauge is half as tall as it is wide, plus 4px for the base. The label fits inside a ring of 120 or more; at 64 the number sits beside it.

## States

| State    | What changes                                                                                                                             |
| -------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Hover    | The slice grows 2px outward; the tooltip.                                                                                                |
| Isolated | A slice hidden from the Frame's legend leaves the ring; the others keep their angles and the track shows through.                        |
| Chosen   | With `onSelect` or `details`: the slices take the pointer, a click chooses one and the others dim; the card opens at the slice's middle. |
| Loading  | A skeleton ring at the size and thickness, pulsing.                                                                                      |
| Entering | The slices sweep round from the top over `motion.duration.slow`.                                                                         |

_Example: story `Stories.Details`._

## Modifiers

- **`arc="half"`** for the gauge; **`size`** and **`thickness`** in pixels; **`texture`** for the patterns.
- **`label`** and **`caption`** for the middle.
- **`format`** for the tooltip and the card.
- **`onSelect`** and **`details`** as in States; the selection is `{ slice, share, index }`.
- **`loading`** draws the skeleton; the Frame sets it from `status="loading"`.
- **`name`** names the ring outside a Frame.

## Content

- **Four slices at most, five with Other.** Past that the angles stop reading; the data is a Bar.
- **The number in the middle is the point**: the share, the total, the score. The slices explain it.
- **A caption is one word**: "satisfied", "open", "posture".
- **Slices in status tones when they are statuses**, the categorical set when they are kinds, and the remainder always `neutral`.
- **A gauge's slice wears the tone its score earns**: `success` past the target, `warning` near it, `danger` below.

## Style

| Element  | Token                                                                                           |
| -------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Track    | `color.chart.track`                                                                             |
| Slice    | `color.chart.<tone>` · 2px `elevation.surface` gap · hover +2px in `color.chart.<tone>.hovered` |
| Label    | `font.heading.xsmall` · `color.text`                                                            |
| Caption  | `font.body.xsmall` · `color.text.subtle`                                                        |
| Dimmed   | `opacity.disabled`, over `motion.duration.fast`                                                 |
| Skeleton | `color.skeleton` ring                                                                           |

## Accessibility

- **Named by `name` or the Frame**, the ring is a group and focusable; unnamed it is decoration beside its Stat, hidden from a screen reader so the number reads once.
- **The number is text**, in the middle, not drawn: a screen reader reads it, and it never wears a chart colour.
- **The legend carries the names**; a slice's tone reinforces its word. Beside a Stat, the legend is a `Chart.Legend`.
- **A chosen slice's card is a dialog**, and focus returns to the ring when it closes. The slices themselves are not buttons, so a filter the ring drives is also a control on the page.
- **Loading is `aria-busy`** and named "[the ring's name], loading".

## Props

_Props: generated from `Chart.Donut`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._

_Example: story `Stories.Playground`._

_Rendered in the Storybook: Controls._

- [Stat](?path=/docs/components-stat--docs): the number a two-slice ring wants to be.
- [Progress](?path=/docs/components-progress--docs): one value against a whole as a bar, and a stacked bar of a register's parts.
- [Bar](?path=/docs/patterns-chart-bar--docs): five or more parts compared.

<!-- page: Patterns/Chart/Heatmap (src/stories/patterns/ChartHeatmap.mdx) -->

# Heatmap

A grid of rows by columns with a value painted in each cell: how much, across two dimensions. One hue from light to dark for a magnitude; two hues around grey for above and below; or the status tones by place, which is the risk matrix. It is a table, in the markup as on the page, so a screen reader reads it as one and the keyboard walks it. `Chart.Scale` is its key. It lives in a [Chart](?path=/docs/patterns-chart-overview--docs) Frame.

_Example: story `Stories.HeatmapMatrix`._

## Anatomy

| Part    | What it is                                                                                                                                                                        |
| ------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Cell    | `radius.xsmall`, 2px from its neighbours, its fill the value's step on the scale; `color.background.neutral.subtle` when there is no value.                                       |
| Value   | Printed in the cell on a status scale (the tone's text on its fill); on a colour scale a screen-reader-only text, or with `showValues` the number on an `elevation.surface` chip. |
| Headers | Column names across the top, row names down the side, in `font.body.xsmall` and `font.body.small`; the corner names the rows.                                                     |
| Scale   | `Chart.Scale`: the five steps in a row with the ends named, and the midpoint's word on a diverging one. Under the grid, `space.150` away.                                         |
| Tooltip | The cell's title: row, column, value.                                                                                                                                             |
| Card    | On a chosen cell: the row and column, the value, then the caller's facts.                                                                                                         |

## Variants

| Variant              | Use                                                                                                                                                                        |
| -------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `scale="sequential"` | How much: findings by family and month, in `color.chart.sequential.1` to `5`. The default.                                                                                 |
| `scale="diverging"`  | Above and below a `midpoint`: schedule variance in days, red below and blue above around grey.                                                                             |
| A tone function      | Status by place: the risk matrix, each cell the tone its position earns, the count printed.                                                                                |
| `showValues`         | The value printed on a colour scale too, when the reader must read every cell: on a surface chip in `color.text`, since text never sits on a chart colour. Off by default. |

_Example: story `Stories.Sequential`._
_Example: story `Stories.Diverging`._
_Example: story `Stories.Status`._

## Sizes

| `size`   | Cell height | Where                                                         |
| -------- | ----------- | ------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `small`  | 24px        | Many rows: families by month in a rail.                       |
| `medium` | 32px        | A Section. The default.                                       |
| `large`  | 40px        | A five-by-five matrix that is a page's point, values printed. |

A cell is at least 40px wide; the grid scrolls sideways inside its own box past the width it has.

## States

| State    | What changes                                                                                                                                         |
| -------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Hover    | The cell's title as a tooltip.                                                                                                                       |
| Chosen   | With `onSelect` or `details` the cells are buttons: a click or Enter chooses one, it takes the focus ring, the others dim, and the card opens on it. |
| Loading  | Every cell in `color.skeleton`, pulsing, at the grid's size.                                                                                         |
| Isolated | Not applicable: a heatmap has no series to hide.                                                                                                     |

_Example: story `Stories.Details`._

## Modifiers

- **`scale`**, **`domain`**, **`midpoint`**, **`showValues`** as in Variants.
- **`rowLabel`**, **`columnLabel`** name the dimensions: the corner cell, and what a screen reader hears.
- **`format`** for the values, the tooltip and the card.
- **`onSelect`** and **`details`** as in States; the selection is `{ row, column, value }`.
- **`loading`** draws the skeleton. The Frame does not set it: a grid's shape is its own.
- **`label`** is required: the grid is a table and needs a name.

## Content

- **A magnitude is one hue.** Never a status tone for a count: nine findings is not "danger".
- **Diverging needs a true midpoint**: zero variance, the plan, last year. Without one the data is sequential.
- **Status by place prints its count**: the tone's text on the tone's fill is the Badge's, already in the contrast test.
- **Name the dimensions**: "Likelihood" by "Impact", "Family" by "Month".
- **The scale's ends are words**: "0" and "12 findings"; "−12 days", "On plan", "+12 days".

## Style

| Element  | Token                                                                                                                                                  |
| -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Cell     | `color.chart.sequential.<step>` · `color.chart.diverging.<step>` · or `color.background.<tone>` with `color.text.<tone>` · `radius.xsmall` · 2px apart |
| Empty    | `color.background.neutral.subtle`                                                                                                                      |
| Headers  | `font.body.xsmall` medium `color.text.subtlest` across · `font.body.small` `color.text.subtle` down                                                    |
| Scale    | Five steps 24 by 8 · `radius.xsmall` · ends in `font.body.xsmall` `color.text.subtlest`                                                                |
| Chosen   | `color.border.focused` outline                                                                                                                         |
| Dimmed   | `opacity.disabled`                                                                                                                                     |
| Skeleton | `color.skeleton`                                                                                                                                       |

## Accessibility

- **It is a table**: a `table` named by `label`, column headers across and row headers down, the corner naming the rows and, for a screen reader, the columns ("Likelihood by Impact"). A screen reader reads each cell as "row, column, value".
- **Every cell has its value in text**: printed on a status scale, screen-reader-only on a colour scale, so the colour is never the only channel.
- **Cells that choose are buttons**, focusable in reading order, with the kit's focus ring; a chosen one says `aria-pressed`. The card is a dialog and focus returns to the cell when it closes.
- **The scale is `aria-hidden`**: its ends are text, and the values are in the cells.
- **Loading is `aria-busy`** and named "[the grid's name], loading".

## Props

_Props: generated from `Chart.Heatmap`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._

### Chart.Scale

_Props: generated from `Chart.Scale`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._

- [Table](?path=/docs/components-table--docs): what a heatmap is, with the values shown and the colour gone.
- [Badge](?path=/docs/components-badge--docs): the tone table a status cell reads.

<!-- page: Patterns/Chart/Line (src/stories/patterns/ChartLine.mdx) -->

# Line

A line per series over an ordered axis: a trend, a burndown, one measure against its plan. Two pixels wide with round joins, a ringed marker on hover, the last value printed after the line when asked. Straight segments by default, because the points are what was counted; a smooth curve never overshoots them. It lives in a [Chart](?path=/docs/patterns-chart-overview--docs) Frame, which names it, keys it and lays it out as a table.

_Example: story `Stories.LineMatrix`._

## Anatomy

| Part      | What it is                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| --------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Line      | 2px in the series' tone, round caps and joins. `curve="smooth"` is a monotone curve through the same points.                                                                                                                                       |
| Marker    | 8px across, ringed 2px in the surface so it reads over the line. On hover always; on every point with `dots`.                                                                                                                                      |
| End label | The series' last value after its line, `font.body.xsmall` in `color.text.subtle`; labels that would collide are pushed apart by a line's height.                                                                                                   |
| Gap       | A missing value breaks the line. `connectNulls` joins across it, for a gap that is not data.                                                                                                                                                       |
| Band      | A 10% wash between two values (the tolerable range, labelled at its top edge) or between two categories or dates (an assessment window, labelled above its middle).                                                                                |
| Reference | A dashed hairline at a value (a target, a limit) or at a category (a milestone), labelled at the end or above the plot.                                                                                                                            |
| Axes      | The category axis with a hairline, or a time axis whose ticks are hours, days, months or years by the span; the value axis from zero, cropped to the data with `baseline="auto"`, or pinned with `domain`. A value below zero draws the zero line. |
| Tooltip   | The category, every series at it keyed by a stroke, and with `delta` each change from the point before. The cursor is a `color.border.bold` hairline across the plot.                                                                              |
| Chosen    | The chosen category ringed on every line, in each series' tone.                                                                                                                                                                                    |

## Variants

| Variant              | Use                                                                                                                     |
| -------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Plain                | Two or three series, each a tone. Findings open and closed.                                                             |
| `curve="smooth"`     | A few points that are readings of one continuous thing. Never for counts that jump.                                     |
| `dots`               | A marker on every point, when each point is an event and there are few of them.                                         |
| `labels="end"`       | The last value after each line: the number the reader takes away. The default for a trend in a Frame.                   |
| `baseline="auto"`    | The value axis cropped to the data: a cumulative in the hundreds where the slope is the story. The description says so. |
| `bands`, `reference` | A burndown: the tolerable range as a band, the limit in `danger`, a milestone on the category axis.                     |
| Emphasis             | One series in `brand`, the rest in `neutral`: the honest answer to "make this clearer".                                 |
| `scale="time"`       | `x` holds dates: the points are spaced by time, the ticks pick their unit, and a band or a reference takes a date.      |
| `domain`             | The value axis pinned, so charts side by side share a scale: small multiples, with `syncId` for one hover.              |
| `delta`              | Each series' change from the point before, in the tooltip and the card.                                                 |

_Example: story `Stories.Lines`._
_Example: story `Stories.Smooth`._
_Example: story `Stories.Burndown`._
_Example: story `Stories.Cropped`._
_Example: story `Stories.Gaps`._
_Example: story `Stories.Dates`._
_Example: story `Stories.Deltas`._

## Sizes

`size` is the plot's height: `small` 120px, `medium` 200px (the default), `large` 320px, or `height` in pixels. Category ticks thin themselves to what fits, keeping the first; a time axis draws at most eight ticks, each at a unit's start; the right margin grows by 44px for end labels.

## States

| State    | What changes                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| -------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Hover    | A hairline across the plot at the category, a marker on every line there, the tooltip.                                                                                                                                                   |
| Isolated | A series hidden from the Frame's legend leaves the plot; the axis keeps its domain.                                                                                                                                                      |
| Chosen   | With `onSelect` or `details`: a click anywhere in a category's column, or Enter on the focused plot, chooses it. Every series is ringed there and the card opens on the point. The selection carries no series: a point is the category. |
| Loading  | A skeleton line on a hairline, pulsing, at the plot's height.                                                                                                                                                                            |
| Entering | The lines draw in over `motion.duration.slow`; a change of data moves them.                                                                                                                                                              |

_Example: story `Stories.Details`._

## Modifiers

- **`curve`**, **`dots`**, **`labels`**, **`baseline`**, **`bands`**, **`reference`**, **`connectNulls`** as in Variants and Anatomy.
- **`scale="time"`**, **`domain`**, **`delta`** as in Variants; **`syncId`** and **`texture`** as on the Frame (a line's stroke stays solid); a series' own **`format`**.
- **`xLabel`**, **`yLabel`** print axis titles.
- **`format`**, **`formatX`** for the numbers and the categories, inherited from the Frame.
- **`onSelect`** and **`details`** as in States; the selection is `{ datum, index }`.
- **`loading`** draws the skeleton; the Frame sets it from `status="loading"`.
- **`label`** names the plot outside a Frame.

## Content

- **The category axis is ordered**: months, weeks, versions. Unordered categories are a Bar. Real dates go on a time axis, so a gap in the sampling is a gap in the plot.
- **Label the end**, never every point. The tooltip carries the rest.
- **A cropped axis is declared** in the description: "the axis starts at the first month's count".
- **A gap is a gap.** Say why in the description; do not join across it unless the gap is a sampling artefact.
- **A limit is `danger`**, a target is `neutral`, a milestone is `neutral` on the category axis, each labelled with its name.

## Style

| Element   | Token                                                                           |
| --------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Line      | `color.chart.<tone>` · 2px · round caps and joins                               |
| Marker    | 8px · 2px `elevation.surface` ring                                              |
| End label | `font.body.xsmall` · `color.text.subtle` · tabular · 8px after the line         |
| Band      | `color.chart.<tone>` at 10% · label `font.body.xsmall` in `color.text.subtlest` |
| Reference | `color.chart.<tone>` · 1px dashed 4 3                                           |
| Cursor    | `color.border.bold` · 1px across the plot                                       |
| Zero line | `color.border.bold` · 1px                                                       |
| Delta     | `font.body.small` · `color.text.subtlest` · tabular · signed                    |
| Chosen    | The series' tone: an 8px marker in a 16px halo at 20%                           |
| Dimmed    | `opacity.disabled`, over `motion.duration.fast`                                 |
| Skeleton  | `color.skeleton` · 2px path on a `color.border` hairline                        |

## Accessibility

- **Named by the Frame**, or by `label`: the plot is a group, focusable, the arrow keys move the tooltip across the categories, and Enter chooses one when the plot has `onSelect` or `details`. The card that opens is a dialog, and focus returns to the plot after.
- **The table is the other copy** of the same numbers, one toggle away in the Frame.
- **Two or more series have a legend**, and each end label is a number in the text colour, not the series colour.
- **A gap is visible under every vision**: it is an absence, not a colour.
- **Loading is `aria-busy`** and named "[the plot's name], loading".

## Props

_Props: generated from `Chart.Line`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._

### Playground

_Example: story `Stories.Playground`._

_Rendered in the Storybook: Controls._

- [Chart](?path=/docs/patterns-chart-overview--docs): the Frame, the tones, choosing a mark, the motion.
- [Area](?path=/docs/patterns-chart-area--docs): the same line with a wash, and stacked parts of a whole over time.
- [Sparkline](?path=/docs/patterns-chart-sparkline--docs): a line with no axes beside its number.
- [Bar](?path=/docs/patterns-chart-bar--docs): the same categories, when the size matters more than the change.

_Example: story `Stories.Dont`._

<!-- page: Patterns/Chart/Scatter (src/stories/patterns/ChartScatter.mdx) -->

# Scatter

A point per record on two value axes: where each thing sits on two measures at once. Risks by likelihood and impact; findings by age and severity. Points fall into groups of a tone, three at most; a bubble's area follows a third value; two references make quadrants. Each point is a record, so a click opens its card. It lives in a [Chart](?path=/docs/patterns-chart-overview--docs) Frame.

_Example: story `Stories.ScatterMatrix`._

## Anatomy

| Part      | What it is                                                                                                                                       |
| --------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Point     | 8px across in its group's tone, ringed 2px in the surface so overlapping points stay apart, with a hit area 24px across.                         |
| Bubble    | With `z`, a point whose area follows the value (twice the value, twice the ink), at 70% so what is under it shows.                               |
| Axes      | Both value axes, a hairline on the category side, ticks in `color.text.subtlest`, titles in `color.text.subtle` when the keys do not say enough. |
| Grid      | Hairlines both ways, since both axes are values.                                                                                                 |
| Reference | A dashed hairline at a value on either axis; one on each makes quadrants.                                                                        |
| Tooltip   | The point's name and group, then each axis as name and value. Per point, not per column.                                                         |
| Card      | On a chosen point: its name, group and axes, then the caller's facts and a way to the record.                                                    |

## Variants

| Variant   | Use                                                                                                                     |
| --------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| One tone  | Every point in `brand`: the shape of the cloud is the point.                                                            |
| `groups`  | Up to three groups by a key, each a tone: status groups in the status tones, kinds in the first three categorical hues. |
| `z`       | A bubble: exposure, cost, count.                                                                                        |
| Quadrants | A `reference` on each axis: the four corners the reader names ("treat", "accept").                                      |

_Example: story `Stories.Groups`._
_Example: story `Stories.Bubbles`._

## Sizes

`size` is the plot's height: `small` 120px, `medium` 200px, `large` 320px (the right one for a scatter that is a page's point), or `height` in pixels. Bubbles range from 64 to 900 square pixels whatever the plot's size.

## States

| State    | What changes                                                                                                                                          |
| -------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Hover    | The tooltip at the point. No cursor band, since there is no category.                                                                                 |
| Isolated | A group hidden from the Frame's legend leaves the plot.                                                                                               |
| Chosen   | With `onSelect` or `details`: the points take the pointer, a click chooses one, the others dim and the chosen one gains a halo; the card opens on it. |
| Loading  | Eight skeleton dots on two hairlines, pulsing, at the plot's height.                                                                                  |
| Entering | The points arrive over `motion.duration.slow`.                                                                                                        |

_Example: story `Stories.Details`._

## Modifiers

- **`z`** for a bubble; **`name`** for the key that names a point.
- **`groupBy`** and **`groups`** for the groups and their tones; **`tone`** for every point when there are none.
- **`reference`**, **`xLabel`**, **`yLabel`**, **`format`**, **`formatX`** as on the other parts.
- **`onSelect`** and **`details`** as in States; the selection is `{ datum, group, index }`.
- **`loading`** draws the skeleton; the Frame sets it from `status="loading"`.
- **`label`** names the plot outside a Frame.

## Content

- **Both axes are measures.** A category on one axis is a Bar or a strip; two categories are a Heatmap.
- **Three groups at most.** The first three hues validate against each other in every pairing; a fourth does not. Finer distinctions are the tooltip's or a filter's.
- **Name the points** with `name`, so the tooltip and the card say which record.
- **Title the axes** when the keys are not words the reader would say: "Likelihood", "Impact".
- **A quadrant's meaning is in the description**, not drawn: "the lines split the register into quadrants".

## Style

| Element   | Token                                                                     |
| --------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Point     | `color.chart.<tone>` · 8px · 2px `elevation.surface` ring · 24px hit area |
| Bubble    | The same at 70% · area from 64 to 900 square pixels                       |
| Grid      | `color.border` · 1px both ways                                            |
| Reference | `color.chart.neutral` · 1px dashed 4 3                                    |
| Chosen    | The point's tone: a halo 8px wider at 20%                                 |
| Dimmed    | `opacity.disabled`, over `motion.duration.fast`                           |
| Skeleton  | `color.skeleton` dots on `color.border` hairlines                         |

## Accessibility

- **Named by the Frame**, or by `label`: the plot is a group and focusable. The arrow keys do not walk points (there is no category axis to walk), so the table is the keyboard's way in: one row per point, a column per axis.
- **A chosen point's card is a dialog**, and focus returns to the plot when it closes.
- **Three groups keep every pair apart** under deutan and protan vision; the legend carries their names, and the tooltip and the card say the group in words.
- **A point's hit area is 24px** whatever its size, so a small point still takes a click.
- **Loading is `aria-busy`** and named "[the plot's name], loading".

## Props

_Props: generated from `Chart.Scatter`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._

### Playground

_Example: story `Stories.Playground`._

_Rendered in the Storybook: Controls._
