- [Heatmap](?path=/docs/patterns-chart-heatmap--docs): the same two dimensions when both are ordinal scales, with a count per cell: the risk matrix.
- [Bar](?path=/docs/patterns-chart-bar--docs): one measure per category.

## Don't

_Example: story `Stories.Dont`._

<!-- page: Patterns/Chart/Sparkline (src/stories/patterns/ChartSparkline.mdx) -->

# Sparkline

A trend with no axes, no grid and no legend, beside the number it belongs to: in a Stat tile, in a table's trend column, after a count. The number carries the value; the sparkline carries the shape. A line by default, a wash or bars when asked, with an end dot for the last point and a hairline for a reference. Ninety-six by twenty-four pixels. Unnamed it is decoration; named, it is a plot with a tooltip.

_Example: story `Stories.SparklineMatrix`._

## Anatomy

| Part      | What it is                                                                                                     |
| --------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Line      | 1.5px in its tone, round joins; `area` adds the tone at 12% under it; `bars` is a column per point, 1px apart. |
| End dot   | A 6px marker ringed in the surface on the last point: where the series is now.                                 |
| Reference | A dashed hairline at a value in `color.chart.neutral`: last period, the limit.                                 |
| Tooltip   | Only when named: the point's value and category.                                                               |

## Variants

| Variant             | Use                                                                                       |
| ------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `appearance="line"` | The default: a count over time.                                                           |
| `appearance="area"` | A count whose size matters, with a reference for the limit.                               |
| `appearance="bars"` | A count per period, where each period is discrete: closed per month.                      |
| In a tile           | Beside the value of a Stat.Tile, `space.150` from the number.                             |
| In a row            | The trend column of a Table, 80 by 20, unnamed, so a screen reader hears the number once. |

_Example: story `Stories.InTiles`._
_Example: story `Stories.InRows`._

## Sizes

| `width` × `height` | Where                                                      |
| ------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------- |
| 80 × 20            | A table row.                                               |
| 96 × 24            | Beside a Stat's value. The default.                        |
| 120 × 28           | Bars, which need the width.                                |
| 160 × 40           | A card's corner, when the trend is the card's second fact. |

Anything larger is a [Line](?path=/docs/patterns-chart-line--docs) in a Frame, with axes.

## States

| State    | What changes                                                       |
| -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Hover    | Nothing, unless named: then a marker and the tooltip at the point. |
| Loading  | A skeleton bar at the size, pulsing.                               |
| Entering | The line draws in over `motion.duration.slow`.                     |

A sparkline does not choose: nothing to click, nothing to open. The number beside it is the way to the record.

## Modifiers

- **`appearance`**, **`tone`**, **`endDot`**, **`reference`** as in Anatomy.
- **`x`** names the category key, for the tooltip of a named sparkline.
- **`width`**, **`height`** in pixels.
- **`format`** for the tooltip.
- **`label`** names it: "Open findings, nine months". Unsaid, it is decoration.
- **`loading`** draws the skeleton; the Frame sets it from `status="loading"`.

## Content

- **Always beside a number.** A sparkline alone says only "up" or "down".
- **One tone, the number's status** when it has one: `danger` beside open findings, `success` beside closed; `brand` or `neutral` otherwise. Never a categorical hue.
- **Six to twelve points.** Fewer is a number; more is a Line.
- **A reference is one value**: last period, the limit. Not a band, not a target series.

## Style

| Element   | Token                                                      |
| --------- | ---------------------------------------------------------- |
| Line      | `color.chart.<tone>` · 1.5px · round joins                 |
| Wash      | `color.chart.<tone>` at 12%                                |
| Bars      | `color.chart.<tone>` · `radius` 1px at the top · 1px apart |
| End dot   | 6px · 2px `elevation.surface` ring                         |
| Reference | `color.chart.neutral` · 1px dashed 3 2                     |
| Skeleton  | `color.skeleton` · `radius.xsmall`                         |

## Accessibility

- **Unnamed, it is `aria-hidden`** and not focusable: the number beside it is the fact, and a screen reader hears it once.
- **Named, it is a group**, focusable, with the arrow keys moving the tooltip across the points, and it should sit where no number says the same thing.
- **Never the only carrier of a value.** If the shape matters enough to say, say it in the tile's note: "Down from 14 in January".
- **The tone is not the meaning**: the number's word or Badge is.

## Props

_Props: generated from `Chart.Sparkline`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._

### Playground

_Example: story `Stories.Playground`._

_Rendered in the Storybook: Controls._

## Related

- [Chart](?path=/docs/patterns-chart-overview--docs): the Frame, the tones, the motion.
- [Stat](?path=/docs/components-stat--docs): the number it sits beside.
- [Line](?path=/docs/patterns-chart-line--docs): the same series with axes, when it needs to say more.
- [Table](?path=/docs/components-table--docs): the trend column.

## Don't

_Example: story `Stories.Dont`._

<!-- page: Patterns/Chart/Treemap (src/stories/patterns/ChartTreemap.mdx) -->

# Treemap

Part-to-whole with a hierarchy: a tile per leaf, sized by value, in the tone of its top-level branch. Findings by system and component; controls by family and enhancement. Where the total goes, and where inside that. A name shows on a tile when it fits; the rest is the tooltip's. A click on a tile drills into its branch, or opens its card. It lives in a [Chart](?path=/docs/patterns-chart-overview--docs) Frame, whose legend names the branches.

_Example: story `Stories.TreemapMatrix`._

## Anatomy

| Part    | What it is                                                                                                                                           |
| ------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Tile    | A leaf, `radius` 2px, in its branch's tone, with a 2px `elevation.surface` gap from its neighbours. Sized by value, 4:3 as far as the layout allows. |
| Name    | The tile's name on an `elevation.surface` chip at 92% in `color.text`, when the tile is at least 64 by 28; cut with the whole in a title.            |
| Tooltip | The tile's name and value, keyed by a square.                                                                                                        |
| Card    | On a chosen tile: its name, its branch and its value, then the caller's facts.                                                                       |

## Variants

| Variant    | Use                                                                                                                               |
| ---------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Branches   | Two levels: systems in the categorical set, their components inside each in the same hue.                                         |
| One branch | One system alone, its components in its one hue: the level under a drill-down.                                                    |
| Drill-down | A click on a tile redraws the treemap with its branch, the way back in the Frame's `path`; a click on a component opens its card. |

_Example: story `Stories.Systems`._
_Example: story `Stories.Drilldown`._

## Sizes

`size` is the plot's height: `small` 120px, `medium` 200px, `large` 320px (the right one: tiles need room for their names), or `height` in pixels. A treemap should be at least 420px wide; narrower, most names fall to the tooltip.

## States

| State    | What changes                                                                                                                 |
| -------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Hover    | The tooltip.                                                                                                                 |
| Isolated | A branch hidden from the Frame's legend leaves the treemap; the rest re-tile. A hovered legend item dims the other branches. |
| Chosen   | With `onSelect` or `details`: the tiles take the pointer, a click chooses one, the others dim; the card opens on the tile.   |
| Loading  | Four skeleton tiles, pulsing, at the plot's height.                                                                          |
| Entering | The tiles arrive over `motion.duration.slow`; a drill-down re-tiles the same way.                                            |

_Example: story `Stories.Details`._

## Modifiers

- **`data`** as nodes: a name, a value on a leaf, children on a branch, a `tone` on a top-level node when the categorical order is not wanted.
- **`format`** for the tooltip and the card.
- **`onSelect`** and **`details`** as in States; the selection is `{ name, value, group }`, `group` being the top-level branch.
- **`loading`** draws the skeleton; the Frame sets it from `status="loading"`.
- **`label`** names the plot outside a Frame.

## Content

- **A hierarchy, or nothing.** A flat list of five is a Bar; a treemap earns its place when the reader asks "where, and where inside that".
- **Six branches at most**, in the categorical set; more folds into Other.
- **Names are short**: a component, a family. What does not fit is the tooltip's, and the table's.
- **Values are one thing**: a count, a cost. Not a score.

## Style

| Element  | Token                                                                                  |
| -------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Tile     | `color.chart.<tone>` · `radius` 2px · 2px `elevation.surface` gap                      |
| Name     | `font.body.xsmall` · `color.text` on an `elevation.surface` chip at 92% · `radius` 2px |
| Dimmed   | `opacity.disabled`, over `motion.duration.fast`                                        |
| Skeleton | `color.skeleton` tiles                                                                 |

## Accessibility

- **Named by the Frame**, or by `label`: the plot is a group and focusable. The tiles are not walked by the keyboard; the Frame's legend and table are the way in, one row per leaf.
- **Text never sits on a tile's colour**: the name is on a surface chip, in the text colour.
- **Every tile has a title** with its whole name and value, whether or not the name fits.
- **A chosen tile's card is a dialog**, and focus returns to the plot when it closes.
- **Loading is `aria-busy`** and named "[the plot's name], loading".

## Props

_Props: generated from `Chart.Treemap`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._

### Playground

_Example: story `Stories.Playground`._

_Rendered in the Storybook: Controls._

## Related

- [Chart](?path=/docs/patterns-chart-overview--docs): the Frame, the tones, choosing a mark, the motion.
- [Bar](?path=/docs/patterns-chart-bar--docs): parts compared without a hierarchy.
- [Donut](?path=/docs/patterns-chart-donut--docs): parts of one whole with the whole in the middle.
- [Tree](?path=/docs/components-tree--docs): the same hierarchy as an outline, when the reader wants to walk it.

## Don't

_Example: story `Stories.Dont`._

<!-- page: Patterns/CommandPalette (src/stories/patterns/CommandPalette.mdx) -->

# CommandPalette

A ⌘K palette over a page or a record: a field at the top, the commands under headings, a shortcut at the end of the ones that have one, the keys in the footer. Choosing a command closes the palette and runs it. The commands are plain objects the caller supplies, so the palette stays presentational and every page can reuse it; `useCommandPalette` holds the open state and toggles it on ⌘K or Ctrl+K anywhere on the page. It runs a command; it does not find a record, which is the [RecordPicker](?path=/docs/patterns-recordpicker--docs), and it does not search the product, which is the top nav's search.

_Example: story `Stories.CommandPaletteStory`._

## Anatomy

| Part    | What it is                                                                    |
| ------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Field   | "Type a command…", focused on open.                                           |
| Heading | The group's name, over its commands: Record, Go to, Preferences.              |
| Command | A verb and its object; the shortcut or hint at the end in `font.body.xsmall`. |
| Empty   | "No commands match."                                                          |
| Footer  | The keys: the arrows to move, Enter to run, Escape to close.                  |

_Example: story `Stories.CommandPaletteMatrix`._

## Variants

CommandPalette has one appearance. What varies is the commands, which are the page's: a record's verbs first, the places to go after, the preferences last.

Not built, and why: search across records in the palette, because a record is found by the top nav's search and picked by the RecordPicker; nested pages of commands, because a command with choices is a Dialog of its own; recent commands at the top, because the order is the page's and it should read the same every time; icons before the commands, because the heading says the kind.

## Sizes

One: the Command dialog at its medium width, 560px, over the page at the top.

## States

| State    | What changes                                                    |
| -------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Closed   | Not rendered. ⌘K opens it.                                      |
| Open     | Over the page at the top, the field focused, every group shown. |
| Filtered | The commands that match, under their headings; empty groups go. |
| None     | The empty sentence.                                             |
| Run      | The palette closes, then the command runs.                      |

## Modifiers

- **`commands`**: id, group, label, hint, run. Commands with the same group in sequence share a heading.
- **`placeholder`** for the field.
- **`useCommandPalette`** returns `open` and `setOpen`, and binds ⌘K and Ctrl+K while mounted.

## Content

- **A command is a verb and its object**: "Record an assessment", "Export the SSP", "Switch the colour mode". Never a noun alone.
- **The headings are kinds of command**: "Record" for what the record does, "Go to" for places, "Preferences" for the reader's own.
- **The hint is the shortcut** when there is one, in the platform's glyphs; otherwise nothing.
- **The page's verbs first**, the places after, the preferences last.

## Style

| Element | Token                                                                                                        |
| ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Dialog  | CommandDialog: `radius.xxlarge` · `elevation.surface.overlay` · `elevation.shadow.overlay` · `color.blanket` |
| Heading | CommandGroup's: `font.body.xsmall` · `color.text.subtle`                                                     |
| Command | CommandItem: `dimension.control.medium` · `color.background.selected` when selected                          |
| Hint    | `font.body.xsmall` · `color.text.subtle` · at the end                                                        |
| Footer  | CommandFooter: `elevation.surface.sunken` · `font.body.xsmall` · Kbd for each key                            |

## Accessibility

- **A dialog named "Command palette"**; focus moves to the field on open and returns to where it was on close.
- **The list is a listbox** with the headings as group labels, so a screen reader hears "Record, group, Record an assessment, A".
- **The arrows move, Enter runs, Escape closes**, and the footer says so with Kbd, each key named in full.
- **⌘K and Ctrl+K both open it**, so the shortcut works on every platform; which glyph the page shows is the product's call, parked in docs/next.md.
- **Running closes first**, so a command that opens a dialog does not stack one over the other.

## Props

_Props: generated from `CommandPalette`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._

### useCommandPalette

The palette's open state, toggled by ⌘K or Ctrl+K anywhere on the page. Returns `{ open, setOpen }`.

## Related

- [Command](?path=/docs/components-command--docs): the dialog and the list.
- [RecordPicker](?path=/docs/patterns-recordpicker--docs): the same CommandDialog, picking one record instead of running a command.
- [Kbd](?path=/docs/components-kbd--docs): the keys in the footer and the hints.

## Don't

_Example: story `Stories.Dont`._

<!-- page: Patterns/Composer (src/stories/patterns/Composer.mdx) -->

# Composer

An experimental shared text composer for messages, comments and other short drafts. Ledger owns keyboard completion, submission progress and recovery. The consuming application owns recipients, permissions, persistence, suggestion identity and serialized text. Owner: Ledger maintainers; consumers own their adapters.

_Example: story `Stories.ComposerMatrix`._

## Anatomy

A named textarea, optional leading marker, contextual fields above, instructions below, optional `actions` before the buttons (a second thing to do with the draft), optional cancel action, and primary submission action. Suggestions attach beneath the field; rejection produces a visible alert.

## Variants

One composition, with optional suggestion and leading slots. No event taxonomy or built-in mention syntax. The example below uses a `#` adapter and stable topic identifiers to demonstrate a non-person use case.

_Example: story `Stories.Suggestions`._

## Sizes

Three initial textarea rows. The layout follows its container; the suggestion popup is bounded by the available width and scrolls when tall. Long option labels truncate visually while retaining their accessible text.

## States

Empty drafts cannot submit. Nonempty drafts submit with the button or Ctrl/⌘ + Enter. While pending, the textarea is read-only and repeat submission and cancellation are blocked. Fulfillment clears the submitted draft; rejection retains it with a retry message. A newer controlled draft is retained when an earlier request resolves. A disabled composer cannot be edited or submitted.

_Example: story `Stories.SaveRecovery`._

## Modifiers

`value` and `onValueChange` select caller-owned state; `defaultValue` supplies an uncontrolled initial draft. Do not switch ownership while mounted. `ref`, `id`, and `name` target the visible textarea. `leading`, `hint`, `children` and `actions` are rendered slots; `actions` sits before the cancel and primary buttons, for a secondary Button the caller wires to the draft it keeps through `value`.

`getSuggestions(text, caret)` returns UTF-16 replacement offsets and ordered options, or null. The caller provides unique option IDs, accessible labels, exact insertion strings, filtering and result limits. Invalid ranges are ignored. The adapter is synchronous; fetching remote candidates belongs to the caller. No rich-text document model is implied.

## Content

Supply a descriptive `label` independently of placeholder text. Translate `submitLabel`, `cancelLabel`, `suggestionsLabel`, `errorMessage` and `hint`. Use stable identities when your product serializes references; a display name need not be an identity. Resolve `onSubmit` only when your application's promised save boundary succeeds; throw or reject on failure.

## Style

Textarea and Button provide the control styling. Layout uses `space.100`; suggestions use the overlay surface, default border and overlay shadow. Pending and error states remain understandable without animation or color alone.

## Accessibility

The textarea keeps focus while suggestions are navigated. Up/Down selects an option, Enter/Tab inserts it, and Escape closes the list without dismissing a containing overlay. IME confirmation does not insert or submit. Suggestions expose listbox/option semantics and an active descendant. Pointer selection returns focus to the textarea. Instructions and errors describe the textarea; rejection is announced through an alert. The completion key handling and save recovery run in both color modes.

## Props

_Props: generated from `Composer`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._
_Example: story `Stories.Playground`._
_Rendered in the Storybook: Controls._

## Related

- [Textarea](?path=/docs/components-textarea--docs) for plain multiline input.
- [Timeline](?path=/docs/components-timeline--docs) for rendering events independently of the composer.
- Application Activity.Composer adapts this contract to its people list and `@[Full Name]` format; those workflows remain in the application.

## Don't

_Example: story `Stories.Dont`._

<!-- page: Patterns/Data table (src/stories/patterns/DataTable.mdx) -->

# Data table

The register with its state. [Table](?path=/docs/components-table--docs) is the markup and stays for a table with nothing to sort, filter, page or choose. `DataTable` is the same parts drawn from a TanStack Table 9 instance: the columns are declared by kind, the state has an owner, and every feature is one option on the hook and one part in the renderer. No route sorts, filters or pages by hand. Spec: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-03-data-table.md`.

_Example: story `Stories.RegisterStory`._

## Anatomy

| Part                                   | What it is                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| -------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `defineColumns<T>((c) => [...])`       | The columns of a record type, by kind. A kind decides alignment, minimum width, sort and filter, and the part that draws the value. Keep the call at module level.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `useDataTable({ columns, data, ... })` | The table instance. `getRowId` names rows; `selectable` draws the checkbox column; `pageSize` pages and draws Pagination, with the Rows per page choice from `pageSizes`; `label` names the table. Any TanStack state slice can be owned outside: pass `sorting` and `onSortingChange`, or `state.columnFilters` from the route's own filters. `initialState` seeds what the table keeps. `manual` hands sorting, filtering or pagination to the server.                          |
| `DataTable table={table}`              | The renderer: the `toolbar` slot above the header, the Table parts closed by a hairline under the last row, the states drawn under the header so it never moves, and [Pagination](?path=/docs/components-pagination--docs) below when the table pages. No frame: the register sits on the page and its rules are the only lines. With `fill` it is the page's one block: it takes the rest of the window, the rows scroll under the header and the pagination sits at the bottom. |
| The toolbar parts                      | `DataTable.Search`, `.Filter`, `.Presets`, `.Columns` and `.Settings`, each taking the `table`; `.SelectionBar` appears above the table while rows are chosen. `Presets` is a strip on its own line, or `variant="menu"` for one button in a toolbar that also holds search and filters.                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| The Table parts                        | It draws `Table.Header`, `.Row`, `.Cell`, `.Id`, `.List`, `.Selection`, `.Disclosure`, `.Group`, `.Detail` and `.Handle`; nothing of its own.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |

## Metrics

`DataTable.Metrics` wraps a toolbar, an optional summary region and the table. It starts closed. Put `DataTable.MetricsTrigger` in the toolbar actions and `DataTable.MetricsContent` directly below the toolbar. Compose the content with `Stat` or the app's existing summary cards.

Opening metrics only changes the disclosure. Search, filters, sorting and selection keep their state. The app supplies the values and decides whether they summarize all records or the filtered rows; make that scope clear in the content.

```tsx
<DataTable.Metrics>
  <Toolbar actions={<DataTable.MetricsTrigger />}>
    <DataTable.Search table={table} />
  </Toolbar>
  <DataTable.MetricsContent className="px-200 py-100">
    <Stat label="Total findings" value={findings.length} />
  </DataTable.MetricsContent>
  <DataTable table={table} />
</DataTable.Metrics>
```

The root accepts [Collapsible](?path=/docs/components-collapsible--docs) props, including `defaultOpen` or controlled `open` and `onOpenChange`. The trigger accepts native button props and a ref, `size` and `variant`; its default is a small secondary button with a chart icon and the localized “Metrics” label. Children replace the label. The content accepts Collapsible content props, including `forceMount`, native props and a ref. Its default region name is localized “Metrics”; `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` can name a custom summary.

_Example: story `Stories.MetricsStory`._

## Group by

`DataTable.GroupBy` replaces a row of grouping pills with one toolbar menu. It shows the selected field, checks that choice in the menu, and offers **None** to return to an ungrouped list. The active treatment matches Metrics. `options` supplies `{ value, label }` fields; `value` and `onValueChange` belong to the caller. The empty string means no grouping. Native button attributes and refs reach the trigger.

For `useDataTable`, bind the same value to `groupBy` and `state.grouping`. Set `initialState.expanded: true` when newly selected groups should start open. Pagination returns when grouping is cleared; search, filters, selection and column settings retain their existing owners.

```tsx
const [group, setGroup] = useState("");
const table = useDataTable({
  columns,
  data,
  groupBy: group || undefined,
  state: { grouping: group ? [group] : [] },
  initialState: { expanded: true },
});
// Inside the toolbar actions:
<DataTable.GroupBy options={groupOptions} value={group} onValueChange={setGroup} />;
```

The menu also works with custom collection renderers. The control board binds it to family, stage, owner and component grouping; the scoped Program controls table offers family, implementation, assessment, owner and applies-to fields. Task tables use the same menu alongside saved views, columns and settings.

`DataTable.Filters table={table} columns={["status", "owner"]}` collects multiple filters in one toolbar popover. It reuses each column's existing checkbox, text or range fields. The trigger shows the number of filtered columns; **Clear all filters** clears column filters while retaining search, grouping and selected records. `DataTable.Filter` remains available for a single exposed filter chip.

For filters owned outside the table, pass `additionalFilters={{ content, count, onClear }}`. The supplied fields appear first, contribute to the active count, and reset with **Clear all filters**. Controls uses this for its URL-backed Scope filter.

_Example: story `Stories.GroupByStory`._

## Variants

Which table first: a table sorts, filters, pages, chooses, pins, nests or scrolls inside itself, `DataTable`; otherwise `Table`. Then the modes, each one option on the hook:

| The register                       | Option                                         | Role       |
| ---------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------- | ---------- |
| Sorted, filtered, paged, chosen    | `pageSize`, `selectable`                       | `table`    |
| A hierarchy with columns           | `tree`                                         | `treegrid` |
| A hierarchy whose rows open too    | `tree` with `detail` and `detailColumn: false` | `treegrid` |
| A record that opens into more      | `detail`                                       | `table`    |
| Records under headings             | `groupBy`                                      | `table`    |
| Rows held above and below          | `pinRows`                                      | `table`    |
| Rows in the reader's order         | `reorderRows`                                  | `table`    |
| A thousand rows                    | `virtualize` with `maxHeight` or `fill`        | `table`    |
| The register that is the page      | `fill` on the renderer                         | `table`    |
| The server sorts, filters or pages | `manual` with `rowCount`                       | `table`    |
| Cells the reader edits in place    | `editable` on a column                         | `grid`     |

There is no per-column filter row under the header: filters are chips in the toolbar, built from the columns. There is no zebra, no radio selection, no expand-all; see Table. There is no third component for a tree: it is a mode of this one.

_Example: story `Stories.TreeStory`._

_Example: story `Stories.TreeWithDetailRows`._

_Example: story `Stories.DetailRows`._

_Example: story `Stories.GroupsStory`._

_Example: story `Stories.PinnedRowsStory`._

_Example: story `Stories.ReorderingRows`._

## Sizes

Rows are `dimension.row` 40px, and `dimension.row.compact` 36px through the reader's density setting, never a prop; the header `dimension.row.header` 32px. Virtualization uses that density as its initial estimate, then measures each mounted record together with any disclosed detail rows. Widths come from the kind (id 92, status 120, person 160, date 112, number 96, actions 40) as minimums; the author gives `width` for fixed columns and one column takes the slack. `resizable` or `reorderable` switches the layout to `fixed`, so a change to one column leaves the others alone; `layout` sets it by hand. `maxHeight` makes the frame scroll inside itself; `fill` takes the rest of the window instead, and wins when both are given.

_Example: story `Stories.PinnedColumns`._

_Example: story `Stories.ColumnGroups`._

## States

| State          | What the renderer draws                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| -------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Ready          | The rows. With none left after the filters, the empty state.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| Loading        | The header kept, a skeleton line per row where the records will be, no Pagination. The height of what is already there never changes.                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| Empty          | No records at all: nothing to search, sort or page, so the toolbar, the header and the hairline go, and the register is one [Empty](?path=/docs/components-empty--docs) on its dashed frame: the `records` picture (or `empty.illustration`), `empty.title`, its description, its `action`, which creates the first record, and `secondary`. |
| Filtered empty | A search or a column filter is active and no rows remain: the toolbar and the header stay, and under the header the table draws the `search` picture, **Nothing matches**, a line of copy and **Clear filters**, which clears the search and every column filter. No Pagination under it. `empty.filtered` overrides each part.              |
| Error          | `error` under the header.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| Sorted         | The header's arrow and `aria-sort`; one column at a time unless the table says `multiSort`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| Filtered       | The applied value on each chip; the presets' counts; the range in Pagination.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| Chosen         | The rows on `color.background.selected` and the SelectionBar above: the count, the verbs, Clear, and "Select all 340" as a second, explicit step.                                                                                                                                                                                            |

The row states (hover, selected, active id, static, scrolled edge, expanded) are Table's.

_Example: story `Stories.StatesStory`._

## Modifiers

The hook's options, each one feature:

- **`selectable`**: the checkbox column; a function says which rows can be chosen. **`pageSize`** pages, and **`pageSizes`** are the sizes the reader can choose from in the Pagination (`10, 20, 50, 100` unsaid); the choice persists with `view`. **`label`** names the table. **`manual`** with `rowCount` hands sorting, filtering or pagination to a server.
- **`pinnable`, `hideable`, `resizable`, `reorderable`, `columnMenu`, `layout`, `view`**: the columns the reader owns. The column menu on a header's hover sorts, pins and hides; `DataTable.Columns` in the toolbar shows and hides, and the gear beside it, `DataTable.Settings`, holds the rows' density and Reset view. The checkbox, the disclosure, the handle and the detail chevron are always the first columns and always pinned; the row's actions are always the last and always pinned to the end, so the kebab sits at the table's trailing edge however far the columns scroll; a pinned column keeps its hairline while the frame is scrolled; a band's heading sticks to the frame's leading edge. The preview eye sits at the end of the row's first value cell, taking no room: it appears on the row's hover and on focus, and stays on the row whose preview is open. A column's `pin` is the author's default and `hideable: false` keeps it on screen. `view: "risks"` names the table, and the reader's order, widths, visibility and pins persist in this browser under `ledger.table.risks.view`; the URL keeps sort, filters and page.
- **`tree`**: `children` reads a row's parts, `label` names the row for the chevron, `hint` is the muted text after a folded row's first value, `initialExpanded` says which open first; a filter or a search keeps a matching row's ancestors, so a child never shows without its parent. The chevron is a leading column of its own, always first and always pinned, so the disclosure never moves when the reader reorders, hides or pins a column. It is one narrow width at every depth, so opening and closing a row never shifts the columns; the nesting reads as an indent on the row's first value. Set `guides: true` to move the existing disclosure into the first value cell alongside vertical ancestor guides. Each guide starts below its parent and spans only its descendant rows; there are no horizontal branches. The chevron, icon and label then indent together at each depth; the separate leading disclosure column is omitted. Guides are decorative, and the disclosure retains its expand/collapse label and keyboard behavior. **`detail`** opens a row into what it returns, a child table included; its open rows are its own state, so a tree's row opens its parts and its detail apart and neither closes the other (`initialState.expanded` still says which details start open). It draws a leading chevron column of its own, which **`detailColumn: false`** leaves out: in a treegrid two chevron columns read as twins, so the row is opened from a cell instead, a `list` column with `opens: "detail"`. **`groupBy`** puts the rows under a band per value; pagination is off while it is on. **`pinRows`** lets `row.pin("top")` and `"bottom"` hold rows under the header or above the footer. **`reorderRows`** puts a handle on every row and tells you which row moved next to which; sorting is off while it is on.
- **`virtualize`**: only the rows in view are drawn; give the renderer a `maxHeight` or `fill` and leave `pageSize` off.
- **A number column's `footer`** totals the rows the filters leave: sum, mean, min, max, count, or your own.
- **`editable`** on a text or status column: `onChange` commits the value at once, `save` settles it (the cell shows saving, saved or the error and rolls back on failure), `validate` blocks a bad value, and a status column's `options` are its menu.

The renderer's: **`toolbar`**, **`state`**, **`empty`**, **`error`**, **`onRowClick`**, **`maxHeight`**, **`fill`**, **`responsive`**, **`className`**. `toRows(table)` and `toCsv(table)` export the rows the filters leave, in the sort chosen, every page, with the columns the reader shows; a custom column exports what its `text` says. The kit has no router, so the app binds sort, page, search and filters to the URL itself (`useTableSearch` in `src/lib/table-state.ts`).

**`fill`** is for the register that is the page: a collection route, a record's register tab, anywhere the table is the one block of content and only a page header, a section heading or a note sits above it. The register takes the rest of the window below its own top edge, the header sticks to the frame, the rows scroll inside it, and the pagination sits at the bottom of the page's inset whether the page has three rows or three thousand; below a header, six rows and the pagination the page scrolls again. Do not fill a table in a dialog, a sheet, a panel, a rail or a card, or one stacked above other content: give those `maxHeight` or let them scroll with the page. The document keeps scrolling for every other page.

_Example: story `Stories.FillStory`._

_Example: story `Stories.ThousandRows`._

_Example: story `Stories.ServerStory`._

_Example: story `Stories.EditingStory`._

## Content

The kinds carry the rules, so a DataTable cannot get them wrong:

| Kind                                           | Aligns  | Sorts by                      | Filters by | Draws                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| ---------------------------------------------- | ------- | ----------------------------- | ---------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `c.id(key, { glance, preview, active, tone })` | start   | alphanumeric                  | text       | `Table.Id`: the eye opens the preview, hover on the id shows the `glance` (the hover ladder's first rung)                                                                                                                            |
| `c.text(key, { wrap })`                        | start   | alphanumeric                  | text       | the value, truncated; `wrap` lets the row grow                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `c.number(key, { format })`                    | end     | numeric                       | range      | integer, decimal, percent or a formatter, tabular numerals                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `c.date(key, { format })`                      | start   | date                          | range      | an ISO date as `d MMM yyyy`; anything else as given                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `c.status(key, { tone })`                      | start   | alphanumeric                  | equals     | `Badge` in the tone the row decides                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `c.person(key)`                                | start   | text                          | equals     | `Person`                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `c.list(id, { items, empty, note, opens })`    | start   | the labels                    | contains   | `Table.List`: the first item by name, the rest as a count, every item in a hover card; the click is the row's preview, or its `detail`, which the line then carries a chevron for and whose card is suppressed while the row is open |
| `c.actions((row) => RowAction[])`              | end     | never                         | never      | the kebab on row hover and focus; always the last column and pinned to the trailing edge                                                                                                                                             |
| `c.custom(id, { cell, sort, align })`          | as said | `sort`'s value, or not at all | never      | whatever `cell` returns: a bar, an icon, a composed cell                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `c.group(header, columns)`                     |         |                               |            | a second header row over the columns                                                                                                                                                                                                 |

Every kind takes `priority` (smaller numbers stay visible longer in responsive mode), `header`, `width` (pixels; also the minimum), `minWidth`, `sortable: false` and `cell(row)` to draw the value its own way while keeping the kind's behaviour. An absent value is `Absent`. Headers are one or two words in sentence case; a number's header ends with its numbers; the id first, the name second, actions last; a status is a Badge and a person a Person. Cells truncate, and the full text is the cell's title; a column that must wrap says `wrap: true` and is never the one sorted by eye.

_Example: story `Stories.ListCells`._

## Style

| Element         | Token                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| --------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Frame           | none: no border, no radius; the header's hairline and the one under the last row bound the register · `fill`: the rest of the window from the register's top edge, never under a header, six rows and the pagination |
| Toolbar slot    | above the header, flush with the table's edge, `space.200` under, no rule                                                                                                                                            |
| Header, rows    | As Table: `dimension.row.header`, `dimension.row`, the hairline, the hovered and selected surfaces                                                                                                                   |
| Leading columns | the checkbox, the handle and the detail chevron 32px, the disclosure 28px, each centred; the tree's indent is `space.200` per level on the row's first value                                                         |
| Preview eye     | over the end of the first value cell, `opacity` 0 until the row is hovered or focused, on the row's own surface                                                                                                      |
| Pinned column   | `elevation.surface.current` · `color.border.bold` at the edge while the frame is scrolled                                                                                                                            |
| Skeleton rows   | one `Skeleton` line per row, the row's height                                                                                                                                                                        |
| Empty           | no records: the Empty alone, on its dashed frame · filtered: under the header, `space.200` around, no frame                                                                                                          |
| Error           | under the header, `space.150` around                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| Selection bar   | `color.border.brand` · `color.background.selected` · `color.text.brand` · `radius.medium` · `space.150` × `space.075`                                                                                                |
| Footer          | `color.border` above · a static row                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| Pagination      | under the closing hairline, `space.100` above, flush with the table's edge · the range, then Rows per page as a small Select, then the pager at the end                                                              |
| Resize guide    | `color.background.brand.bold`, 2px, on hover and while dragging                                                                                                                                                      |

## Accessibility

- **The role follows the mode.** A DataTable is a `table`: Tab moves through the interactive elements in reading order and that is enough. A `tree` is a `treegrid`: the arrow keys move, open and close, Home and End jump. An editable table is a `grid` with a roving tabindex: Enter commits and moves down the column, Tab keeps its meaning and moves across. The plain table stays a table; the treegrid and grid roles are the ARIA patterns for what those modes add.
- **Named.** `label` names the table and, through it, its pagination ("Findings pagination"). The header checkbox is "Select all rows on this page"; each row's is "Select" and the id. The eye is "Preview row"; the tree's chevron names its row; the detail row's chevron carries `aria-controls`; the handle is "Reorder row"; the resize handle is a vertical `separator` named "Resize column"; the Rows per page select is named so.
- **Sorting** reports `aria-sort`; the chevron shows on hover and on focus. **Filtering** reads on the chips (pressed or expanded, the value in the text) and in the presets' counts. **Selection** is the checkbox, never the row's click; the SelectionBar is a region named "Selection" and Escape clears it.
- **Loading never removes the header** or changes the height of what is already there, so nothing jumps under a screen reader's cursor. Error and the filtered empty sit under the header. With no records at all there is no table: the region is the Empty and its action, so a screen reader meets the message first and the way forward second, not eight empty column headers.
- **A thousand rows may be chosen one at a time**: a row is memoized on what it shows, so one checkbox redraws one row.
- **Known gap.** Resizing is pointer-only; a keyboard user's widths come from `Reset view`. Reordering columns and rows takes the keyboard (Space, the arrow keys).

## Props

`DataTable` is generic over the row type, so its table is written here rather than generated.

| Prop         | Type                                                                     | Does                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| ------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `table`      | `DataTableInstance<T>`                                                   | From `useDataTable`. Required.                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| `toolbar`    | `ReactNode`                                                              | Sits above the header, flush with the table's edge.                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `state`      | `"ready"`, `"loading"`, `"empty"`, `"error"`                             | Drawn under the header. Default `ready`; `ready` with no rows is empty.                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `empty`      | `{ title, description?, action?, secondary?, illustration?, filtered? }` | What the empty state says. `illustration` is `records`, `search`, `done` or `false`. `filtered` is the narrowed state's `{ title?, description?, action?, illustration? }`; its defaults are localized and its default action clears the filters. |
| `error`      | `ReactNode`                                                              | What the error state shows.                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `onRowClick` | `(row: T) => void`                                                       | Opens the record. Never selects.                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `maxHeight`  | `number`                                                                 | Pixels; the frame scrolls inside itself past it.                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `fill`       | `boolean`                                                                | The register is the page's one block: it fills the window, the frame scrolls inside, the pagination stays at the bottom. Wins over `maxHeight`.                                                                                                   |
| `className`  | `string`                                                                 |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |

The hook's options are the Modifiers above; `DataTableOptions<T>` is exported with each one described.

_Example: story `Stories.DataTableMatrix`._

- [Toolbar](?path=/docs/patterns-toolbar--docs), [FilterChip](?path=/docs/components-filterchip--docs), [Pagination](?path=/docs/components-pagination--docs): what surrounds it.
- [Editable](?path=/docs/patterns-editable--docs): the cell an editable column draws. [Empty](?path=/docs/components-empty--docs), [Skeleton](?path=/docs/components-skeleton--docs): its states.

## Don't

_Example: story `Stories.Dont`._

## Responsive containers

Set `<DataTable responsive table={table} />` when the table must fit its container. Set `priority: 0` and a readable minimum width on the primary identity; the renderer retains it and row actions, then fits other columns by priority. Lower-priority fields appear in each row's localized More fields disclosure with their labels and original cell renderers. A reader-hidden column stays hidden. Resizing does not change the table's column-visibility state, view persistence, selection, sort, filters or export. The observer follows the container, including a neighbouring panel, rather than a viewport breakpoint.

Responsive mode uses fixed column geometry and keeps virtualization active. Expanded fields contribute their measured height to the same virtual record; scrolling away and back preserves its disclosure state. Column or container changes invalidate cached heights, including records outside the rendered window. Paging remains an independent choice. `c.id` honours an explicit `minWidth` when no width is supplied.

Use responsive mode for record lists whose drafts belong to a form outside the cells. A field that moves between its cell and the More fields disclosure remounts its renderer, so a local inline editor's uncommitted draft is not retained through that move. Generic editable or wide comparison tables keep the default horizontal scrolling until their draft state is owned outside those renderers.

_Example: story `Stories.ResponsiveContainers`._

_Example: story `Stories.ResponsiveGroupedHeaders`._

_Example: story `Stories.ResponsiveVirtualRows`._

<!-- page: Patterns/Editable (src/stories/patterns/Editable.mdx) -->

# Editable

A value edited where it sits. The reader clicks it, changes it, and it saves: no form, no Save button, no dialog. It commits at once and shows the save beside the value; a refused save puts the old value back with the reason under it. **Editable.Text** edits text, with `multiline` for full paragraphs; **Editable.Select** is one of a fixed set, drawn as the record draws it.

It is for one value on a record that already exists: the owner in the rail, the next action in a table's cell, the status as a Badge. A record that does not exist yet is a [form](?path=/docs/patterns-forms--docs); several values that change together are a form in a Dialog; a paragraph uses `Editable.Text multiline` to edit in a Textarea in the same cell.

_Example: story `Stories.Rail`._

## Anatomy

| Part    | What it is                                                                                                                                                                      |
| ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Row     | A button the full width of its cell, 24px tall. The value sits flush on the text column; under the pointer the row tints, the tint reaching `space.050` past the value.         |
| Value   | The committed value in `font.body`, one line that truncates. Empty, the `placeholder` in `color.text.subtlest`, or the muted dash.                                              |
| Mark    | At the end of the row: a Spinner while saving, a check in `color.icon.success` for a moment after, a warning in `color.icon.danger` after a refusal. A chevron on a Select.     |
| Field   | Text, editing: an input of `dimension.control.xsmall` in the value's place, its box reaching `space.050` past the column so the text stays on it.                               |
| Menu    | Select, editing: the options under the row, the current one marked, and nothing else; a short set uses Select; a long set uses Combobox with its search input inside the popup. |
| Message | Under the row in `font.body.xsmall` and `color.text.danger`: what `validate` refused, or why the save failed.                                                                   |

## Variants

Two, by what the value is. **Text** for a value the reader writes: a name, an acronym, a next action, a date typed as text. **Select** for one of a fixed set: a status, a method, an owner from a roster, drawn by `render` as the record draws it, a Badge or a Person, so the rail and the table agree.

Where it lives: in a [KeyValue](?path=/docs/components-keyvalue--docs) row of the rail, in a [Fact](?path=/docs/components-fact--docs), in a [Table](?path=/docs/components-table--docs) cell under the column's heading. A [DataTable](?path=/docs/patterns-datatable--docs) column with `editable` draws these itself.

_Example: story `Stories.InTable`._

Use `multiline` for criteria and other paragraphs: the entire value wraps at rest, and the textarea grows with its content. Enter adds a newline, Ctrl/Cmd+Enter or leaving the cell saves, and Escape cancels and returns focus. Validation and save recovery are the same as single-line text.

_Example: story `Stories.Multiline`._

## Sizes

One: 24px, `dimension.control.xsmall`, so the row is a line of body text with `space.025` above and below, the height of the KeyValue row and the table cell it sits in. The width is the cell's.

Each instance accepts one save at a time. While saving, the resting control cannot reopen for another edit. A rejected save restores its previous value only while this request still owns the current value; an external update is preserved. Completion after unmount is ignored. The caller remains responsible for reconciling server updates to the record.

## States

| State   | Look                                                                                                                                         |
| ------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Rest    | The value, flush. Nothing says it edits until the pointer arrives; the rail's rows all edit, so nothing needs to.                            |
| Hover   | The row tints `color.background.neutral.subtle.hovered`; pressed, `.pressed`.                                                                |
| Focus   | The kit's focus outline on the row.                                                                                                          |
| Editing | Text: the field in the value's place, focused, the existing value ready to edit. Select: the listbox or searchable popup open under the row. |
| Invalid | Editing, the field's border `color.border.danger` and the message under it, as the reader types. The commit is refused while it shows.       |
| Saving  | The new value shows at once and a Spinner sits at the end of the row.                                                                        |
| Saved   | A check for `motion.duration.slower` twice, then nothing.                                                                                    |
| Failed  | The old value is back, the warning mark at the end, the reason under the row. It stays until the next edit.                                  |
| Empty   | The placeholder in `color.text.subtlest`, or the muted dash. Never a grey instruction.                                                       |

There is no disabled state. A value the reader cannot change is plain text in the same row, which lines up with the editable ones.

_Example: story `Stories.EditableMatrix`._

## Modifiers

- **`validate`**: a function of the draft that returns a message or null. It runs as the reader types and again at the commit, so a rule is seen before Enter is refused.
- **`save`**: a promise. Resolved, the check; rejected, the rollback and the error's message. `onChange` is called at once with the new value, and again with the old one when the save fails, so the caller's state is always what the reader sees.
- **`placeholder`** on Text: what goes here, as a noun.
- **`options`** and **`render`** on Select: the set, and how a value is drawn.
- **`label`**: the field's name for a screen reader. The KeyValue or the column shows the visible one.

_Example: story `Stories.Validation`._

_Example: story `Stories.Failing`._

## Content

- **The label is the field's name as the rail shows it:** "Owner", "Next action". The same word as the KeyValue's label or the column's heading.
- **A placeholder says what goes here, as a noun:** "Unassigned", "Add next action". Not "Click to edit", not "Enter a value".
- **A validation message says the rule, in one sentence:** "Two to twelve letters, digits or hyphens." Not "Invalid".
- **A save failure says why, from the server's message when it has one,** and "Could not save" when it does not.
- **A Select's options are the record's words,** drawn as the record draws them.

## Style

| Element | Token                                                                                                                                       |
| ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Row     | `dimension.control.xsmall` 24px · `space.025` block · `space.075` gap · `radius.small` · tint reaching `space.050` past the column          |
| Value   | `font.body` · `color.text` · `color.text.subtlest` for the placeholder                                                                      |
| Tint    | `color.background.neutral.subtle.hovered`, `.pressed` · `motion.duration.fast` on `motion.easing.standard`                                  |
| Field   | `dimension.control.xsmall` · `color.background.input` · `color.border.input`, `color.border.focused` focused, `color.border.danger` invalid |
| Mark    | `dimension.icon.small` 14px · `color.icon.success` · `color.icon.danger` · the Spinner                                                      |
| Message | `font.body.xsmall` · `color.text.danger`                                                                                                    |
| Focus   | The kit's focus outline, `color.border.focused`                                                                                             |

## Accessibility

- **The row is named by the label and the value:** "Owner: Dana Whitfield". The label is read before the value, so a screen reader hears what the field is where a sighted reader reads the KeyValue's label beside it.
- **The field is named by the label** (`aria-label`) and, invalid, is `aria-invalid` and described by the message.
- **Keyboard:** Tab reaches the row; Enter or Space opens the field with the existing value; Enter commits and Escape puts the old value back, and either returns focus to the row. Leaving the field by Tab or a click commits and focus goes where the reader sent it. Select and searchable Combobox triggers expose the native combobox role. Enter, Space or Down opens the options; arrows move between them and Enter chooses. Escape closes without changing the value. While saving, the trigger stays focusable and read-only, with `aria-disabled` announcing that another edit must wait.
- **A landed save is announced:** "Saved", or "Not saved", from a status region under the row; the Spinner says "Saving".
- **The stories** exercise validation, keyboard selection, search, save rejection, rollback, pending guards and focus restoration in both themes.

## Props

Editable keeps its value, validation and save contract while composing the shared Input, Select and Combobox. No application API migration is required. The searchable popup follows [shadcn](https://ui.shadcn.com/docs/components/base/combobox#popup) and [Base UI](https://base-ui.com/react/components/combobox#input-inside-popup).

### Editable.Text

| Prop          | Type                                  | What it is                                                                       |
| ------------- | ------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `label`       | `string`, required                    | The field's name for a screen reader: "Owner".                                   |
| `value`       | `string`, required                    | The committed value, shown at rest.                                              |
| `onChange`    | `(next: string) => void`, required    | Called at once with the new value, and with the old one again if the save fails. |
| `save`        | `(next: string) => Promise`, required | Saves it. Rejected, the value rolls back and the error's message shows.          |
| `validate`    | `(next: string) => string \| null`    | A message blocks the commit; null lets it through.                               |
| `placeholder` | `string`                              | What goes here, as a noun, shown while empty.                                    |

### Editable.Select

| Prop         | Type                               | What it is                                                                                                |
| ------------ | ---------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `label`      | `string`, required                 | The field's name, for the screen reader; the options have no heading.                                     |
| `value`      | `T`, required                      | The current option.                                                                                       |
| `options`    | `readonly T[]`, required           | The set, in the order it shows.                                                                           |
| `onChange`   | `(next: T) => void`, required      | As Text.                                                                                                  |
| `save`       | `(next: T) => Promise`, required   | As Text.                                                                                                  |
| `validate`   | `(next: string) => string \| null` | As Text: a status the record is not ready for, with the reason.                                           |
| `render`     | `(value: T) => ReactNode`          | Draws a value: a Badge, a Person. Unsaid, the value as text. The same rendering appears in short and searchable lists; option names and search use the original string. |
| `searchable` | `boolean`                          | A search field over the rendered options. On by itself past eight options.                         |
