<!-- page: Patterns/Forms (src/stories/patterns/Forms.mdx) -->

# Forms

**Forms is a pattern**, composed from Field, input controls, layout primitives and buttons. There is no standalone Form component. TanStack Form owns form state and validation; Ledger owns the presentation.

How the form controls go together: which control answers which question, how a form is laid out, how required fields and errors work, and where the buttons go. Each control has its own page; this one is the choice between them and the rules they share.

_Example: story `Stories.Fields`._

## Variants

| The answer                                               | The control                                                                                                       |
| -------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| One line of free text: a name, an email, a number        | [Input](?path=/docs/components-input--docs), with `type` for the value's kind.                                    |
| Several lines: a note, a description, a narrative        | [Textarea](?path=/docs/components-textarea--docs), with `rows` for the expected length.                           |
| A search box, a number with a unit                       | [InputGroup](?path=/docs/components-inputgroup--docs) around the Input.                                           |
| One answer from visible choices                          | [RadioGroup](?path=/docs/components-radiogroup--docs).                                                            |
| One of four to a dozen plain words                       | [Select](?path=/docs/components-select--docs).                                                                    |
| One of a short list whose options carry a Dot or a Badge | [Select](?path=/docs/components-select--docs).                                                                    |
| One of many, or names the reader would type              | [Combobox](?path=/docs/components-combobox--docs).                                                                |
| Several things that can each be true                     | [Checkbox](?path=/docs/components-checkbox--docs)es in a FieldSet with FieldLegend.                               |
| An on/off setting                                        | [Switch](?path=/docs/components-switch--docs), with an external label or Field.                                   |
| A day to schedule                                        | [DatePicker](?path=/docs/components-datepicker--docs). A remembered date is an Input with the format in the hint. |
| A record: a person, a control, a requirement             | Combobox, or a [RecordPicker](?path=/docs/patterns-recordpicker--docs) when the choice needs more than a row.     |

_Example: story `Stories.Pickers`._

## Anatomy

Compose each [Field](?path=/docs/components-field--docs) from a FieldLabel, control and FieldDescription or FieldError. Native IDs and ARIA connect them. A group of choice controls uses FieldSet and FieldLegend. The Fields stack `space.200` apart, or sit in a Grid when the answers are short. The buttons come last.

| Part    | What it is                                                                                                                   |
| ------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Field   | Label, control, message. The label is a noun in sentence case; the hint a sentence; the error what fixes it.                 |
| Group   | FieldSet and FieldLegend: a legend over Checkboxes or a RadioGroup, with the hint and the error for the group.               |
| Section | Group related fields under a clear heading, with `space.300` between sections.                                               |
| Buttons | An Inline at the end of the form, aligned to the end: Cancel as a subtle Button, then the primary. The primary says the act. |

_Example: story `Stories.Choices`._

## Sizes

- **Labels above by default.** Horizontal and responsive fields support compact choices and settings rows.
- **Each field as wide as its answer.** In a six-column Grid, an acronym takes two columns, a name four, an owner three, a description the row. A field wider than its answer lies about the answer.
- **One column on a narrow screen.** The Grid collapses; the order stays.
- **`space.200`** (16px) between fields, **`space.300`** (24px) between sections, **`space.100`** (8px) between the choices of a group.
- **The first field takes focus** in a dialog or a sheet that exists to fill the form (`autoFocus`). On a page, nothing does.

_Example: story `Stories.Layout`._

## Modifiers

- **Required is marked, optional is not.** Add an aria-hidden asterisk to FieldLabel and `aria-required` to the control; the form checks on submit.
- **When most of a form is required, mark nothing**, and say "Optional." in the hint of the few that are. The rule is per product, not per form: the products' record forms mark required.
- **Choose one validation presentation.** Use `noValidate` when the application supplies its own error summary and inline messages. Native `required` remains available for native form validation; `aria-required` communicates the requirement on the control.

## States

- **TanStack Form owns state.** Create the form with `useForm`, bind each control through a `form.Field` render prop, and submit a native `<form>` with `form.handleSubmit()`.
- **Validate with Zod.** The main example uses `onDynamic` with `revalidateLogic({ mode: "blur", modeAfterSubmission: "change" })`: validate on blur initially, then on change after submission, with errors shown for touched invalid fields. One validation slot avoids stale messages from another mode. The example below uses only `onSubmit`, so validation runs when Save is pressed. Submit-only validation does not promise immediate feedback as the user repairs a value.
- **Keep Save available for incomplete values.** Disable it while submitting, using `form.Subscribe`; show success only after persistence completes. The examples save locally for demonstration.
- **Expose errors accessibly.** Render issue messages with FieldError. Set `data-invalid` on Field, `aria-invalid` on the control, and connect the message ID with `aria-describedby`. The main example focuses the first invalid control after submission.
- **Reset deliberately.** Use `form.reset()` for an explicit Reset action. Preserve the draft after a server failure.

_Example: story `Stories.RequiredOnSubmit`._

## Content

- **Cancel, then the primary**, at the end of the row, aligned to the end. The primary's label is the act: Create program, Save statement, Assign. Never OK or Submit.
- **A form that saves as it goes has no buttons**: an [Editable](?path=/docs/patterns-editable--docs) value on a record, a Switch in a settings list.
- **A destructive act is not a form's primary**; it is a danger Button with an [AlertDialog](?path=/docs/components-alertdialog--docs).

## Style

| Form                                   | Where                                                                                                           |
| -------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| A focused create or edit task          | Dialog, with first-field focus and a DialogFooter outside the scrolling body.                                   |
| A multi-step setup                     | A page wizard when the workflow needs several stages.                                                           |
| One contextual filter or reason        | Popover at its trigger.                                                                                         |
| One value on a record                  | Editable, read in place and edited on activation.                                                               |
| A selection or parent-owned draft task | A specifically documented Sheet or RecordBrowser workflow; not a second default for ordinary create/edit forms. |

Use Cancel as a subtle button before the operation's primary. Preserve dirty drafts and pending saves when closing or navigating. In Program Assurance, the product contract names the closed exception list; field count alone never switches a create/edit task between Dialog and Sheet.

## Related

- [Field](?path=/docs/components-field--docs): the label, hint and error around one control or one group.
- [Input](?path=/docs/components-input--docs), [Textarea](?path=/docs/components-textarea--docs), [InputGroup](?path=/docs/components-inputgroup--docs): the fields.
- [Checkbox](?path=/docs/components-checkbox--docs), [Switch](?path=/docs/components-switch--docs), [RadioGroup](?path=/docs/components-radiogroup--docs): the choice controls.
- [Select](?path=/docs/components-select--docs), [Combobox](?path=/docs/components-combobox--docs), [DatePicker](?path=/docs/components-datepicker--docs), [Calendar](?path=/docs/components-calendar--docs): the pickers.
- [Button](?path=/docs/components-button--docs): the primary and its Cancel.

## Accessibility

Use a visible label for every control. Connect FieldLabel using `htmlFor` and the control’s `id`; connect descriptions and errors using `aria-describedby`. Custom controls forward native IDs, ARIA and refs to their actual input. Groups use a fieldset and legend. On failed submit, focus the first invalid field and present all errors together when a form spans several sections. Keep submitted values after a server failure.

## Form libraries

Forms is a composition pattern, with no component props of its own. Import `useForm` from `@tanstack/react-form` and `z` from `zod` (Zod 3.25+ or 4 supports Standard Schema). Applications declare these dependencies themselves; Ledger's controls do not depend on a form library.

### TanStack and shadcn anatomy

This follows the [shadcn TanStack Form guide](https://ui.shadcn.com/docs/forms/tanstack-form) and [TanStack validation documentation](https://tanstack.com/form/latest/docs/framework/react/guides/validation). Field uses the same flat label, description and error parts. FieldGroup, Stack or Grid supplies layout. The caller puts `data-invalid` on Field and `aria-invalid` on the actual control.

```tsx
const form = useForm({
  defaultValues: { title: "" },
  validators: {
    onSubmit: z.object({ title: z.string().trim().min(1, "Enter a title.") }),
  },
  onSubmit: async ({ value }) => {
    await saveRecord(value);
  },
});

<form
  onSubmit={(event) => {
    event.preventDefault();
    void form.handleSubmit();
  }}
>
  <Stack space="space.200">
    <form.Field name="title">
      {(field) => {
        const isInvalid = field.state.meta.isTouched && !field.state.meta.isValid;
        return (
          <Field data-invalid={isInvalid}>
            <FieldLabel htmlFor="title">
              Title
              <span aria-hidden className="text-danger">
                {" "}
                *
              </span>
            </FieldLabel>
            <Input
              id="title"
              aria-describedby={isInvalid ? "title-error" : undefined}
              name={field.name}
              value={field.state.value}
              required
              onBlur={field.handleBlur}
              onChange={(event) => field.handleChange(event.target.value)}
              aria-invalid={isInvalid}
            />
            {isInvalid && <FieldError id="title-error" errors={field.state.meta.errors} />}
          </Field>
        );
      }}
    </form.Field>
    <Button type="submit">Save</Button>
  </Stack>
</form>;
```

The live examples use `noValidate` to demonstrate schema errors. For production, retain native constraints such as `required`, `type` and `maxLength`; omit `noValidate` when native browser feedback is appropriate. Use `aria-required` and a visible label marker when only an accessible requirement is intended.

Bind Input, and Textarea with `value`, `onBlur={field.handleBlur}` and `onChange` passing `event.target.value`. Select and RadioGroup use `value` and `onValueChange={field.handleChange}`; Checkbox and Switch use boolean `checked` and `onCheckedChange`; a checkbox’s mixed presentation uses the separate boolean `indeterminate` prop. Combobox uses Root `value`/`onValueChange` and forwards blur through ComboboxInput; DatePicker uses `value`/`onChange`. Forward blur to the focusable control. For checkbox arrays, use `form.Field` with `mode="array"` and TanStack's `pushValue`/`removeValue` helpers.

### Validation and recovery

The recovery example combines native inputs, a custom input, Select and Combobox. TanStack owns editable values and metadata; native form submission also includes a control associated from outside the form. Its Zod schema requires an owner only for Assigned status; changing that status clears the obsolete error. A local async validator simulates a server rejection for `taken@example.test`, preserving the draft for correction and resubmission. Error-summary buttons and explicit refs focus the actual controls. Reset clears the draft and validation state.

_Example: story `Stories.ValidationRecovery`._

### Migrating from useRequired

`useRequired` is removed. Use TanStack's `useForm` and `form.Field`, schema validators, and `revalidateLogic({ mode: "submit", modeAfterSubmission: "change" })` for required checks that update as the user repairs a submission. Use `form.reset()` for Reset, and `onSubmitInvalid` with a form-scoped invalid-control lookup or an explicit ref for focus. Return field errors from `onSubmitAsync` for server validation. Simple visual-state examples can pass `aria-invalid` and FieldError directly.

The application-owned `useRecordForm` keeps its record-specific validation and submission policy. Package examples import TanStack directly; they do not import that application helper.

## Don't

Do not disable submit merely because values are incomplete, discard a draft after failure, use placeholders as labels, or announce success before saving. Do not put a button inside a link. Keep essential instructions visible, and let long translated labels wrap.

<!-- page: Patterns/Gates (src/stories/patterns/Gates.mdx) -->

# Gates

The conditions an action waits on, what a record still needs, a phase's entry and exit criteria. A met gate is a check and its label, muted. An unmet gate is a Dot in its tone, the label, the reason under it and the action that meets it. A list, never a score: the reader sees which, and why. The nearest thing elsewhere is a pull request's merge checks: a set, where a progress tracker is a sequence.

_Example: story `Stories.GatesStory`._

## Anatomy

| Part   | What it is                                                                                  |
| ------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Mark   | A 16px box: a check in `color.icon.success` when met, the 6px Dot in the tone when not.     |
| Label  | `font.body.small`: the condition. `color.text.subtle` when met, `color.text` when not.      |
| Reason | `font.body.xsmall` in `color.text.subtle` under the label: what is missing, or the finding. |
| Action | At the end of the row: a link Button or a TextLink, the one thing that meets the gate.      |
| List   | A `ul`, `space.050` between rows, `space.100` between the mark and the label.               |

_Example: story `Stories.GatesMatrix`._

## Variants

Gates has one appearance. What varies is the unmet tone, and where the list lives.

| Unmet tone | Use                                                                                    |
| ---------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `warning`  | The default: the gate can be met from this record, and the reason says how.            |
| `danger`   | Nothing on this record can move it: the source gives no reason, the PM has not signed. |

| Where                         | What                                                                                     |
| ----------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| A record's rail               | Under a Collapsible titled Gates with the unmet count: what the requirement still needs. |
| A Needs block on the overview | Unmet gates only, each with its action.                                                  |
| A revision's submit gates     | Every gate, met and not, under the revision's facts.                                     |

What is not a gate: a workflow's steps, which are a [Stepper](?path=/docs/components-stepper--docs); a checklist the reader ticks, which is a group of [Checkbox](?path=/docs/components-checkbox--docs); a fraction met, which is a score and belongs to nothing here.

## Sizes

One size: the row is one line of `font.body.small`, and a second of `font.body.xsmall` when there is a reason. The list is as wide as its rail or block; a long reason wraps under its label, never beside it.

## States

| State          | What changes                                                                                |
| -------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Met            | The check, the label in `color.text.subtle`, no reason unless the finding is worth reading. |
| Unmet, warning | The warning Dot, the label in `color.text`, the reason, the action if there is one.         |
| Unmet, danger  | The danger Dot; otherwise the same.                                                         |
| All met        | Every row a check: a quiet list, which is the point of a list that is done.                 |

_Example: story `Stories.AllMet`._

## Modifiers

- **`met`** on each item: what the mark, the label's colour and the spoken state follow.
- **`tone`** for the unmet colour: `danger` when nothing here can move it.
- **`reason`** for the sentence under the label. On an unmet gate always; on a met one only when the finding is worth reading, such as who signed and when.
- **`action`** for the one link that meets it, on the gates the reader can meet from here.

_Example: story `Stories.InRail`._

## Content

- **The label names the condition as a noun phrase:** "Owner", "Success criterion", "Contested overlays resolved". Not a verb ("Add an owner") and not a question.
- **The reason is one sentence:** what is missing, or the finding. "Nothing decides that it is met." "SI-7(1) gives no reason."
- **The action is a verb:** "Add", "Allocate", "Resolve". It goes to where the gate is met.
- **The order is the order they are checked**, met and unmet together, not sorted by state. The reader learns the list.

## Style

| Element | Token                                                                                            |
| ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Mark    | 16px box · check `dimension.icon.small` in `color.icon.success` · Dot 6px in `color.icon.<tone>` |
| Label   | `font.body.small` · `color.text.subtle` met · `color.text` unmet                                 |
| Reason  | `font.body.xsmall` · `color.text.subtle` · `space.025` under the label                           |
| Row     | `space.100` between mark, text and action · `space.050` between rows                             |
| Action  | The link Button's or TextLink's own style                                                        |

The Dot is Badge's, so an unmet gate in `warning` is the same amber as a warning Indicator.

## Accessibility

- **It is a list**: `ul` and `li`, so a screen reader announces the count and moves row by row.
- **The state is spoken.** "Met:" or "Not met:" is visually hidden before each label; the check and the Dot are hidden from assistive technology, so nothing is said twice.
- **The unmet tone is not spoken.** A danger gate's reason says that nothing here can move it, in words.
- **The action is the only focusable part**, named by its own text; the label before it in reading order gives the context.
- **No live region.** Gates change when the record changes, and the page re-renders; an Alert says what happened if something must be announced.

## Props

_Props: generated from `Gates`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._

### Gates.Item

_Props: generated from `Gates.Item`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._

### Playground

_Example: story `Stories.Playground`._

_Rendered in the Storybook: Controls._

## Related

- [Stepper](?path=/docs/components-stepper--docs): steps in order, which gates are not.
- [Checkbox](?path=/docs/components-checkbox--docs): a list the reader ticks.
- [Alert](?path=/docs/components-alert--docs): what is wrong, when it is one thing and not a list.
- [Badge](?path=/docs/components-badge--docs): the tone table and the Dot.

## Don't

_Example: story `Stories.Dont`._

<!-- page: Patterns/Glance (src/stories/patterns/Glance.mdx) -->

# Glance

A compact record summary: an id and status, a title, a meta line and selected facts. It supplies content for a [HoverCard](?path=/docs/components-hovercard--docs); the product chooses the facts and the link's destination.

_Example: story `Stories.GlanceStory`._

## Anatomy

| Part          | Behavior                                                                              |
| ------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Id and status | The id uses small subtle text; the optional status sits at the other end of the line. |
| Title         | Medium body text, clamped to two lines.                                               |
| Meta          | Small subtle text for kind, path, owner or other context.                             |
| Facts         | Up to four KeyValue rows with 88px labels. Additional facts are omitted.              |

Use a Badge or Indicator with a text label for status. Select facts that help readers decide whether to open the record; keep any essential information available at the destination.

_Example: story `Stories.GlanceMatrix`._

## Surface and interaction

Glance supplies content and has no width or open state of its own. These examples use a 300px surface. A HoverCard defaults to 256px; set `style={{ width: 300 }}` on `HoverCardContent` when the summary needs more space.

HoverCard opens after delayed pointer hover or keyboard focus on its trigger, and dismisses on leaving, outside press or Escape. Its content does not add a Tab stop or move focus. Use the trigger link to reach the destination, where the summary's information and actions remain available.

When rendered on a page, Glance's text reads in order: id, status, title, meta, then facts. The component has no interactive controls.

## Props

_Props: generated from `Glance`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._

_Example: story `Stories.Playground`._

_Rendered in the Storybook: Controls._

## Related

[HoverCard](?path=/docs/components-hovercard--docs) · [PreviewSheet](?path=/docs/patterns-previewsheet--docs) · [KeyValue](?path=/docs/components-keyvalue--docs) · [Pages](?path=/docs/layout-pages--docs)

<!-- page: Patterns/PickerSheet (src/stories/patterns/PickerSheet.mdx) -->

# PickerSheet

Choosing many from hundreds: the association panel. A [Sheet](?path=/docs/components-sheet--docs) whose toolbar is a search field and the filters, whose body is a [DataTable](?path=/docs/patterns-data-table--docs) with sortable headers and a selection, and whose footer names how many are chosen and the one thing to do with them. The selection survives search and filters. When the chosen rows need fields of their own, a second frame of the same sheet shows them as a compact table with editable cells and a defaults row applied to all; `onBack` returns to the first frame with the selection kept. The kit owns the frame; the caller owns the columns, the rows and the selection. When the many are found by name rather than by attribute, a [Combobox](?path=/docs/components-combobox--docs) is the picker, and when there is one to pick, the [RecordPicker](?path=/docs/patterns-recordpicker--docs).

_Example: story `Stories.PickerSheetStory`._

## Anatomy

Back is rendered only when `onBack` is supplied. The toolbar and its divider are omitted when `search`, `filters` and `toolbar` are all absent.

| Part     | What it is                                                                                       |
| -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Back     | A chevron before the title on the second frame.                                                  |
| Title    | The task: "Allocate requirements".                                                               |
| Subtitle | What the chosen rows will be attached to: "Flight computer · 14 allocated today".                |
| Toolbar  | The search field and the FilterChips; on the second frame, the defaults row. It does not scroll. |
| Body     | Frame one: the DataTable with Table.Selection. Frame two: the chosen rows with editable cells.   |
| Count    | At the start of the footer: "12 chosen of 28", "28 to choose from", with Clear beside it.        |
| Actions  | At the end of the footer: a lesser button, Cancel, then the primary named in full.               |

## Variants

| Frame    | Use                                                                                                                            |
| -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Choosing | Search, filters, the sortable table, the selection, the count. The primary continues or attaches.                              |
| Details  | The chosen rows as a compact table with editable cells and a defaults row; "Does not apply" per row; back keeps the selection. |

Not built, and why: a Combobox with hundreds of options, because the many are found by attribute and a table sorts and filters; the selection lost on search, because the reader searches several times before attaching; a wizard of three frames, because choosing and describing are the two steps there are; a picker that attaches one at a time, because the footer attaches all at once and says how many.

## Sizes

One: 760px, room for a table of four columns; `width` for more. On a narrow screen the sheet takes the full width and the table scrolls inside it.

## States

| State          | What changes                                                               |
| -------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Nothing chosen | The footer says what there is to choose from; the primary waits, disabled. |
| Some chosen    | The count and Clear; the primary is live and names the number.             |
| Filtered       | The count says "of" the rows on offer; the selection is kept.              |
| Frame two      | The back chevron; the toolbar is the defaults row.                         |

## Modifiers

- **`search`**, **`filters`**, **`toolbar`** for the row that stays put.
- **`selected`**, **`total`**, **`onClear`** for the footer's count.
- **`action`**, **`secondary`** for the footer's buttons; **`onBack`** for the second frame; **`width`**.

## Content

- **The title is the task**, a verb and its object: "Allocate requirements", "Tailor the baseline".
- **The subtitle is what the rows attach to**, and a read-out: "Flight computer · 14 allocated today".
- **The primary is named in full**: "Allocate 12 to Flight computer", "Continue with 12". Never "OK", "Submit", "Done".
- **The count is a sentence of numbers**: "12 chosen of 28", "Nothing chosen yet", "28 to choose from".
- **The secondary is the lesser way through**: "Continue without details".

## Style

| Element | Token                                                                                                                                  |
| ------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Sheet   | Sheet's: `elevation.surface.overlay` · `elevation.shadow.overlay` · `color.blanket` behind                                             |
| Toolbar | `space.200` inline · `space.100` block · `color.border` under · `space.100` between its rows                                           |
| Search  | InputGroup 240px · Input small                                                                                                         |
| Body    | The DataTable without its own frame, edge to edge                                                                                      |
| Footer  | `elevation.surface.sunken` · `color.border` above · `font.body.small` `color.text.subtle` count, tabular · `space.100` between buttons |

## Accessibility

- **A dialog named by the task** and described by the subtitle; focus moves to the search field on open and returns to the opener on close.
- **The table is the DataTable's**: a grid with the selection column's checkboxes named by the row, sortable headers that say their order.
- **The count is live text**: it changes as rows are chosen and a screen reader reads it on request, not on every change.
- **The primary is disabled until something is chosen** and named with the number, so the reader hears what will happen to how many.
- **Escape closes the sheet** on either frame; the back chevron goes to the first frame with the selection kept.

## Props

_Props: generated from `PickerSheet`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._

## Related

- [Pages · Choosing many](?path=/docs/layout-pages--docs#choosing-many): the two frames, what the kit owns and what the caller owns, and the spec.
- [DataTable](?path=/docs/patterns-data-table--docs): frame one is a DataTable in the sheet.
- [Sheet](?path=/docs/components-sheet--docs): the frame.
- [RecordPicker](?path=/docs/patterns-recordpicker--docs): picking one record from a list.
- [Combobox](?path=/docs/components-combobox--docs): choosing by name.

## Don't

_Example: story `Stories.Dont`._

<!-- page: Patterns/PreviewNavigation (src/stories/patterns/PreviewNavigation.mdx) -->

# PreviewNavigation

Use in `Shell.Panel.actions` for a record preview beside a register. The panel title is the record's name. These controls move through the table's displayed results and open the full record in a new tab.

_Example: story `Stories.Collection`._

The application owns selection, filtered and sorted row order, and real record destinations. Supply a one-based `position`, `total`, and callbacks for adjacent records. `openLink` is an anchor or router link with its real destination, `target="_blank"`, and `rel="noopener noreferrer"`. It must lead to that record, not its collection.

If filtering removes the selected record, keep the preview open with `position={0}`. Both navigation buttons become disabled and the status explains that the record is outside the current results. The full-record link stays available.

_Example: story `Stories.OutsideResults`._

The controls have consistent accessible names: “Previous record”, “Next record” and “Open full record in new tab”. The screen reader status announces “n of m records”. Focus stays on the navigation control as the preview content changes.

_Props: generated from `Stories.Collection`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._

<!-- page: Patterns/PreviewSheet (src/stories/patterns/PreviewSheet.mdx) -->

# PreviewSheet

A modal record task surface built from shadcn's Base UI Sheet. It supports focused work such as evidence-version review. Collection browsing normally uses Shell.Panel with PreviewNavigation. The outer header holds global navigation and Close. The body begins with an inner PageHeader for the record's name and commands; metadata follows below it.

_Example: story `Stories.CollectionTask`._

The following specimen demonstrates generic metadata options and frame replacement for consumers with a different product contract.

_Example: story `Stories.PreviewSheetStory`._

## Anatomy

| Slot                        | Purpose                                                                                                    |
| --------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| title                       | The inner PageHeader's h2; its SheetTitle also names the modal.                                            |
| actions                     | Record commands in PageHeader.Actions beside the title; use small controls.                                |
| id, status, subtitle, facts | Optional body metadata below the record header; absent content leaves no placeholder rows.                 |
| onBack                      | Return to the previous frame from the outer header.                                                        |
| navigation                  | Global controls in the outer header, normally PreviewNavigation with previous/next and a full-record link. |
| openTo                      | Fallback full-record link in the outer header when navigation is absent.                                   |
| links                       | Related destination links in the footer; no repeated full-record link.                                     |
| children                    | Scrollable work area after the record header and metadata.                                                 |
| initialFocus, finalFocus    | Native Base UI focus targets for the consuming workflow.                                                   |

## Variants and states

Choose this surface when the current task benefits from containing focus; use Shell.Panel for selected work alongside a queue. Both support record actions in the inner record header. The sheet defaults to 720px and fits narrower screens. Keep commands concise: one small primary action and an overflow menu for additional commands.

The outer header never repeats the visible record name or holds record commands. It contains Back when provided, collection navigation or the fallback full-record link, and Close. Supplying `navigation` suppresses `openTo`; include the full-record destination in that navigation. The footer, when present, contains related links only.

The caller controls `open` and owns dismissal, in-progress work and the related-record stack. Back changes the frame; Close dismisses the sheet. Keep browser history aligned when that stack is represented in the URL.

_Example: story `Stories.CompleteReview`._

## Accessibility

Base UI provides the dialog semantics, modal focus containment, Escape dismissal and focus return. By default, PreviewSheet focuses its title so users encounter the identity before the record's structured content. Use `initialFocus` for an appropriate field in a task-oriented form, and `finalFocus` when completing work removes the opener. A short supplied subtitle becomes the description; an absent subtitle creates no empty description.

The visible Close remains available in the outer header. Keep pending/unsaved-work handling in the caller, including dismissal guards where the actual workflow needs them. Navigation uses named anchors; record commands use buttons in the inner header.

Sources: [shadcn Base Sheet](https://ui.shadcn.com/docs/components/base/sheet), [implementation](https://github.com/shadcn-ui/ui/blob/main/apps/v4/registry/bases/base/ui/sheet.tsx), [Base UI Dialog](https://base-ui.com/react/components/dialog), [WAI-ARIA dialog guidance](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/dialog-modal/).

## Props

_Props: generated from `PreviewSheet`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._

## Related

[Shell.Panel](?path=/docs/layout-shell--docs), [PreviewNavigation](?path=/docs/patterns-previewnavigation--docs), [Sheet](?path=/docs/components-sheet--docs), [Pages](?path=/docs/layout-pages--docs).

<!-- page: Patterns/RecordBrowser (src/stories/patterns/RecordBrowser.mdx) -->

# RecordBrowser

Find, compare and select related records without leaving the current record. Use this for evidence, assessment objectives and other collections where a compact picker cannot show enough information to make a decision.

_Example: story `Stories.BrowseAndLink`._

## Anatomy

A Base UI Dialog occupies 90% of the viewport. Its header names the relationship task; search, column filters and permanent actions sit above a selectable DataTable. Preview uses the table's existing eye in the first value cell, visible on row hover, keyboard focus or while active. A separate preview pane shows the complete record, previous/next controls and a selection checkbox. The footer keeps the selection count, Cancel and the linking action visible.

The caller supplies eligible records, columns including a `c.id` column, preview content and the linking callback. The pattern connects the ID column's existing preview callbacks and owns the temporary search, filters, sort, pagination, selection and preview state. Business rules and record content stay in the application.

## Behavior

Previewing never selects or links a record. Checkboxes select; only the footer confirms. Selection survives search, filtering, pagination and preview navigation. Clear selection resets it. By default, closing the dialog discards the selection; reopening starts a new session. Callers can retain selection across a related creation workflow with `selectedIds` and `onSelectionChange`. Link failures show an error and preserve selection for retry.

Arrows traverse the rows on the current table page in their displayed order. At the ends they are disabled. When a preview is outside the filtered results, its arrows are disabled and its selection remains available.

At narrow dialog widths the preview replaces the results area while keeping the table mounted. Back to results restores the previous view and focus. Table scrolling stays within its own region.

## Accessibility

The dialog uses the existing [shadcn Base UI composition](https://ui.shadcn.com/docs/components/base/dialog) and [Base UI focus management](https://base-ui.com/react/components/dialog). Opening a preview focuses its heading; closing it restores the row's preview button. Escape closes the internal preview first, then the dialog. Nested filter menus consume their own Escape. Closing the dialog returns focus to its opener.

Name each column and provide a clear `recordTitle`. Preview content can contain ordinary disclosures for related information. Keep related previews inside this dialog.

## Props

`records` contains eligible records with stable IDs. `columns` uses `defineColumns`; `filters` names filterable columns. `recordTitle` and `renderPreview` describe the preview. `onConfirm` receives all selected records, including selections hidden by filters or pagination; it may return a promise. `confirmLabel` names the action. `context` is optional relationship context; `actions` holds permanent controls such as New evidence reference.

`selectedIds` and `onSelectionChange` optionally let the caller own selection. This supports a sequential New evidence flow that closes the browser temporarily and returns with the earlier selections intact. The caller decides when to clear its controlled selection. The default behavior is unchanged when these props are omitted.

_Example: story `Stories.RetainedSelection`._

## Related

Use RecordPicker for quick single-record selection. PickerSheet remains useful for allocation workflows with extra relationship fields. RecordBrowser is the comparison and bulk-linking experience; it composes Dialog, Toolbar and DataTable.

_Example: story `Stories.FailedLink`._

<!-- page: Patterns/RecordPicker (src/stories/patterns/RecordPicker.mdx) -->

# RecordPicker

Pick one record from a list: evidence to link, a requirement to derive from, a person to assign. A [Command](?path=/docs/components-command--docs) dialog whose rows are the id, the name with its meta under it and one badge at the end, with the count of matches in the field and the keys in the footer. Presentational: the caller supplies the records and gets the chosen one back, and the picker closes itself. For choosing many by attribute, the [PickerSheet](?path=/docs/patterns-pickersheet--docs); for choosing by name inside a form, a [Combobox](?path=/docs/components-combobox--docs).

_Example: story `Stories.RecordPickerStory`._

## Anatomy

| Part   | What it is                                                                  |
| ------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Field  | The search, focused on open, with the count of matches at its end.          |
| Row    | The id in `color.text.subtle`; the name, the meta line under it; one badge. |
| Empty  | "Nothing matches." when the query finds none.                               |
| Footer | The keys: the arrows to move, Enter to choose, Escape to close.             |

_Example: story `Stories.RecordPickerMatrix`._

## Variants

RecordPicker has one appearance. What varies is the record: with a badge for its state or freshness, without; with a meta line, without; with keywords that match the query and are never shown.

Not built, and why: picking several with checkboxes, because many are chosen by attribute in a PickerSheet; a "create new" row, because a record is created on its own page; groups by kind, because the records offered are one kind and the caller narrows them; a preview of the chosen record, because the row says enough to choose and the link on the record after says the rest.

## Sizes

One: the Command dialog at its large width, 640px, the list at most 46% of the viewport's height so the field and the footer stay in view.

## States

| State    | What changes                                                      |
| -------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Closed   | Not rendered.                                                     |
| Open     | Over the page at the top, the field focused, every record listed. |
| Filtered | The rows that match, the count in the field.                      |
| None     | The empty sentence.                                               |
| Chosen   | The picker closes and the caller has the record.                  |

## Modifiers

- **`records`**: id, title, meta, badge, keywords.
- **`title`**, **`placeholder`**, **`emptyHint`** as in Content.

## Content

- **The title is the task**: "Link evidence", "Assign to", "Derive from".
- **The placeholder says what to type**: "Search evidence…", "Search people…". Not "Search…".
- **The meta is kind, source, date** in a few words: "Evidence · 12 Aug 2026".
- **One badge**, the state or the freshness the choice turns on: Fresh, Stale, Draft.
- **Keywords are for matching**, never shown: "dr disaster recovery" under "Backup restore drill".

## Style

| Element | Token                                                                                                        |
| ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Dialog  | CommandDialog: `radius.xxlarge` · `elevation.surface.overlay` · `elevation.shadow.overlay` · `color.blanket` |
| Row     | CommandItem, as tall as two lines · `space.100` block · `color.background.selected` when selected            |
| Id      | Id · `color.text.subtle`                                                                                     |
| Meta    | `font.body.xsmall` · `color.text.subtle`                                                                     |
| Badge   | Badge, xsmall                                                                                                |
| Footer  | CommandFooter: `elevation.surface.sunken` · `font.body.xsmall` · Kbd for each key                            |

## Accessibility

- **A dialog named by the title**; focus moves to the field on open and returns to the opener on close.
- **The list is a listbox** and each row an option named by its text: the id, the name, the meta and the badge, so "EV-0412 Firewall ruleset export Evidence 12 Aug 2026 Fresh".
- **The arrows move, Enter chooses, Escape closes**, and the footer says so with Kbd, each key named in full for a screen reader.
- **The count of matches is text** in the field's hint, read with the field.

## Props

_Props: generated from `RecordPicker`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._

## Related

- [Command](?path=/docs/components-command--docs): the dialog and the list.
- [PickerSheet](?path=/docs/patterns-pickersheet--docs): choosing many by attribute.
- [CommandPalette](?path=/docs/patterns-commandpalette--docs): the same CommandDialog, running a command instead of picking a record.
- [Combobox](?path=/docs/components-combobox--docs): one by name, inside a form.

## Don't

_Example: story `Stories.Dont`._

<!-- page: Patterns/Related (src/stories/patterns/Related.mdx) -->

# Related

A card of linked records, in a rail or in the body of a page. Its header is the kind of record, a Count and the way to add one. Its body is a row per record in a rail, or a card per record on a page: the name as the link, a mark, one status, the properties the reader decides by, and the actions that show on hover. Its footer is "See all" when it shows a handful of many. When nothing is linked it is a proper [Empty](?path=/docs/components-empty--docs), the mark, a statement and the way to fill it, never a line of grey text.

On the body of a page: a header with the kind and "+ Add", a card per related record with its name as the link and up to six properties, the actions in a menu that shows on hover, "view all" at the bottom. In the rail, one row per record. A card is metadata with actions on hover, and a card that carries actions of its own cannot be one click target. So the title is the link and the actions are stops of their own, in both layouts.

_Example: story `Stories.RelatedMatrix`._

## Anatomy

The header and the footer are the card's; the rows are [Item](?path=/docs/components-item--docs)s; the cards are `Related.Card`.

| Part              | What it is                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| ----------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Title             | The kind of record, a noun, an h3 in `font.body` semibold: "Linked findings", "Systems", "Team".                                                                                                        |
| Count             | After the title: how many are linked.                                                                                                                                                                   |
| Action            | At the end of the header's line: one small button, "Add" or "Link" with a plus, or a TextLink. The way to add one; it stays when the card is empty.                                                     |
| Row (`list`)      | An Item, flush: a mark or an id, the name as the link, and the state or the date at the end. The hairlines and the hover fill span the card; the text sits at its inset.                                |
| Card (`cards`)    | A `Related.Card` in a grid: the mark, the name as the link, the status and the meta under it, the properties, the actions at the top end, a line of its own under.                                      |
| Card · Leading    | The mark before the name, 32px, spanning the name and the meta line: a medium Avatar, square for a thing, round for a person.                                                                           |
| Card · Title      | The record's name, `font.body` medium, one line. With `link`, the link, underlined on hover.                                                                                                            |
| Card · Meta       | Under the name, `font.body.small` subtle: kind, path, owner.                                                                                                                                            |
| Card · Status     | One Badge or Indicator at the start of the meta line.                                                                                                                                                   |
| Card · Properties | Label and value pairs under the head, KeyValue rows with a 96px label: four fit, six is the most.                                                                                                       |
| Card · Actions    | Icon buttons at the top end, their space kept so nothing shifts: open in a new tab, a menu with the rest. Hidden until hover or focus, always shown on a touch screen, kept shown while a menu is open. |
| Card · Children   | A line of its own under the properties: a row of Badges, a sentence.                                                                                                                                    |
| Footer            | Under the rows or the cards, after a rule: "See all 14" as a TextLink.                                                                                                                                  |
| Empty             | Where the rows would be: a compact Empty with a link icon, the title, a line and an action, from `empty`.                                                                                               |

## Variants

| Layout          | Use                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| --------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `list`          | A rail beside a record: one Item row per record, compact. What a row can carry at 270px is an id, a name and one thing at the end.                                                              |
| `cards`         | The body of a page: a grid of cards, as many across as fit at 240px each, sharing the row's width. A card carries the mark, the name, the status and the meta, four properties and the actions. |
| A related table | When the records need columns to compare: a Table in a [Card](?path=/docs/components-card--docs), headed by CardHeader. Not a Related; it is a section of the page.                             |

_Example: story `Stories.RelatedTable`._

Not built, and why: the whole card as the link, because a card that carries its own actions cannot be one click target and the actions are here; a card that scrolls, because a rail shows a handful and the footer says See all; search, sort and filters in the header, because a card long enough to need them is the record's tab, where the Table has them; a card that folds, because a handful of rows has nothing to fold; drag to reorder, because links have no order of their own.

## Sizes

| Size      | Row                             | Where                                           |
| --------- | ------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------- |
| `compact` | 28px for one line, the default. | The rail beside a record's overview.            |
| `default` | 36px for one line.              | A list beside a page's body, in a wider column. |

The size is the list's; every row in one card is the same height. A card in the grid is at least 240px wide and as many share a row as fit; it is as tall as its properties, and four properties keep a row of cards one height. The inset is `space.150` in a card, `space.200` in the header.

## States

| State           | What changes                                                                                                                      |
| --------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Hover on a card | `elevation.shadow.raised` under it; the actions appear; the name underlines under the pointer.                                    |
| Focus in a card | The actions appear while anything in the card has focus, so a keyboard reaches them; the focus ring is on the name or the button. |
| Touch           | The actions are always shown; there is no hover to reveal them.                                                                   |
| A menu open     | The actions stay shown while the card's menu is open.                                                                             |
| Hover on a row  | The Item's: `color.background.neutral.subtle.hovered` across the row.                                                             |
| Empty           | The compact Empty where the rows would be; the header and its action stay.                                                        |

## Modifiers

- **`title`**, **`count`**, **`action`**, **`footer`**, **`layout`**, **`size`**, **`empty`** as in Anatomy. `empty` is a string, the Empty's title, or the Empty's title, description, action and icon.
- **The rows** take the Item's props: `id`, `leading`, `title`, `meta`, `trailing`, `link` or `onSelect`.
- **The cards** take **`leading`**, **`title`**, **`link`**, **`meta`**, **`status`**, **`properties`**, **`actions`** and children.

## Content

- **The title is a noun**, the kind of record: "Linked findings", "Systems", "Team". Never a sentence.
- **A row is an id and a name**, and one thing at the end: the state as a word, or the date. A rail is too narrow for meta beside the name; a role beside a person's name is as much as fits.
- **A card is the name, the meta, one status and four properties**: the ones the reader decides by. Six is the most; past that the record has them.
- **The actions are what is done to the link**, not to the record: open in a new tab, edit the link, unlink. Never "Open"; the name is that. Unlink is the menu's last item, in danger.
- **A handful, then See all.** Five rows in a rail, a row of cards on a page; the footer says how many there are, and the record's tab lists them.
- **The empty state says what would be here and how to fill it**: "Nothing linked yet", "Not in a package yet", with the line and a link button. The header's action stays, so the way to add one is there twice at most, never nowhere.
- **People are neutral.** A round Avatar and the name; colour is for state.

## Style

| Element    | Token                                                                                                                                                                |
| ---------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Card frame | Card: `radius.large` · `color.border` · `elevation.surface.raised`                                                                                                   |
| Header     | `font.body` semibold · `color.text` · Count · `space.200` inline · `space.100` block · `color.border` rule under                                                     |
| Rows       | Item, `compact`, flush: `space.050` block · `space.200` inline · `color.border` hairlines across the card · `space.050` above and below the list                     |
| Grid       | `space.200` inset · `space.150` between cards · columns of at least 240px, as many as fit, sharing the width                                                         |
| Card       | `radius.large` · `color.border` · `elevation.surface.raised` · `space.150` inset · `space.100` between the head and the properties · hover `elevation.shadow.raised` |
| Card name  | `font.body` medium · `color.text` · underline on hover                                                                                                               |
| Card meta  | `font.body.small` · `color.text.subtle`                                                                                                                              |
| Properties | KeyValue, label 96px · `space.025` between                                                                                                                           |
| Actions    | IconButton, subtle, small · opacity 0 to 1 in `motion.duration.fast` · `space.025` between                                                                           |
| Footer     | `font.body.small` · `color.border` rule above · `space.200` inline · `space.100` block                                                                               |
| Empty      | Empty, compact · `space.200` inline · `space.150` block                                                                                                              |

## Accessibility

- **The heading is an `h3`** under the rail's or the section's h2, and the rows or the cards are a list named by it: a screen reader hears "Systems, list, 3 items".
- **The name is the link**, in a row and in a card, named by the record's name alone; the id, the status, the meta and the properties are read as the text beside it. A row's link is stretched over the row; a card's is the name, because the card has actions of its own.
- **The actions are always in the tab order.** They are hidden by opacity, not removed, and they show while any of them has focus; a keyboard reader reaches "Open Ground segment in a new tab" and "More for Ground segment" after the name. On a touch screen they are always shown.
- **Each action is a labelled icon button** that names the record: "Unlink" alone would be six identical buttons on a page of cards.
- **The count is text**, read after the title; the footer's link says how many.
- **The empty state is text, then the action**: the icon is hidden, the title and the line are read first, the button is a stop after them.
- **The hover shadow is decoration.** Nothing is said by it.

## Props

_Props: generated from `Related`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._

### Related.Card

_Props: generated from `Related.Card`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._

### Playground

_Example: story `Stories.Playground`._

_Rendered in the Storybook: Controls._

## Related

- [Item](?path=/docs/components-item--docs): the rows.
- [Card](?path=/docs/components-card--docs): the frame, and the related table.
- [Empty](?path=/docs/components-empty--docs): the compact empty state inside the card.
- [KeyValue](?path=/docs/components-keyvalue--docs): the properties.
- [Pages](?path=/docs/layout-pages--docs): supporting context and route content.

## Don't

_Example: story `Stories.Dont`._

## Record navigation

A card can open a preview through a separate action while its title remains a native link. The preview keeps a link to the full record and can include linked history.

_Example: story `Stories.RecordNavigation`._

## Migration

`Related.Row` and `RelatedRowProps` are removed. Use `Item`: `leading` replaces `lead`, `title` replaces `label`, and `onSelect` or `link` replaces `onClick`. Card links compose native props and refs through Base UI; leave the supplied link empty to use the card title, or supply its own children to override the link text.

<!-- page: Patterns/TaskRow (src/stories/patterns/TaskRow.mdx) -->

# TaskRow

An experimental shared completion row for checklists and work queues. The package owns the completion control, row layout and independent navigation/actions. The application owns its task model, status vocabulary, deadlines and persistence. Owner: Ledger maintainers; consumers own state mappings.

_Example: story `Stories.TaskRowMatrix`._

## Anatomy

A completion checkbox, text title, optional contextual meta, and trailing owner/date/status content. Actions and title navigation are separate interactive targets. TaskRow renders a list item: place it inside Item.Group for list headings, aligned columns and empty content.

## Variants

The same presentation supports interactive completion or a row without a completion control. Omitting `onCompletedChange` removes that control. Status is caller-rendered content; the package has no waiting/blocked enum.

## Sizes

Inherits the surrounding Item.Group's default or compact density. There is no second independent row-size scale. The title truncates within the row; dense metadata should be kept concise in narrow layouts.

## States

`completed` is caller-owned and strikes through the title. `onCompletedChange` requests the next boolean; it does not persist or optimistically change the row. Use `completionDisabled` while the application is saving and explain that state in `status`. Read-only rows can still navigate or expose separate actions.

_Example: story `Stories.Completion`._

## Modifiers

`assignee`, `due`, `status`, `meta` and `actions` are content slots. `dueDateTime` adds a semantic time element around due content. Without it, relative words remain plain content. The caller computes overdue status and supplies the corresponding styling. `link` or `onSelect` makes the title interactive; choose one. Completion and action controls remain siblings of the title control.

## Content

Use a short action as the title, such as “Review draft.” Supply formatted date content and a machine-readable date where possible. Translate `completionLabel` to name the current action and its row; English defaults are “Complete: title” and “Reopen: title.” Keep status wording and owner identity in the application.

## Style

Item supplies the shared row grid and interactive hit areas. Checkbox supplies focus and checked styling. Completed titles use subtle text and a line-through; due content retains tabular numerals. The product supplies any semantic status or deadline tone.

## Accessibility

Completion is a named, controlled checkbox with Space-key operation. Completing a task does not activate its row navigation. Title and action buttons are independent keyboard stops, without nested interactive elements. Completed rows without a checkbox include screen-reader text from `completedLabel` (English default “Completed”), so the strike-through is not the only completion cue.

## Props

_Props: generated from `TaskRow`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._
_Example: story `Stories.Playground`._
_Rendered in the Storybook: Controls._

## Related

- [Item](?path=/docs/components-item--docs) for general rows and groups.
- [Checkbox](?path=/docs/components-checkbox--docs) for independent boolean input.
- [Badge](?path=/docs/components-badge--docs) for caller-owned status content.
- The application's Task wrapper maps open/waiting/blocked/done, owner names and overdue presentation onto this contract. Create-task workflows remain in the application.

## Don't

_Example: story `Stories.Dont`._

<!-- page: Patterns/Toolbar (src/stories/patterns/Toolbar.mdx) -->

# Toolbar

The row above a table: search first, saved views next, filters after them, and display controls/actions at the end. Everything in it is the small size, so the row is one height and the table starts right under it. A [DataTable](?path=/docs/patterns-data-table--docs) takes it as `toolbar`, above its frameless rows; a plain [Table](?path=/docs/components-table--docs) puts it above.

It is a row of controls, not a heading. A standalone register has a PageHeader; an embedded register can use a Section. Toolbar contains controls only.

_Example: story `Stories.ToolbarMatrix`._

## Anatomy

| Part    | What it is                                                                                                                                                                              |
| ------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Search  | An [InputGroup](?path=/docs/components-inputgroup--docs) with the search icon and a small `Input` of type search, 200px, named by its placeholder. Only with `onSearch`.                |
| Views   | `views`, after search: permanent saved-view controls that never collapse into More.                                                                                                     |
| Filters | `filters`, after saved views: [FilterChips](?path=/docs/components-filterchip--docs), a [ToggleGroup](?path=/docs/components-togglegroup--docs) of lenses, a small Select that narrows. |
| Actions | `actions`, pushed to the end: small Buttons with the primary last, or a count as text, "12 of 340 controls".                                                                            |

## Variants

Toolbar has one appearance. What varies is which parts the register needs:

| The register                       | Use                                                                  |
| ---------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Searched, filtered, acted on       | Search, chips, actions.                                              |
| Seen through lenses                | No search; a ToggleGroup in `filters`, a count at the end.           |
| One thing to choose about the view | A small Select as a permanent child.                                 |
| Only a count or an Export          | `actions` alone.                                                     |
| Rows chosen for a batch action     | Not a Toolbar: the DataTable's SelectionBar appears above the table. |

There is no title in a Toolbar, no tall Toolbar (the kit's rows are one height and so is the row above them), and no collapsed search that opens from an icon: a register that is searched shows its field.

## Sizes

One height: every control in the row is small, `dimension.control.small` 28px, so a Button in it says `size="small"` and a SelectTrigger `size="sm"`. The toolbar measures its available container width. When the controls no longer fit, only `filters` move into More. Saved views (`views`), display controls (`children`) and `actions` remain visible. The popover uses ordinary Tab navigation so nested filters and menus keep their native behavior. At phone widths search gets a dedicated row when necessary to keep permanent controls visible. Filters never wrap across the toolbar. The caller owns surrounding spacing.

_Example: story `Stories.Live`._
_Example: story `Stories.Constrained`._

## States

The toolbar has no states of its own; its controls have theirs. The search field is empty (the placeholder names what is searched), typed, or focused, and the table under it narrows on every keystroke. A count at the end says how many rows remain, so the result of typing is read as well as seen.

## Modifiers

- **`search`, `onSearch`, `placeholder`**: the field, its value, and what it searches. Without `onSearch` there is no field.
- **`views`**: permanent saved-view controls immediately after search.
- **`filters`**: collapsible filters, after saved views.
- **`children`**: permanent display controls, such as grouping, columns and settings.
- **`actions`**: what sits at the end.
- **`className`** for a frame's own padding; inside a DataTable the frame gives it.

## Content

- **The placeholder names what is searched**: "Search controls", "Control or title". Not "Search…".
- **Filters are nouns**: Owner, Status, Gaps.
- **Up to five actions**; more go under a More menu. The primary last.
- **A count reads "12 of 340 controls"**, tabular, `font.body.small` in `color.text.subtle`. It is text, not a Badge or a Count.

## Style

| Element | Token                                                                                             |
| ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Row     | flex, one row · gap `space.100` · container-driven overflow into More                             |
| Search  | 200px · `dimension.control.small` · the search icon `dimension.icon.small` in `color.icon.subtle` |
| Actions | at the end · gap `space.100`                                                                      |
| Count   | `font.body.small` `color.text.subtle` · tabular numerals                                          |

## Accessibility

- **A plain row, not the ARIA `toolbar` role.** That role promises arrow-key movement between its controls; a row of a search field, chips and buttons is better served by Tab in reading order, so Toolbar renders a plain layout div.
- **The search field is named** by its placeholder through `aria-label`; the icon is decorative.
- **Typing narrows the table** under it. The count at the end is the result, in text a screen reader can read back.
- **The chips say pressed**; a chip that opens a popover says expanded. See FilterChip.
- **Order:** search, saved views, filters, display controls, actions. The reader narrows first and acts last, and Tab follows.

## Props

_Props: generated from `Toolbar`; the Storybook page and the package's `.d.ts` list them._

### Playground

_Example: story `Stories.Playground`._

_Rendered in the Storybook: Controls._

## Related

- [Table](?path=/docs/components-table--docs) below it; [Pagination](?path=/docs/components-pagination--docs) under the table.
- [DataTable](?path=/docs/patterns-data-table--docs): `DataTable.Search`, `.Filter`, `.Presets` and `.Columns` are the parts a toolbar holds when the table has state; `.SelectionBar` is the bar that replaces it while rows are chosen.
- [FilterChip](?path=/docs/components-filterchip--docs), [ToggleGroup](?path=/docs/components-togglegroup--docs): the filters.
- [PageHeader](?path=/docs/layout-pageheader--docs) names a standalone register; Section can name an embedded collection.

## Don't

_Example: story `Stories.Dont`._

# Tokens

Every design value is a token. The utility is the Tailwind class the lint allows; the CSS variable carries the light and dark values. Deprecated tokens are rejected by `ledger/no-deprecated-token`.

| Token | Utility | Variable | State | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `color.background.neutral` | `bg-neutral` | `--ds-color-background-neutral` |  | The default background for neutral elements, such as default buttons. |
| `color.background.neutral.hovered` | `bg-neutral-hovered` | `--ds-color-background-neutral-hovered` |  | Hovered state of the default neutral background. |
| `color.background.neutral.pressed` | `bg-neutral-pressed` | `--ds-color-background-neutral-pressed` |  | Pressed state of the default neutral background. |
| `color.background.neutral.subtle` | `bg-neutral-subtle` | `--ds-color-background-neutral-subtle` |  | Use for the background of elements that appear to have no background in a resting state, such as subtle buttons and menu items. |
| `color.background.neutral.subtle.hovered` | `bg-neutral-subtle-hovered` | `--ds-color-background-neutral-subtle-hovered` |  | Hovered state of elements that have no background at rest, such as subtle buttons and menu items. |
| `color.background.neutral.subtle.pressed` | `bg-neutral-subtle-pressed` | `--ds-color-background-neutral-subtle-pressed` |  | Pressed state of elements that have no background at rest. |
| `color.background.neutral.bold` | `bg-neutral-bold` | `--ds-color-background-neutral-bold` |  | A vibrant background option for neutral UI elements, such as announcement banners. |

| `elevation.surface.raised.pressed` | `bg-surface-raised-pressed` | `--ds-elevation-surface-raised-pressed` |  | Pressed state of raised surfaces. |
| `elevation.surface.overlay` | `bg-surface-overlay` | `--ds-elevation-surface-overlay` |  | Use for the background of elements that sit on top of the UI, such as modals, dropdown menus, flags and inline dialogs, with elevation.shadow.overlay. |
| `elevation.surface.overlay.hovered` | `bg-surface-overlay-hovered` | `--ds-elevation-surface-overlay-hovered` |  | Hovered state of overlay surfaces. |
| `elevation.surface.overlay.pressed` | `bg-surface-overlay-pressed` | `--ds-elevation-surface-overlay-pressed` |  | Pressed state of overlay surfaces. |
| `elevation.shadow.raised` | `shadow-raised` | `--ds-elevation-shadow-raised` |  | Use for the box shadow of raised card elements, such as cards on a board. |
| `elevation.shadow.overlay` | `shadow-overlay` | `--ds-elevation-shadow-overlay` |  | Use for the box shadow of elements that sit on top of the UI, such as modals, menus and popovers. |
| `elevation.shadow.overflow` | `shadow-overflow` | `--ds-elevation-shadow-overflow` |  | Use to create a shadow when content scrolls under other content, such as a scrolling table. |
| `utility.elevation.surface.current` | `bg-surface-current` | `--ds-utility-elevation-surface-current` |  | The surface an element currently sits on. Surface-owning components set this variable; sticky and masking children read it. |
| `font.family.body` |  | `--ds-font-family-body` |  | The one UI face. Identifiers, dates and numbers use it too. |
| `font.family.heading` |  | `--ds-font-family-heading` |  | Same face as body today; a token so a theme may split them. |
| `font.family.code` |  | `--ds-font-family-code` |  | Code blocks and data previews only. Never UI text. |
| `font.weight.regular` | `font-regular` | `--ds-font-weight-regular` |  | Body, cells, controls. |
| `font.weight.medium` | `font-medium` | `--ds-font-weight-medium` |  | Labels, UI headings, emphasis inside body text. |
| `font.weight.semibold` | `font-semibold` | `--ds-font-weight-semibold` |  | Page and record titles only. |
| `font.letterSpacing.0` |  | `--ds-font-letter-spacing-0` |  |  |
| `font.letterSpacing.100` |  | `--ds-font-letter-spacing-100` |  | Smallest sizes. |
| `font.letterSpacing.200` |  | `--ds-font-letter-spacing-200` |  | Body sizes. |
| `font.letterSpacing.300` |  | `--ds-font-letter-spacing-300` |  | Headings up to 20px. |
| `font.letterSpacing.400` |  | `--ds-font-letter-spacing-400` |  | Display sizes. |
| `font.letterSpacing.500` |  | `--ds-font-letter-spacing-500` |  | Uppercase micro labels: eyebrows, group headings. |
| `font.body.large` | `font-body-large` | `--ds-font-body-large` |  | Reading text and dialog body. |
| `font.body.small` | `font-body-small` | `--ds-font-body-small` |  | Table headers, field labels, badges, KeyValue. Labels add font.weight.medium. |
| `font.body.xsmall` | `font-body-xsmall` | `--ds-font-body-xsmall` |  | Eyebrow, counts, metadata. |
| `font.body` | `font-body` | `--ds-font-body` |  | Controls, cells, tabs, inputs, menu items. The UI size. |
| `font.heading.large` | `font-heading-large` | `--ds-font-heading-large` |  | Display: a stat value, a dashboard number. Not a page title. |
| `font.heading.medium` | `font-heading-medium` | `--ds-font-heading-medium` |  | Page and record titles. The only semibold. |
| `font.heading.small` | `font-heading-small` | `--ds-font-heading-small` |  | Section headings. |
| `font.heading.xsmall` | `font-heading-xsmall` | `--ds-font-heading-xsmall` |  | Dialog and card titles. |
| `font.heading.xxsmall` | `font-heading-xxsmall` | `--ds-font-heading-xxsmall` |  | Eyebrows, group headings and menu section labels. The component adds the uppercase. |
| `font.code` | `font-code` | `--ds-font-code` |  | Code blocks only. |
| `motion.duration.micro` | `duration-micro` | `--ds-motion-duration-micro` |  | A toggle's thumb, a checkbox's tick, a chevron turning: the smallest moves. |
| `motion.duration.fast` | `duration-fast` | `--ds-motion-duration-fast` |  | Hover and press colour, a tooltip's fade, a menu or a popover leaving. |
| `motion.duration.medium` | `duration-medium` | `--ds-motion-duration-medium` |  | A menu or a popover arriving, a section expanding or collapsing, a dialog or a sheet leaving. |
| `motion.duration.moderate` | `duration-moderate` | `--ds-motion-duration-moderate` |  | A dialog or a sheet arriving, the panel sliding in, a toast, a page's content rising. |
| `motion.duration.slow` | `duration-slow` | `--ds-motion-duration-slow` |  | Marks arriving on a chart, and a drill-down redrawing it. |
| `motion.duration.slower` | `duration-slower` | `--ds-motion-duration-slower` |  | The blanket dimming the page under a dialog or a sheet. |
| `motion.stagger` |  | `--ds-motion-stagger` |  | Between one item's entrance and the next when a set arrives together: tiles, cards. Six at most, so the last lands within a moderate duration. |
| `motion.easing.standard` | `ease-standard` | `--ds-motion-easing-standard` |  | For what stays on screen throughout: colour, a chevron, a sort, a side panel leaving. |
| `motion.easing.enter` | `ease-enter` | `--ds-motion-easing-enter` |  | For what arrives: in quickly, slowing to a stop. |
| `motion.easing.exit` | `ease-exit` | `--ds-motion-easing-exit` |  | For what leaves for good: speeding up out of view. |
| `opacity.disabled` | `opacity-disabled` | `--ds-opacity-disabled` |  | Use for the opacity of disabled elements when a disabled token does not exist. |
| `opacity.loading` | `opacity-loading` | `--ds-opacity-loading` |  | Use for the opacity of content in a loading state. |
| `radius.xsmall` | `rounded-xsmall` | `--ds-radius-xsmall` |  | Draft, on a 5px base. Checkbox, tiny chips. |
| `radius.small` | `rounded-small` | `--ds-radius-small` |  | Draft. Badges, count chips, Kbd, skeleton, inline hit targets. |
| `radius.medium` | `rounded-medium` | `--ds-radius-medium` |  | Draft. Buttons, inputs, chips, menu items. |
| `radius.large` | `rounded-large` | `--ds-radius-large` |  | Draft. Cards, popovers. |
| `radius.xlarge` | `rounded-xlarge` | `--ds-radius-xlarge` |  | Draft. Dialogs, sheets. |
| `radius.xxlarge` | `rounded-xxlarge` | `--ds-radius-xxlarge` |  | Draft. Large surfaces, spotlight cards. |
| `radius.full` | `rounded-full` | `--ds-radius-full` |  | Dots, avatars, pills, meters. |
| `border.width.selected` | `border-w-selected` | `--ds-border-width-selected` |  | The width used to indicate a selected element, such as an active tab or a chosen item. |
| `border.width.focused` | `border-w-focused` | `--ds-border-width-focused` |  | The width used for the focus ring on interactive elements. |
| `border.width` | `border-w-default` | `--ds-border-width` |  | The default width for all standard component borders and dividers. |
| `space.0` | `p-0 · gap-0 · m-0 · w-0 …` | `--ds-space-0` |  | No space. |
| `space.100` | `p-100 · gap-100 · m-100 · w-100 …` | `--ds-space-100` |  | Standard small: control clusters, chip rows. |
| `space.150` | `p-150 · gap-150 · m-150 · w-150 …` | `--ds-space-150` |  | Standard medium: cell padding, card header inset. |
| `space.200` | `p-200 · gap-200 · m-200 · w-200 …` | `--ds-space-200` |  | Standard large: card padding, form grids. |
| `space.250` | `p-250 · gap-250 · m-250 · w-250 …` | `--ds-space-250` |  | Comfortable. |
| `space.300` | `p-300 · gap-300 · m-300 · w-300 …` | `--ds-space-300` |  | Relaxed: between header and actions. |
